* {{i|Dark Bum}} / {{i|Cambion Conception}}: Each Dark Bum tracks the collected hearts separately.
* {{i|King Baby}} / {{t|RC Remote}}: No effect.
* {{i|Options?}}: If one of the options is a Red Heart variant, Dark Bum may collect it, making the other option disappear.

sections.Effect:
* Upon use, rerolls each of Isaac's [[passive item]]s into new ones.
** {{dlc|na+}} The new items will be drawn from the [[Treasure Room (Item Pool)|Treasure Room item pool]].
** {{dlc|a+}} The new items will be drawn from the item pool where the original item was acquired.
** {{dlc|r}} If health upgrade items are removed by a reroll, the health they granted is subtracted.
sections.Notes:
* The D4 does not reroll {{i|Dead Cat|nr}}, {{i|Halo of Flies|nr}}, {{i|Key Piece 1}}, {{i|Key Piece 2}}, {{i|Missing No.}}, {{i|The Negative}}, {{i|The Polaroid}}, or {{i|Tonsil}}.
** {{dlc+|r}} The D4 can reroll Dead Cat and Halo of Flies, but will not reroll {{i|Dad's Note}}, {{I|Damocles}}, {{i|Dogma}}, {{i|Knife Piece 1}} and {{i|Knife Piece 2}}, and glitched items, in addition to the above.{{dlc-}}
** Note that {{i|Missing No.}} can be rerolled into, but not rerolled out of.
* The D4 does not remove traits or abilities inherent to a character, such as {{c|Azazel}}'s Brimstone-like attack, {{c|Lilith}}'s Incubus, or {{C|The Forgotten}}'s bone attack.
** Starting items from [[Challenges]] will also not be rerolled.
** {{dlc|r}} {{C|The Lost}}'s {{i|Holy Mantle}} is included.
** {{dlc|r+}} Characters' starting passive items (except {{c|Eden}}'s and {{c|Tainted Eden|n}}'s) are now inherent to them and will also not be rerolled.
* Items that grant pickups (like {{i|Pyro}} or {{i|A Dollar}}) do not remove their bonuses when rerolled.
** These same items also do not grant pickups when another item is rerolled into them.
* The D4 can grant items that have not yet been unlocked.
* The items gained by the D4 count towards the [[collection page]].
* Multiple copies of the same item (as generated by {{i|Diplopia}}, the [[Debug Console]], or gathering them from multiple item pools (e.g. {{i|Steam Sale}} from both the {{r|Shop}} and {{E|Greed}}) will each be rerolled into a different item, {{dlc|nr}} even though the duplicates are not present on the pause screen.
* There is a small chance that D4 will not reroll every item: the game makes a number of attempts to reroll each item, but if they all fail to produce a new item that is available and applicable, the original remains unchanged.
* Smelted/Swallowed trinkets (via {{i|Marbles}}, {{i|Smelter}} or [[Gulp!]]) will not be rerolled.
* Will reroll {{C|Eden}}'s starting item(s).
* {{dlc|nr}} Items rerolled away don't return to circulation and can't be encountered again.
** {{dlc|r}} Items rerolled away return to circulation and can be encountered again.
* {{dlc|nr}} D4 doesn't remove transformation progress, meaning that he will keep a transformation or gain one if he gets a transformation item while having two points of this transformation before rerolling.
* {{dlc|r}} D4 removes transformation progress.
* {{dlc|nr}} If it is unlocked, {{C|The Lost}} starts with this item along with spectral tears and flight. Using it ''will'' reroll {{i|Holy Mantle}}.
* {{dlc|r}} The D4 does not give hearts that would be otherwise gained from item pickups, but will remove previously collected health upgrade items.
* {{dlc|r}} If used while playing as {{C|Jacob and Esau|n}} or {{C|Tainted Lazarus|n}}, it will only reroll the items on the character that used it.
* {{c|Tainted Isaac}} can avoid having their health subtracted form rerolling health up items by dropping health items for full inventory before rerolling.
* {{dlc+|r+}} D4's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Abyss}}: Locusts created by Abyss are not rerolled.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Removes all of Isaac's wisps and gives him one random wisp for every two items rerolled. Book of Virtues will not be rerolled in the process.}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Car Battery|anr}}: Instantly rerolls Isaac's items twice, which doubles the speed at which the item pools are exhausted and transformations are achieved.
* {{i|Potato Peeler|a+nr}}: Every {{i|Cube of Meat}} produced counts as an item available to reroll. Because health usually is not removed when using the D4, this is useful to increase the number of items at the expense of the item pool.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, reveals the [[floor]] layout and all special rooms except the {{R|Super Secret Room}} and {{R|Ultra Secret Room}} and drops either a {{e|Soul Heart}} or a random [[Cards and Runes|card or rune]]. (50% chance of either)
* {{dlc+|r}} While held, increases the chance of finding a {{R|Planetarium}} by 15%, or 100% if a treasure room has been skipped.{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* Crystal Ball can be obtained by playing a {{e|Fortune Telling Machine}}.
** It's possible to get more than one Crystal Ball from {{e|Fortune Telling Machine}}s on a single run.
* The map revealing effect will not work if the {{cu|Lost}} is active.
* {{dlc+|r}} The Planetarium bonus guarantees the level generation to ''attempt'' placing one, but the level layout may not have enough room. Read the article on {{r|Planetarium}}s for further details.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Wisps have much greater health than normal wisps. Tears that are fired from the wisps will auto aim towards  nearby enemies, similar to {{I|Demon Baby}}.}}
sections.Interactions: * {{t|Daemon's Tail}}: The chance to drop cards or runes will change to 90%/10% in favor of {{e|Soul Heart}}.

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|nr}} Upon use, rerolls all [[monster]]s in the [[room]].
* {{dlc|r}} Upon use, replaces all [[monster]]s in the [[room]] with weaker monsters. Each monster type has a specific weaker monster it will transform into. If the monster is already at its weakest level, it usually transforms it into a background critter or kills it outright.
** Some enemies can be transformed into obstacles or pickups instead.

{{Clear}} <!--This is here to give the tables max width for better visibility-->
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} Rerolling a monster will replace it with an entirely new one from any floor, making it dangerous to use early on in the game (as Isaac could get monsters from {{s|Depths}} or later).
* {{dlc|nr}} The D10 will not reroll [[Boss]]es but can reroll monsters spawned by bosses.
* {{dlc+|r}} Transforming an enemy with the D10 does not always make it objectively easier to kill, as enemies can become capable of ranged attacks when they previously weren't (e.g. {{e|Globin}}s turning into {{e|Clotty|text=Clotties}}, or {{e|Evis}} turning into {{e|Double Vis}}).{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} The D10 will not reroll [[friendly]] enemies.
* Using this item can cause some rooms to become impossible to clear. Jumping or flying monsters may become trapped behind rocks after being rerolled, and therefore become unbeatable.
** Sealed doors open after 2 minutes, though there are situations that can prevent this failsafe from triggering.
* {{dlc|anr}} Flying monsters will only be rerolled into other flying monsters, and ground monsters can only be rerolled into ground monsters. ({{e|Horf}}s are classified as ground monsters by the D10).
* {{dlc|r}} Some invincible enemies will be rerolled, while others (including most Grimace variants) are completely unaffected.
* Using this item in a room with {{e|Mom's Hand}} can be very dangerous, as unless they have already landed, they will be directly on top of Isaac, resulting in the new monsters spawning directly on top of Isaac, instantly dealing contact damage.
* Using this item, then exiting the room, such as by teleporting or a bombed door, will cause the enemies to be in their original forms upon Isaac's return.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns orange wisps in the middle ring. Tears shot from these wisps have a 10% chance to replace enemies with their weaker variants.}}
* {{I|Car Battery|r}}: Weakens affected enemies twice.
sections.Interactions: * {{t|Broken Remote|nr}}: Using D10 while holding this will first teleport Isaac, and then reroll the enemies in the new room.

sections.Effects:
* Grants charged tears which fires a tight burst of tears. Firing mid-charge will shoot fewer tears depending on the charge time.
** {{dlc|nr}} The full burst size is four tears.
** {{dlc|r}} The full burst size is five tears.
** {{dlc|nr}} Quickly tapping the fire key will result in no tears being fired.
** Charging while a burst is currently firing will prevent the rest of the shots from being fired.
* Taking damage while mid-charge (holding fire, but not fully charged) will teleport Isaac into another room.
sections.Notes:
*In most cases effects that override cursed eye will remove the teleporting effect. 
**{{C|Tainted Samson}}/{{C|The Forgotten}}/{{I|Berserk!}}: While in their melee form, getting hit while charging a shot will cause the teleport effect regardless of items that normally override the effect.
*The damage per second increase is dependent on Isaac's current [[tears]] stat, with lower tears showing a larger increase. Ranging from a ~90% increase at a tear stat of 0.96 to becoming a damage loss at tear stat of ~23 or above. <ref>https://youtu.be/vUfkIGd-W2M </ref> 
*Having a high [[Tears]] stat around 10 or above without forms of auto firing such as {{i|Soy Milk}} or {{i|Marked}} can make it difficult to properly time charge shots, potentially leading to a damage loss.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Black Candle|a}}: Teleport effect is removed.
* {{i|Holy Mantle|a}}: Losing Holy Mantle while charging Cursed Eye will not teleport Isaac.
* {{i|Incubus|a+}}:
** {{dlc|nr}} Incubus fires 3 tears for each one that normally would be fired, with no change in delay.
** {{dlc|r}} Incubus has the same charge shots as most characters would. Getting hit while charging will have the chance to teleport, as usual.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Marked}}: Tears are charged and automatically fired to varying levels depending on the distance between Isaac and the reticule. The firing rate is greatly increased without affecting the tears stat, even beyond normal maximum fire rate. The teleport effect is removed.
* {{I|Technology|r}}: Becomes a quick charging laser that shoots multiple lasers on release.
* {{I|Epiphora|r}}: Epiphora's tear rate multiplier affects the number of tears in a burst for a total of ten shots with a full Epiphora charge.
* {{i|Technology 2}}: Laser fires while charging Cursed Eye. Tear delay for the charge is unaffected by Tech 2. Allows {{C|Cain}} to fire normal tears.
** {{dlc|r}} Tears are replaced with lasers, fired from the same eye of Tech 2. {{tf|Conjoined}} transformation removes the synergy.
* {{i|Mutant Spider}} / {{i|The Inner Eye}} / {{i|20/20}} / {{i|The Wiz}} / {{tf|Conjoined}}: Isaac shoots multiple tears from each eye, the amount is item-dependent.
* {{c|The Lost}}/{{c|Tainted Lost}}: Since The Lost dies in one hit, it is effectively immune to its teleportation effects, making this item much safer to use.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Almond Milk}}/{{i|Kidney Stone}} (when the barrage of tears is fired)/{{I|Soy Milk}}: Cursed Eye is automatically charged and fired when the fire key is held. The charge bar of Cursed Eye becomes invisible. The teleport effect remains.
** Having a [[tears]] stat of 30 or higher will trigger this effect as well, the above items will trigger this effect regardless of Isaac's [[tears]] stat.
** {{C|Lilith}} + {{I|Kidney Stone}}: When the kidney stone is shot, Incubus is unable to shoot for the duration of the effect, making this a anti-synergy.
* {{i|Anti-Gravity}}: Anti-Gravity effect cannot be used, as releasing a tear fire button also releases the Anti-Gravity Effect.
* {{C|Azazel}}/{{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|Dr. Fetus}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}/{{i|The Ludovico Technique}}/{{i|Mom's Knife}}/{{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Overrides Cursed Eye.
** With {{C|Tainted Samson}}/{{C|The Forgotten}}/{{I|Berserk!}}: While charging your bone you will be teleported if hit.
* {{I|C Section}}/{{I|Neptunus}}/{{I|Spirit Sword}}/{{C|Tainted Azazel}}: Overrides Cursed Eye.
** With {{C|Tainted Samson}}/{{C|The Forgotten}}/{{I|Berserk!}}: While charging your bone you will be teleported if hit.
* {{i|Chocolate Milk}}: Charged tear is followed by up to 3 minimum-power tears, depending on Cursed Eye's charge.
** {{Dlc|r}} Cursed Eye takes longer to charge, but low damage shots can be fired rapidly. If fully charged, Isaac fires five Chocolate Milk shots.
* {{i|Eye of the Occult}}: The tears stack on top of each other, and only move forward when holding a direction afterwards.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}: The skeleton form's charge attack becomes a rapid barrage of hits; the amount depends on how full the charge is, up to 4.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: At full charge, quick bursts of ipecac shots are fired.
* {{i|Neptunus}}: Overrides Cursed Eye.
* {{i|Sprinkler}}: Overrides Cursed Eye.
* {{C|Tainted Lilith}}: The fetus gains the effect of Cursed Eye and the teleportation effect does not happen.
* {{i|Technology|nr}}: Overrides Cursed Eye.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Overrides Cursed Eye.
* {{i|Urn of Souls}}: Opening the urn while charging will hold the charge until the urn is closed. As such, the teleport effect will always occur when hit with the opened urn.

sections.Effects:
* +0.5 [[Damage]].
* ×1.5 Damage multiplier.
sections.Notes: * The ×1.5 damage multiplier does not stack with the ×1.5 damage multiplier from {{i|Magic Mushroom}}, from the combination of {{i|The Book of Belial}} and {{i|Blood of the Martyr}}, or itself (by using an item such as {{i|Diplopia}}, for example). However, it will stack with any other multipliers, such as {{i|Sacred Heart}}.
sections.Synergies: * {{I|Abyss}}: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Cricket's Head, it turns into a larger red locust dealing {{dlc|rnr+}} triple / {{dlc|r+}} double Isaac’s damage per tick.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns an ice cube familiar. It cannot move on its own, but slides around when Isaac walks into it, uses a melee attack on it, or when Isaac or enemies shoot at it.
* The familiar damages and [[slow]]s enemies it touches while moving. It can deal up to 17.5 damage when it collides with enemies, depending on how fast it's moving.
* Monsters killed by Cube Baby are [[Freeze|frozen]].
** Frozen monsters will follow the same physics as Cube Baby, and will shatter on impact creating ice shards that are capable of freezing other monsters
* Cube Baby can block enemy projectiles.
* {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}
sections.Notes:
* Killing enemies by freezing them does not however count as a "kill" for the purposes of activating the on kill effects of certain items and trinkets. Because of this, only enemies killed by icicles from statues, bombs, familiars and other sources will count towards the on kill effects, rendering them quite difficult to use. These items and trinkets are: {{t|Bat Wing}}, {{i|Berserk!}}, {{i|Charm of the Vampire}}, {{t|Eve's Bird Foot}}, {{i|Jumper Cables}}, {{i|Lusty Blood}}, {{I|Red Stew}}, {{t|Samson's Lock}}, {{t|Sigil of Baphomet}}, {{i|Toxic Shock}}, and {{i|Vasculitis}}.
* If a non-boss enemy dies within 10 ticks (0.33 seconds) after being hit by '''Cube Baby''', it will be frozen regardless of what killed it.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Mom's Bracelet}}: Cube Baby can be picked up and thrown. It will then slide at maximum speed in the direction it's thrown at and leave a trail of damaging white creep until it slows down.
* {{I|BFFS!}}: Increases the size and doubles the damage dealt.

sections.Effects:
* Re-rolls Isaac's [[damage]], [[tears]], [[range]], and [[speed]].
** Each stat is given a multiplier, ranging from 0.5x to 2.0x, which applies after all other adjustments.
sections.Notes:
* [[Luck]], [[Shot Speed]], and {{dlc|nr}} [[Tear Falling Speed]] are unaffected.
* The Tears multiplier can cause Isaac's tear delay to decrease beyond the normal cap of 5.
* The Speed multiplier cannot cause Isaac's speed to decrease or increase past the normal range of 0.1 to 2.0.
** The multiplier overrides the Speed Up effect of {{i|A Pony}} or {{i|White Pony}}, which normally raise Isaac's Speed to 1.5 if it is below that value.
** {{dlc|nr}} The hidden maximum Speed value also gets the same multiplier, which may further cap Isaac's Speed.
* The multipliers are chosen in a way that keeps their total product roughly the same; the item will most often increase two and decrease two of Isaac's stats, although it can increase three and decrease one or increase one and decrease three. Larger increases are balanced by larger decreases.
* In the area where you claim {{i|Knife Piece 2}}, the multipliers granted by d8 will remain, when activated using {{i|Void}} (possible bug). This can be detrimental if there are negative multipliers to fire rate or speed.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Car Battery}}: Re-rolls twice instantly without any benefits.
** {{i|Rock Bottom}}: Considers both sets of multipliers, allowing higher stats to be reached faster.
* {{C|Jacob and Esau|r}}: Only the brother using D8 will get their stats rerolled with the exception of Speed, which is shared between both brothers.

sections.Effect:
* Upon use, duplicates one random [[pickup]] in the current room, including [[Card]]s, [[Rune]]s, {{E|Chest}}s, and [[trinket]]s.
* {{dlc|r}} Duplicated pickups may not be identical to the original; for example, a duplicated card may be a different one than the original.
sections.Notes:
* It is possible to duplicate {{r|Shop}} pickups that have not been purchased yet.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{p|Jera}} can not be duplicated.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{E|Mimic Chest}}s will not be duplicated until their spikes are exposed.
* {{dlc|nr}} Opened chests will be duplicated into an unopened copy.
* {{dlc|nr}} A normal Chest may be duplicated into a Red Chest or a Mimic Chest.
* {{dlc|nr}} A duplicated trinket is mostly useless, as you cannot pick up two of the same trinket even with {{i|Mom's Purse}}, {{i|Belly Button|n}}, or {{i|Smelter}}.
** However, with "consumable" trinkets such as {{t|Store Credit}} or {{t|Bag Lunch}}, it can be extremely powerful.
* {{dlc|nr}} In combination with a [[48 Hour Energy]] pill and {{t|Paper Clip}}, the initial Locked Chests on {{s|Chest}} can be infinitely duplicated and opened.
* {{dlc|nr}} In [[Greed mode]], if a Lil' Battery appears in the {{r|Shop}} and a {{p|2 of Diamonds}} is acquired, infinite money can be gained by duplicating the Two of Diamonds.
* {{dlc|nr}} By dropping a card, rune, or pill in a room with no other pickups, then using D1, this item can function similarly to {{i|Blank Card}} and {{i|Placebo}}.
** {{dlc|r}} By dropping a card, pill, or trinket in a room with no other pickups, then using D1, this item can function similarly to {{i|Deck of Cards}}, {{i|Mom's Bottle of Pills}}, or {{i|Mom's Box}} (But without the luck up or doubled trinket effects).
* {{dlc|r}} A duplicated card has a very rare chance to turn into a {{p|Dice Shard}}, {{P|Cracked Key|n}}, or {{p|Emergency Contact}}; however, these will always duplicate as themselves instead of duplicating as a card.
* {{dlc|r}} A duplicated [[Golden Pill]] will turn into a random Pill chosen from the Pill Pool.
* When duplicating any type of [[chest]], the contents of the original chest will be invisibly rerolled.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Car Battery}}: Generates two pickups instead of just one. 
** {{i|Car Battery}} + {{E|Lil' Battery}}: Allows for infinite generation of Lil' Batteries. {{dlc|r}} While it's still possible to generate infinite batteries with this synergy, it is slow to do so since mostly Micro Batteries will spawn. The occasional Lil' Battery or other battery spawn is needed to build up the battery pile.
*** {{dlc|nr}} An endless supply of Lil' Batteries allows for endless duplication of all pickups, chests, and trinkets on the floor.
*** {{dlc|r}} An endless supply of Lil' Batteries allows for an endless supply of every kind of unlocked pickups, chests, and trinkets, as long as there is at least one of the initial pickup type on the floor.
**** [[Card]]: Allows for an infinite supply of every kind of unlocked card.
**** [[Pill]]: Allows for an infinite supply of every kind of pill in the current run's pill pool.
***** [[Pill]] + {{i|PHD}}: Allows for an infinite supply of beneficial pills.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a white six-sided die wisp on the middle ring. An extra wisp spawns if no pickups are duplicated.}}
* {{c|Tainted Lost}}: Duplicated cards have an increased chance to be {{p|Holy Card|n}}s.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Guppy's Eye}}: Guppy's Eye can be used to see what changed when duplicating a chest. It will not immediately show the new contents, but leaving the room and returning will reveal the changes. This essentially allows rerolling the rewards within them, especially useful in {{s|Chest}} and {{s|Dark Room}}.
** {{dlc|r+}} The contents are immediately updated upon reroll.

sections.Notes:
* When {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}} or {{i|Shoop da Whoop!}} is chosen, Dead Sea Scrolls will not lose its charge until said item is thrown or released.
** This allows Isaac to press Spacebar again if need be to skip over said items in the rotation while keeping full charge, allowing it to be used again for a different effect.
*** This doesn't work if Bethany has Soul Charges and {{i|Book of Virtues}}.
* It may be helpful to use Dead Sea Scrolls upon entering an enemy room, as many of its effects such as {{i|The Gamekid}} and {{i|Tammy's Head}} are helpful in combat.
* As many of Dead Sea Scrolls effects involve explosions, using it near [[Rocks|Tinted Rocks]] or potential {{R|Secret Room}} entrances can potentially be helpful when low on bombs.
** While {{I|Anarchist Cookbook}} and {{I|Kamikaze!|nr}} can hurt the player, effects such as {{I|Book of Revelations}}, {{I|The Nail}}, {{I|Crystal Ball|r}} and {{I|Prayer Card|r}} will pay out with more health than is lost long-term.
* {{dlc|r}} Since {{i|We Need To Go Deeper!}} guarantees a crawlspace if used on special tiles, it may be helpful to use Dead Sea Scrolls on such tiles whenever possible.
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Each wisp spawned has the attributes of the active item that was triggered.}}
sections.Interactions: * {{I|Car Battery}}: Two effects are activated, with only one being named on screen.

sections.Effects:
* Initiates the [[Ascent]] sequence.
* Any trinkets left in {{r|Treasure Room}}s and {{r|Boss Room}}s will turn into {{p|Cracked Key}}s.
sections.Notes:
* Dad's Note cannot be rerolled or destroyed in most ways, such as with {{i|The D6}}, {{i|Void}}, {{I|Abyss}}, or even {{I|Spindown Dice}}.
* Dad's Note cannot be duplicated via {{i|Crooked Penny}}, even if other items in the same room would be duplicated. Other duplication items such as {{i|Diplopia}} work as normal.
* The boss room containing Dad's Note cannot be exited once entered, similar to the {{e|Mom}} boss fight. The only way to exit is through teleportation.
* The only item that can be taken in the boss room of this special version of {{s|Mausoleum}}/{{s|Gehenna}} is Dad's Note. No other items will be spawned.
** {{i|Lemegeton}} pulls from the [[Boss (Item Pool)|Boss Pool]] when used.
* {{R|Treasure Room}} and {{R|Shop}} will still generate in this special floor as in usual floors, giving Isaac more options.
* If Dad's Note is obtained outside of the special boss room via unintended means (such as using {{I|Spindown Dice}} on {{I|Sausage}}), the music will slowly fade out, but the Ascent will not start.
* {{r|Red Room}} doors cannot appear on the borders of the map, preventing access to the {{r|I AM ERROR}} room and {{s|Womb}}/{{s|Utero}}/{{s|Scarred Womb}}.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, summons a sword that hangs directly above Isaac. As long as the sword hangs above Isaac, all [[item]] pedestals are doubled, spawning an additional free item next to them.
** Items spawned via other means, like [[Machines]], {{e|Beggar}}s, and certain [[items]] and [[Cards and Runes|cards]], are also doubled.
** The extra item will be pulled from the current room's item pool, even if the original item is from a different pool (ex. Beggars or items from {{I|Alabaster Box}}).
* After Isaac takes damage (with exceptions, see below) once with the item activated, at any time with only a brief warning, the sword may fall, instantly killing Isaac regardless of his health. The sword has a 1/10000 chance every 4 game ticks (every 0.133 seconds) to fall, so on average, 50% of all Damocles runs will not drop the sword until after at least 15 minutes and 24 seconds have passed.
** Self-damage (such as from a {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}, {{e|Devil Beggar}}, {{r|Curse Room}}, {{r|Sacrifice Room}}, {{e|Spiked Chest}}, Bad Trip pill, or self-damage Active Items) does not count as damage taken for Damocles, and will not give it the chance to fall.
sections.Notes:
* The chance for the sword to fall does not increase beyond the first hit taken.
* Items from {{E|Chest}}s will not be doubled, which greatly limits Damocles' benefit in [[Chapters#Chapter 6 .28Optional.29|Chapter 6]].
** The exception to this is {{E|Mega Chest|text=Mega Chests}}, which will spawn one extra item alongside the 2 original items for a total of 3 items.
* In scenarios that have multiple items to choose from (such as rare double {{r|Treasure Room}} layouts and {{r|Boss Rush}}), an additional set of items for Isaac to choose from spawns. Only one item from each set can be taken.
* In alternate path treasure rooms, one item from the second set is known.
* Having multiple Damocles active at once does not spawn additional items.
* The only way Isaac can survive the falling sword is if he's invincible at the time it falls or, by technicality, with a respawn item. After the sword falls, extra items will no longer spawn.
** Losing a life before the sword falls does not remove the sword or its threat.
* Items with associated costs, like those in {{R|Devil Room}}s or {{R|Shop}}s, will not create additional items. This severely limits this item's benefit when used as {{C|Tainted Keeper}}, since most items that are normally created as pedestals are instead Shop items.
* This can cause items that are in inaccessible spots in certain room layouts to be moved to a more convenient location due to not having space for two pedestals in that spot. It can also cause items to move to less convenient spots.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Damocles' quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Belial synergy|description=The sword also increases Judas' damage by x1.4 then a flat +1 while it's active.}}
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a wisp on the middle ring, looking like a sword. The wisp's tears look like {{I|Spirit Sword}}'s beams, but there are no other effects.}}
* {{i|Blanket}} / {{I|Holy Mantle}} / {{p|Holy Card}} / {{T|Wooden Cross}}: Damage blocked by the shield doesn't count as damage taken. It will not, however, protect Isaac from the falling sword.
* {{i|Book of Shadows}} / {{i|Empty Vessel}} / {{p|Algiz}} / other items that give [[shield]]: Nullifies the instant kill of Damocles if the shield is active when the sword falls.
* {{i|Cone Head}} / {{I|Host Hat}} / {{I|Infamy}} / {{i|Metal Plate}}: Blocked damage does not count as damage and can delay the triggering of Damocles.
* {{I|Crooked Penny}} / {{I|Diplopia}}: An extra item is spawned per each item cloned.
** However, duplicating Damocles itself and activating additional copies has no effect.
* {{I|Dark Arts}}: When in the shadow state, Isaac can survive the instant kill of Damocles, though this requires precise timing and can be impossible if Dark Art's charge is empty as the sword is falling.
* {{t|Filigree Feather}}: [[Angel]]s spawn 2 items when defeated. However, if a [[Key Piece]] spawns, a second pedestal will not appear.
* {{i|Genesis}}: If the player acquires Damocles and uses it before all items have been collected, then each subsequent item spawned after using it will each spawn an extra item. Unlike the Genesis choices, the other extra items will not disappear upon collecting one of them, potentially allowing the player to obtain a much higher amount of items than usual.
** Using Genesis will remove the hanging sword and its effects.
* {{i|Gnawed Leaf}}: If in the form of the statue, Isaac will be immune to the falling sword.
** {{I|Tooth and Nail}}'s statue form can also save Isaac, but the statue transformation time lining up with the sword falling is unlikely.
* {{C|Lazarus}}' revival mechanic allows him to continue the run after dying to Damocles.
** This extends to other extra-life items such as {{I|1up!}} or {{I|Dead Cat}}.
* {{c|The Lost}} / {{c|Tainted Lost}}: Any damage the Lost would take is likely to kill him instantly, meaning that the item's downside is greatly mitigated. Dying and respawning, however, will still trigger the chance of falling.
* {{I|Magic Skin}}: Spawns 2 items on every use instead of 1.
* {{i|My Little Unicorn}} / {{i|Unicorn Stump}} / other items that give [[invulnerability]]: If active, will negate the sword's lethal fall, saving Isaac.
* {{i|Mega Mush}}: When activated, protects from falling Damocles.
* {{i|Mystery Gift}}: When Damocles is activated, a second item will be spawned with adherence to the item pool for the current room. Even if Mystery Gift "fails" and spawns either {{i|The Poop}} or {{i|A Lump of Coal}}, a second item from the room's item pool will be rewarded.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: The sword will appear larger, but will gain no actual benefits.
* {{i|Blood Oath}}: Getting stabbed by Blood Oath does not trigger the chance of falling.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{i|Clicker}}: The sword cannot be removed from Isaac's inventory.
* {{i|D4}} / {{i|D100}} / {{c|Tainted Eden}}: The sword does not get rerolled.
* {{t|Devil's Crown}}: The Devil Room items that appear are not doubled.
* {{I|Flip}}: The extra item will not have a "ghost" item to flip to.
* {{i|Glitched Crown}}: Duplicated item pedestals do not reroll.
* {{i|Holy Mantle}}: Does not protect Isaac from death when the sword falls.
* {{i|Isaac's Heart}}: Taking damage still allows it to fall, and the sword will still kill Isaac if it falls.
* {{C|Jacob and Esau}}: The sword only gains the chance to fall if the brother who used it takes damage.
* {{i|Metronome}}: Can invoke the effect of Damocles, which applies permanently.
* {{t|Panic Button}}:  '''Not recommended.''' Panic Button will activate Damocles right before Isaac takes damage, guaranteeing Damocles will fall later in the run even if Isaac hasn't activated it yet.
* {{I|Spirit Shackles}}: Does not protect Isaac from death when the sword falls.
* {{c|Apollyon}} / {{i|Void}}: Using Void on Damocles will activate the effect and begin hanging the sword above Isaac on the next use of Void. Subsequent uses of Void will do nothing in regards to Damocles.
** If the player has {{i|Damocles}} and {{I|Birthright}} on {{c|Apollyon}} and after using Void, a previously destroyed item appears, Damocles will spawn an additional item.
* {{C|Tainted Eden}}: Taking damage does not reroll an active Damocles.
* {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}: The sword will hang over Tainted Forgotten's body but will still kill the character despite being invincible.
* {{c|Tainted Isaac}}: Damocles does not count toward his passive item count, and cannot be removed.
* {{C|Tainted Lazarus}} / {{i|Esau Jr.}}: The character that used Damocles must be active for double items to spawn.
** In the case of {{r|Boss Room}}, the form of Lazarus that did not use Damocles must fight the boss for it to drop double items.
** If the player has {{I|Birthright}} as Tainted Lazarus and the inactive form has Damocles, the sword can fall on them and kill the player, bypassing the inactive form's immunity to damage.
* {{p|XVII - The Stars?}}: The sword will not be removed from Isaac's inventory.

sections.Effects:
* Grants [[piercing tears|piercing]] and [[spectral tears|spectral]] tears.
* {{dlc|nr}} +0.25 [[range]].
* {{dlc|r}} -1.5 [[range]].
* -0.4 [[shot speed]].	
* {{dlc|nr}} -0.5 [[tear falling speed]].
* {{Dlc|nr}} Tear size multiplier: 1.5x.
* {{Dlc|r}} +0.22 tear size.
sections.Notes:
* Although the description says "Toxic aura tears", the tears do not inflict [[poison]] damage.
* Due to the spectral tears, tears will go through walls and the floor in a {{R|Crawl Space}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Incubus}}: Does not affect shot speed or tear size, but still gives the piercing effect.
** {{dlc|r}}: Shot speed, range, and tear size will be affected.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: Tears will destroy enemy projectiles without being destroyed in the process.
sections.Interactions:
* {{C|Azazel}}:  Range penalty is the only effect.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs are slow to fire and will pass through enemies, making it far more difficult to hit them with explosions.
** {{Dlc|r}} Bombs also deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}} / {{i|Brimstone}}: Overrides Dead Onion, although stat effects apply.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Tear moves very slowly making it hard to kill mobile enemies.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Overrides Dead Onion.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung|nr+}}: Fires a barrage of large tears that disappear at close range. Spectral and piercing effects make it very effective at close range.
* {{i|My Reflection|nr}}: Tears will travel a very short distance before they return to Isaac and eventually disappear.
* {{i|Proptosis}}: While tears do massive damage at short range, it makes it a lot easier to be damaged by explosive enemies or enemies that do contact damage.
* {{i|Rubber Cement}}: Edges of tears retain both piercing and spectral effects; however, the center of the tear will lose them and bounce.
* {{i|Sulfuric Acid}}: Acid Tears no longer impact objects and can no longer open Secret Rooms.
** {{dlc|r}} Acid Tears can break objects.
* {{i|Technology|r}}: Laser size is increased.

sections.Effects:
* Isaac's [[damage]] increases for each successive tear hit on enemies.
** The multiplier increases by 0.25x for each hit, going up to a maximum of 2x after 4 successive hits.
** If a tear misses and hits nothing (wall/floor), there is a chance for the multiplier to be reset back to 1.
*** The chance is 20% for the first miss, 33% for the second miss, and 50% for the third miss and beyond.
** As the multiplier increases, Isaac's tears glow red and increase in size.
sections.Notes:
* The effect is triggered by many entities aside from enemies. Shooting {{Dlc|nr}} {{E|Fire Place}}s, {{g|Poop}}, {{E|Wall Hugger}}s, and {{E|Stone Grimace}}s will count towards the multiplier. This can be used to preemptively increase damage before entering a new room.
** {{Dlc|nr}} Because blue fires do not deteriorate when shot at with tears, maximum damage can always be achieved as long as the fire is not destroyed by an explosion.
** Shooting {{E|Host}}s will increase the damage multiplier even if their skull is lowered down.
* If Dead Eye is removed by re-rolling it with {{i|D4}}, {{i|D100}}, or a 1 or 6 pip {{R|Dice Room}}, the damage multiplier will be removed, but the tears will continue to glow red.
* Tears do not have to be landed on only one enemy to build the multiplier; as long as they do not miss, Isaac gains damage.
* {{dlc|r}} Because there are no walls or floors for tears to collide with in the fight with {{E|The Beast|n}}, the damage boost will not fade away.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}/{{i|Haemolacria}}/{{i|Lachryphagy}}: Main tears and burst tears will contribute to damage multiplier.
** {{i|Lachryphagy}} Firing into the floating tear won't reset the multiplier unless it hits a wall.  The burst tears never reset the multiplier.
* {{i|Dark Arts}}: Hitting enemies/bullets successfully with Dark Arts contributes to Dead Eye's damage multiplier.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Damage bonus increases until it hits the max of 2x. Since the controllable tear never hits the ground or wall, the bonus cannot be lost.
* [[Petrification]]/[[Slow]] items: Enemies will be petrified or slowed, making them easier to hit without missing.
* {{i|Pop!}}: Tears that miss an enemy and do not hit a wall or obstacle will not fall to the ground immediately, allowing many damage-amplified tears to be fired before the damage boost is lost.
* {{i|Proptosis}}: Tears are larger and easier to hit with at a low range. Additionally, if the tear fades out of existence instead of running out of range or hitting a wall/obstacle, it does not count as a miss.
* {{i|Spirit Sword}}: Dead Eye will increase the damage every slash until it hits the max of 2x. The bonus can be lost if a sword projectile doesn't hit anything.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: Isaac's tears no longer hit walls and stay in the air for longer, allowing many damage-amplified tears to be fired before the damage boost is lost.
* {{i|Akeldama}}: The tears in the trail will contribute to the damage boost, making it possible to stack damage while having items that do not interact with Dead Eye on their own (such as {{i|Brimstone}}).
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone}} / {{i|Dr. Fetus}} / {{i|Epic Fetus}} / {{i|Mom's Knife}} / {{i|Technology}} / {{i|Tech X}}: Will not increase or decrease Dead Eye's bonus, resulting in it remaining as it was prior to their pickup.
* {{i|20/20}}/{{i|The Inner Eye}}/{{i|Mutant Spider}}/{{I|Cursed Eye}}: If all tears hit, they all contribute to the damage multiplier. However, the spread shot granted by The Inner Eye and Mutant Spider may make it hard to retain the damage multiplier.
* {{C|Azazel}}: Gains no benefit by picking up Dead Eye unless his tear effect has been replaced.
* {{i|Cricket's Body}}/{{i|The Parasite}}: Split tears that do not hit enemies are considered misses, nearly guaranteeing the chance of losing the multiplier.
* {{i|Flat Stone}}: Each skip counts as missing.
* {{dlc|a+}} {{C|The Forgotten}}: The Forgotten's swing increases the multiplier when successfully hitting enemies, making it much easier to maintain the damage buff. Resets the multiplier upon swinging and missing. The multiplier changes normally when firing tears as {{C|The Soul}}, and the two forms share the same multiplier.
** {{C|The Forgotten}} + {{I|Soy Milk}}: Damage multiplier will not reset as long as the fire key is held, and will quickly build up to the maximum value of x2. The multiplier will only reset if, upon releasing the fire button, the thrown bone does not hit any enemy.
*{{i|Rock Bottom}} The damage multiplier stays, even if you reset the item bonus.
* {{i|Host Hat}}: Tears fired by the Host are affected by Dead Eye.
* {{i|Immaculate Heart}}: The tears from Immaculate Heart can add to the damage multiplier and cannot lower it by missing. This can be particularly useful with items that normally prevent the damage multiplier from increasing, such as {{i|Brimstone}}.
* {{i|Incubus|nr}}: Incubus's tears do not affect the multiplier, but Incubus can gain damage from Isaac's normal tears increasing the multiplier. The familiar's tears do not reset the multiplier if they miss, either.
** {{dlc|nr}} {{C|Lilith}}'s Incubus doesn't work with Dead Eye.
** '''Incubus''' + {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Tears fired by Incubus are now affected by Dead Eye.
* {{i|Isaac's Tears}}: If the tears fired by Isaac's tears miss, they cause the multiplier to reset.
* {{i|Jacob's Ladder}}: Electricity sparks do not contribute to damage multiplier.
* {{i|Marked}}: Damage buff often lost quickly because of the constantly firing tears.
* [[Piercing tears]]: Damage buff is halved, .125x, reaching the 2x multiplier with 8 successive hits.
* {{i|Rubber Cement|nr}}: Tears that hit enemies may bounce off and still count as misses.
* {{i|Sad Bombs}}: Tears spawned by sad bombs that miss will reset the multiplier.
* {{i|Saturnus}}: Tears spawned when entering the room and enemy tears collected by the ring can add to the damage multiplier and cannot lower it by missing. This can be particularly useful with items that normally prevent the damage multiplier from increasing, such as {{i|Brimstone}}.
* {{i|Technology 2}}: No effect from the laser itself, but the tears fired from the second eye are affected by Dead Eye.
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: Electricity connecting tears will not increase the damage multiplier.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Cannot increase Dead Eye's bonus, but can lose it.

sections.Effect:
* {{dlc|nr}} Allows Isaac to carry two [[Cards and Runes|cards]] or [[pills]] (or a combination of both) at the same time.
* {{dlc|r}} Increases the [[coin]] cap to 999.
* {{dlc|r}} If a room would otherwise yield no reward, 1-3 random coins will spawn.
** All coins spawned will be of the same type.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} This item has the same effects as {{i|Little Baggy}} and {{i|Starter Deck}}, but without removing pills/cards from the game.
* {{dlc|a+nr}} This item has the same effect as {{i|Polydactyly|n}}.
* {{dlc|r}} Has no effect on spawning coins in [[Greed mode]], including the trapdoor/exit room.
* {{dlc|r}} Losing this item while holding more than 99 coins will reduce coin count to 99. Picking it back up again (if playing as{{C|Tainted Isaac}}, for example) will not restore lost coins.
** {{dlc|nr+}} This includes going for {{I|Knife Piece 2|n}} in {{s|Mines|n}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|A Dollar|r}}: Allows Isaac to gain the full 100 coins when picking this up.
* {{i|Contract From Below|r}} / {{i|Guppy's Tail}}: If the room clear reward is removed, spawns 1-3 random coins. Allows Deep Pockets to remain useful at high luck.
* {{i|Greed's Gullet|r}}: After exceeding 100 coins, Isaac gains an extra [[Health#Red Heart Containers|Heart Container]] for every 100 coins instead of every 25.
** {{C|Keeper}}/{{C|Tainted Keeper}}: The limit of 12 heart containers can be bypassed, allowing for up to 15 [[Health#Coin Hearts|coin hearts]] at 999 coins. Additional coin hearts past 12 are not displayed.
* {{i|Money Power|r}}: Increases maximum [[damage]] bonus. The damage caps at +39.96 damage with 999 coins.
* {{i|Midas' Touch|r}}: Increases maximum contact damage. The damage caps at 203.3 damage with 999 coins.
* {{i|Options?}}: A [[pickup]], card, pill, [[trinket]], or {{E|Chest}} will accompany each coin.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Diplopia|nr}}: No effect, only two pills or cards can be held.
** {{dlc|r}} No effect. Only 999 coins can be held.
* {{t|Perfection}}: Possibly detrimental. Since room clear rewards become very common at high luck, the 1-3 coin drop will rarely occur.

sections.Effect: * Upon use, opens all doors in the current [[room]] in almost all circumstances.
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Creates wisps in the middle ring. If the wisps touch {{E|Locked Chest}}s, Special Room doors, or uncleared room doors, they will unlock and open them, destroying themselves in the process. These wisps can open ''any'' locked door they touch, including the door to the {{e|Mega Satan}} arena, {{a|A Strange Door}}, and the flesh door to {{s|Corpse}}. {{e|Bomb Chest}}s and {{e|Mega Chest}}s are unaffected. They will also donate to {{e|Key Master}}s on touch, destroying themselves in the process. Opening a chest in a {{r|Challenge Room}} with a wisp will ''not'' start the challenge.}}
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.

sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} D100 is a [[special item]].
* {{Dlc|nr}} See the {{i|D4}}, {{i|The D6}}, and the {{i|D20}} to learn more about the respective individual effects.
* {{Dlc|r}} See the {{i|D1|dlc=n}}, {{i|D4}}, {{i|The D6}}, {{i|D7|dlc=n}}, {{i|D8|dlc=n}}, {{i|D10}}, {{i|D12|dlc=n}}, and the {{i|D20}} to learn more about the respective individual effects.
* If Missing No. is given to the player, it will activate and remove the D100, preventing further rerolls.
** Note that {{i|Missing No.}} can be rerolled into, but can't be rerolled out of.
* {{dlc+|r+}} D100's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Rerolls all of Isaac's wisps and gives him one random wisp. Book of Virtues will not be rerolled in the process.}}

sections.Effects:
* Grants 2 {{E|Soul Heart}}s.
* Replaces normal tears with blue diamond tears while all of Isaac's [[Red Heart container]]s and {{E|Bone Heart}}s (if any) are full.
** This includes whenever Isaac has zero Red Heart containers.
** Containers can be filled with {{E|Rotten Heart}}s and still activate the effect.
** The coin health containers of {{C|Keeper}} and {{C|Tainted Keeper}} count as red heart containers for the purposes of this item.
* While the effect is active, grants the following stats:
** 2x [[damage]].
** {{dlc|nr}} +5.25 [[range]].
** {{dlc|nr}}+0.5 [[tear falling speed]].
** -0.30 [[shot speed]].
* The crown will glow blue while active; if inactive, it will appear grey.
* The effect will deactivate for the rest of the current room when damage is taken, regardless of Isaac's health.
** Fighting waves in [[Greed mode]] won't reactivate the crown.
sections.Notes:
* Because the effect occurs if Isaac has no Red Heart containers at all, this is an extremely beneficial item for {{C|???}}, {{C|Tainted ???}}, {{C|The Lost}}, {{C|Tainted Lost}}, {{C|Black Judas|r}}, {{C|Tainted Judas}}, {{C|Tainted Bethany}} and {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}.
* Due to the fact that they will be at full health a larger portion of the time than most characters, this item is also very powerful for {{C|Keeper}} and {{C|Tainted Keeper}}.
* If the damage is lost with {{C|Tainted Isaac}}, he can pick up another item in the same room and then swap it back to refresh the effect.  Holding onto pedestal generation like {{I|Mystery Gift}} will allow him to place an item inside a difficult boss room and regain the bonus damage after being hit.
* Using {{P|XI - Strength}} when already at a maximum 12 hearts, but having taken damage (hence visually having full maximum health) will not reactivate the item.
* Additional copies of the item will grant 2 {{E|Soul Heart}}s upon pickup, but no change in stats.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Holy Mantle}}: This will block damage and keep Crown Of Light active.
* {{i|Rock Bottom}}: While the diamond tear effect will disappear when Isaac is hit, the damage up will not be reverted.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns an [[orbital familiar]] around Isaac which blocks shots and deals {{dlcalt|105|r=52.5}} contact damage per second.
* Each subsequent Cube of Meat obtained is combined with the first one (increasing its 'level'), changing its characteristics:
** Level 2: Gives the orbital the ability to shoot tears that deal 3.5 damage once every {{dlcalt|second|r=0.73 seconds}}.
** Level 3: Changes it from an orbital to a Meat Boy that chases nearby enemies dealing {{dlcalt|8.75|r=12.5}} contact damage per second.
** Level 4: Increases the size of the Meat Boy and increases its damage to {{dlcalt|13.75|r=25}} contact damage per second.
** The fifth Cube of Meat will create a new Level 1 cube, and start the cycle again.
sections.Synergies:
* [[Invulnerability]] and [[shield]]s are very useful with orbitals like {{i|Cube of Meat}}.
** This is even more useful with invulnerability items which doesn't allow to do contact damages, like {{i|Unicorn Stump}}.
* {{i|Book of Revelations}}: Ensures that [[Harbinger]]s that haven't already been defeated will replace their respective floor's boss, making it drastically easier to collect multiple Cubes of Meat.
* {{i|Box of Friends}} / {{i|Monster Manual}}: Additional copies of Cube of Meat combine with the first, increasing its level as normal.
* {{i|Potato Peeler}}: Consumes 1 [[Red Heart container]] in return for creating 1 Cube of Meat and increasing damage a little.
sections.Interactions:
* {{t|Duct Tape}}: Familiar will stay in place relative to Isaac at levels 1 and 2. No effect at levels 3 and 4.
* [[Pretty Fly]]: Cube of Meat will replace one if Isaac already has 3 Pretty Flies. If the Cube of Meat reaches level 3 or 4, the Pretty Fly will come back until another Cube of Meat orbital is obtained.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, rotates every enemy and pickup 90 degrees and moves its sprite up and left for the current room.
** Enemy hitboxes remain the same.
* Increases one of Isaac's [[Attributes|stats]] and decreases another. Possible stat changes include:
** ± 1 flat [[damage]]
** ±0.5 {{dlcalt|[[tears]]|r=[[fire rate]]}}
** ±0.2 [[speed]]
*** {{dlc|nr}} Also affects maximum speed, if some other item has reduced it below 2.0 (but still cannot increase it above the hard cap of 2.0)
** ±0.2 [[shot speed]]
** ±1 [[luck]]
** {{dlcalt|±0.5|r=±2.5}} [[range]]
* Adds random tear effects for the current room.
* Distorts the music for the current room.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Rerolls any item in the room to a glitched {{i|TMTRAINER}} item.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a special wisp on the middle ring that is otherwise undistinguishable from a normal wisp. These wisps' tears have a 5% chance of transforming any non-boss enemy into random wisps.}}
* {{i|Rock Bottom}}: The stats are locked to the highest number achieved, though the lowered stat will still be more difficult to increase.
sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|r}} If the tears stat reaches a negative number, there will be a wrap-around into the maximum fire rate of 120; if the tears stat is boosted back into a positive number, fire rate will again become low.
** If Rock Bottom is obtained while the tears stat is negative, fire rate will stay at 120 even if boosts are obtained.
* The minimum values for each stat are as follows:
** Damage: 0.5
** Speed: 0.1
** Shot Speed: 0.6
** Range: 1.0
* Further changes to Isaac's stats are still calculated normally behind the scenes, but their ''effective'' values cannot go below the minimum. For example, 0.5 Shot Speed will ''behave'' as though it were 0.6, but a 0.2 Shot Speed increase would apply to the true stat value of 0.5, meaning the new stat value would be 0.7.
* {{dlc+|r}} Using Dataminer during the fight against {{E|The Beast}} is '''not recommended''', as it will distort the stalagmites and stalactites, causing them to be incredibly difficult to dodge.{{dlc-}}

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|nr}} +1.5 [[range]].
* {{dlc|r}} +2.5 [[range]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +1 [[tear falling speed]]
* Drops a {{E|Lucky Penny}}.
sections.Notes: * {{dlc|r}} Dad's Lost Coin's quality is considered 2 for the purposes of {{i|Bag of Crafting}}.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, transports Isaac to an abandoned and expanded version of {{S|Home}}, which has one copy of almost '''every''' item the player has unlocked on that save file on pedestals. After taking an item from a pedestal, Isaac returns to the room he used Death Certificate in.
** There are also several [[pickups]] and {{E|Chest||chests}} in the area. Picking them up/opening them will not cause Isaac to leave the area.
*** If a chest in the area contains an item, picking it up will ''not'' cause Isaac to leave the area.
*** Items spawned through the use of pre-obtained items brought into the area, such as {{i|Eden's Soul}} or {{i|Mystery Gift}}, will also not cause Isaac to leave the area.
sections.Notes:
* Items that have not been unlocked will not show up in this unique location.
* If Death Certificate is used on a floor while {{curse|blind}} is active, the area will not be affected by the curse, meaning all items will be revealed. {{I|Chaos}} doesn't affect the area either.
* Items that are typically only granted under special circumstances like {{i|Dogma}} and {{i|Mom's Shovel}} are present.
* The layout of the area is randomly generated, and items will show up in order of lowest ID number to highest (starting at items in the original ''Flash'' version and working up to the ''Repentance'' items).
** A new Death Certificate area is randomly generated on the next floor.
** If more items are added to the game through [[modding]], the area will expand to include them, ordered after the ''Repentance'' items.
* The only items that do not show up in the Death Certificate area are {{i|Dad's Note}}, hidden items ({{i|Recall}}, {{i|Hold}}, passive {{i|Damocles}}, passive {{i|The Book of Belial}}), Death Certificate itself, and [[G FUEL!]].
** During a [[Challenge]], [[Daily Challenge]], or playing [[Greed Mode]] their [[Item_Tags|respective banned items]] will not appear.
* Using Death Certificate while in the area that generates from using it consumes the item without doing anything.
* Using this item multiple times in the same floor will always teleport to the same areas, without respawning the items that were taken or destroyed.
** If an item is taken, it will only destroy the other ones in the current room or any other room Isaac travels to after taking an item, meaning other items present in the remaining rooms will still be available.
** The player can be softlocked by using Death Certificate while having already taken/destroyed all items that were in the area.
* Using this item during the fight against {{E|The Beast}} resets the fight after Isaac leaves the special area.
* Using this item while in the {{i|Genesis}} room will teleport Isaac back into the {{i|Genesis}} room after taking an item.
** Doing this will turn the current 3 choice pedestals into permanent ones and spawn the next set right on top of them.
* This item can be crafted from {{i|Bag of Crafting}} with eight {{e|Bone Heart}}s.
sections.Synergies:
* {{p|? Card}}: Mimics the effect of Death Certificate without consuming it.
* {{i|Diplopia}}: Has no use inside of the Home area, as Isaac can only take 1 item. However, it can be used to duplicate the Death Certificate item, allowing Isaac to enter the area twice.
* {{c|Jacob and Esau}}: Both characters can take an item from any given room if they're lined up correctly and take them at the same time. This can be very powerful in the case of Brimstone and Mom's Knife, as they are both close together.

* {{i|Red Key}}: Using the Red Key in this area has a chance of spawning rooms with many items from the [[Treasure Room (Item Pool)|Treasure Room pool]] in them, all of which can be taken without being returned back to the floor. It can also spawn special rooms from {{s|Home}}. If Mom's bedroom is spawned and Isaac sleeps in the bed, it will behave like a normal bed, but can be slept in while at full health.
* {{i|Schoolbag}}: Allows Isaac to hold another Active item in the area along with Death Certificate.
* {{c|Tainted Cain}}: Unlike his modified pedestal behavior in the rest of the run, Tainted Cain can pick up an item like normal in this area, effectively allowing him to craft any specific item for the cost of 8 bone hearts (the guaranteed recipe for Death Certificate in the Bag of Crafting).
* {{p|Wild Card}}: Will use Death Certificate if it was the item/card Isaac most recently used.
* {{i|Metronome}}: Can invoke the effect of Death Certificate as normal, even if it is not unlocked.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Abyss}} / {{P|Black Rune}} / {{i|Void}}: Only allows the consumption of one item per room and the consumed item is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.
* {{i|Binge Eater}}/{{i|Glitched Crown}}: No effect; items will not cycle through multiple items.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{i|Moving Box}}: Takes one random item which is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.
* {{i|Book of Virtues}}: Spawns a single, regular wisp with no special properties.
* {{i|Damocles}}: No effect; Damocles doesn't duplicate the item pedestals in any room.
* {{t|NO!}}: causes Death Certificate to no longer spawn. inside Death Certificate floor Ignores changes to item availability.
* {{i|Sacred Orb}} / {{C|Tainted Lost}} / [[Birthright (The Lost)|The Lost's Birthright]]: Ignores changes to item availability caused by characters/items.
* {{p|IX - The Hermit?}}: When used with items present no coins are spawned and the floor exit sequence is triggered as if Isaac had taken an item.

sections.Effects: * Upon use, re-rolls all [[pickup]]s, [[chest]]s, and [[trinket]]s in the current [[room]].
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|r}} Chests are more likely to be re-rolled into other chests.
* {{dlc|nr}} The empty chest object that is left behind after opening any kind of chest can be re-rolled into another pickup. As empty chests disappear after leaving a room, it's better to wait until D20 is fully charged before opening chests.
* {{dlc|nr}} D20 cannot re-roll pickups into {{E|Lil' Battery||Lil' Batteries}}, but can re-roll pickups into {{e|Grab Bag}}s which can contain Lil' Batteries.
* {{dlc|r}} D20 can re-roll pickups into {{E|Lil' Battery||Lil' Batteries}} and other battery pickups, and can re-roll pickups into {{e|Grab Bag}}s which can contain Lil' Batteries.
* D20 can re-roll pickups into chests or trinkets and vice versa.
** On {{s|Chest}} and {{s|Dark Room}}, the re-rolled chests will always contain items unless they are a {{e|Red Chest}} or a {{E|Wooden Chest}}.
** Re-rolls create trinkets far less often than pickups and chests.
* It can re-roll pickups sold in the {{r|Shop}}.
** {{dlc|r}} When used to reroll pickups in any shops, pickups may be rerolled into items instead.

sections.Effects:
* While firing, creates an aura around Isaac that [[Status Effects#Poison|poisons]] any nearby enemies for 2 ticks.
** The poison may stack up to 6 ticks at a time.
** The aura range is approximately two tiles.

sections.Effects:
* Daddy Long Legs' shadow follows Isaac and stomps on enemies for 20 damage per tick, with each stomp capable of hitting a single enemy twice for a total of 40 damage. The delay between stomps is approximately 4 seconds.
* In a room with multiple enemies, Daddy Long Legs will prioritize on monsters with the most health first.
** If all monsters are of the same type, the familiar will attack the closest enemy.
* {{dlc+|r}}{{transformation contribution|Spider Baby}}{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:

* {{t|The Twins}}: Has a chance to spawn an additional foot when entering a new room.
sections.Interactions:
* {{t|Duct Tape}}: No effect.
* {{t|Forgotten Lullaby}}: No effect.
* {{i|Sacrificial Altar}}: Daddy Longlegs cannot be sacrificed.

sections.Effects:
* Throws Isaac's head while allowing to shoot from the spot it lands, blocking enemy shots as well as dealing contact damage to nearby enemies. Meanwhile, Isaac's body can no longer shoot tears.
** The head does 24 damage on impact and 4 damage per tick (12 damage per second) on contact when it's on the ground.
** The head can return by picking it up with the body, or by using the item again without requiring charges. Both the throwing and retaking of the head can deal damage to enemies passing through.
sections.Notes:

sections.Synergies:

sections.Interactions:

* {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}: Throws the head of Tainted Forgotten, but the bone attack still remains on his body. The head can only be recalled by reactivating the item or having the body touch the head.

* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The knife still follows and shoots from the body, the head doesn't shoot tears.

sections.Effects:
* Taking damage summons a bird [[familiar]] that chases enemies for the remainder of the current [[Rooms|room]], dealing 2 damage per tick (~4.3 damage per second).

sections.Effects:
* When at exactly 1 {{E|Red Heart}}, some of Isaac's stats are increased.
** {{Dlc|nr}} +0.75 [[tears]].
** {{Dlc|r}} +2.0 [[fire rate]]. The bonus can break the soft tears cap.

** {{Dlc|nr}} +1 [[tear falling speed]].

* This item only affects {{C|The Forgotten}} when he has one full Bone Heart.

sections.Effects:
* Grants [[piercing]] tears that travel through enemies (but not obstacles) instead of breaking on impact with them.
** {{dlc|nr}} Also pierces through {{g|Poop}} and {{e|Fire Place}}s.

sections.Effects:
* When Isaac's normal tears disappear (either from hitting the ground or hitting something else), they spawn 4 smaller tears.
** Each smaller tear deals half of Isaac's normal [[damage]].
** Split tears are scaled down by 0.6x from the main ones, ignoring damage-based size reduction.
* {{Dlc|nr}} Tear size multiplier: 1.2x.
* {{Dlc|r}} +0.1 tear size.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{tear delay down|1}}
* {{dlc|r}} +0.5 [[fire rate]].
* {{dlc|nr}} -10 [[range]].
* {{dlc|r}} 0.8x [[range]] multiplier.
sections.Notes:
* Split tears will inherit the main tear's [[status effect]], if any.
* If Isaac has less than {{dlc|nr}}10 range/{{dlc|r}}10 [[tear height]], the split tears appear but cannot cause damage before hitting the floor.
** {{dlc|nr}} {{c|Cain}}, {{c|Lazarus}}, and {{c|Samson}} have lower starting range and are particularly susceptible.
** [[Tear falling speed]] ups can't mitigate this downside.

sections.Effect:
* Upon use, has a 50% chance to double all [[item]]s, [[pickup]]s, [[trinket]]s, and {{e|Chest||chests}} in the current room.
** If the effect fails, the items, pickups, and chests disappear, and a {{e|Penny}} is spawned.
sections.Notes:
* If used in a {{R|Shop}} or {{R|Devil Room}}, the duplicated items and pickups can be taken for free.
* If the effect fails in a shop that contains a {{e|Shop Restock Machine}}, then the Restock Machine can be used to refresh the Shop, bringing back new items and pickups.
* {{dlc|nr}} If used in the {{R|Boss Rush}} room, it can duplicate the items, and all of them can be taken without affecting the originals. Successfully duplicating the items will trigger Boss Rush, and failing to duplicate them will not.
* {{dlc|nr}} If used on {{i|The Polaroid}} and {{i|The Negative}} after defeating {{e|Mom}}, it can duplicate them, and they can both be taken without affecting the originals.
* The 50% chance is predetermined after each use of Crooked Penny. By force quitting or using {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} after each failure, this can be exploited to generate large numbers of copies of useful items — if the penny is going to fail, then use it in a different room, recharge it, and try again.
** {{Dlc|r}} The outcome of Crooked Penny is determined on a per-room basis, meaning that it will succeed in certain rooms and fail in others respecting the 50/50 chance. Using Crooked Penny will still advance an RNG step, however, and re-roll the outcome of the other rooms.
* If used in {{R|Boss Rush}} and the items disappear, the boss rush cannot be started.
* If Crooked Penny is used right after taking an item from a choice pedestal (such as those created by {{i|More Options}}), it is possible to double the other item(s) as they disappear. The copies of items will not disappear and will act normally.
* Unlike {{i|Diplopia}}, Crooked Penny can be used to duplicate trinkets.
sections.Synergies:
''See [[Diplopia#Synergies]] for info about stacking duplicate items.''
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a coin wisp on the middle ring. The wisps have a 50/50 chance to duplicate all their copies or destroy all their copies when one takes damage. Does not affect wisps other than ones made by this item. Using Crooked Penny always spawns one wisp, with no chance to affect the others.}}
* {{dlc|nr}} {{i|Void}}: Void's item-absorbing effect activates before Crooked Penny's effect, but Crooked Penny nonetheless has a chance of doubling the absorbed items, leaving behind copies of them. Missing with Crooked Penny still results in the item being absorbed, but one penny also appears.
** {{Dlc|r}} Void does not absorb the item if Crooked Penny fails, but one penny still appears. Void absorbs only the original item if Crooked Penny succeeds, leaving behind a copy.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|nr}} {{i|Car Battery}}: Activates the item twice, quadrupling all items/drops in the room at a 25% chance. However, if the first activation fails, and the second activation succeeds, a copy of the item will be created as the original disappears, and the new copy will have no cost if it were in a {{R|Shop}} or {{R|Devil Room}}. This has a 25% chance as well, leaving the overall failure chance at 50% (a success followed by a fail will have the same effect as two fails).
** {{Dlc|r}} Activates the item twice, quadrupling all items/drops in the room at a 25% chance but having a combined 75% chance to fail. A failure followed by a success generates 2 pennies.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] who follows Isaac around and automatically fires normal tears at enemies in its range 3 times per second that each do 3.5 damage.
* {{transformation contribution|Conjoined|dlc=r}}

sections.Synergies:
