* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs travel through enemies. When combined with {{I|Ipecac}}, bombs do not explode upon hitting enemies.
** {{Dlc|r}} Bombs also deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Stat effects apply. Fired tears will retain piercing effect; however, burst tears will not. All other effects do not apply.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Tears explode at their center, not where they touch the enemy, which means the very large size from Death's Touch may be detrimental. Piercing effect does not apply.
* {{I|Trisagion}}: Overrides Death's Touch. Only stat changes apply.
* {{I|Spirit Sword}} Overrides the scythe visual including the ranged attack.
* {{I|Tech X}}: Overrides Death's Touch. Only stat changes apply.

sections.Effect:
* Gives Isaac a random [[card]].
* If all of Isaac's card slots are full, the card given by the Deck of Cards is placed in the first slot, dropping the card that was in it on the ground.
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns card-like wisps on the inner ring which spawn a [[card]] when destroyed.}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Little Baggy}}: Gives [[pills]] instead. Deck of Cards have then the same effect as {{i|Mom's Bottle of Pills}}.
** {{dlc|nr}} Picking up {{i|Starter Deck}} will nullify this effect but pills are only transformed into cards when they are dropped on the ground.
** {{dlc|r}} Picking up {{i|Starter Deck}} will nullify this effect.

sections.Effects:
* Upon entering a room, a skull appears over an enemy's head.
** The marked enemy will have a bigger shadow.
** Killing the marked enemy will cause the skull to move to a different enemy.
** If all enemies in the room are cleared in the order they are marked, Isaac gains one of the following rewards at random:
*** A {{e|Soul Heart}}, a [[pill]], a {{e|Key}}, a {{e|Bomb}}, or a {{e|Nickel}}.
*** +0.2 [[speed]], +0.5 [[range]], {{dlc|nr}} +0.5 [[tears]], {{dlc|r}} +0.5 [[fire rate]], +0.2 [[shot speed]], +1 flat [[damage]], or +1 [[luck]].
** If a non-marked enemy is killed, the skull will disappear and no bonuses will be granted for that room.
sections.Notes:
* Losing this item will not remove stat rewards.
* As long as the room is not cleared, Isaac can re-attempt a Death's List by leaving and re-entering.
* The marked enemies are chosen in the same order in a given room, starting from the top-left corner with enemies that are vulnerable at their spawn time (from top to bottom, then from left to right). If new enemies are spawned via Portals or on death, they are added to the end of the marked queue.
* The marked {{e|Army Fly}} will always be the last one in the line of Army Flies.
* {{e|Bishop}}s can shield the marked enemy unless frozen or petrified beforehand.
* Killing all piles of a {{e|Cursed Globin}}s counts as one kill.
* A room with no enemies that instead requires {{g|Pressure Plate}}s to be pressed will also give a reward when cleared.
* If a reward stat is chosen that is already at maximum, the sound effect and Isaac's thumbs up animation will play, but there is no other effect.
* Bosses may also be marked.
* If a {{e|Portal}} is marked and despawns, no other enemy will be marked and the bonus is lost.
* Enemies that are not spawned when the room is entered (such as [[Angel]]s from bombed Angel Statues and enemies in {{r|Challenge Room}}s, [[Greed Mode]], and {{r|Boss Rush}}) will not be marked.
* In the {{e|Mom}} boss fight, each of Mom's body parts (eyes, foot, and hands) is considered as a different enemy, and Isaac has to kill the foot to get the bonus.
* If the doors open automatically due to spending a long enough time in the room, any existing mark will disappear.
* [[Familiar]]s, especially ones that passively or actively damage enemies of their own accord, may make killing enemies in order difficult, if not impossible.
* Ace cards will kill the enemies in the correct order when possible.
* If a {{e|Mr. Maw}} is marked, killing either part of its body will not forfeit Death's List, as the remaining enemy of said Mr. Maw will still be marked.
* This item has little to no effect in Greed Mode.
* Waiting for the [[User:Blcd/RandomTidbits#Room Anti-softlock|Room Anti-softlock]] to trigger will always grant a reward from Death's List.
* [[Friendly]] enemies cannot be marked, and their deaths do not cause the mark to disappear.
sections.Synergies:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Enemies that die by being turned into [[pickup]]s don't disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into pickups still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.
* {{t|Door Stop}}: If Isaac has failed Death's List but hasn't cleared the room, leaving and re-entering will reset the list.
* {{i|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Enemies that die by being turned into poop do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into poop still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.
* {{i|Eraser}}: Erasing enemies makes it easier to complete the list as erased enemies do not disrupt the Death's List chain and rooms cleared by Eraser's effect will also reward the bonus.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}} [[Frozen|Freezing attacks]]: Enemies that die by freezing do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by freezing its enemies still grants Isaac the Death's List reward, though the shards caused by them breaking do.
** {{dlc|r+}} Frozen enemies do disrupt Death's List's chain.
* {{i|Toxic Shock}}: Not recommended. If multiple enemies are killed by Toxic Shock at the same time, the mark will disappear and no reward will be given, even if the enemy next in line to be marked was killed at the same time as the marked one.

sections.Effects: * If Isaac has one red heart or less at the beginning of a floor, an empty heart container is added.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Adrenaline}}: Activates the damage up effect of Adrenaline if conditions are met to grant an empty heart container at the beginning of each floor.
* {{T|Crow Heart}}: If no {{e|Devil Beggar}}s  or {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s can be found, the Crow Heart trinket is a great way to guarantee red hearts are lost so long as you still have non-red health available.
* {{I|Dark Prince's Crown}}: The heart containers are empty when granted, which allows the crown's buff to stay active when advancing floors.
* {{I|Guppy's Paw}}: The heart containers granted by Empty Heart can be used by Guppy's Paw while staying at or below 1 red heart, granting massively increased survivability.
* {{C|Lazarus}}: The heart containers granted by Empty Heart allows Lazarus to effectively negate the downside that removes a single heart container on death, allowing him to purposefully use his mechanic to get a +0.5 damage up per floor. (As long as he still proceeds at one red heart or less)
* {{I|Potato Peeler}}: The heart containers granted by Empty Heart can be used by Potato Peeler while staying at or below 1 red heart, granting increased damage and a {{I|Cube of Meat}} per floor.

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|nr}} [[Tear delay]] gradually decreases by intervals as the player shoots in one direction. Accuracy also decreases as the fire rate increases.
** At max "charge", it will reduce tear delay by half, rounding down.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Fire rate]] gradually increases by intervals as the player shoots in one direction. Accuracy also decreases as the fire rate increases.
** {{dlc|r+}} Fire rate increases smoothly instead of intervals.
** At max "charge", it will increase fire rate by double.
* The time required to reach max charge is {{dlc|nr+}} 9 / {{dlc|r+}} 6 seconds.
* Rate of fire returns to its original value if Isaac stops firing, changes firing directions, uses an active item, or is hit.
** {{dlc|a+}} Being hit, changing rooms, and using items no longer reset the Epiphora bonus.
** {{dlc|rnr+}} Entering an unexplored boss room will reset the Epiphora bonus.
*** During the delay when transitioning between rooms, picking up an item, or using an active item, it's possible to change the firing direction without resetting the bonus.
sections.Notes: * Epiphora technically works with items that require a charge (such as {{i|Monstro's Lung}}), but requires releasing the key or button, causing players to lose the effect.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Analog Stick}}: Epiphora's bonus will not reset when switching fire diagonally, as long as Isaac's head doesn't turn.
* {{i|Continuum}}: Reduces the need to change firing direction, allowing Isaac to maintain the increased rate of fire.
* {{i|Cursed Eye|r}}: Epiphora's tear rate multiplier affects the number of tears in a burst for a total of ten shots with a full Epiphora charge.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}} / {{i|Ipecac}}: Firing bombs continually will decrease tear delay, although doing so is '''not recommended''' since it increases the risk of self-damage.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}: When tapping the attack button in a single direction repeatedly, the Ephiphora effect will cause the bone swings to speed up.
* {{i|How to Jump}}: Changing firing direction while jumping does not reset the bonus, similar to when changing rooms.
* {{i|Incubus}}: Incubus's fire rate will match Isaac's.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Fire rate increases while moving the tear in one direction; it has a negligible effect during normal gameplay.
* {{i|Marked}}: Both items work as normal, with tear rate gradually increasing until Isaac turns his head, which can happen via him or the crosshair moving too out of parallel.
* {{i|Rubber Cement}}: Reduces the need to change firing direction allowing Isaac to maintain the increased rate of fire.
* {{i|Rock Bottom}}: Isaac will never lose the benefits of Epiphora, even after he stops firing. This effectively makes Epiphora a substantial tears up. Fully charging Ephiphora is still needed to gain a higher tears stat if an item that would increase the tears stat is picked up.
* {{i|Tractor Beam}}: Fire rate still increases when shooting in one direction, but will stay on the line (i.e. no loss in accuracy).
* {{i|Loki's Horns}} / {{i|Mom's Eye}}: Allows for firing in multiple directions at once, decreasing need to change firing direction.
sections.Interactions:
* Charging items such as {{i|Brimstone}}, {{i|Chocolate Milk}}, {{i|Cursed Eye|nr}}, {{i|Mom's Knife}}, {{i|Monstro's Lung}}, and {{i|Tech X}}: Effect only activates when holding charge in a specific direction, and deactivates when the charge is released, effectively making Epiphora useless unless Isaac has exceedingly low fire rate.
** {{dlc|r}} {{i|Soy Milk}} / {{i|Almond Milk}} + {{i|Chocolate Milk}} / {{i|Cursed Eye}} / {{i|Monstro's Lung}} / {{i|Tech X}}: Due to constant firing, Epiphora's fire rate bonus can now be used.
** {{dlc|r}} {{i|Soy Milk}} / {{i|Almond Milk}} + {{i|Brimstone}}: The Brimstone laser only gains the increased damage from higher tear rates when the laser starts firing, making Epiphora's bonus useless.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Overrides Epiphora.
* {{C|Lilith}}: Lilith and her Incubus cannot gain extra fire rate from Epiphora.
** {{dlc|r}} Incubus' fire rate will increase without the accuracy penalty
* {{c|Tainted Isaac}}: If you pick up an item and drop Epiphora while holding the attack button you will keep the fire rate. The effect will disappear upon entering a new floor.
* {{i|Bag of Crafting}}: Bag of Crafting can be used to switch directions without reducing fire rate when activated.

sections.Effects: * Grants [[flight]] and one {{E|Eternal Heart}}.
sections.Notes: * Taking this item as {{c|Keeper}} will grant [[Blue Fly|Blue Flies]] instead of the Eternal Heart.

* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Clog}}.{{dlc-}}
* Poops created by this item are not tiles, but entities. As such, they are not grid-aligned, and behave differently:
** The poops vanish if the room is left and then returned to.
** Things that automatically target enemies, such as {{i|Monstro's Tooth}} and {{p|II - The High Priestess}}, will also target the poops.
** The poops can be slowly moved by pushing them.
** The poops cannot create a bridge if they are bombed near a pit.
** {{dlc|na+}} The poops will flash red when hit, similar to damaging [[monster]]s.
** {{dlc|a+}} The poops will crumble when hit, identically to regular poops.
* {{dlc+|a}} Instead of being turned into poop, poop-themed enemies like {{e|Dip}} and {{e|Squirt}} are flushed away without leaving a poop behind.{{dlc-}}
* Enemies that are turned into poop do not count towards on kill effects such as health regeneration from {{i|Charm of the Vampire}} or {{dlc+|r}} the damage increase from {{i|Lusty Blood}}{{dlc-}}.
* If the Fear effect is applied, the poop will stay a dark red.
* Does not work against any of the following:
** {{E|Lil' Haunt}}s when fighting {{E|The Haunt}}.
*** {{dlc|na}} The first Lil' Haunt can be flushed, but this softlocks the game.
** {{e|Mom's Hand}}.
** Enemies in an intangible state, such as invisible {{e|Wizoob}}s.
** {{dlc|anr+}}{{e|Turdlings|n}}, {{E|Colostomia}}, and {{E|Turdlet}}, despite them being poop-themed.
** Mini-bosses.
* Using it against the [[Champion]] version of a monster will forfeit the chance to get the champion's drop.
* {{dlc|a}} When used inside a {{r|Crawl Space}}, the ladders will be covered in water but the walls will not.
sections.Synergies:
* {{dlc+|r}} {{I|120 Volt}} / {{I|Jacob's Ladder}}: Since Flush! floods the room with water, it is now considered a wet environment, which significantly increases the arcing distance of the electricity created by these items.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: Instantly tames a hostile Blood Puppy and leaves behind a poop.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns brown wisps in the middle ring. An additional wisp is spawned for each enemy turned into {{g|Poop}}.}}
* {{t|Butt Penny|a+}}/{{t|Petrified Poop}}: Grants poops made from enemies a chance to drop pickups.
* {{i|Death's List}}: Enemies that die by being turned into poop do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into poop still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.
* {{i|Dirty Mind}}: Enemies that are turned into poop generate double the normal amount of Dips.
* {{i|Midas' Touch|na+}}: Touching poops made from enemies turns them into {{g|Golden Poop}}s just before being destroyed dropping the normal {{g|Golden Poop}} pickups including {{t|Counterfeit Penny}}.
* {{tf|Oh Crap|r}}: Isaac can heal by destroying poops created from enemies.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|nr}}{{i|Bob's Brain}}: Bob's Brain will explode upon hitting an enemy that has been turned into poop.
* {{dlc|na+}} {{t|Butt Penny}}/{{t|Petrified Poop}}: Poops made from enemies still do not drop pickups.
* {{I|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{tf|Oh Crap|anr}}: Destroying poops created from enemies do not heal Isaac.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] that follows Isaac around and blocks enemy projectiles. Upon blocking a shot, it has a 25% chance of triggering {{i|The Necronomicon}} effect, dealing 40 damage to all enemies in the room. This effect of the familiar has a cooldown of 150 frames.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* This item can rarely drop from destroying [[Rocks#Skulls|skulls]].
* {{i|The Necronomicon}} effect can occur multiple times in the same room with a small delay in-between each activation.
* It can be used to block multiple shots if positioned correctly.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars.
** {{dlc|nr+}} Dry Baby has 4th priority.
** {{dlc|r+}} Dry Baby has 6th priority.
* It is possible to activate The Necronomicon effect in a different room than the one it was hit in if Isaac transitions between them quickly enough.
sections.Synergies:
* {{T|A Missing Page|r}} / {{I|Missing Page 2|r}}: Dry Baby will deal an additional +40 damage. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.
* {{T|Duct Tape}}: Picking up Duct Tape while Dry Baby has the same position as Isaac will result in Dry Baby blocking almost all projectiles that would hit him while holding the trinket.
** This can be achieved by standing in a doorway, dropping Duct Tape, leaving the room, then re-entering the room slowly.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: No effect on damage or blocking radius; only the visual size is changed.
* {{i|Isaac's Heart}}: {{dlcalt|If Isaac has obtained Dry Baby in the first familiar spot ''before'' Isaac's Heart, the baby will block enemy tears before they can hit the heart. Enemies touching the heart can still do damage, and picking up the baby after the heart will cause the heart's hitbox to be checked first against shots.|r=No longer follows Isaac in a way where Dry Baby can constantly block it from tears.}}

sections.Effects:
* When used, swaps between the current character and Esau Jr., who has three {{e|Black Heart}}s, +2 flat [[damage]], and [[flight]]. When used as Esau Jr., swaps back to the original character.
* [[Coins]], {{e|Bomb}}s, and {{e|Key}}s are shared between the two characters, but everything else (including hearts, [[items]], [[cards]]/[[pills]], and [[trinkets]]) are not shared and apply only to the character that collects them.
* When used for the first time, Esau Jr. gains a random item for each item the original character had. Each new item comes from the same item pool the respective original item was taken from.
** [[Trinkets]], [[Cards]], [[Pills]], and/or [[Items|Active items]] are not given; only passive items are.
** Quest items like {{I|The Polaroid}} are given to both characters, as is the Esau Jr. item.
** Pickups that would normally be generated by the new items will not drop when Esau Jr. is first used.
* If either character dies, they both die, regardless of whether the other character has any remaining health.
* If multiple copies of Esau Jr. are used, starting from the fifth one, instead of activating its regular effect, the item is consumed and spawns a [[familiar]] that behaves like {{I|Abel}} but deals 7.5 damage per shot with higher fire rate.
sections.Notes:
* Unlike {{c|Lazarus Risen}} and {{c|Black Judas}}, Esau Jr. is not an actual character. He is merely a costume applied to the current character, and as such retains all of the special features of the character such as health mechanics, {{c|Lilith}}'s blindfold, and pocket active items.
* Despite starting with only black hearts, Esau Jr. is able to gain heart containers if the original character could.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Esau Jr. will not keep any passive starting items the original character had, and they won't count towards the number of items Esau Jr. will get.
* {{dlc|r+}} Esau Jr. keeps all the default starting passive items the character had.
** {{c|Eden}}'s passive starting item is neither preserved, or grants Esau Jr. an item. The same applies to items granted by {{i|Eden's Blessing}}.
* If a character has an {{e|Eternal Heart}}, then that character must be active when going to a new floor for the eternal heart to turn into a heart container.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Using Esau Jr. removes the damage penalty on [[Daily Challenges]] while retaining the schwag bonus. {{I|Deep Pockets|r}} schwag only persists if you don't transition between rooms.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Esau Jr.'s quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a black wisp when used to turn into Esau Jr. that is otherwise identical to a normal one; turning back into the original character spawns a normal wisp. Each form will retain their own set of wisps.}}
* {{t|Butter!}}: Puts Esau Jr. on a pedestal and generates an extra copy for the swapped character to hold, duplicating the item.
sections.Interactions:
* {{c|Bethany}}: Esau Jr. will have one heart container, but can still gain heart containers up to the character's normal cap. Soul Hearts will still be used as soul charges instead of health.
* {{i|Blood Oath}} / {{I|Card Reading}} / {{I|Dream Catcher}} / {{i|Empty Heart}} / {{I|Isaac's Tomb}} / {{i|Luna}} / {{i|Missing No.}} / {{I|Voodoo Head}}: The character that has the item must be active going to a new floor for it to have its effect.
** In the case of Luna, the character that has the item must also be active going into Secret Rooms for them to spawn beams of light. However, either character can then enter the beam of light to gain tears and soul hearts.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{i|Chaos}} / {{i|Sacred Orb}} / {{i|TMTRAINER}}: Will affect the items given to Esau Jr. when used for the first time, but will not affect subsequent uses. Item generation is only affected if the character that has it is currently active.
* {{c|The Forgotten}}: Esau Jr. will have one empty bone heart and three black hearts if used as The Forgotten, and one additional empty bone heart if used as {{c|The Soul}}.
* {{I|Genesis}}: Using Genesis as Esau Jr. will revert back to the original character.
* {{C|Keeper}} / {{c|Tainted Keeper}}: Esau Jr. will have two coin heart containers, but only one is filled.
* {{i|Lost Soul}}: The character that holds Lost Soul must be the one to enter a new floor to get its rewards.
* {{t|'M}}: Esau Jr. activates as normal, without being rerolled.
* {{t|Panic Button}}: Activates Esau Jr. before the active character takes damage, redirecting the damage to the inactive character. The item's charge is used in the process.
* {{i|Schoolbag}}: The extra active item will continue to be held by the character that has Schoolbag. However, it cannot gain charges through any means until the character becomes active again.
* {{c|Tainted Cain}}: Each item given to Esau Jr. on the first use is based on the item pool of the last spawned item pedestal before each item is crafted. Esau Jr. starts with a separate bag of crafting that has its own inventory and starts empty. The crafting inventories of both characters are saved. Other abilities are unchanged.
* {{c|Tainted Eden}}: Taking damage will visually turn Esau Jr. back into Tainted Eden, but will maintain Esau Jr.'s flight and flat damage bonus.
* {{c|Tainted Jacob}}: Tainted Jacob and Esau Jr. both become ghosts if any of them get touched by {{E|Dark Esau}}.
* {{c|Tainted Magdalene}}: Esau Jr.'s starting black hearts will quickly drain down to half a heart; he must obtain heart containers while in this form to have any survivability.
* {{I|Void}}: Has no effect when absorbed.

sections.Effect:
* Spawns a floating finger [[familiar]] that can be aimed with the fire buttons in all directions.
** The finger fires invisible [[spectral]] lasers, doing 10% of Isaac's [[Damage]]. The lasers fire 10 times per second and are not affected by Isaac's tear rate.
** The lasers have thickness based on Isaac's Damage, making it easier to inflict damage on higher Damage.
** While not being aimed with the fire buttons, the finger points in the direction of movement or downwards if standing still.
* {{Dlc|nr}} The Finger!'s lasers can apply Isaac's [[Tear effects]], which makes status effects trigger very often.
sections.Notes:
* Finger! will fire in the exact direction it's pointed, meaning it can be fired diagonally, or at any angle, if using a controller - the same effect as {{I|Analog Stick}}.
* The beam can be used to destroy {{g|TNT}} (among other destructible obstacles).
* The Finger! does not do contact damage.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|BFFS!}}: Doubles the finger's damage, but does not affect its lasers' thickness.
* {{I|Box of Friends}}: Adds another finger on top of the previous one, effectively doubling its damage.
* '''Finger!''': Multiple fingers will stack on top of each other and move simultaneously, effectively boosting the damage of the original one.
** Having too many fingers can cause the game to lag.
* {{i|Spirit Sword}}: When doing a spin attack, the familiar will spin with the sword.
* {{tf|Guppy}}: Flies are generated from the damage the finger does.
* {{I|Ipecac}}: The finger gains massive damage boost as expected.
** {{Dlc|nr}} The finger can [[poison]] enemies.
* {{I|Proptosis}}:
** {{Dlc|nr}} Almost doubles the finger's damage as expected. Has no damage penalty with range.
** {{Dlc|r}} Triples the finger's damage, but does not affect its lasers' thickness. Has no penalty with range.
* {{I|Sulfuric Acid}} / {{I|Terra}}: The finger has a chance to destroy rocks when pointing at them.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Godhead}}: Only increases damage.
* {{I|Terra}}: Causes the finger to constantly destroy obstacles in its line of sight.
* [[Homing tears]]: The finger's lasers do not become homing.
* {{I|A Lump of Coal}}: No effect on the finger's damage.
* {{I|Marked}}: While actively aiming, the finger behaves as normal and while fire keys are not pressed, it points towards the targeting crosshair.
* {{I|Trinity Shield}}: When not firing, the finger will point towards the nearest cardinal direction as to where the shield is left. This favors the vertical directions when the shield is at a 45° angle.
* {{I|Trisagion}}: No effect on the finger's damage.
* {{I|Angelic Prism}}: No effect on the finger's fire.

sections.Effects:
* Gives Isaac +2.0 [[luck]].
* Makes Isaac immune to:
** [[Confusion]] and [[fear]] status effects.
** [[Burn]] effects.
*** {{dlc|r+}} And damage from {{e|Fire Place}}s, enemy fires (i.e. {{e|Candler}}), and fire projectiles (i.e. {{e|Great Gideon}}).
** Toxic clouds (i.e. {{E|Gasbag}}s).
*** {{dlc|r+}} This includes poison effects such as those from destroying [[Mushroom (Obstacle)|Mushrooms]].
** The {{i|Godhead}} aura from {{E|Dogma}}'s projectiles.
** {{dlc|r+}} Slowdown from [[cobweb]]s.
* {{dlc|r+}} Isaac can stand in enemy [[creep]] for 1 second before taking damage.

sections.Effects:
* +1.5 [[range]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +1.0 [[tear falling speed]].
* Grants [[piercing tears]].
* After piercing one enemy, tears will gain double [[damage]], [[homing tears|homing]], and a 1.3x size multiplier.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}}The piercing effect makes placed {{e|Bomb}}s, {{e|Troll Bomb}}s, and {{e|Mega Troll Bomb}}s unable to be pushed around by Isaac's tears.
* Tears will also gain homing and double damage when they pierce bombs and entities the game considers enemies, like {{E|Stone Grimace}}s and {{e|Fire Place}}s.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}/{{i|Cricket's Body}}/{{i|The Parasite}}: Tears that pass through enemies will become Belial tears and split into smaller Belial tears. Non-Belial split tears can also turn into Belial tears if they pass through enemies.
* {{i|C Section}}: Fetuses will continue to deal damage per tick after gaining the effect, almost doubling total damage output.
* {{i|Godhead}}: Normal tears and Eye of Belial tears will retain damaging aura.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Eye of Belial tears can still be fed and will burst, and burst Eye of Belial tears will still be homing. Tears from regular bursts can also turn into Eye of Belial tears.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: Piercing through a projectile triggers the double damage and homing effect.
* {{i|Remote Detonator}}: Placed Bombs won't explode automatically, so they can be placed and have tears fired through them to activate double damage and homing.
* {{dlc|r}}{{I|Tiny Planet}}: After piercing an enemy, tears will continue orbiting rather than homing, but each tear can gain multiple damage and size multipliers. These tears can make quick work of even most bosses.
* {{dlc+|r}}{{I|Saturnus}}: When an orbiting tear hits an enemy, it will turn into an Eye of Belial tear. From that point, the tear gets out of {{I|Saturnus}}' orbit every time an enemy is nearby, becomes autonomous and chases every enemy in the room. It won't be destroyed by enemies anymore. When there's no enemy close from it, it comes back into the orbit. As all 7 tears can become Eye of Belial ones, this synergy is significantly powerful.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: All tears will be connected with electricity. Electricity will double in damage when the tears change.

sections.Effects:
* Everything Jar can be activated while not fully charged.
* If the item is not fully charged, it spawns a [[pickup]] based on how many charges it had:
** 1: A {{g|Poop}}.
** 2: A {{E|Penny}}.
** 3: A {{E|Bomb}}.
** 4: A {{E|Key}}.
** 5: A full {{E|Red Heart}}.
** 6: A [[pill]].
** 7: A [[card]], [[Cards and Runes|rune]], or [[Cards and Runes|soul stone]].
** 8: A {{E|Soul Heart}}.
** 9: A {{E|Gold Heart}}.
** 10: A {{E|Golden Key}}.
** 11: A {{E|Golden Bomb}}.
* If the item is fully charged, it instead has one of the following effects:
** Spawns a random amount of various different pickups, including coins, hearts, bombs, keys, cards, pills, and trinkets.
** Spawns a {{E|Fly}}.
** Spawns an assortment of [[friendly]] [[dip]]s, [[blue spider]]s, and [[Familiar#Blue Flies|blue flies]].
** Spawns random enemies in front of every door and closes the doors.
*** Enemies also spawn in front of adjacent {{r|Secret Room}}s and {{r|Super Secret Room}}s if there are any.
** Does nothing.
** Spawns an [[item]] pedestal that cycles between 9 different items 30 times per second. The item selection is from the current room's item pool.
** Spawns many colored beams of light around the room that deal damage to enemies. These beams of light varyingly scale with Isaac's damage.
** Fills the room with {{g|Poop}}, similarly to {{P|A Card Against Humanity}}
** Spawns 6 {{e|Troll Bomb}}s around the room, similarly to {{I|Anarchist Cookbook}}.
** Flips all sprites to the side, gives Isaac random tear effects for the rest of the room, and permanently increases and decreases one of Isaac's stats, similarly to {{I|Dataminer|dlc=x}}.
*** {{dlc|r+}} This also rerolls any item in the room into a glitched {{i|TMTRAINER}} item.{{dlc-}}
** Spawns many {{E|Shopkeeper}}s around the room. These have a chance to be special/error shopkeepers.
** Spawns a {{E|Giga Bomb}} pickup that gives Isaac a bomb and converts his next bomb into a giga-bomb that deals 300 blast damage, spawns many rock projectiles that deal 15 damage, and creates 13 holes in a diamond shape around the blast zone that deal 99 damage to enemies that were in their areas. These holes cannot spawn if they would close Isaac's path around the room.
*** This bomb has a chance to be lit when it spawns.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a random wisp.}}
* {{i|Hallowed Ground}}: Using the first charge will always spawn a white poop.
* {{i|Bag of Crafting}}: Allows Isaac to consistently produce high quality pickups or specific types of pickups for use in known recipes.
* {{i|Mama Mega!}} + {{i|Schoolbag}}: Consistent spawning of golden bombs allows for Mama Mega to be reused repeatedly.
* {{i|Midas' Touch}}: Chance to spawn a golden poop on 1 charge use
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|9 Volt}}: Fully recharges Everything Jar upon pickup. It also slowly recharges Everything Jar's first charge while Isaac is in an uncleared room.
* {{I|Car Battery}}: Instead of doubling its effect, Everything Jar will spawn a poop alongside its normal drop.
* {{i|Glitched Crown}} / {{p|Soul of Isaac}} / {{c|Tainted Isaac}}: The rapidly cycling item pedestal does not gain more items in its selection or slow down.
* {{I|Void}}: Consuming the Everything Jar will cause Void to spawn a poop when used, regardless of charge level.
sections.Notes: * Everything Jar can spawn gold hearts and bombs even before they are unlocked.

sections.Effects:
* +0.3 [[damage]].
* +0.1 [[speed]].
** {{dlc|nr}} Also affects maximum speed (may never exceed 2.0).
* When entering a room connected to an undiscovered {{R|Secret Room}} or {{R|Super Secret Room}}, a howl sound effect will play.
* A barking sound will play if there is an undiscovered {{R|Crawl Space}} in the room.
sections.Notes:
* A sound won't play in the first room of a new floor until you re-enter the room.
* An extra Crawl Space added by {{t|Stud Finder}} will not trigger the sound.

sections.Effects:
* When Isaac has no [[Health#Red Heart Containers|Red Hearts]]:
** Grants [[flight]].
** Every 40 seconds since activation or pickup, when the seconds on the timer hit 00, 20, or 40, while in a room with enemies, a [[shield]] triggers, nullifying all types of damage for 10 seconds.
* Grants 2 {{e|Black Heart}}s on pickup.
sections.Notes:
* Does not affect {{C|Keeper}}/{{C|Tainted Keeper}}.
* {{dlc|nr}}This item is difficult to use for anyone with red health, as it is impossible to have no red hearts without removing all heart containers (such as through [[Devil Room|Devil deals]]). It is best used by characters that cannot gain red health at all, such as {{C|???}}.
* {{dlc|r}}Characters can now deplete their red health fully through sources like {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s while having other hearts like {{e|Soul Heart}}s. As a result, this item is usable for a wider amount of characters, and has synergies with characters who prefer to have no red health (such as {{C|Eve}}).
* {{e|Rotten Heart}}s also prevent Empty Vessel's effects.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Brittle Bones}}: The empty {{e|Bone Heart|x}}s will trigger Empty Vessel.
* {{I|Gnawed Leaf}}: If the player has no Red Hearts, they can stand still and wait for the shield to activate, allowing the player to deal damage without leaving invulnerability.

sections.Effects:
* 2x [[damage]] multiplier.
* -0.5 [[shot speed]].
* {{Dlc|nr}} 0.5x fire rate multiplier.<!--The previous description was confused about tears / tear delay / fire rate but seemed to suggest this.-->
* {{Dlc|r}} 0.66x fire rate multiplier.
sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|nr}} Eve's Mascara is DPS neutral, though often the reduction of shot speed is a downgrade.
* Combos very well with any item that scales with damage but not with fire rate, such as {{i|Rotten Baby}} or {{i|Fate's Reward}}.
* {{Dlc|r}} Eve's Mascara is effectively a 33% increase in DPS, and the shot speed down is no longer as detrimental due to changes in how range works.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Abyss}}: When Eve's Mascara is picked up instead of being converted into a locust, it grants all of Abyss's locusts the high damage up without suffering the fire rate reduction allowing Isaac to increase his damage rate substantially the more items he uses Abyss on.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Missiles are not affected by low shot speed and the fire rate difference is negligible, granting double damage with nearly no downside.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The Knife is not affected by shot speed. Fire rate reduction down and 2x damage multiplier still apply.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Beams turn black and do double damage. The low shot speed makes beams damage enemies more frequently.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Tech X benefits from a lower shot speed due to it staying on enemies longer and is also not affected by range, giving little downsides.
** {{Dlc|r}} The fire rate reduction can be a major downside as it takes longer to charge Tech X and shots deal less damage when not fully charged.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}} / {{i|Ipecac}}: Shots travel a very short distance, so having {{i|Host Hat}} or {{i|Pyromaniac}} is strongly recommended.
* {{i|Eve's Mascara}}: No further effect when stacked.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: '''Not recommended.''' Tear travels very slowly, making it hard to kill mobile enemies.

sections.Effects: * Double tapping a fire key creates a Divine Shield that slowly moves in the chosen direction. * The Divine Shield has a variety of effects. ** Enemies are pushed back in the opposite direction, completely reversing their trajectory with some added momentum. *** Enemies pushed into walls or [[obstacles]] take 10 + 2 * (floor - 1) damage and deal that same damage to other enemies they collide with. ** Enemy tears are reflected, dealing damage back to enemies depending on the source of the tear. *** The reflected projectiles deal 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart. *** Reflected projectiles do not gain [[Tear effects]] from Isaac. **** Explosive projectiles (e.g. from {{E|Gurgle}}) explode as normal, dealing as much damage as they would have. **** Projectiles that create other projectiles (e.g. {{E|Shady}}) can harm Isaac and be reflected. **** Homing projectiles (e.g. from {{E|Psychic Horf}}) do not retain their homing effect after being reflected. *** Can reflect: **** Fire projectiles (e.g. from {{E|Mega Satan}}). **** Obstacles thrown by {{E|Polty}} or {{E|Kineti}}, dealing a flat 35 damage. *** Does not reflect: **** Lines of fire (e.g. from {{E|Dragon Fly}}), but can reflect fireballs (e.g. from {{E|Crackle}}) and their lines of fire do not harm Isaac. **** Projectiles from {{E|Big Bony}}, {{E|Coal Boy}}, {{E|Danny}}. ** Enemy {{i|Brimstone}} lasers are reflected, dealing 7 damage per tick (105 damage per second) to enemies hit by the reflection. It can even deflect the colossal brimstone laser fired by {{E|The Beast}}. *** White beams, such as those used by {{E|Dogma}} in its second phase, are reflected into {{I|Revelation}} beams. * The shield lasts 1 second and has a cooldown of 3 seconds. * {{transformation contribution|Seraphim}}
sections.Notes:
* If any charged item is obtained along with Divine Intervention e.g. {{I|Brimstone}} or Revelation, a different fire key may be pressed to put out the shield without forfeiting the charge of said item.
* The Blindfolded status from certain challenges disables the ability to fire, which also disables the ability to double tap to fire Divine Shields.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Divine Intervention}}: Multiple copies of this item (from effects such as {{I|Diplopia}} or {{I|Crooked Penny}}) have no effect aside from being counted for {{tf|Seraphim}}.

sections.Notes: * While most orbital familiars orbit Isaac counter-clockwise, Distant Admiration orbits clockwise. It shares this orbit ring, speed, and pattern with {{i|Bot Fly}}.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] that follows Isaac around and blocks enemy projectiles. Upon blocking a shot, it has a 25% chance of farting. Farting has a cooldown of 210 frames. There are three possible fart effects:
** [[Charm]]s all nearby enemies.
** [[Poison]]s all nearby enemies.
** [[Knockback|Knocks back]] nearby enemies {{dlc|r}}and hostile tears.
* {{dlc+|r}}{{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* Farting Baby does no contact damage.
* The knockback fart deals no damage.
** {{dlc|r}} The reflected tears deal 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart.
* The charm fart deals 5 damage.
* The poison fart initially deals 5 damage and the poison deals 3.5.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Farting Baby having the lowest priority at {{dlc|nr+}} 6th / {{dlc|r+}} 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|BFFS!}}: No effect on damage or blocking radius; only the visual size is changed.

sections.Effects:
* On use, the current [[floor]] will be [[Level Generation|completely re-generated]] and Forget Me Now will be removed from Isaac's inventory.
** Isaac will restart the level as if he had entered a new floor.
** This will be a brand new floor, with different rooms and mapping generation.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.

sections.Effects: * Tears bounce off the floor as they travel. Whenever a tear bounces, it creates a small splash that deals 25% of Isaac's [[Damage|tear damage]] to enemies.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Bob's Rotten Head|r}}: Will now bounce once, causing two explosions and two gas clouds to appear.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}: Bone tears will bounce normally, and bone shards will only bounce once.
* {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|Haemolacria}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Tears release smaller tears every time they bounce.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs bounce, dealing damage to nearby enemies when they bounce.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}: The bone club bounces when thrown. Works even with {{i|Tech X}} .
* {{i|Ipecac}}: The explosive shot bounces, poisoning and dealing high damage to nearby enemies every time it bounces.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: The tear constantly bounces.
** With {{i|Compound Fracture}}, bone shards burst on every bounce.
** With {{i|Ipecac}}, the tear causes a poisonous explosion when it bounces. The first bounce when entering a room does not explode, allowing moving the tear with less risk of self-damage.
** With {{i|Jacob's Ladder}}, electricity sparks on every bounce.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The knife bounces as it flies away from Isaac. Each bounce splashes, dealing the current damage of Isaac's tears.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: All tears bounce simultaneously, greatly increasing reach of the burst.
* {{i|Mysterious Liquid}}: Tears leave a pool of creep with each bounce.
* {{i|Pop!}}: Eyeball tears bounce repeatedly against the floor when they are about to disappear, but can be knocked by other tears to reset their range, meaning tears can be kept in the air forever as long as they are hit when they are bouncing against the floor.
* {{i|Lead Pencil}}: Tears fired by Lead Penicl also bounce, greatly increasing their range.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}/{{i|Tech X}}/{{i|Technology}}: Overrides Flat Stone.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}: No split tears on bounces.
* {{i|Dead Eye}}: Each time the tear touches the ground, there is a chance for the damage bonus to reset, making it nearly impossible to stack or keep it.
* {{i|Incubus}}: The effective range of Incubus' tears is roughly doubled, with a single bounce in the middle of the flight.
* {{i|Jacob's Ladder}}: No electricity on bounces.
* {{i|Kidney Stone}}: The stone fired by Kidney Stone doesn't bounce.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Initial tears will act as normal for Lachryphagy but tears from burst will bounce.
* {{I|Technology Zero}}: Only the last two tears will connect via electricity.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Beams continually shrink and grow. Shrunken beams do roughly 75% of normal beams' damage.

sections.Effect: * Sets the Angel Deal chance to 100% and the Devil Deal chance to 0% regardless of all other modifiers (except {{i|Duality}}), guaranteeing an {{R|Angel Room}} Door will spawn whenever possible and preventing it from closing.
sections.Notes:
* If the Devil Room has been visited before picking up Eucharist, an Angel Room will not replace it on the current floor, despite the Angel Room chance displaying 100%. However, Eucharist will still cause the door to remain open.
* In {{mode|greed|greedier}} [[Greed Mode]], Angel Room doors will not remain open after exiting the room.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Duality}}: Both Angel and Devil Room doors spawn after every boss, and the selected door will never disappear.
* {{t|Filigree Feather}}: Due to Angel Rooms being guaranteed, a large influx of items can be obtained over time.
* {{i|Red Key}}: Devil rooms can still be spawned via the creation of red rooms.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Goat Head}}: Overridden by Eucharist.

sections.Effect:
* Upon activation, a large red crosshair will appear on the ground. The crosshair can be moved using tear controls.
* After approximately 2 seconds, a large missile will land on the red marker. The missile acts like a large bomb explosion, dealing 20 times Isaac's damage (the same as {{i|Epic Fetus}}).
sections.Notes:
* The red marker works different from Epic Fetus' marker when controlled with the mouse: While pressing mouse left button, it keeps going away from Isaac, not following the mouse.
* Activating the item again while the crosshair is on the ground will cancel the animation of Isaac holding up the remote and allow him to shoot tears sooner.
** Activating the item again while having full charge (e.g. with {{i|The Battery}}) will also deplete the charge, wasting it.
** {{dlc|nr}} Taking damage also cancels the animation.
** {{dlc|nr}} The missile will still drop on the crosshair, which can no longer be controlled.
** {{dlc|r}} This will cancel the missile drop and remove the crosshair.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Car Battery|nr+}}: No effect.
* {{C|Tainted Azazel}}: Shoots thin {{I|Brimstone}} beams when rocket explodes. This behavior is not shared with {{I|Epic Fetus}}, which produces no brimstone lasers.

sections.Effects:
* When Isaac shoots, he has a chance to fire 1-3 additional tears in random directions.
** The chance to fire extra tears is unaffected by luck.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Brimstone}}: Gives a chance to shoot 1-3 additional Brimstone lasers in random directions.
** '''Brimstone''' + '''Monstro's Lung''': Overrides the Monstro's Lung + Brimstone synergy.
* {{I|Epic Fetus}}: More marks appear orbiting around where you're aiming.
* {{I|Eye of the Occult}}: Control of all tears' direction means all of the extra shots still travel in the direction in which the fire button is held, providing a substantial increase in DPS.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Gives a chance to shoot 1-3 additional Monstro's Lung bursts in random directions.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Gives a chance to shoot 1-3 additional laser rings in the same general direction as the main laser ring. Extra rings randomly deviate by up to about 25 degrees from the main ring, and their size and damage also scale with the main one.
* {{i|Technology}}: Gives a chance to fire 1-3 additional lasers in random directions.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: The 1-3 additional tears orbit as Isaac's normal tears would, noticeably increasing damage.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Dr. Fetus}}: '''Not recommended.''' When Isaac shoots, he has a chance to fire 1-3 additional bombs in random directions. Without {{i|Pyromaniac}} or {{i|Host Hat}}, self damage likely to happen.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Overrides Eye Sore.
* {{i|Sprinkler}}: Sprinkler does not shoot extra tears.
* {{i|Tractor Beam}}: Extra tears do not follow the beam.

sections.Effects:
* During the transition between floors, Isaac's nightmare shows the item that will be found in the {{r|Treasure Room}} and what [[Boss]] will be at the end of the floor.
** {{cu|Blind}} items will be revealed, as well as the hidden second item on the alternate floors ({{s|Downpour}}, etc.)
* Grants a {{e|Half Soul Heart}} upon entering a new floor (this includes each floor of the [[Ascent]]).
sections.Notes:
* On {{cu|XL}} floors, both items and bosses are shown.
* If the floor Isaac is going to has no Treasure Rooms, Dream Catcher will simply show the floor's boss. If there are no Treasure Rooms or bosses on the floor (i.e. in {{s|The Shop}}, {{s|Ultra Greed}}, and {{s|Home}}), the dream will instantly be skipped.
* Dream Catcher cannot show glitched items generated by {{i|TMTRAINER}}. Instead, it will just show {{i|The Sad Onion}}.
* Dream Catcher will show a poop in the Treasure Room if there are no item pedestals in the room.
* On {{s|Corpse}} II, the boss will appear as a blank space; on the special {{s|Mausoleum}}/{{s|Gehenna}} II floor that leads to {{s|Home}}, it will appear as {{E|Mom}}.
* On {{s|The Void}}, the Dream Catcher will show all the bosses that can be found in the various boss rooms, starting with {{E|Delirium}}.
* {{dlc|r+}} When holding Dream Catcher, the dream sequence is unskippable, except when entering {{s|The Void}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Book of Revelations}}: If the floor boss is revealed to be one of the [[The Harbingers|horsemen]], therefore Book of Revelations can be used early, as the downside is no longer relevant.
* {{i|Satanic Bible}}: If the floor boss is revealed to be one of the horsemen, and if the player has no interest in the {{i|Cube of Meat}} or doesn't mind paying health for it, Satanic Bible can be used early.
sections.Interactions:
* {{t|Devil's Crown}}: Dream Catcher will show what the Treasure Room will have if Isaac chooses to enter the room without the crown.
* {{t|Found Soul}}: The soul will receive half a soul heart for every new floor he follows Isaac to, allowing him to survive multiple hits and gather up to a maximum of 12 soul hearts. His health resets when the trinket is dropped.
* {{I|More Options}} + {{s|Downpour}} / {{s|Dross}}, etc.: Dream Catcher will not show the third item if going to the alternate floors.
* {{I|Red Key}}: When on alt path, if a bonus Treasure Room is encountered ''before'' the regular Treasure Room, the left item showed in the dream sequence will appear in that red Treasure Room, but the right item showed in the dream sequence will still be in the regular Treasure Room.
* {{i|Tarot Cloth|r}} + {{p|XVII - The Stars}}: The boosted reverse Stars card converting a Treasure Room into a double choice treasure room will make Dream Catcher's prediction inaccurate, neither of the items offered is likely to be the one displayed.

sections.Notes:
* Bosses cannot be turned into poop.
* Enemies that are turned into poop do not count towards on kill effects such as health regeneration from {{i|Charm of the Vampire}} or the damage increase from {{i|Lusty Blood}}.
** {{dlc|r}} This is especially detrimental for {{c|Tainted Keeper}} or {{c|Tainted Magdalene}} which depend on pickups generated on enemy kills.
* Poops created by this item are not tiles, but entities. As such, they are not grid-aligned, and behave differently:
** The poops vanish if the room is left and then returned to.
** Things that automatically target enemies, such as {{i|Monstro's Tooth}} and {{p|II - The High Priestess}}, will also target the poops.
** The poops can be slowly moved by pushing them.
** The poops cannot create a bridge if they are bombed near a pit.
** {{dlc|na+}} The poops will flash red when hit, similar to damaging [[monster]]s.
** {{dlc|a+}} The poops will crumble when hit, identically to regular poops.
* Touching the middle section of a {{E|Grub}} with E. Coli will split it and create a second head (rather than destroying the Grub and spawning {{E|Maggot}}s).
* {{dlc|nr}}{{E|Mulliboom}}s can be turned into poop without taking damage.
* Turning [[Champion]] versions of a monster into poop will forfeit the chance to get the champion's drop.
sections.Synergies:
* {{T|Brown Cap}} : The generated poops explode when destroyed.
* {{t|Butt Penny|a+}} / {{t|Petrified Poop}}: Grants poops made from enemies a chance to drop pickups.
* {{i|Death's List}}: Enemies that die by being turned into poop do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into poop still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.
* {{i|Dirty Mind}}: Enemies that are turned into poop generate double the normal amount of Dips.
* {{i|Holy Mantle}} / {{i|Isaac's Heart}} / [[Temporary_Buffs#Invulnerability|Invulnerability]] : The effect can be applied without taking contact damage.
* {{I|Lodestone}}: If an enemy is hit by a lodestone tear perfectly simultaneously with it being turned into poop, the resulting poop will be tinted black and have a lodestone aura that sucks in enemies. This poop will return to normal after a few seconds.
* {{i|Midas' Touch}}: Enemies touched are turned into {{g|Golden Poop}}.
* {{tf|Oh Crap|r}}: Isaac can heal by destroying poops created from enemies.
* {{C|Tainted Forgotten}}: The body will turn enemies into poop on contact.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Bob's Brain|nr}} : Bob's Brain will explode upon hitting an enemy that has been turned into poop.
* {{t|Butt Penny|na+}} / {{t|Petrified Poop}}: Poops made from enemies still do not drop pickups.
* {{i|Hallowed Ground}} / {{t|Meconium}}: The poop colors are not changed.
* {{tf|Oh Crap|anr}}: Destroying poops created from enemies do not heal Isaac.
* {{i|Serpent's Kiss}} / {{i|The Virus|anr}}: The poops won't drop Black Hearts, negating the touch effect from these items on non-bosses.

sections.Effect:
* Isaac will occasionally fire a slow-moving eye with an infinite range that fires tears identical to Isaac's tears.
* The eyes fire in the same direction as Isaac.
sections.Notes:
* The chance to fire an eye tear depends on the [[luck]] stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\min(\frac1 {30 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor},10\%)</math>
** At base Luck (0), the chance is 3.33%, maxing out at 10% at 20 Luck.
* The eye has the same rate of fire and damage as Isaac. Its travel speed is also affected by Isaac's [[shot speed]].
* If the eyes are spawned from {{C|The Forgotten}}'s melee attack, the eyes will pick up items off the floor in the same way The Forgotten's melee attack does.
* The eyes are not treated as familiars and therefore will not synergize with items like {{i|BFFS!}}.
* Eyes disappear when hitting walls, enemies, and obstacles, even if Isaac has piercing or spectral tears.
** Familiars like {{I|Dry Baby}}, {{I|Angry Fly}} and even {{I|Finger!}} also destroy the eye on collision.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Astral Projection}}: During the time-stop period of Astral Projection, there is a chance that the eyes fired will stop in the air instead of flying in a direction, and will last indefinitely until an enemy bumps into it, greatly increasing the lifetime of evil eyes. Triggering of Astral Projection also greatly increases fire rate, giving a higher chance to fire eyes.
* {{I|Ghost Pepper}} / {{I|Bird's Eye}}: Eye tears won't shoot fires. Instead, they make Isaac shoots fire more frequently.
* {{i|Pause}}: After using pause, eyes will remain frozen in place even after pause's effect has ran out.
* [[Homing tears]]: Eyes will fire homing tears; however, the eye itself will not home in on enemies.
* {{i|Mom's Eye}} / {{i|Loki's Horns}}: Evil Eye has a chance to be shot in the corresponding direction. {{dlc|r}} Eyes shot in other directions will still fire in the direction Isaac is shooting.
* {{i|Spirit Sword}}: Eyes swing a sword with slightly reduced range in the direction Isaac is firing.
* {{I|Tear Detonator}}: All tears generated have a chance to be eyes. Eyes themselves do not detonate into six tears.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Eyes will fire beams. Occasionally causes Trisagion beams to stay static in the air for a few seconds, dealing damage to enemies that come in contact with them.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|20/20}}/{{i|Cursed Eye}}/{{i|The Inner Eye}}/{{i|Mutant Spider}}: No effect; the eyes will still fire single tears.
* {{i|Angelic Prism}}: Eyes that hit the prism will be destroyed. Tears that the eyes fire will split if they travel through the prism.
* {{C|Azazel}}/{{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|Dr. Fetus}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}/{{i|The Ludovico Technique}}/{{i|Mom's Knife}}/{{i|Technology}}/{{i|Tech X}}: Overrides Evil Eye.
* {{I|Ball of Bandages}}/{{I|Cube of Meat}}/{{i|Dry Baby}}: Blocks the Evil Eye, making it hard to use.
* {{i|Chocolate Milk}}: The tears fired by the eyes match Isaac's current charge. The eyes still have continued fire rather than charging shots.
* {{i|Continuum}}: Eyes will still disappear when hitting walls; however, they will fire tears that can travel through walls.
* {{i|C Section}}/{{c|Tainted Azazel}}: Overrides Evil Eye.
* {{I|Eye of the Occult}}: The eye itself cannot be controlled, but the tears it shoots can be.
* {{i|Incubus}}: Incubus cannot fire eyes.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Tears fired by eyes can damage Isaac.
* {{i|Lead Pencil}}: Eyes will fire barrages of tears every 15 times they fire their own tears.
* {{i|Lil Gurdy}}: Destroys eyes if it touches them.
* {{dlc|r}}{{i|Marked}}: Tears shot from the eye shoot in the direction that Isaac is moving the marker towards, not at the marker.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Eyes spawn more often but only fire one tear at a time.
* {{i|Pop!}}: Eyes will fire eyeball tears but cannot be knocked around by them.
* {{i|Sprinkler}}: Sprinkler cannot fire eyes.
* {{i|Tech.5}}/{{i|Technology 2}}: Eyes only fire normal tears and the laser cannot fire eyes.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: Eyes travel straight forward, and tears fired by eyes orbit around Isaac.
* {{i|Tractor Beam}}: Neither the eyes nor their shots are affected by Tractor Beam.

sections.Effects:
* Firing in a direction causes all of Isaac's tears to move in that direction. Tears will stay in place if a fire button is not being pressed.
** The flight duration of tears is determined by the [[Range|range stat]].
* +1 [[damage]].
* +2.0 [[range]].
* -0.16 [[shot speed]].
* {{transformation contribution|Leviathan}}
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|The Adversary}}.{{dlc-}}
* Items which use charge mechanics (like {{I|Chocolate Milk}}, {{I|Cursed Eye}} or {{I|Monstro's Lung}}) require precise input to be able to both charge the shot and then move the tears, making it significantly harder to control.
** Beams and lasers like {{i|Brimstone}} are unaffected by this.
* This item replaces Isaac's regular white aura with a dimmer purple one which lowers visibility in {{curse|darkness}}.
* ''MouseControl=1'' enabled via the options.ini file does not allow the player to control the tears by mouse. Synergies which add a crosshair, however, will allow the tears to be controlled by mouse normally. (Further detail on valid synergies below)
sections.Synergies:
Synergies which cause auto-fire can have the firing stopped by pressing the "drop" key or button. Pressing Fire will resume auto-firing.

* {{i|Anti-Gravity}} + {{i|Proptosis}}: Tears travel and keep their initial size as long as the fire key is held, allowing for massive damage.
* {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: Isaac can control the mid-flight direction of the head, however its air-time is not increased.
* {{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|Technology}}: The laser becomes dark purple and automatically fires at a controllable crosshair. The crosshair behaves nearly identically to the one created by {{I|Marked}} (including in its synergies and interactions with other items), but the laser itself always fires in the cardinal directions and bends toward the crosshair rather than directly targeting it.
** {{C|Azazel}}: Like Brimstone, except that his short beam becomes a lasso. The loop starts where the beam would normally end and extends out to the cross-hair.
** '''Brimstone'''/'''Technology''' + {{i|Chocolate Milk}}: The closer the crosshair is to Isaac, the less charged the laser will be, and vice versa.
** '''Brimstone'''/'''Technology''' + {{I|Incubus}}/{{i|Twisted Pair}}: The familiars fire a straight laser towards the crosshair.
** '''Brimstone'''/'''Technology''' + {{I|Marked}}/{{I|Analog Stick}}: The laser more closely follows the crosshair's position relative to Isaac. In Brimstone's case, moving the crosshair while the laser is firing makes the laser bend toward it rather than changing the firing angle of the laser itself.
** '''Brimstone'''/'''Technology''' + {{i|Montezuma's Revenge}}: The brown beam has a similar interaction as {{C|Azazel}}'s beam but cannot create the crosshair on its own. Corn shots are unaffected.
** '''Brimstone'''/'''Technology''' + {{i|Revelation}}/{{i|Tech.5}}/{{i|Technology 2}}: The Revelation, Tech.5, and Technology 2 lasers are also affected by the crosshair but cannot create the crosshair on their own.
* {{i|Cain's Other Eye}}/{{i|Sprinkler}}: The familiar's and sprinkler's tears travel a very short distance in their original direction and can be controlled afterwards.
* {{tf|Conjoined}}/{{i|Eye Sore}}/{{i|Loki's Horns}}/{{i|Mom's Eye}}/{{i|The Wiz}}: Extra tears fly in the same direction making it easier to hit every shot increasing damage substantially.
* {{I|Isaac's Tears}}/{{i|Tammy's Head}}/{{i|Tear Detonator}}/{{i|Varicose Veins}}: Generates a halo of tears that don't break their shape.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}}: While holding a direction, the Ludovico tear will constantly shoot out controllable tears in random directions. The air time of these tears scales with the range stat.
* {{i|Marked}}: Turns the Marked crosshair purple. Tears target the crosshair's exact position. Upon reaching it, tears follow and hover on top of the crosshair for their remaining airtime.
* {{i|Technology}}: The laser becomes dark purple and automatically fires at a controllable crosshair. The crosshair behaves nearly identically to the one created by Marked (including in its synergies and interactions with other items) with the exception that lasers often arch towards the crosshair rather than traveling towards it directly and any other projectiles affected by Eye of the Occult that are not lasers (such as from {{i|Eye of Greed}} or {{i|Fate's Reward}}) will chase the crosshair and hover above it for the remainder of their range.
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: Static beams persist between tears while moving.
* {{I|Trisagion}}: The Trisagion beams will fire in the direction of cross-hair and after the fire button is released they stay in place until they fade away.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Anti-Gravity}}: Overridden by Eye of the Occult. Tears up still applies.
* {{T|Brain Worm}}: Tears will veer slightly towards enemies when travelling by, but will quickly return to player control.
* {{I|Brimstone}} + {{I|Twisted Pair}}: Twisted pair will only fire brimstone when the crosshair is moved.
* {{I|Brimstone}} + {{i|Taurus}}: When Taurus' effect triggers, Isaac will be unable to move the crosshair, but he'll keep firing the Brimstone laser at wherever the crosshair remained before Taurus triggered, effectively circumventing Taurus' penalty of being unable to fire during the invincibility period.
* {{i|Chocolate Milk}}: Not Recommended. Releasing the key to fire tears will stop the tear's movement, making it difficult to shoot enemies.
* {{i|C Section}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}/{{i|Mom's Knife}}: Overrides Eye of the Occult, stat effects still apply.
* {{i|Cursed Eye}}: The tears stack on top of each other, and only move forward when holding a direction afterwards.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs will now be controlled both in direction and range.
* {{i|Evil Eye}}: Eyes cannot be controlled, but the tears they shoot can be.
* [[Tear Effects#Homing|Homing Tears]]: Tears still home towards enemies, but controlled movement is stronger than the homing effect.
* {{I|Immaculate Heart}}: Extra tears are not affected by Eye of the Occult. Stat changes still apply.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}} + {{i|Technology}}: Overrides Eye of the Occult, stat effects still apply.
* {{i|My Reflection}}: Causes the pull to be lessened while actively controlling the tears. Pull returns to normal when not firing.
* {{i|Pop!}}: When being actively moved, tears can stay in the air until the fire button is let go.
* {{I|Saturnus}}: Extra tears are only affected by Eye of the Occult when holding fire while moving between rooms causing some of the orbiting tears' spacing and shot speed to be uneven. Stat changes still apply.
* {{i|Sprinkler}}: Sprinkler's tears travel a very short distance in their original direction and can be controlled afterwards.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Overrides Eye of the Occult; however, the shot speed down is still beneficial for Tech X.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: Not Recommended. The tears will stop moving when not shooting in the direction of their orbit, making it nearly impossible to control where they go.
* {{i|Tractor Beam}}: Tears will only move forward while being fired, but control is otherwise overridden.

sections.Effects:
* Tears are replaced with {{e|Bomb}}s that explode approximately one second after being fired.
** {{Dlc|na}} Each bomb deals 3 times the character's normal [[Damage|tear damage]].
** {{Dlc|anr}} Each bomb deals 5 times the character's normal tear damage plus a flat 30 damage. The flat 30 is not affected by damage multipliers.
** {{Dlc|r}} Dr. Fetus has two formulas for calculating the damage it does. At first, each bomb deals 10 times the character's normal tear damage. If the previous formula would lead to the bombs doing more than 60 damage, the bombs instead deal 5 times the character's normal tear damage plus a 30 flat damage. The flat 30 is not affected by damage multipliers.
** [[Tears]] down: {{Dlc|nr}} Tear Delay × 2.5 / {{Dlc|r}}Fire Rate ÷ 2.5.
** {{dlc|nr}} The [[range]] and [[shot speed]] stats both affect the velocity at which the bombs are fired out. Delay before the explosion is not affected by either.
*** {{Dlc+|r}} Bomb velocity formula has not been updated to account for the new [[range]] stat so it uses [[tear height]] for calculation (and not the actual range stat), resulting in the range stat effectively not working for Dr. Fetus with exceptions being {{I|Number One}}, {{I|Kidney Stone}}, {{i|Pluto}}, and {{i|Inner Child}}'s revive, which make velocity absurdly low. [[Shot speed]] still increases bomb velocity.{{dlc-}}
** {{Dlc|r}} Bombs grow larger or smaller with tear size modifiers and deal no knockback to each other.
sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|nr}} Dr. Fetus is a [[special item]].
* Dr. Fetus overrides multiple [[tear effect]] items, but benefit some/{{dlc|a}}all bomb-enhancing effects like {{I|Mr. Mega}}.
* Dr. Fetus bombs deal half a heart of damage to Isaac. Other explosion damage is not affected.
** Self-damage is increased to a full heart if the bomb would deal 85 damage or more. This includes effects from bomb modifiers, not just raw base damage.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Apple!}} / {{I|Euthanasia|n}} / {{I|Tough Love}}: Damage multiplier may be applied to the non-flat damage without a visual difference.
** {{dlc|nr}} Euthanasia bombs do not retain the instant kill ability.
** {{dlc|r}} Euthanasia bombs retain the instant kill ability.
* {{t|Bob's Bladder}}: Bombs from Dr. Fetus leave creep, allowing for extra damage.
* {{I|Bobby-Bomb}} / {{Dlc|a}} [[Tear Effects#Homing|Homing Tears]]: Bombs home in on enemies.
* {{I|Bomber Boy}}: Bombs explode in a large cross-shaped pattern.
** '''Bomber Boy''' + {{I|Cricket's Body}} / {{I|The Parasite}} / {{I|Polyphemus}} / {{I|Scatter Bombs|n}}: The subsequent bomb or bombs explode in a cross-shaped pattern.
* {{I|Blood Bombs}}: Bombs leave behind a pool of red creep.
* {{i|Brimstone|anr}} / {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Isaac continuously fires bombs while charging the beam/knife.
* {{I|Brimstone Bombs}}: The activation rate of the {{I|Brimstone}} lasers is random and dependent on [[Luck]]. The chance is 11% at 0 Luck, increasing by 3% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 29.67 luck and minimizes at 0% at -3.67 luck. The beams of Brimstone Bombs can push fired bombs, making this item powerful but hazardous.
* {{I|Butt Bombs}}: Bombs inherit the Butt Bomb effects.
** {{Dlc|r}} The activation rate is random and dependent on luck. The chance is 20% at 0 Luck, increasing by 3% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 26.67 luck and minimizes at 0% at -6.67 luck.
** {{dlc+|a}} Unlike normal Butt Bombs, this synergy cannot heal {{E|Brownie}}, {{E|Clog}}, {{E|Colostomia}}, {{E|Dangle}}, or {{E|Dingle}}. Both the explosion and the cloud effect deal full damage.{{dlc-}}
* Poisonous Tears : Fires {{I|Bob's Curse}} bombs.
* {{I|Cricket's Body|a}}: The bombs split outwards into 4 tiny bombs, which detonate almost immediately.
** The split bombs deal a flat {{dlc|nr}} 21 damage / {{dlc|r}} 35 damage.
** {{dlc|r}} Increases range instead of decreasing it.
** '''Cricket's Body +''' {{I|The Parasite}}: Bombs split outwards into 4 Cricket bombs and 2 Parasite bombs, which detonate and split a second time into the other type, for a total of 23 explosions.
* {{I|C Section}}: C Section has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. The fetuses drop small bombs when they touch an enemy. The bomb's damage follows Dr. Fetus' damage calculation, based on half of the fetuses damage. A fetus can drop only one bomb.
** The fetuses' bombs do not benefit from Isaac's bomb effects such as {{I|Hot Bombs}} or {{I|Bobby-Bomb}}. However, they do benefit from Isaac's tear effects and have appearance of the corresponding bombs. For example, {{I|Hot Bombs}} from {{I|Fire Mind}}, {{I|Bobby-Bomb}} from [[Tear Effects|Homing Tears]]. As such, {{I|Cricket's Body}}, {{I|The Parasite}} and {{I|Polyphemus}} leave a subsequent bomb or bombs, and {{I|Mysterious Liquid}} leaves a creep.
** '''C Section''' + {{I|Ipecac}}: The fetuses explode before dropping any bomb.
* '''Dr. Fetus''': Each additional copy of this item, such as from {{I|Diplopia}} / {{I|Crooked Penny}}, causes Isaac to fire one additional bomb in a side by side spread up to a maximum of 16 bombs. This maximum can’t be surpassed by other multi-shot effects such as 20/20.
* {{I|Eye of Belial|dlc=}}: Bombs get piercing. No more further effect.
** {{dlc|r}} Bombs deal 2.5x piercing damage.
* {{I|Fire Mind}} / {{I|Hot Bombs|a}}: The bombs leave behind a fire that damages enemies on contact after exploding, and bombs themselves deal {{Dlc|anr}} 1 / {{Dlc|r}} points of 16 damage on contact.
** {{dlc|r}} For '''Hot Bombs''', the activation rate of the fire is dependent on luck. The chance is 26% at 0 Luck, increasing by 6% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 12.34 luck and minimizes at 0% at -4.34 luck.
** {{dlc|nr}} Fire Mind + {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|Scatter Bombs}}: The fire spawned from split bombs can damage Isaac.
* {{dlc+|r}}{{I|Ghost Bombs}}: Bombs gain spectral and create ghosts when they explode. The activation rate of the ghosts is dependent on luck. The chance is 34% at 0 Luck, increasing by 8% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 8.25 luck and minimizes at 0% at -4.25 luck.
** '''Ghost Bombs''' + {{i|Almond Milk}} / {{i|Haemolacria}} / {{i|Monstro's Lung}} / {{i|Scatter Bombs}} / {{i|Soy Milk}}: While the bombs are mini, any created ghosts are smaller too and instantly launch themselves at enemies and explode, destroying nearby enemy tears, similar to {{i|Purgatory}}. They each deal 2x Isaac's damage, up to 4 times.{{dlc-}}
* {{I|Godhead}}: Does not give bombs the damaging aura, but does give them the [[homing]] effect.
* {{dlc|r}} {{tf|Guppy}}/{{I|The Mulligan|n}}: Explosions can spawn flies.
* {{I|Haemolacria}}: Haemolacria has priority. Applies +10 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Dr. Fetus tears down. The main tear is reminiscent of a bomb and scatters into 3-5 bombs that explode simultaneously. The split bombs deal half of Dr. Fetus' damage calculation based on the main tear's damage.
** '''Haemolacria''' + {{I|Sad Bombs}}: Sad bombs from Haemolacria tears shoot 10 Haemolacria tears, which then scatters into bombs without Sad Bombs' property.
* {{I|Ipecac}}: The bombs become {{I|Bob's Curse}} bombs. Isaac is immune to his bomb shots (not explosives or placed bombs). Shots will also explode immediately on impact with enemies, [[rocks]], {{g|Poop}}s, angel statues, devil statues, or walls. Does not apply Ipecac's tears down.
** {{dlc|nr}} The damage is massively increased, as the +40 damage from Ipecac is run through the damage multiplier of Dr. Fetus.
** {{Dlc|r}} The effect on damage becomes a flat +2 bonus instead of +40. Bombs leave behind a cloud of poison gas that will poison enemies in contact with it.
** {{dlc|nr}} '''Ipecac''' + {{I|Cricket's Body}} / {{I|The Parasite}} / {{I|Polyphemus}} / {{I|Sad Bombs}} / {{I|Scatter Bombs}}: Isaac is immune to the main bomb shot, but not to the explosive shrapnel.
*** {{Dlc|r}} Isaac is immune to the shrapnel bombs left by Cricket's Body, The Parasite, Polyphemus, and Scatter Bombs. Isaac is not immune to Ipecac shots from Sad Bombs.
** '''Ipecac''' + {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Isaac is no longer immune to his own bombs, and since they explode as soon as they make contact, it makes self-damage very likely. {{dlc|r}} The flat damage bonus is increased to +40.
** '''Ipecac''' + {{I|Tech X}}: Isaac is immune to the main bomb shot, but not the explosions created by the laser ring.
* {{i|Little Horn|r}}: Black-tinted bombs can summon Big Horn's hand to instantly kill non-boss enemies or to deal damage against bosses.
* {{I|Monstro's Lung}}: Monstro's Lung has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. Fires 6 bombs which detonate {{dlc|anr}} simultaneously / {{dlc|r}} at different times.
** Multi-shot effects add 1 bomb to the barrage, up to 21 bombs.
* {{I|Mr. Mega}}: Adds 25 flat damage to bomb explosions.
** {{dlc|r}} The bonus damage is only applied if the bombs are visually Mr. Mega bombs, which means items like {{I|Soy Milk}} won't get the bonus damage.
* {{I|Mysterious Liquid|a}}: Exploding bombs leave behind a large pool of creep.
* {{I|The Parasite|a}}: Upon exploding, bombs split into two other bombs, which explode almost immediately.
** The split bombs deal a flat {{Dlc|nr}} 24 damage/{{Dlc|r}} 40 damage.
* {{Dlc|r}} [[Piercing tears]]: Bombs deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.
* [[Status Effects#Poison|Poison tears]]: This is guaranteed by {{I|Bob's Curse}}, {{I|Ipecac}}, and {{I|Scorpio}}, and also has a chance to trigger from {{I|The Common Cold}}, {{t|Black Tooth}}, {{t|Pinky Eye}} or {{I|Serpent's Kiss}}.
** {{Dlc|r}} Poison bombs leave behind a cloud of toxic gas that will poison enemies in contact with it aside from the main target.
* {{I|Polyphemus}}: The bombs increase in size and do increased damage.
** {{Dlc|a}} The bombs become {{I|Mr. Mega}} bombs. After they detonate, they leave behind a regular-sized bomb that deals a flat {{Dlc|nr}} 60 damage/{{Dlc|r}} 100 damage, much like a standard bomb.
* {{I|Proptosis}}: Distance penalty does not apply.
** The non-flat damage for Dr. Fetus' damage calculation is {{Dlc|nr}} doubled / {{dlc|r}} tripled.
* {{I|Pyromaniac}}: Explosions heal Isaac, essentially making him invincible as long as he has at least one red heart container.
* {{I|Remote Detonator}}: The bombs can be detonated on command, making it easier to hit moving enemies. Unlike placed bombs, they will eventually detonate on their own.
* {{I|Rocket in a Jar}}: Shoots rockets.
** [[Piercing tears]]: Rockets do not pierce through enemies. However, they deal both piercing damage and explosion damage on impact with an enemy.
** '''Rocket in a Jar''' + {{I|Polyphemus}}: Rockets will “bounce” off of enemies, rocks, and walls, detonating twice. This is easily observable by firing parallel to a wall while moving towards it.
* {{I|Sad Bombs|a}}: Fires tears as normally placed Sad Bombs would.
** {{Dlc|r}} The activation rate is random and dependent on luck. The chance is 11% at 0 Luck, increasing by 3% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 29.67 luck and minimizes at 0% at -3.67 luck.
* {{I|Scatter Bombs}}: The bombs split into {{Dlc|nr}} 2-4/{{Dlc|r}} 4-5 tiny bombs. The bombs deal half damage of the bomb it came from.
** {{Dlc|r}} The activation rate is random and dependent on luck. The chance is 34% at 0 Luck, increasing by 8% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 8.25 luck and minimizes at 0% at -4.25 luck.
* {{i|Stye}}: The bombs have a 50% chance of gaining Stye's damage boost but not its range upgrade/shot speed downgrade. Affected bombs and their explosions are tinted a pale blue.
** The damage boost is applied to Isaac's base tear damage and does not affect any other aspect of Dr. Fetus's damage calculation.
* {{i|Technology|anr}}: Both fire normally.
* {{I|Tech X}}: Dr. Fetus has priority. The bombs have a laser ring around them.
** '''Tech X''' + {{I|Cricket's Body}} / {{I|The Parasite}} / {{I|Polyphemus}} / {{I|Scatter Bombs}}: The subsequent bomb or bombs do not have the laser ring.
* {{I|Uranus}}: The bombs freeze enemies upon killing them.

sections.Effects:
* +7 {{e|Bomb}}s.
* Removes the delay between bomb placements, allowing them to be placed rapidly.
* {{dlc|r}} Fast Bombs inflict no knockback on Isaac's bombs.
sections.Notes:
* Holding the bomb button will not automatically place them. Each bomb needs to be manually placed.
* On {{plat|PC}}, it's possible to bind two buttons to lay bombs and use both for even higher rates of bombing.
sections.Synergies: * {{i|Remote Detonator}}: Since bombs can be placed rapidly, this can be used to do lots of damage at once to a boss or enemy.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: No effect.

sections.Effect:
* Grants a 50% chance to drop a random {{e|Penny|text=Coin}}, {{e|Bomb}}, {{e|Key}}, or {{e|Red Heart|text=Heart}} whenever Isaac takes damage.
** The chances of the drops between each category are roughly equal.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Fanny Pack}}: Having multiples of Fanny Pack neither increases the amount of drops, nor the drop chance.
* {{i|Blood Oath}}: Each half-heart lost has a chance of spawning a pickup from the fanny pack.
* {{i|Scapular}}: Allows for infinite pickups once Isaac is at half a red heart (or full red heart in [[Chapter 4]] onward) by moving between rooms to reset Scapular's effect.
* {{i|Placenta}}: Similar to Scapular, allows for unlimited pickups provided a disregard for time.
* {{i|Sharp Plug}}: Each half a heart lost from the use of sharp plug has a chance of spawning a picking from the fanny pack.
* {{i|Spindown Dice}} + [[Greed Mode]]: Turns into {{i|Humbleing Bundle}} when rerolled by Spindown Dice (which is not normally obtainable in Greed Mode) and this allows penny drops from each wave a chance of turning into double pennies.

sections.Effect: * Instantly spawns a copy of all [[pickup]]s and pedestal [[item]]s on the floor in the current room, then disappears.
sections.Notes:
* If used in a room with anything that has a cost to obtain, including a {{R|Shop}}, {{R|Devil Room}} or the {{R|Black Market}}, the duplicated items and pickups will spawn without a cost attached and can be taken for free. 
** The original items will remain unchanged, and Deal with the Devil precedent will not be set by collecting the free copies. 
* If an item pedestal that is duplicated is visible as "?" (for example with the {{cu|Blind}}), duplicate will be visible as "?" until taken, just like the original item pedestal.
* Diplopia cannot be copied with another copy of Diplopia or any duplication that mimics the effect. Other forms of item duplication, such as {{i|Crooked Penny}} work as normal. 
* {{dlc|nr}} Using Diplopia on a [[trinket]] will spawn another random trinket instead of duplicating the trinket.
** {{dlc|r}} Using Diplopia on a trinket does nothing.
* {{dlc|r}} Does not duplicate {{p|Jera}}.
* {{dlc|na+}} Using Diplopia on an empty item pedestal will spawn another random item.
* {{dlc|nr}} Picking up multiple copies of items that can cause Isaac to [[transformation|transform]] will not count towards transformation progress.
** {{dlc|r}} Multiple copies of the same item do count towards transformations.
* {{dlc|nr}} If Diplopia is used in a room that offers a choice between multiple items, all of the duplicated items can be taken. The original items will still behave as normal: once an item is chosen, the others will disappear, but the duplicates will remain. This also includes {{R|Boss Rush}} ('''though taking any duplicate will still start the Boss Rush''')
** {{dlc|r}} Only one duplicate can be taken. This affects {{R|Treasure Room}} on the alternate path, {{R|Angel Room}} that has multiple [[item]] pedestals, the {{i|The Polaroid}} and {{i|The Negative}} after defeating {{E|Mom}}, the item {{i|More Options}}, {{R|Boss Rush}}, etc.
* {{C|Jacob and Esau}} can use this item to duplicate an active item to each have the same active item.
* Tear-boosting items, if stacked, cap at shooting 16 tears at once.
sections.Synergies:
* Most passive item stats bonuses stack normally when duplicated. 
* Active item copies do not share charges, and appear with a full charge (unless the item normally spawns empty of charges). 
* {{i|20/20}}: Isaac fires 3 tightly-packed tears with no increase in tear delay.
** {{dlc|r}} Damage down does not stack.
