** Additional copies of Book of Virtues do not have any effect. 
* {{i|Brimstone|nr}}: Isaac fires two lasers simultaneously.
** {{dlc|r}} Isaac gains a powered-up version of Brimstone with a unique costume that deals 1.2x damage and has +1 damage. Further copies will add another +1 damage.
* {{i|Contract From Below}}: Triples the drops upon clearing a room.
* {{I|Damocles}}: Spawns an extra item for each item cloned.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Isaac fires two bombs simultaneously.
* {{i|Eden's Blessing}}: Tears upgrades stack and Isaac gains two items at the start of the next run. Stacks up to {{dlc|nr+}} 10 / {{dlc|r+}} 2 times.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Two missiles drop, one after the other.
* {{i|The Inner Eye|nr}}: Isaac fires 6 tears. Tears down stat does not stack.

* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: A smaller tear orbits the main tear.
* {{i|Maw Of The Void|nr}}: Increased damage for tears and ring.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Isaac fires two knives simultaneously.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: The tear burst gains another {{dlc|nr}}10 tears/{{dlc|r}}12 tears, nearly doubling in size. Stacks up to 4 times.
* {{i|Mutant Spider|nr}}: Isaac fires 8 tears. Tears down stat does not stack.

* {{i|The Relic}}: An extra soul heart is given for each relic familiar.
* {{i|Schoolbag}} + any active item: While there is no use in duplicating the Schoolbag, it gives Isaac a use for duplicating an active item.
* {{i|Steam Sale|nr}}: All items in Shops become free. With {{i|Restock}}, items can be infinitely bought for free.

* {{i|Technology}}: Isaac fires two lasers simultaneously.

* {{i|Purity}}: No effect. Aura changes after a second pickup.
* {{i|Quints}}: Increases maximum familiar count by 5.
* {{i|Revelation}}: Only adds soul hearts with no addition effect on the beam.
* {{i|Sacred Heart}}: Further decreases tears and shot speed with no increase in damage.
* {{i|Stop Watch|dlc=r}}: Further increases speed with no further effect on movement speed or shot speed of enemies.
* {{i|Sulfuric Acid}}: Only further increases damage.
* {{i|Tractor Beam}}: Further increases shot speed, fire rate, and range with no other effects.

sections.Effects:
* Adds a golden tear every 20 tears fired, which causes enemies to turn gold and [[Status Effects#Petrification|petrifies]] them for a few seconds (similar to {{i|Midas' Touch}}) at the cost of one {{e|Penny}}. Golden tears can still be fired if Isaac has no money.
** Unlike other tear effects, golden tears are fired alongside regular tears rather than replacing a regular tear.
** With multi-shot abilities, whichever tear is the 20th since previous will produce the additional golden tear.
** {{Dlc|nr}} The golden tear does 2x normal [[damage]].
** {{Dlc|r}} If Isaac has no money, the golden tear does normal tear damage. If Isaac does have money, the golden tear deals 1.5x normal damage +10.
** {{Dlc|nr}} Enemies killed while golden will drop 1-4 coins.
** {{Dlc|r}} Enemies killed while golden will drop 1-3 coins.
** {{dlc|r}} If Isaac has money, golden tears that hit enemies will drop a {{e|Penny}}, effectively returning the cost.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Chocolate Milk}}: How much the 20th tear was charged determines the size and damage of the golden tear.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}} / {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Golden tears will still look like coins and will still split into other golden coins when hitting obstacles.
* {{T|Equality!}}: The coin lost when firing the tear can be quite useful for equalizing the pickup counter.
* {{I|Humbleing Bundle|r}}: Affects coins dropped from hitting enemies, allowing Isaac to potentially farm money.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Golden tears can also be fed and will burst into split tears. Burst tears are not golden.
* [[Piercing tears]]: The golden tear will petrify all enemies it hits, {{dlc|r}} and will drop a penny for each one.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Golden tears become blast that constantly drop Pennies on hit.
* {{I|Urn of Souls}}: Golden tears still shoot as normal while using the urn.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Petrified enemies that are turned into [[pickup]]s don’t also drop coins from the petrification effect.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Brimstone}}: Overrides Eye of Greed.
** {{dlc|r}} Occasionally fires a coin tear with the beam.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Overrides Eye of Greed.
** {{dlc|r}} A coin shot is fired every 20 shots, but it's very likely to hit the bomb. This makes Eye of Greed drain money over time for no benefit, unless [[Tear Effects|piercing]] is gained.
* {{I|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Petrified enemies that are turned to poop don't drop coins.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Overrides Eye of Greed.
** {{dlc|r}} Occasionally fires a coin tear in the direction of the cross similarly to {{i|Marked}}.
* {{I|Fate's Reward}}: Does not shoot coin tears.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Flat Stone}}: No effect.
* {{dlc|r}}[[Freeze|Freeze Effects]]: Petrified enemies that are frozen don’t drop coins.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Incubus}}: Does not shoot coin tears.
** {{dlc|r}} Incubus will fire coin tears in tandem with Isaac. His shot counter is independent of Isaac's. Coin tears still subtract from Isaac's pennies.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Lost Contact}}: No effect.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Overrides Eye of Greed.
** {{dlc|r}} Isaac occasionally fires a coin tear towards the controlled tear.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Overrides Eye of Greed.
** {{dlc|r}} Occasionally fires a coin tear in addition to the knife.
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{i|Technology}}/{{i|Tech X}}: Overrides Eye of Greed.
* {{I|Twisted Pair}}: The two familiars will also fire coin tears which spend Isaac's coins. Their shot counter are independent from Isaac's.

sections.Effects: * Isaac's tears have a 25% chance to stick to enemies and explode a few seconds afterward, dealing 60 damage plus Isaac's tear damage.
sections.Notes:
* Explosivo does damage to Isaac if he is hit by the explosion.
* {{dlc|nr}} Tears that stick to enemies do not deal any damage until they explode.
* {{dlc|r}} Explosivo shots deal regular tear damage upon sticking to an enemy.
* If an enemy dies or teleports with an Explosivo tear attached, the tear detaches and drops to the ground. If the detached tears touch an enemy, they will stick to that enemy and explode.
** However, when an Explosivo tear is attached to {{E|Loki}} or {{E|Lokii}}, the tear teleports with the respective boss when the boss teleports.
* Since Explosivo causes large tears to grow even larger, they can completely obscure enemies and their surroundings.
* The special tears can stick to the various spiked blocks ({{E|Wall Hugger}}, {{E|Slide}}, and {{E|Poky}}) as well as the variants of {{E|Stone Grimace}}, even when they are inactive. They will not destroy them, however. This can be used to destroy rocks or other obstacles around the tile.
* Explosivo is not affected by [[luck]].
* Explosivo shots can go through any type of {{e|Fire Place}} and {{dlc+|r}} coal from {{e|Coal Spider}} and {{e|Coal Boy}}{{dlc-}}.
* Tears that are attached to enemies can destroy {{g|Poop}}s and hit other enemies if they are close enough.
sections.Synergies:
* {{dlc|r}}{{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|The Ludovico Technique}}/{{i|Mom's Knife}}/{{i|Tech X}}: Every tick of damage Isaac’s tears deal have a chance to attach a separate Explosivo tear on a hit enemy.
* {{i|Cricket's Body}}: The explosion results in split Explosivo shots being generated. {{dlc|nr}} If the target survives, they're likely to immediately stick again. {{dlc|r}} The split tears explode when they hit an enemy or the ground.
* {{dlc|r}} {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Dr. Fetus bombs may occasionally turn into {{i|Sticky Bombs}}, but don't spawn spiders or slowing white creep.
* {{i|Fire Mind}}: Explosivo tears leave a flame behind after exploding.
* {{i|Godhead}}: The tear keeps its damaging aura while attached to the enemy, the aura grows as the tear does until it explodes. The aura can damage only enemies other than the one the tear is stuck to, however.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Main tears and burst tears can have the Explosivo effect. If a main tear has the Explosivo effect, it will burst with its explosion, the burst tears dealing damage based off the explosion damage.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Sticky shots will explode even if they fall to the floor after the initial target dies.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Explosivo tears can be fed and will burst into Explosivo tears; however, if normal tears are fed first, Explosivo fed to the normal tears will not give the tear the Explosivo effect.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: Tears that stick to enemies can still block/be destroyed by enemy shots.
** {{dlc|r}} Shielded Explosivo tears are no longer destroyed by shots while they're stuck to enemies. Up to the point that they explode, they block all enemy shots that come into contact with them, effectively cutting off an entire direction of attack (much like Dry/Fart Baby, but with a larger area of blockage and without forcing the player to waste time positioning). As such, this is an extremely powerful synergy between otherwise adequate items.
* {{i|Mr. Mega}}: Increases the damage bonus of Explosivo's explosions to 110.
* {{i|Mysterious Liquid}}: Leaves a pool of green creep on the floor.
* {{I|Parasitoid}}: Egg sacs that trigger the explosion will leave a larger pool of slowing creep.
* {{t|Nose Goblin}}/{{i|Sinus Infection}}: Explosivo tears can also be booger tears which damage the enemy over time while stuck to them before exploding.
* {{i|Soy Milk}}: The 60 point explosion damage bonus is not affected by Soy Milk's penalty, combining efficiently with the high fire rate.
* {{i|Spirit Sword}}: The fired projectile can take on Explosivo's effects. The sword swing can leave behind Explosivo tears.
* {{i|Strange Attractor}}: When a tear sticks to an enemy, nearby enemies will be quickly pulled in the direction of the tear. The constant pull may however make enemy movement unpredictable.
* {{Dlc|r}}{{I|Tech.5}}: The laser also has a chance to apply explosive tears on enemies.
* {{dlc|r}}{{i|Technology}}: Regular explosive tears may stick to enemies hit by the laser.
* {{Dlc|r}}{{I|Technology 2}}: The laser has a chance to apply an explosive tear every tick. The 60 point explosion damage bonus is not affected by the laser's penalty, combining efficiently with the high tick rate.
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: Stuck tears will still generate arcs of electricity. Multiple tears stuck to a single enemy can cause very rapid damage.
* {{i|Trisagion|r}}: Every tick of damage Isaac’s tears deal have a chance to attach a separate Explosivo tear on a hit enemy.
sections.Interactions:
* [[:Category:Bomb items|All other bomb modifiers]]: No bomb modifier outside {{I|Mr. Mega}} and {{T|Short Fuse}} has an effect on Explosivo tears.
* {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: Bob's Rotten Head has a chance to stick onto enemies. The explosion damage bonus increases to 110.
* {{dlc|nr}}{{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|Dr. Fetus}}/{{i|Mom's Knife}}/{{i|Technology}}/{{i|Tech X}}: Overrides Explosivo.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Overrides Explosivo.
* {{Dlc|r}}{{I|Holy Light}}: Some Explosivo tears have the Holy Light effect applied to them. These tears spawn a beam of light after a few seconds of sticking to an enemy instead of exploding.
* {{I|Immaculate Heart}}/{{I|Saturnus|n}}: Orbiting tears that stick to an enemy will return to the ring if the enemy cannot be stuck to anymore before the tear's duration ends.
* {{Dlc|nr}}{{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Not recommended. Tear will alternate between "normal" and black. If it touches an enemy, it will stick to it, grow in size, then explode. While the tear is stuck to an enemy, it stops doing damage and cannot be controlled, leaving the player helpless.
* {{Dlc|nr}}{{i|Tech.5}}/{{I|Technology 2}}: The laser is unaffected by Explosivo.
* {{i|Trisagion|a+nr}}: Overrides Explosivo.

sections.Effects:
* Grants [[flight]].
* Grants a one-time {{i|Holy Mantle}}-like effect. This effect wears off upon leaving the room.
* Prevents Isaac's [[speed]] from going under 1.1.
* +2 [[damage]].
* If Isaac has fewer than six full [[health|hearts]] of health, Isaac is given enough hearts to get to six full hearts, first by restoring empty [[Health#Red Heart Containers|red heart containers]], and then by granting [[Health#Soul Hearts|soul hearts]] if that isn't enough.
** Does not affect {{c|The Lost}} or {{c|Tainted Lost}} normally.
** {{c|Keeper}} and {{c|Tainted Keeper}}'s [[Health#Coin Hearts|coin heart containers]] are affected by the red heart healing, but they will gain [[Blue Fly|Blue Flies]] instead of soul hearts.
** {{c|The Forgotten}} will have all his bone hearts replenished, and any soul hearts earned will go to The Soul.
** {{c|Bethany}} will gain soul charges instead of soul hearts.
** {{c|Tainted Lazarus}} will receive the flight and stat bonuses for both forms. Since defeating Dogma will swap between forms, the active character before the cutscene will ''not'' receive the healing and shield effect, which will instead be given to the form present after the cutscene.
** {{I|Alabaster Box}} will take the soul hearts before they're given to Isaac, like normal.
* {{mode|normal}} On Normal mode, grants {{I|The Wafer}} effect, reducing all damage taken to half a heart.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, replaces every pedestal item in the current [[Rooms|room]] with other random items corresponding to the current room's [[Item Pool|item pool]].
** Each pedestal item rerolled has a 25% chance to disappear.
sections.Notes:
* {{c|The Lost}} starts with this item, even if it hasn't been unlocked yet.
* Killing Florian last in an {{E|Ultra Pride}} fight has a chance to drop the Eternal D6 if unlocked.
* In rooms with multiple item pedestals, each pedestal has a separate chance of disappearing when rerolled.
* Despite being described as a 25% chance, whether a pedestal disappears is determined by its InitSeed.
** The result can be predicted by applying a 32-bit xorshift to the InitSeed with shifts 5, 27, and 8. If the resulting unsigned value is less than 2<sup>30</sup> (1,073,741,824), the pedestal disappears; otherwise, it is rerolled.
** InitSeeds 8, 41, 74, 107, 140, and 173 are observed edge cases that also cause the pedestal to disappear. Including these edge cases, the actual probability is slightly higher than 25%: approximately 25.0000014%.
* [[Luck]] has no effect on the item.
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=50% to spawn an eternal white glowing wisp on the middle ring, which cannot be destroyed. Every use has a 50% chance to destroy all the wisps instead of spawning another. Does not affect wisps other than the ones made by this item. Rerolling items does not affect this chance.}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Car Battery}}: Re-rolls twice like {{i|The D6}}, but the 25% chance of the item disappearing is increased to approximately 44%.
* {{i|Crooked Penny}}: If a reroll would make an item disappear, all items on pedestals spawned by Crooked Penny will disappear.

{{cit|ua|r}} It is the starting item for {{C|Tainted Lazarus}}.

sections.Effects:
* While holding Flip, when Isaac enters a new room containing an item ({{r|Treasure Room}}, {{r|Shop}}, etc.), the item pedestal will have a second "ghostly" item behind it.
** The real item can be interacted with normally, while the ghostly item cannot.
** The ghostly item will vanish if there is no real item on the pedestal and Isaac leaves the room.
* Upon use, flips all real / ghostly items around on pedestals, allowing Isaac to collect the ghostly items. Does not affect pedestals that do not contain a ghostly item.
** As long as Isaac does not exit the room, empty pedestals can be flipped, meaning both the original item and the flipped ghostly item can be collected.
* If playing as {{C|Tainted Lazarus}}, activating it also flips between them and {{C|Dead Tainted Lazarus}}.
** {{dlc|r+}} Tainted Lazarus' Flip also only requires 4 charges.
sections.Notes:
* Flip has no effect on item pedestals that do not generate upon the creation of the room (i.e. Boss items, items from chests / beggars, etc.).
* Buying a real item, such as from a {{R|Shop}} or {{R|Devil Room}}, will also buy the ghostly version for free, although it can still only be obtained using Flip.
** Flipping an unbought item will update the price to the ghostly item's. 
* Ghostly items do not count as seen or collected before they have been flipped into existence.
** Once a ghostly item has been chosen for a pedestal by encountering it, it will stay even if collected elsewhere before flipping.
sections.Interactions:
* {{c|Tainted Isaac}} /  {{I|Glitched Crown}}: The cycling effect only gets applied to the primary item; the ghostly item does not cycle. Using Flip on a cycling item pedestal will cause the currently visible item to switch places with the ghostly one, after which neither item will cycle.
* {{i|The D6}} / {{p|Perthro}} / {{p|Dice Shard}}, etc.: Only rerolls visible item. Ghostly items remain unchanged.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{i|Damocles}}: Additional pedestals will not have ghostly items.
* {{i|Void}}: Ghostly items no longer appear when absorbed by Void, rendering Flip useless.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, Isaac holds an Eraser above his head, which can be thrown in any cardinal direction. Upon hitting a [[monster]], the enemy will be "erased", preventing any of the same enemy from appearing for the rest of the run.
** Deals 15 damage to [[boss]]es. If fatal, erases the boss for the rest of the run.
* Can only be recharged by entering a new floor. [[Batteries]] and most other methods of recharging have no effect.
sections.Notes:
* Erased enemies and bosses appear as a brief pink puff of smoke. Any on-death effects are not checked.
** The [[Seven Deadly Sins]] minibosses and [[Angel]]s will still drop their respective pickups or items.
** If used on multistage bosses like {{e|Hush}} or {{e|Ultra Greed}}, erasing the first phase skips any further phases.
** Erasing the first phase of {{e|Mega Satan}} will not end the fight until his hands are also defeated.
* Has no effect on invincible enemies, such as {{E|Stone Grimace}}s, lowered {{E|Host}}s, or {{E|Eternal Fly}}s.
* {{E|Bulb}}s can steal charges from the Eraser.
* If Eraser's projectile hits an enemy's projectile that has collision with Isaac's tears and isn't considered an enemy (e.g. {{e|Fire Worm}}'s fire, {{e|Coal Boy}}'s coal, {{e|Big Bony}}'s thrown bone) it has no effect and Eraser's projectile will be destroyed .
* Although the thrown Eraser cannot hit [[friendly]] enemies these enemies can still be erased if their hostile variants are erased. This also means that when effects such as {{I|Friend Finder}} attempts to spawn an erased enemy it only creates the brief puff of pink smoke wasting the effect.
* Erased enemies will remain erased if a [[Victory Lap]] is started.
** Erased enemies will also remain erased if items such as {{I|R Key}} or {{I|Genesis}} are used.
* Entities such as {{e|Ultra Greed Coin (Spinner)|text=Ultra Greed Coins}} or {{E|Little Horn}}'s {{E|Dark Ball}}s are considered enemies and can be erased.
* It is possible to erase {{E|Chubber}}'s launched Charger, rendering it unable to attack.
* Erasing {{E|Polty}}s will render {{E|Haunted Chest}}s harmless, but may make some rooms impossible to complete without bombs or flight as they rely on a Polty clearing a path.
* Each floor traveled up during the [[Ascent]] will recharge the Eraser.
* If a segmented worm-boss such as {{e|Larry Jr.}} or {{e|Scolex}} is removed via Eraser, {{e|Delirium}} will disappear if it attempts to turn into that boss. This will spawn the ending chest and count as having defeated Delirium. Other multipart bosses' erased pieces may be unable to spawn, but do not kill Delirium entirely.
* Erased enemies don't grant exploration bonuses in [[Daily Challenges]].
sections.Synergies:
* {{p|? Card}}: Can throw an additional Eraser.
* {{i|Angelic Prism}}: Throwing the Eraser through the Angelic Prism will cause it to split into four.
* {{i|The Battery}}: The eraser can gain an extra charge if it is not used on one floor.
* {{c|Bethany}} / {{c|Tainted Bethany}}: Soul and blood charges can be used with the Eraser, allowing multiple uses per floor.
* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: Throwing the Eraser at an enraged Blood Puppy (second stage) will 'erase' its enraged form, keeping it permanently tame.
** Throwing the Eraser at its third stage will make it cycle through its normal and second stage as it kills enemies.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a pink eraser wisp on the middle ring. The wisp is immune to projectiles. If a [[monster|non-boss enemy]] touches the wisp, it is erased and the wisp is destroyed. The wisp cannot erase [[boss]]es, regardless of how much health they have left.}}
* {{I|Void}}: An eraser can be thrown with each use of Void after absorbing it, allowing multiple uses per floor.
* {{c|Tainted Lazarus}}: Enemies erased in one form will still be erased when Tainted Lazarus flips.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|9 Volt}} / {{I|Battery Pack}}: Item doesn't fully charge the Eraser when picked up.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{i|Kidney Stone}} / {{i|Number One}} / {{i|Pluto}} / {{i|Inner Child}}'s revive: Lowers the Eraser's range drastically and can only be improved with [[tear height]] ups.
* {{I|My Shadow}} / {{I|Shade}}: Erasing a {{E|Charger}} will prevent all newly created [[friendly]] Chargers from spawning, rendering the item useless as this item spawns a normal Charger before changing it to the special My Shadow variant.
* {{i|Sharp Plug}}: Attempting to recharge the Eraser with the Sharp Plug hurts Isaac for half a heart without recharging the item.
* {{I|Habit}}: Taking damage with Habit will not charge Eraser.

sections.Effects:
* Isaac's tears are replaced with guided missiles. Pressing the fire buttons spawns a crosshair that can be moved freely, dropping a missile on its position from above 1.5 seconds later.
** Missiles deal 20 times Isaac's damage.
** Isaac's tear delay determines how quickly a new missile can be fired after the previous one has landed.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} Epic Fetus is a [[special item]].
* {{dlc|nr}} Epic Fetus overrides most items in the game and has the highest priority of all tear modifiers, over {{i|Brimstone}} and {{i|Mom's Knife}}.
* Missiles benefit from some bomb modifier items, though at a lesser scale compared to {{i|Dr. Fetus}}.
* Stacking multiple copies of the item causes a barrage of missiles in quick succession without resetting the crosshair's position, up to sixteen at a time.
* Missiles deal a full heart of damage to Isaac if they deal 85 or more damage.
sections.Synergies:
* {{dlc+|a}} {{i|20/20}}/{{tf|Conjoined}}{{dlc-}}/{{tf|Bookworm}}/{{i|Mutant Spider}}/{{i|The Inner Eye}}: Fires a barrage of missiles corresponding with the amount of tears.
* {{i|Bomber Boy|r}}: Missiles explode in a large cross-shaped blast, with each explosion dealing 0.75x times damage. Unlike with regular bombs, getting hit by every separate explosion from Epic Fetus won't decrease the damage for each successive explosion, drastically increasing damage.
* {{i|Blood Bombs}}: Every missile explosion leaves a large, lasting pool of red creep.
* {{i|Blood Clot}}/{{i|Chemical Peel}}: Each missile has a 50% chance to deal 20 or 40 points more damage, respectively.
* [[Status Effects#Poison|Poison tears]]: This is guaranteed by {{I|Bob's Curse}}, {{I|Ipecac}}, and {{I|Scorpio}}, and also has a chance to trigger from {{I|The Common Cold}}, {{t|Pinky Eye}} or {{I|Serpent's Kiss}}.
** {{dlc|r}} Explosions leave behind a cloud of poison gas that will poison enemies in contact with it aside from the main target.
* {{i|Brimstone|a}}: Missile explosions shoot ten blood lasers in all directions.
* {{i|Brimstone Bombs}}: Missile explosions have a chance to shoot four Brimstone lasers in the cardinal directions. The chance scales with Isaac's luck.
* {{i|Butt Bombs}}: Missile explosions will cloud up the screen, briefly [[Confusion|confusing]] and dealing 10 damage to all enemies in the room.
* {{I|Eye Sore}}: More marks appear orbiting around where you're aiming.
* {{i|Fire Mind}}/{{i|Hot Bombs}}: Missile explosions leave behind a fire that damage enemies on contact. Fire Mind's [[burn]] effect is overridden.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}: The charge attack is replaced by a missile in the Forgotten's hand and a crosshair that may be moved for an indefinite amount of time. The missile is thrown at the crosshair when all attack buttons are released, with an additional melee swing in the same direction. The melee attack is unaffected.
* {{i|Glitter Bombs}}: Missile explosions have a small chance of spawning pickups.
* {{dlc|a}} [[Homing tears]]: The crosshair slowly slides towards enemies.
* {{i|Host Hat}}/{{I|Pyromaniac}}: Isaac becomes immune to his own airstrikes.
* {{i|Incubus|r}}: Incubus fires a missile alongside Isaac's.
* {{dlc|nr}}{{i|Ipecac}}: Missiles have a poison effect, have a larger blast radius and deal drastically increased damage, as the +40 damage from Ipecac is run through the damage multiplier of Epic Fetus.
** {{dlc|r}} Adds flat +2 damage instead of +40. Explosions leave behind a cloud of poison gas that will poison enemies in contact with it aside from the main target.
* {{t|Lil Clot}} / {{c|Tainted Eve}}: The clots have their own targeting reticles and fire simultaneously with Isaac.
* {{i|Mom's Knife|a}}: Missile explosions shoot a ring of ten knives.
** {{dlc+|a}} With a second {{i|Mom's Knife}} a second missile will be shot similar to {{i|20/20}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Monstro's Lung|a}}: 2 to 4 additional crosshairs orbit the main crosshair, and missiles are fired onto each crosshair.
* {{i|Mysterious Liquid}}: Every missile explosion leaves a small, lasting pool of creep.
* {{i|Nancy Bombs}}: Explosions have a chance to be affected by any of the bomb-modifier effects that synergize with Epic Fetus.
* {{i|Polyphemus}}: Increased tear delay, but massively increases the missiles' blast radius and damage, as Polyphemus' damage multiplier is run through the damage multiplier of Epic Fetus.
* {{i|Sad Bombs}}: Missile explosions fire ten tears in all directions. The shrapnel's damage is not run through the damage multiplier of Epic Fetus.
** {{dlc|r}} The chance for the effect to proc is dependent of Isaac's luck. Chance goes up to 100% at 30 luck.
* {{i|Sticky Bombs}}: Missile explosions leave a puddle of slowing white creep.
** {{dlc|r+}} Missiles also spawn [[Blue spider|Blue Spiders]] and [[Blue fly|Blue Flies]] upon damaging an enemy.
* {{i|Strange Attractor|a}}: Enemies, pickups and trinkets get drawn towards the crosshair.
* {{i|Technology|anr}}: Both fire normally and the missile explosions shoot ten Technology beams in all directions.
** {{dlc|r}} Only Epic Fetus crosshairs are fired, but missile explosions still shoot ten Technology beams in all directions.
** {{i|Ipecac|r}}: Not recommended. Technology beams explode and may end up catching you off guard.
* {{i|Technology 2|anr}}: Both fire normally.
** {{dlc|r}} Does not reduce missiles' damage, and both fire normally at the cost of a slightly higher delay between each crosshair appearing.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Missile explosions shoot ten Technology beams in all directions.

sections.Effects:
* Adds a chance to fire needles which deal triple Isaac's [[Damage|tear damage]].
** Needles will instantly kill [[Monsters|regular enemies]] and cause them to burst into 10 more tears in all directions.
** The chance to fire a needle depends on [[luck]].
** {{dlc|nr}} The formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\frac1 { 30 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \times 2 \right \rfloor}</math>
*** At base luck (0), the chance is 3.33%, maxing out at 100% at 14.5 luck.
** {{dlc|r}} The formula used to determine the chance is: <math>min(\frac1 { 30 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \times 2 \right \rfloor},25\%)</math>
*** At base luck (0), the chance is 3.33%, maxing out at 25% at 13 luck.
** The tears released upon an instant-kill ''also'' have a chance to be needles, though these ones ''do not'' have the instant-kill ability. They do retain the 3× damage, however.
* {{transformation contribution|Spun}}
sections.Notes:
* The needle tears can kill enemies that are normally invincible, such as {{E|Peep}}'s eyes, {{E|Death's Head}}s, and {{E|Stoney}}s.
* The needle tears can kill {{E|Stone Grimace}}s and {{E|Spikeball}}s, allowing Isaac to permanently remove any obstacle in a room.
** {{dlc|r}} The needle tears can kill {{E|Bomb Grimace|n}}s, dropping 10 unlit Throwable Bombs. This can make it detrimental to shoot at them, since they are usually provided as a tool rather than an obstacle.
* The tears in the burst are larger than normal but do not have a damage bonus.
* Unless piercing is obtained, {{E|Knight}}s will still block the needles if shot from the front.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone|nr}} / {{I|Dr. Fetus|nr}} / {{I|Mom's Knife}} / {{i|Technology}} / {{i|Trisagion}}: No appearance change, tear burst, or instant kill, but triple damage still works.
* {{i|Brimstone|r}} / {{I|Dr. Fetus|r}}: Enemies killed by a needle burst into normal tears.
* {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Needles will always split into needles, although some of them may be incorrectly displayed as regular tears. Burst tears will split as normal.
* {{i|Godhead|nr}}: The aura of a needle tear will also do triple damage, but does not cause tear burst or instant kill.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: No tear burst or instant kill, but triple damage still works.
** {{Dlc|r}} Enemies killed by a needle burst into ipecac shots.
* {{I|Jacob's Ladder|r}}: The electric arcs released from a needle shot also retain the needle's instant kill and tear burst properties.
* {{i|Little Horn}}: If a tear has both the Euthanasia and Little Horn effects and instantly kills an enemy, it does not cause a tear burst.
* {{i|Tech.5}}: The tears that Isaac fires work normally, and the laser has a chance to deal triple damage with no other effects.
* {{i|Tech X|nr}}: Completely overrides Euthanasia. No triple damage, no tear burst, or instant kill.
** {{Dlc|r}} Laser Rings will sometimes deal triple damage/instantly kill regular enemies, and enemies killed by needles burst into normal tears.
* {{dlc|r}} {{i|Technology}}: Killed enemies can burst into black tears normally.
* {{i|Technology 2}}: The tears that Isaac fires work normally, but the laser is completely unaffected.
** {{dlc|r}} The laser has an extremely high chance of executing normal enemies.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: Euthanasia's tear bursts will follow the orbit in 2 close groups of 5 tears. One group travels clockwise and the other travels counterclockwise.
* {{I|Spirit Sword}}: Each swing of the sword has a chance to do 3x damage and instantly kill a non-boss enemy, causing a tear explosion.

sections.Effects:
* Converts all enemy {{e|Dip}}s and {{e|Drip}}s into [[Familiar#Dips|Dip Familiars]].
* Rocks have a chance to be replaced with poop when generated.
** The formula to calculate the chance is: <math>\mathit{Chance} = \mathit{Luck} \times 0.5 + 6.25</math>, capped at 10% at 7.5 Luck.
* Destroying {{g|Poop}}s spawn 1-4 Dip Familiars, which loosely follow Isaac around, block enemy shots, and deal contact damage to enemies.
** Dips deal contact damage to enemies equal to the [[damage]] Isaac had at the time it spawned, and can deal up to 2 ticks of contact damage and/or block 2 shots before dying.
* Destroying different types of poop will spawn special Dips:
** {{g|Corny Poop}}s create Corny Dips that spawn 1 [[Blue Fly]] on death.
*** Brownie Dips spawned by {{E|Brownie}} and {{E|Dangle}} have the same behavior.
** {{g|Red Poop}}s create Red Dips that deal twice as much damage and autonomously charge at enemies, but automatically die after 15 seconds.
** {{g|Golden Poop}}s create Gold Dips that have a chance to inflict the {{i|Midas' Touch}} effect on enemies they hit. They can also take 5 hits before being destroyed, at which point they will drop 2-3 random coins.
** {{g|Rainbow Poop}}s create Rainbow Dips that [[charm]] enemies they hit and have a chance to drop a {{e|Half Red Heart}} on death.
** {{g|Black Poop}}s create Black Dips that leave a trail of [[slow]]ing [[creep]].
** {{g|White Poop}}s create White Dips that recreate the effect of {{I|Hallowed Ground}} and can take 3 hits before being destroyed.
* Poops unique to {{C|Tainted ???}} and {{I|IBS}} also spawn Dips with special effects:
** Stone Poops create Rock Dips that deal an additional 3.5 damage per hit and can take 6 hits before dying instead of 2.
** Stinky Poops create Stinky Dips that release toxic gas as they move and a larger cloud of toxic gas when they die.
*** The toxic gas does 0.5x Isaac's damage per tick (~1.2x Isaac's damage per second) and [[poison]]s enemies; clouds left behind while alive last 1.5 seconds and the cloud created on death lasts 8 seconds.
** Fire Poops create Flaming Dips that [[Status Effects#Burn|burn]] enemies they hit and leave behind a fire when they die.
*** The burn deals 3.5 damage up to 6 times, and the fire deals 8 damage at full durability, 6 after taking 1 hit, and 4 otherwise, for a maximum of 22 damage.
* {{transformation contribution|Oh Crap}}
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Brownie}}.{{dlc-}}
* The familiars are destroyed by {{e|Bomb}}s, making them very easy to destroy when trying to blow up walls or rocks.
* Familiars remain if this item is lost (re-rolled, etc.).
* Enemies that charge towards Isaac, such as {{E|Gurdy Jr.}}, can deflect off of friendly Dips in unpredictable directions.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|BFFS!}}: Doubles damage dealt and halves damage taken by Dips, as well as increasing their size.
* {{T|Butt Penny}}: Grants a chance to spawn a Dip each time a coin is picked up.
* {{p|A Card Against Humanity}}: Allows Isaac to obtain a large number of Dips.
* {{i|E. Coli}} / {{I|Flush!}}: Poops generated by these items spawn double the normal amount of Dips.
* {{I|Mom's Bracelet}}: Friendly Dips can be picked up and thrown.
* {{T|Mysterious Candy}}: Allows a steady supply of Dips, with time. Useful for later chapters.
* {{I|The Poop}}: Allows generation of extra Dips after every room.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Compost}}: Compost does not multiply Dips.
* {{I|Sacrificial Altar}}: All Dips are sacrificed and a [[coin]] is spawned for each Dip sacrificed. The Dips do not count towards the 2 [[familiar]] limit of Sacrificial Altar.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a blue attack fly that [[Familiar#Orbital Familiars|orbits]] a long distance from Isaac and deals 2 damage per tick or 30 damage per second on contact.
* {{transformation contribution|Beelzebub}}
sections.Notes: * {{dlc|a+}} This item can drop from killing {{E|Super Envy}}. {{dlc|nr}} Super Envy can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.Effects:
* Increases the [[fire rate]] of tears fired from Isaac's left eye by 40%.
** The difference in fire rates causes Isaac's tears to be fired at a staggered rate.
** The first shot in a while is always a double shot.
sections.Notes:
* The listed fire rate on found hud is x1.2 fire rate excluding any items that add to fire rate directly.
* Every type of attack that does not use both of Isaac's eyes benefits from the fire rate up, but will not have staggered attack rate. These include, for example:
** All charged attacks such as {{i|Brimstone}} and {{i|Monstro's Lung}}.
** All tear replacers such as {{i|Dr. Fetus}} and {{i|Technology}}.
** All one-eyed characters and item effects, such as {{c|Cain}} and {{i|Stapler}}.
** Attacking via familiars, such as {{i|Incubus}} and {{c|Tainted Lilith}}.
* Multi-shot attacks such as {{i|20/20}} and {{i|Mutant Spider}}  ''do'' have staggered firing.
sections.Synergies: * {{i|Blood Clot}}/{{i|Chemical Peel}}/{{I|The Peeper}}: The bonuses these items give go to Isaac's left eye, making them more beneficial.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Bag of Crafting}}/{{i|Crooked Penny}}/{{i|Diplopia}}: Multiple copies of Eye Drops do not stack.

* Spawns a pill.
* Grants one {{E|Black Heart}} on pickup.
* Converts all good pills into their bad counterparts.
* Grants +0.6 [[damage]] for each stat down pill and +1.2 [[damage]] for each stat down [[Pills#Horse Pills|horse pill]] Isaac has taken, including those taken before acquiring False PHD.

sections.Notes:
* Bad Trip and Health Down pills will turn into I Found Pills when Isaac is at one heart.
* Neutral pills will not have a secondary effect.
* Telepills will be converted to ??? even if the latter has not yet been unlocked.
* Gulp! and Vurp! will be converted to Horf! even if the latter has not yet been unlocked.
* Pills are only converted while held by a character with False PHD. For example: If playing as {{c|Jacob and Esau}} and {{c|Jacob}} has this item, pills that got converted into 'bad' pills like a Tears Down pill can be given to {{c|Esau}} to convert them back into whatever the pill was originally.
* Losing the item by either dropping it as {{c|Tainted Isaac}} or re-rolling it via {{i|D4}}, etc., causes the damage buffs given to be removed.
* With {{i|Little Baggy}} and False PHD, the [[Rocks#Marked Skulls|Marked Skull]] in {{S|Depths}} II will drop a ??? pill, making it much harder to open {{A|A Strange Door}} that run.
* This item can be crafted from {{i|Bag of Crafting}} with seven [[pill]]s and one {{e|Black Heart}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|A Pony}}/{{I|White Pony}}: Effectively converts all Speed Down pills into Damage Up as long as one of the ponies are being held, since they will always give a minimum of 1.5 speed.
* {{t|Black Feather}}: Counts as an evil item, granting a damage up.
* {{i|Lucky Foot}} / {{i|PHD}} / {{i|Virgo}}: Pills can now be both good and bad again. The other effects of False PHD still apply when taking bad pills.
** Getting multiple of the pill-upgrading items has no effect, bad pills can still appear.
* {{i|The Wafer}}: Using a Bad Trip pill will only deal half a heart of damage and spawn a full Black Heart, resulting in a net gain of health.
** The Wafer + {{i|Placebo}}: Allows for farming infinite health using Bad Trip pills.
* {{i|Rock Bottom}}: Prevents stat-decreasing pills from decreasing your current stats. They still have an effect in the background, making it more difficult to raise that stat in the future.
sections.Interactions: * {{I|Libra}}: The balancing of stats mostly leads to a net decrease between Stat Downs and +0.6 [[damage]] up, while Luck Down provides +0.6 damage and -1 [[luck]].

sections.Effect:
* Tears inflict [[burn]] to enemies.
* Tears have a chance to explode on impact with an enemy, leaving behind a fire.
** Explosions do Isaac's current tear damage, in addition to the tear's hit.
** {{dlc|nr}} The fires deal 22 damage per tick.
** {{dlc|r}} Each fire deals up to 4 ticks of damage: 1st tick deals 23 damage, 2nd tick 17.3 damage, and 3rd and 4th tick 11.5 damage.
*** {{dlc|r}} Fires can block projectiles, up to 4 times, each time getting smaller.
**** Isaac cannot take damage from the flame, but can still take damage from the explosion.
* {{dlc|a}} Isaac gives a wide glow lighting up dark areas, such as those under the effects of the {{cu|Darkness}} or the {{E|Dark One}}'s attacks.
sections.Notes:
* The explosion effect chance depends on the [[luck]] stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.7 \right \rfloor}</math>
** At base Luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 100% at 12.86 Luck.
* {{dlc|nr}} An exploding tear does not set either the hit enemy or anything in the blast range on fire.
** {{dlc|r}} All enemies hit by the explosion will be set on fire.
* Explosive and burning damage is equal to Isaac's current damage stat.
* The flame will transform certain enemies into their fire-related versions (e. g. {{E|Hopper}}s into {{E|Flaming Hopper}}s).
* Tears can explode upon hitting {{e|Bomb}}s of any kind.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Abyss}}: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Fire Mind it turns into a burning locust that sets enemies on fire but does not explode.
* {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: Creates fire when the head lands.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}/{{i|Cricket's Body}}/{{I|Haemolacria}}/{{i|The Parasite}}: Each fractal tear has its own chance to explode. However, if the main tear explodes, all fractal tears explode.
* {{dlc|na}} {{i|Death's Touch}}: Adds burn damage to the scythes, but will not cause explosions.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: All Dr. Fetus bombs will leave a flame behind after exploding, similar to the effect of {{I|Hot Bombs}}.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: The missile will leave behind a fire.
* {{i|Explosivo}}: Explosivo tears leave a flame behind after exploding.
* {{i|Finger!|nr}}: Finger familiar can set enemies on fire but won't cause explosions.
* {{i|Host Hat}}/{{i|Pyromaniac}}: Makes Isaac immune to explosions caused by flaming tears.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Every time the tear explodes, it will leave a fire.
* {{i|Jacob's Ladder}}: Sparks can set enemies on fire but won't explode.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: Tears can explode when they destroy an enemy's tear.
* [[Piercing tears]]: Tears will pierce enemies and retain the chance to self-destruct each time it hits an enemy.
** {{Dlc|r}} Tears will pierce enemies without exploding, then self-destruct when they hit a wall or fall to the ground.
* {{Dlc|r}} {{I|Soy Milk}}: Explosions are smaller (similar to those of {{I|Scatter Bombs|n}}) and do not reach Isaac as easily.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone}}: Adds burn damage to the beam, but will not cause explosions.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}: Club turns orange and burns enemies, but doesn't cause explosions.
* {{C|The Lost}} /{{C|Tainted Lost}}: Since you'll likely have {{T|Perfection}}, Fire Mind is an awful item to obtain due to the explosion being based on luck.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Tears retain the ability to ignite enemies and explode. Tears will respawn at Isaac's location after the explosion.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Overrides the explosion chance, but the knife can still set enemies on fire.
* {{i|Mysterious Liquid}}: Overrides the explosion chance, but tears can still set enemies on fire.
** {{dlc|a}} When the Fire Mind tear explodes, a much larger pool of creep is left behind.
* {{i|Sinus Infection}}: Tears will still stick to enemies, but lose the booger appearance. The booger tears will not constantly burn the enemy they are stuck to.
* {{i|Technology}}/{{i|Technology 2}}/{{i|Tech.5}}/{{i|Tech X}}/{{i|Technology Zero}}: Adds burn damage to the beam, but will not cause explosions.
* {{dlc+|a+nr}} {{i|Trisagion}}: Beams can burn enemies, but won't cause explosions.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Rubber Cement}}: Causes tears that bounce off of enemies after exploding to also explode when the tear lands.

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|na+}} Randomly increases at least 1 and decreases 1-3 of Isaac's [[Attributes|stats]]. The same stats can be increased/decreased multiple times.
* {{dlc|a+}} Randomly increases 4 and decreases 2 of Isaac's [[Attributes|stats]].
* Each increase or decrease for a stat will change it by a fixed value:
** ±1 [[health]].
** ±1 flat [[damage]].
** {{dlc|nr}} ±0.5 [[tears]].
** {{dlc|r}} ±0.5 [[fire rate]].
** {{dlc|nr}} ±0.5 [[range]].
** {{dlc|r}} ±2.5 [[range]].
** ±0.2 [[shot speed]].
** ±0.2 [[speed]].
*** {{dlc|nr}} Also affects maximum speed (may never exceed 2.0).
** ±1 [[luck]].
* If a stat that is already at an upper or lower limit is chosen, there is no visible effect.
* {{transformation contribution|Spun}}
sections.Notes:
The stat changes are permanent and will not go away if the item is removed.
* {{dlc|r}} This makes the item especially useful for {{c|Tainted Isaac}}, since he gets to keep the stats while having the option to switch Experimental Treatment for another item and the transformation progress isn't lost in the process.
{{dlc|r}} The tears up from this item is allowed to go past the normal tear cap of 5.0. However if it decreases tears, the normal tear cap will also be decreased.

sections.Effects:
* Whenever a {{R|Devil Room}}/{{R|Angel Room}} spawns after defeating a boss, the other will also spawn.
** Upon entering one, the other one will disappear.
** Both rooms will spawn even if a devil deal was made before.
** In rooms without enough accessible walls, only one of the two will spawn.
sections.Notes:
* Even with {{i|Goat Head}} or {{i|Eucharist}}, both rooms will not stay open, and entering either of the rooms will make the other disappear.
* Teleportation via a {{p|Joker}} card, a {{E|Red Chest}}, or a {{R|Sacrifice Room}} ''before'' defeating the boss and choosing a door will follow the normal rules of Devil/Angel Room generation, instead of a 50/50 chance.
** This means that if Duality was taken as a Devil deal, or any other deal with the Devil was made in the run, teleportation will always lead to the {{R|Devil Room}}.
** The room that was chosen this way will be the only one that opens once the boss is defeated.
** Teleporting after choosing a door will always take you to the same room.
** Gaining Duality during Greed/Greedier Mode will only generate one room as per normal, rendering it normally useless. However, both rooms will generate in the penultimate floor, The Shop.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Goat Head}} / {{I|Eucharist}}: Guarantees an Angel & Devil room to spawn after every boss.
* {{i|Glowing Hourglass|r}}: Time can be reversed while inside one deal to go into another.

sections.Effects: * When Isaac uses a [[Card]], [[Pill]], or [[Rune]], he also uses a copy of the previous three Cards/Pills/Runes he used after picking up Echo Chamber.
sections.Notes:
* Previously used cards, pills, and runes are effectively used again, meaning items that modify the effects of cards, pills, or runes will also modify the effects that Echo Chamber activates.
** As a result, previously taken golden pills and blank runes will activate a random effect each time Echo Chamber activates them.
* If Isaac uses cards that convert/destroy pickups (such as {{p|Ace of Spades}}, {{p|Black Rune}}, {{p|IX - The Hermit?}}, etc.), any other cards Echo Chamber activates that generate pickups have a high chance to have their pickups converted.
* It is advised to avoid using cards that teleport Isaac, as he will be teleported to a specific room the next three times he uses a consumable. This effectively negates any current-room effects from consumables, such as {{p|XV - The Devil}} or {{p|Algiz}}, during that period, as Isaac is teleported after they activate.
** Similarly, it is also advised to avoid using unidentified pills, as Isaac runs the risk of activating either a stat down or [[Telepills]] for the next three consumables he uses.
* When obtained on {{c|Jacob and Esau}} / {{C|Tainted Lazarus}}, Echo Chamber will only duplicate the last three cards or pills previously used on the character with Echo Chamber. As a result, the character without Echo Chamber can safely use teleport cards or unidentified pills.
* If this item is somehow removed and reobtained during the run (such as when obtained from {{i|Lemegeton}} or {{t|Modeling Clay}}), the last three consumable types used during the time Isaac had Echo Chamber will be remembered. {{i|Genesis}} and [[Victory Lap]]s will erase all of the remembered consumable types, however.
* A card, rune, or pill must be '''consumed''' for the effect of Echo Chamber to trigger. That means using {{i|Blank Card}}, {{i|Placebo}}, or {{i|Clear Rune}} will not trigger Echo Chamber.
** Consuming {{p|XIV - Temperance?}} will trigger its effect normally. The pills consumed as a result of using the card are not added to Echo Chamber, and any pills in the current run's pool can be picked as normal.
* While {{P|Cracked Key}} will activate the effect of Echo Chamber and trigger the last three consumables used, using a different consumable near a wall that a red room could be created on will not create a red room, even if a Cracked Key has been used before.
* Getting automatically revived by {{P|Soul of Lazarus}} does not add it to the queue, and directly using the soul stone will not allow for automatic revival in the future.
sections.Synergies:
* {{p|? Card}} + {{P|Ancient Recall}} / [[Pills#Pill Effects|Vurp Pill]] + {{I|R Key}}: The ? Card effect can be used in conjunction with R Key without consuming it, allowing the player to in theory (with the help of {{I|Clicker}}) obtain completion marks for up to four additional routes and characters in a single run.
* {{p|Ancient Recall}}: Can be used to spawn many extra cards.
* {{I|False PHD}}: Taking benign pills (e.g. puberty) will give black hearts or damage ups for each of the pills that are activated. Caution should be exercised when using this synergy, since the last three pills taken will be converted to their bad counterparts, and one stat down can ruin the synergy.
* {{i|PHD}}, {{i|Virgo}}, or {{I|Lucky Foot}}: The last three activated pills are converted to their good counterparts, including pills taken prior to picking up {{i|PHD}}, {{i|Virgo}}, or {{I|Lucky Foot}}.
* {{I|R Key}}: Using the R key does not reset the consumable pool, as such they stay the same in Echo Chamber too.
* {{p|Jera}}: Allows for repeat duplication of consumables in the room, up to 16x if used four times.
* {{p|Suicide King}} + {{i|Dead Cat}}: Can be used to generate many pickups and items at the cost of three extra lives.
* {{i|Tarot Cloth}}: Every activated tarot card will be given a bonus effect.
* [[Pills#Pill Effects|Vurp Pill]]: Can be used to spawn infinite pills.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Genesis}}: The consumable pool is reset when Genesis is used, so if it's re-obtained after using Genesis, the previously stored consumable types won't be activated.
* {{i|Placebo}}/{{i|Blank Card}}/{{i|Clear Rune}}: Doesn't cause Echo Chamber to activate, or put the pill/card/rune into the queue.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] that fires tears with the same [[damage]] and [[tear effects]] as Isaac's tears.
* Fires at half the normal fire rate of a familiar.
** Since the normal fire rate of familiars (such as {{i|Little Steven}}, {{i|Robo-Baby}} or {{i|Seraphim}}) is {{dlc|nr}} once per second / {{dlc|r}} 1.36 times a second, Fate's Reward shoots {{dlc|nr}} once every 2 seconds / {{dlc|r}} 0.68 times a second.
* The familiar is not affected by {{dlc|nr}} [[range]]/{{dlc|r}} [[tear height]]; only [[tear falling speed]].
** {{dlc|r}} Since increasing tear height and shot speed lowers tear falling speed in order to adjust Isaac's range, increases to either stat will decrease the familiar's range, and decreases to either stat will increase the familiar's range.
sections.Notes: * {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Fate's Reward having {{dlc|nr+}} 5th / {{dlc|r+}} 7th priority.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Flat Stone}}: Familiar's tears will travel very far and then bounce once, traveling up and hitting the nearest wall.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Will fire tears that burst into split tears. Does not affect fire rate.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Will fire explosive tears. Does not affect fire rate.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}} + {{i|Brimstone}}: The tears fired by the familiar will eventually explode in a star-like pattern of Brimstone lasers if they don't hit anything.

sections.Effects:
* Grants one {{e|Bone Heart}}.
* +0.7 [[tears]].
* Spawns {{t|Mysterious Paper}} if it has been unlocked and not previously encountered during the run.

sections.Effect: * Hurts Isaac without taking away health, giving him invincibility frames equal to a full heart damage and activating any items that trigger upon getting hit.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|r}} The item will cost 10 cents if found in a {{r|Shop}}.
* As using the Dull Razor will grant extra invincibility frames like normal damage, this item can be used to enter {{r|Curse Room}} for free, or, with proper timing, allow Isaac to avoid taking damage from an enemy or obstacle.
* {{dlc|nr}} The invincibility frames allow Isaac to use {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s and {{e|Devil Beggar}}s for free.
* {{dlc|r}} Dull Razor ignores shields granted by {{i|Holy Mantle}}, and similar items.
sections.Interactions:
For a full list of items that work with Dull Razor, see the list of [[:Category:Damage-triggered items|damage-triggered items]]. Note that any specific extra conditions the items may have for their activation still apply.

* {{dlc|nr}} {{i|Blanket}} / {{i|Holy Mantle}} / {{t|Wooden Cross}}: Absorbs the "hit", wasting both items.
* {{i|Cone Head}} / {{i|Star of Bethlehem}} / Aura from {{g|White Poop}}s or [[Familiar#Dips|White Dips]]: Can block the "hit" Dull Razor inflicts, nullifying the invincibility frames and causing no effect.
* {{i|Crown Of Light}}: Disables the effect for the current room.
* {{i|Habit}}: Will try to charge Dull Razor itself, but fails due to the effect trigger before the charge bar is emptied.
** '''Habit''' + {{i|The Battery}}: Will charge Dull Razor itself only when the charge bar is not filled by extra charges.
*** '''Habit''' + '''The Battery''' + {{i|Car Battery}}: Will fully charge Dull Razor itself, allowing for infinite uses of the item.
** '''Habit''' + {{i|Schoolbag}}: The secondary item will be charged.
*** '''Habit''' + '''Schoolbag''' + {{i|9 Volt}}: If Dull Razor is copied into the second active item through an effect such as {{i|Diplopia}} or {{i|Crooked Penny}}, the two Dull Razors can be switched between infinitely.
* {{i|Isaac's Heart|nr}}: Completely nullifies the effect of Dull Razor.
* {{t|Perfection}}: Is not destroyed by a use of Dull Razor, as it counts as self-damage.
* {{i|Purity}}: Cancels the current effect of Purity, allowing a different aura to be gained instead.

sections.Effects: * Upon use, spawns two random item pedestals using the [[Item Pool|item pool]] of the current room. Eden's Soul is consumed and vanishes from Isaac's inventory.
sections.Notes:
* Starts with no charges when first picked up.
* {{dlc|nr}} Unlike {{i|Mega Blast}}, this item can be charged with a single {{E|Lil' Battery}}.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|The Battery}}: Eden's Soul cannot be activated twice with a double charge.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: Does not affect Eden's Soul. Only two items will spawn upon use.
* {{i|Void|r}}: If absorbed, Eden's Soul is stored, and allows for a single use in a desired location. Also effectively reduces charge time to {{dlc|r}} 6 / {{dlc|r+}} 4 rooms.
** {{dlc|r}}{{i|Car Battery}} + {{i|Void}}: Eden's Soul is Voided and then immediately consumed, spawning 2 items from the current item pool. This is likely to be the Angel Room as that is where Eden’s Soul is usually found. Effectively removes the charge time of Eden’s Soul.
*** If Car Battery is picked up after Eden's Soul was absorbed, the next Void use will spawn 2 item pedestals and immediately Void them.

sections.Effects:
* +0.7 [[tears]] up.
* Grants a random [[item]] at the start of the next run.
sections.Notes:
* Quest items, such as {{i|Key Piece 1}}, {{i|Key Piece 2}}, {{i|Broken Shovel 1}}, {{i|Broken Shovel 2}}, {{i|Mom's Shovel}}, {{i|Knife Piece 1}}, {{i|Knife Piece 2}}, and {{I|Dogma}} cannot be granted.
* The effect still occurs whether the run was successful or not, even if the run was restarted.
* The effect does not work if Eden's Blessing was obtained on a [[seed]]ed run, during a [[Victory Lap]], a [[RERUN]], or during a [[challenge]].
** Likewise, Eden's Blessing will not grant a free item at the start of a challenge or RERUN, instead granting the free item on the next valid run started.
*** Interestingly, seeded runs will still gain the benefit of banked Eden's Blessings, without depleting them. This means that it is possible to play an infinite amount of seeded runs, and they all start with a free item until a normal run is started.
* Even if Eden's Blessing is re-rolled, such as with the {{i|D4}} or {{i|D100}}, a random item will still be granted at the start of the next run.
** If Eden's Blessing is obtained via a re-roll, it will not grant an extra item in the next run.
** Picking up Eden's Blessing and then using {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} to pick it up again will not reward more than one extra item on the next run.
** {{dlc+|a+}} Absorbing Eden's Blessing with {{i|Void}} will not grant an extra item in the next run.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc+|r}} Removing Eden's Blessing as {{C|Tainted Isaac}} or with {{i|Genesis}} will still grant an extra item in the next run.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc+|r}} Obtaining Eden's Blessing temporarily by using {{p|Soul of Jacob and Esau|n}} will grant an extra item in the next run.{{dlc-}}
* Eden's Blessing can choose itself as the free item you gain, but will not give you an item on your next run.
* If more than one Eden's Blessing is acquired in a single run, that quantity of random items will be granted at the start of the next run, {{dlc|a+}} although it's capped at {{dlc|nr+}} ten {{dlc|r+}} two items.
** It is possible to obtain multiple copies of an item at once this way.
* {{dlc+|a+}} If Eden's Blessing effect is obtained through {{i|Metronome}}, no extra item will be given.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} If gained from {{I|Lemegeton}}, it will not grant an item next run.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} Taking Eden's Blessing and then starting a run as {{c|Jacob and Esau}} will only give item(s) to Jacob.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} As {{c|Tainted Lazarus|n}}, the item will be given to his alive form.
** If {{c|Tainted Lazarus}} somehow acquires the item before flipping for the first time of the run, Eden's Blessing will be consumed upon flip and a random item will be granted to {{C|Dead Tainted Lazarus}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} If {{i|Strawman|n}} picks up Eden's Blessing, the item will be granted on the next run whether Strawman Keeper survives or not.
* {{p|XVII - The Stars?}} can't remove the item(s) given by Eden's Blessing and using it will consume the first item(s) acquired after them or do nothing if there are no other items.
* {{p|XVII - The Stars?}} can remove Eden's Blessing and the item will be granted in the next game.
* Eden's Blessing will never attempt to give more than one [[activated item]]. Even if there are multiple Blessings and one of them gives Isaac a {{i|Schoolbag|n}}, only one activated item can be generated.
* From the bugs listed below, one can potentially "soft-lock" the game by overflowing the number of items one gets. This repeats and crashes until it fully loads, which may take several attempts to load. Anywhere over 1000 Eden's Blessings will have an increased chance to permanently soft-lock the game; therefore, these bugs are highly unadvised to abuse.
** {{dlc|a+}} Up to 10 Eden's Blessing items will be given per run. Any remaining Blessings will continue to be given each run until you have no more left.
** {{dlc|r}} Free items gained from Eden's Blessing do not carry over to subsequent runs and are capped at 10 free items for only the next run.
** {{dlc|r+}} The cap has been reduced to 2 free items for the next run.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Glowing Hourglass|nr}}: If Isaac starts with this item and immediately uses it in the starting room, the room will be reset, and all starting items and trinkets removed.
** {{dlc+|r}} Instead of the starting room being reset, Isaac is taken to the starting room of {{S|Home}}. If used again in this room without having entered any other rooms, the room will be reset, and all starting items and trinkets removed except Glowing Hourglass.{{dlc-}}

sections.Effects:
* Turns Isaac's tears into large blood tears fired in an arc. Upon hitting the floor, an obstacle, or an enemy, they burst into smaller tears in all directions.
** The number of burst tears is random between 6-11 and they have an equal chance of occurring.
** The scattered tears deal random damage that is 50-83.33% of the main tear. On average, they deal 66% damage.
* {{Dlc|nr}} Tear Delay × 2 + 10<!--unconfirmed whether it was different before Repentance but the page has said +10 for a long time-->
* {{Dlc|r}} Tear Delay × 2 + 11
** The tear delay adjustment is applied after additive fire rate modifiers (e.g. {{T|Cancer}}) and multipliers less than 1 (e.g. {{I|Polyphemus}}), and before fire rate multipliers greater than 1 (e.g. {{I|Soy Milk}}).
** I.e. calculate tear delay from tears, then fire rate from tear delay, then apply additive modifiers and multipliers less than 1, then recalculate tear delay from fire rate, then multiply by 2 and add 11, then recalculate fire rate from tear delay, then apply fire rate multipliers greater than 1.
* {{dlc|nr}} 1.31~× damage multiplier.
* {{Dlc|r}} +1 damage and 1.5× damage multiplier.
* {{Dlc|r}} Range down: 0.8× range multiplier.
* The main tear has a roughly 1.71× size multiplier.
sections.Notes:
* Higher [[shot speed]] lowers the arc of the main shot, whereas lower speed heightens it, resulting in a very minor change in effective range.
** The split tears are affected normally by shot speed.
* {{dlc|nr}} The [[tear falling speed]] stat is entirely ignored for both the main shot and the split tears.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: When the head lands, tears are fired.
* {{I|Brimstone}}: Haemolacria has priority. +20 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Brimstone tears down. The main tears burst into 4-7 brimstone beams instead of smaller tears. The beams deal 100% damage per tick.
** This does not apply to {{C|Azazel}}/{{C|Tainted Azazel}}'s default brimstone beam, which is overridden but with no special effects.
** {{Dlc|r}} If the powered-up version is acquired through another Brimstone or through {{i|Sulfur}}, the 1.2× damage multiplier is overridden by Haemolacria's own 1.5× damage multiplier. The beams' width doubles.
** Brimstone + {{I|Chocolate Milk}}: The brimstone beams deal 100% damage regardless the charge. Chocolate Milk allows for rapid firing of Haemolacria tears, giving Isaac the ability to flood the room with Brimstone lasers.
** {{Dlc|r}} Brimstone + {{I|Technology}}: The lasers coil the beams, which is purely visual, and Technology does not grant 1.5× damage multiplier.
** Dangerous when combined with {{I|Ipecac}}.
* {{I|Berserk!}} / {{C|The Forgotten}} / {{C|Tainted Forgotten}}: Burst effect occurs on each enemy hit. It also increases the size of the club, similar to {{I|Polyphemus}}. The throw is unaffected and does not scatter blood tears.
** {{C|The Soul}} uses Haemolacria as normal.
* {{I|Chocolate Milk}}: Completely charged shots and their burst tears are larger and deal higher damage than normal. Chocolate Milk also allows low-damage Haemolacria shots to be fired rapidly.
** {{Dlc|nr}} Increased tear delay.
* {{I|Compound Fracture}} / {{I|The Parasite}}: The main tears can split as they burst upon hitting an obstacle, or an enemy, but not upon hitting the floor. The split tears can burst, but burst tears from the main tears do not split.
* {{I|Cricket's Body}}: Main tears can split as they burst upon hitting the floor, an obstacle, or an enemy. The split tears can burst, but burst tears from the main tears do not split.
** {{dlc|r}} Haemolacria's ×0.8 range multiplier does not stack with Cricket's Body's own ×0.8 range multiplier.
* {{I|Dead Eye}}: Both the main tear and the burst tears can increase the damage bonus, but missing the burst tears won't reset it.
* {{I|Dr. Fetus}}: Haemolacria has priority. +10 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Dr. Fetus tears down. The main tear is reminiscent of a bomb and scatters into 3-5 bombs that explode simultaneously. The split bombs deal half of Dr. Fetus' damage calculation based on the main tear's damage.
** {{Dlc|r}} Double Dr. Fetus: Isaac fires one additional Haemolacria tear, essentially a multi-shot effect, without stat change.
** Dr. Fetus + {{I|Sad Bombs}}: Sad bombs from Haemolacria tears shoot 10 Haemolacria tears, which then scatter into bombs without Sad Bombs' property.
* {{I|Ipecac}}: Tear delay is increased by 1/3 compared to either of the items on their own, but Isaac now fires Ipecac shots that release poisonous, high-damage but non-explosive split tears on impact.
** {{dlc|r}} Haemolacria's ×0.8 range multiplier does not stack with Ipecac's own ×0.8 range multiplier. Can be dangerous when combined with {{I|Brimstone}}.
* {{I|Lachryphagy}}: Main tears can feed on other main tears or burst tears while burst tears cannot feed. The main tears will burst into 8 tears that have Haemolacria's burst effect upon impact or being fed enough. If they impact too soon after being fired or hit an enemy, they will burst into Haemolacria's burst tears. Lachryphagy's burst tears do not benefit from Haemolacria's synergies with other items, such as {{I|Brimstone}} or {{I|Tech X}}.
* {{I|Lead Pencil}}: Fires 12 Haemolacria tears, all of which will burst.
* {{I|Mom's Knife}}: Haemolacria tears fire while Mom's Knife is charging.
** {{Dlc|r}} Overridden by Mom's Knife. Stat changes still apply; however, the tears down is instead a +10 Tear Delay.
* {{I|Monstro's Lung}}: Monstro's Lung has priority. Fire rate is reduced. Fires 8 Haemolacria tears, all of which will burst.
* {{I|My Reflection}}: Range becomes extremely high, making Haemolacria tears follow Isaac for a long time before hitting the ground. Burst tears do not have a boomerang effect.
* {{I|Proptosis}}: Effects combine to create large tears that bounce off each other and burst into smaller, standard tears that are not affected by Proptosis.
* {{I|Technology}}: Haemolacria has priority. Fires arcing tears that release Technology lasers upon bursting. The lasers deal 100% of Isaac's Damage.
** {{Dlc|r}} Double Technology: Isaac fires one additional Haemolacria tear, essentially a multi-shot effect.
* {{I|Tech X}}: Haemolacria has priority. The tears burst into 3-5 Tech X rings on impact. The sizes of the rings are various, but they deal 100% of Isaac's Damage.
** {{Dlc|r}} Double Tech X: Isaac fires one additional Haemolacria tear, essentially a multi-shot effect.
* {{I|Trisagion}}: Both Trisagion and Haemolacria fire at the same time, Haemolacria does not keep spectral tears despite its tears sprite change but the arced tear keeps piercing.
** {{Dlc|r}} Haemolacria becomes one big Trisagion beam that splits into more beams when it reaches its max range.
sections.Interactions:
* {{C|Azazel}}: Haemolacria overrides Azazel's Brimstone.
* {{i|The Book of Belial|dlc=r}} + {{i|Blood of the Martyr}}/{{I|Cricket's Head}}/{{i|Magic Mushroom}}: Haemolacria's 1.5× damage multiplier stacks with these items' own 1.5× damage multipliers as expected.
* {{I|C Section}}: C Section has priority. +4 Tear Delay, instead of Haemolacria tears down. Fetuses explode into a burst of tears when they hit the ground.
* {{I|Epic Fetus}}: Epic Fetus has priority. +10 Tear Delay, instead of Haemolacria tears down.
* {{I|Flat Stone}}: At the base range, the main tear bounces once, releasing burst tears {{dlc|nr}} which do not bounce, and then burst normally. At a high range, the main tear can bounce multiple times.
** {{dlc|r}} Burst tears also bounce.
* {{I|Godhead}}: The main tear retains all effects, but burst tears do not.
** {{Dlc|r}} The main tear has the damaging aura as well as the burst tears.
* '''Haemolacria''': Additional copy of this item, such as from {{I|Diplopia}} / {{I|Crooked Penny}}, grants +1 damage instead of normal stat changes.
* {{I|Holy Light}}: The main tear can be a holy tear and bursts normally in addition to the light beam. Burst tears have an independent chance of being holy tears.
** {{Dlc|r}} The burst tears inherit the effect from the main tear. They do not have an independent chance.
* {{I|Kidney Stone}}: Overridden by Haemolacria. Only stat changes apply.
** {{Dlc|r}} Works as expected. The kidney stone also bursts when it reaches its max range.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}}: Overridden by Haemolacria, provides piercing.
* {{I|Mysterious Liquid}}: Only the main tear will leave creep.
** {{Dlc|r}} Both main and burst tears spawn creep.
* {{i|Number One|dlc=r}}: '''Not recommended.''' Unlike other similar items, Haemolacria's ×0.8 range multiplier does stack with Number One's own ×0.8 range multiplier, thus drastically reducing range.
* [[Piercing tears]] / [[Spectral tears]]: The main tear gains these effects, but the burst tears don't inherit them.
** {{Dlc|r}} Burst tears inherit these effects.
* {{I|Polyphemus}}: Stat changes applied as normal. The main tear gains the semi-piercing ability and may not burst when hitting a weaker enemy. Burst tears do not semi-pierce.
** {{Dlc|r}} Burst tears do semi-pierce.
* {{I|Pop!}}: Tears no longer arc, but will still burst when hitting an obstacle or stopping and falling to the ground. Burst tears do not bounce off of each other.
* {{I|Sharp Key}}: Split tears from thrown keys are normal tears.
* {{I|Sinus Infection}}: If the main tear is a booger, it will get stuck and not burst on hitting an enemy. Split tears have an independent chance of being booger tears.
** {{Dlc|r}} The burst tears inherit the effect from the main tear. They do not have an independent chance.
* {{I|Spirit Sword}}: Spirit Sword has priority. +10 Tear Delay, instead of Haemolacria tears down. The projectiles from the sword arc and burst.
* {{I|Technology Zero}}: Only main tears can be connected.
** {{Dlc|r}} Main tears and bursts can be connected via electricity.
* {{I|Tractor Beam}}: The main tear follows the beam, but the burst spreads normally.

sections.Effects: * When Isaac is hit, his active item gains 1 room's worth of charge.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Blood Rights}}/{{i|Razor Blade}} + {{i|Schoolbag}}: Damage from the item grants a point of charge to Isaac's other held active item.
* {{i|9 Volt}} + {{i|Yum Heart}}: Isaac could potentially become invincible on early floors or with {{i|The Wafer}}, losing only half a heart per three hits taken.
* {{i|The Battery}} + {{dlc|r}} {{i|Sharp Plug}}: Isaac gains one charge from Habit for every half-heart of damage that Sharp Plug deals, effectively granting double the charges when using Sharp Plug.
* {{i|Dull Razor}} + {{i|Schoolbag}}: Using the Dull Razor activates the Habit, but this does not restore its charge, only that of the item in the Schoolbag.
* {{i|Dull Razor}} + {{i|Car Battery}} + {{i|The Battery}}: Using Dull Razor activates the Habit, fully recharging Dull Razor, allowing for infinite uses of the Dull Razor, infinite invincibility frames, and infinite proccing of on-hit effects.
* {{I|Larynx}}: Both on-hit charge effects stack, granting Larynx 2 charges per hit.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}} {{I|Glass Cannon}}: Upon taking damage, {{I|Broken Glass Cannon}} will be half-charged. However, taking damage before the last charge will break the cannon again.
* {{I|Habit}} Duplicates: Doesn't stack; will still yield one charge per hit.
* {{I|Eraser}}: Taking damage with Eraser in your active item slot will not charge Eraser.

sections.Effects:
* Isaac's head becomes an orbital [[familiar]] that blocks shots and deals contact damage. Tears are still fired from the rotating head.
* +1 [[damage]].
* {{dlc|nr}} {{tear delay down|1}}
* {{dlc|r}} +0.5 [[fire rate]].
* The head orbital deals 7 damage per tick or {{dlcalt|105|r=56}} damage per second.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|r}} Isaac's body will spew a fountain of blood like a {{E|Gusher}}. This is purely cosmetic.
* While Isaac's actual hitbox (his body) does not change, the position of the head can obscure the body's exact position, making things such as dodging or collecting pickups more difficult.
* Items that apply contact damage and effects ({{I|The Virus}}, {{I|Aries}}, etc.) do not apply to the head.
* The head orbital ignores the normal three orbital cap used by items such as {{I|Cube of Meat}} and {{I|Sacrificial Dagger}}.
* The orbital is larger than most other orbitals, making it easier to use both offensively and defensively.
** Despite changing size with Isaac, the orbital's hitbox does not change, which can be deceptive.
* Standing near a wall may cause the head to go inside the wall while rotating, blocking tears.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Guillotine's quality is treated as 1 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Although the head doesn't increase in size, doubles the contact damage.
* {{I|Big Fan}}: Slows down the head orbital.
* {{I|Diplopia}}: Additional copies provide the stat increase as well as an orbital head familiar that doesn't fire.
* {{I|Guardian Angel}}: Does not increase the head's rotation speed.

sections.Notes:
* {{C|Tainted Azazel}} begins with an inherent version of Hemoptysis that allows him to deal full damage to cursed enemies.
** The innate sneeze ability is entirely separate from Hemoptysis, and so the sneeze can be triggered twice in quick succession. However, triggering the sneeze from Hemoptysis will cancel Tainted Azazel's brimstone charge, meaning that this item is largely ineffective as this character.
* The sneeze's range is affected by the [[shot speed]] stat, and not by the [[range]] stat itself.
* The sneeze can push {{E|Bomb}}s, pickups and enemy shots.
* The collision damage can be used to damage {{E|Host}}s while their skulls are lowered.
* Brimstone lasers shot by enemies who are not charmed, such as {{e|Monstro II}}, will also do increased damage to cursed enemies.
* {{I|Revelation}}'s charged attack will not deal increased damage to cursed enemies.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Fire Mind}}: The sneeze will still set enemies on [[Status Effects#Burn|fire]], but not cause explosions, similar to its interaction with {{i|Brimstone}}.
* {{I|Loki's Horns}}: Chance to sneeze in all cardinal directions.
* {{I|Monstro's Lung}}: Multiple sneezes are applied around the character.
* {{i|The Wiz}}: Shoots two sneezes diagonally instead of one straight forward.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: The sneeze causes an explosion. The explosion deals additional damage equal to 3x Isaac's damage +10 and will not hurt Isaac.

* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs pull their effects from bomb modifiers ({{i|Bobby-Bomb}}, {{i|Bob's Curse}}, {{i|Bomber Boy}}, {{i|Butt Bombs}}, {{i|Glitter Bombs}}, {{i|Hot Bombs}}, {{i|Mr. Mega}}, {{i|Sad Bombs}}, {{i|Scatter Bombs}}, {{i|Sticky Bombs}}) as well as tear effects.
* {{i|Finger!}}/{{i|Technology 2}}/{{i|Brimstone}}: Each tick has a random effect, allowing it to rapidly afflict enemies with multiple status effects.
** {{dlc+|a+}} This also includes the {{i|Sulfuric Acid}} effect to destroy rocks and enter secret rooms.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Isaac's Tears}}/{{i|Tammy's Head}}/{{i|Tear Detonator}}: Each tear will have its own tear effect.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: The tear will cycle through different effects, based on Isaac's tear rate.
** {{dlc+|a+nr}} If Isaac stays in one room long enough the Ludovico tear will often fill the room with many stationary {{i|Trisagion}} tears that last until Isaac leaves the room. This combination can easily clear most rooms.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The benefits of fruit cake still occur but are short lived due to the high damage of Mom's knife.
*{{i|Trisagion}}: Each Trisagion tear only has one effect with each tick having a chance to trigger the same effect.
sections.Notes:
*Fruit Cake has the potential to break rocks and open secret rooms with the effects of {{i|Sulfuric Acid}}, {{i|Ipecac}}, or {{i|Terra}}. However this can be time consuming dependent on Isaac's tear rate and number of tears fired. 
*Avoid shooting walls, obstacles and enemies close to Isaac as a {{i|Ipecac}} tear may explode and damage Isaac. {{i|Fire Mind}} & {{i|Explosivo}} tears can hurt Isaac as well when hitting an enemy. 
**{{i|Kidney Stone}} & {{i|Azazel's Rage}} cause periods of uncontrolled continuous fire that will trigger many effects, potentially damaging Isaac.
**{{i|Mom's Eye}}, {{i|Eye Sore}}, {{i|Loki's Horns}}, {{i|Cain's Other Eye}}: Fire additional tears around Isaac, increasing the risk of self damage. 
**{{i|Saturnus}}, {{i|Maw Of The Void}}, {{i|Immaculate Heart}}, {{i|Tiny Planet}}, {{i|My Reflection}}: Can potentially cause explosions nearby Isaac. 
*Fruit Cake has multiple effects that may spawn coins upon hitting an enemy, this can be beneficial to {{c|Keeper}} & {{c|Tainted Keeper}} to regain health in longer boss fights.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns [[Creep#Yellow Creep|a pool of Lemonade]] similar to the Lemon Party [[pill]] effect underneath Isaac.
** The creep deals 8 damage per tick (24 per second) and lasts ~19 seconds.
sections.Notes: * {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Peep}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns large, yellow wisps on the middle ring. The wisps make small puddles of yellow creep every other shot, which last for 3 seconds and deal 7 damage per tick to enemies that walk over them (56 damage per second).}}
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.

sections.Effects: * Spawns a hairball [[familiar]] that loosely follows behind Isaac, blocks shots, and can be swung like a flail to damage enemies. ** The ball deals 5 damage per tick, but grows, increasing damage by 2 each time it kills an enemy — up to 4 times for a maximum of 13 damage. The damage it deals per tick (each half-second) is (level × 2) + 3. ** The hairball level decreases upon entering a new floor: if level 2, it reverts to level 1. If level 3 or 4, it reverts to level 2. If level 5, it reverts to level 3. * {{transformation contribution|Guppy}}
sections.Notes:
* The hairball's hitbox is the same size regardless of level.
* {{dlc|na+r}} If Isaac has transformed into {{tf|Guppy}}, Guppy's Hairball spawns Blue Flies when it deals damage.
* If [[Blindfolded]], the ball occasionally spawns a [[Blue Fly]] while it's damaging an enemy.
* {{dlc|r}} The hairball will be reset to level 1 after entering and leaving the {{e|Mother's Shadow|n}} escape sequence.

* The size change is only cosmetic, the flies' hitboxes remain the same.
* {{dlc|nr}} This item does not affect Fly familiars or orbitals.
* No effect on flies made passive by {{I|Skatole}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{tf|Guppy}}: Doubles the damage of all Blue Flies spawned greatly increasing damage output.
* {{I|Brown Nugget}}: Turret does 7 damage instead of 3.5
* {{I|Mom's Wig}}: Doubles spider limit of the wig to 10 spiders.
* {{I|Plum Flute}}: Doubles {{E|Baby Plum}}'s contact damage, but not projectile damage. Plum is also larger.
* {{dlc|a+}}[[Familiars#Locusts|Red Locusts]]: Contact damage is doubled as normal and explosions will deal an additional 25 flat damage.
* {{I|Sissy Longlegs}}: Increases familiar's size. Spiders spawned by Sissy are affected by Hive Mind.
* {{i|Abyss|r+}}: Spawned locusts deal increased damage.
sections.Interactions: * {{dlc|r}} {{i|BFFS!}}: Does not give any additional benefit to fly and spider familiars.

sections.Effects:
* Shows the contents of {{E|Chest}}s, {{E|Fire Place}}s, {{E|Grab Bag}}s, and {{E|Shopkeeper}}s before they're opened/destroyed.
* {{transformation contribution|Guppy}}
sections.Notes:
* Guppy's Eye does not show the contents of [[tinted rock]]s, {{g|Poop}}s, and other obstacles.
* Guppy's Eye does display enemies that can be contained within chests.
* {{E|Chest}}s and {{E|Grab Bag}}s can only display up to four pickups at a time. If there are more than four, higher-value pickups like {{E|Bomb}}s, {{E|Key}}s, and {{E|Soul Heart}}s will have priority on the display.
* If a {{E|Red Chest}} looks like it doesn't have anything in it, it will teleport Isaac to the floor's {{r|Devil Room}} / {{r|Angel Room}}.
