* Due to how [[Trinkets]] generate, if a Chest displays a trinket, all future Chests will also display/give that trinket until it spawns in some way, at which point all Chests will display a new trinket.
** This means it is worthwhile opening even chests containing undesirable trinkets so that the trinket cycle advances.
* {{E|Mimic Chest}}s will change their contents whenever their spikes pop out. The unchanged drops can still be obtained by:
** Opening them with {{t|Flat File}} or {{i|Magneto}}.
** Using swing attacks (such as {{c|The Forgotten}}, {{i|Notched Axe}}, {{i|Spirit Sword}}, etc.)
* This effect works on all non-[[ending]] chests, including {{E|Mom's Chest}}.
* This item is substantially less useful in [[Greed Mode]], due to the scarcity of chests.
* The contents of Sacks or Chests that haven't spawned yet will still be revealed (for example, in rooms that spawn such Chests or Sacks when Isaac pressed a hidden switch, etc.).
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|D1|nr+}}: When duplicating a [[chest]] with D1, the original's contents will be changed. Guppy's Eye will not immediately show the new contents, but leaving the room and returning will reveal the changes. This essentially allows rerolling the rewards within them, especially useful in {{s|Chest}} and {{s|Dark Room}}.
** {{dlc|r+}} The contents are immediately updated upon reroll.
* {{t|Poker Chip}}: Guppy's Eye will show which chests contain an {{e|Attack Fly}}. This allows Isaac to drop the Trinket, leave the room, and return to reset the chest's contents.
* {{i|Sack Head}}: Sack Head rerolls pickups into {{E|Grab Bag}}s after they are spawned, making Guppy's Eye less effective on non-Grab Bag contents.
* {{i|Guppy's Eye}}: Picking up a second copy of the item gives Isaac a unique costume with both eyes replaced. This is purely cosmetic, and it will otherwise have no effect.

sections.Effects:
* Grants 5 {{e|Bomb}}s.
* Isaac's bombs have a 25% chance to spawn a [[pickup]] or [[trinket]] when they explode including other bombs.
** {{dlc|r}} Isaac's bombs have a 63% chance to spawn a pickup or trinket when they explode, but the chance for either to generate decreases by 1% for each spawn until Isaac enters a new floor. This is to prevent items such as {{i|Dr. Fetus}} or a {{e|Golden Bomb}} from providing unlimited resources. This means that the maximum spawns per floor is 63, although the final generation of a pickup or trinket will have a 1% chance to occur.
* Isaac's bombs have a 15% chance to [[charm]] random enemies in the room when they explode.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} Picking up a {{e|Golden Bomb}}, {{i|Dr. Fetus}}, {{i|Epic Fetus}}, or {{i|No. 2}} with Glitter Bombs allows infinite pickup generation.
** {{dlc|nr}} In [[Greed Mode]], Glitter Bombs cannot generate coins. Infinite pickup generation that isn't coins is still possible, however, so this can be worked around if Isaac has the {{t|Swallowed Penny}} or {{i|Piggy Bank}}, since it does still produce health.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Anarchist Cookbook}}/{{i|Curse of the Tower}}/{{p|XVI - The Tower}}: Each Troll Bomb has a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket including a {{E|Lil' Battery}} or {{e|Red Heart|text=Heart}} which can be taken advantage of for repeated uses of Anarchist Cookbook or Curse of the Tower respectively.
* {{I|Best Friend}}/{{I|Bob's Rotten Head}}/{{I|Mr. Boom}}/{{I|BBF}}/{{I|Bob's Brain}}/{{I|Kamikaze!}}: Has a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket when exploding.
* {{I|Bomber Boy|nr}}: Each additional explosion created has a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket.
* {{I|Doctor's Remote}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}: Missiles have a chance of spawning a pickup or trinket upon exploding.
* {{I|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets upon exploding.
* {{I|Everything Jar}}: At eleven charges guarantees a golden bomb.
* {{I|No. 2}}: The butt bombs have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets upon exploding.
* {{dlc|r}}[[Familiars#Locusts|Red Locusts]]: Red locust explosions have a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket.
* {{I|Scatter Bombs}}: Each smaller bomb also has a chance of dropping a pickup or trinket.
* {{t|Swallowed M80}}: Swallowed M80 explosions have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Bomber Boy|r}}: Extra explosions are unaffected by Glitter Bombs.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: No effect on shots.
* {{dlc|a+nr}}[[Familiars#Locusts|Red Locusts]]: No effect on red locust explosions.

sections.Effect: * Spawns a conjoined [[familiar]], much like {{E|Gemini}}'s small twin, Suture. It chases enemies close to Isaac, dealing 3 damage per tick (~6.43 damage per second).
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Gemini}}.{{dlc-}}
* Despite its appearance and description, Gemini does not count towards the {{tf|Conjoined}} transformation.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a white fly [[familiar]] that slowly [[Familiar#Orbital Familiars|orbits]] Isaac and deals 3 damage per tick or 45 damage per second on contact.
* {{transformation contribution|Beelzebub}}
sections.Notes: * This familiar orbits Isaac at a middle-length distance somewhere between {{i|Distant Admiration}} and {{i|Forever alone}}.

sections.Effects:
* Gives Isaac a [[familiar]] that mimics {{E|Baby Plum}}'s attack of shooting tears and propelling itself diagonally around the room. It deals 2 contact damage per tick to enemies (6 per second). It fires 15 tears per second behind itself while moving which deals 3 damage.
** Fruity Plum will prioritize moving towards nearby enemies.
** If there are no enemies, Fruity Plum loosely orbits Isaac.
* {{transformation contribution|Beelzebub}}
sections.Notes: * Since the achievement to unlock explicitly states you must merely '''defeat''' Baby Plum, regardless of the method used, sparing Baby Plum and letting her leave counts towards the unlocking of this item.
sections.Synergies:
* {{T|Baby-Bender}}: The [[homing]] effect is applied as normal which drastically improves its damage output.
* {{I|BFFS!}} / {{I|Hive Mind}}: Doubles its contact damage and tear damage. The effect does not stack.
sections.Interactions:
* {{T|Child Leash}}: No effect.
* {{T|Forgotten Lullaby}}: Does not increase its fire rate.
* {{T|Friendship Necklace}}: No effect.
* {{T|RC Remote}}: No effect.

{{nav|fly}}

sections.Effect:
* Spawns a white poop [[familiar]] which turns into a {{g|White Poop}} when Isaac is hurt.
** White Poop has an aura that multiplies both [[fire rate]] and [[tear delay]] by x2.5 and has a 50% chance to ignore damage similarly to {{i|Cone Head}}, except the chance is higher.
** {{dlc|r}} White Poop has similar durability to {{g|Golden Poop}}. The aura additionally increases [[damage]] by 20% and gives Isaac's tears a [[Tear Effects#Homing Tears|homing]] effect.
** Hallowed Ground will not activate if the player negates the source of damage through items such as {{i|Holy Mantle}}.
* The familiar will respawn after Isaac leaves the room.
* {{Dlc|r}} This item belongs to the {{tf|Oh Crap}} set. Collecting three items from this set will transform Isaac into a walking pile of poop.
sections.Notes:
* Aligning a white poop to drop next to a {{e|Devil Beggar}}, a {{e|Blood Donation Machine}} or a {{e|Confessional}} is a great way to save on health, as the aura will allow for frequent free plays.
* Damage from {{r|Sacrifice Room}} spikes can be blocked by Hallowed Ground, but no payout is rewarded.
* White Poop is impervious to enemy shots and charging attacks.
* White Poop is not immune to explosive damage or stomping attacks.
* {{e|Chubber}} attacks cannot destroy White Poop, but can still harm Isaac.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Hallowed Ground having the lowest priority at {{dlc|nr+}} 6th / {{dlc|r+}} 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.
* {{Dlc|r}} This item does not produce White Poop in {{e|The Beast|n}}'s boss arena.
sections.Synergies:
* {{p|A Card Against Humanity}} / [[Re-Lax|Re-Lax pill]]: The poops created have a 33% chance to become white.
* {{i|Blood Rights}}/{{i|IV Bag}}/{{i|Kamikaze!}}/{{i|Razor Blade}}: The aura has a chance to block the damage inflicted, but the effects will still occur.
* {{I|Dirty Mind}}: Destroying the White Poop will spawn friendly white Dips which give off a small version of the aura.
* {{i|Everything Jar}}: Using the first charge will always spawn a white poop.
** Barring Everything Jar is only used at its first charge, when used along with items that grant active item charges, white poop can be spawned more than once in the same room, making this item much more powerful. If used with {{I|Habit}}, allows white poop to be spawned indefinitely rather than only on the first hit.
* {{i|The Poop}}: Using The Poop will always spawn a white poop.
** When used along with items that grant active item charges, white poop can be spawned more than once in the same room, making this item much more powerful. If used with {{I|Habit}}, allows white poop to be spawned indefinitely rather than only on the first hit.
* {{I|Rock Bottom}}: Isaac will keep the stat upgrades even after leaving the aura. However, it won't keep the homing effect outside of the aura.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Increases [[familiar]]'s size but otherwise has no effect.
* {{i|Box of Friends}}: All poop familiars turn into white poop at the same time, and their affects are accumulative. A new poop familiar appears even if the previous poops have been used up.
* {{i|D12}}: Does not increase the chance for rerolled obstacles to become {{g|White Poop}}.
* {{i|Holy Mantle}} / {{c|The Lost}}: Breaking the holy mantle shield does not count as damage taken, so the white poop will not drop.
* {{I|Immaculate Heart}}: The damage multiplier does not stack with that from a white poop.
* {{I|Star of Bethlehem}}: The star's aura does not stack with the poop's aura.
* {{i|Mom's Eye}} / {{i|Loki's Horns}}: '''Not recommended.'''  Backwards/cross shots from these items make it very easy to destroy the white poop by accident.
* {{t|Meconium}}: Although Meconium cannot replace the poop {{i|Hallowed Ground}} spawns with, {{g|Black Poop}} has a chance to replace {{g|White Poop}}s that would have been created by other items which have synergies with {{i|Hallowed Ground}}.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, spends 5 {{E|Penny|text=pennies}} and grants +1.2 [[damage]] for the current room.
** The effect can be stacked.
** If Isaac has fewer than 5 coins, nothing happens.
* Grants 5 pennies upon being picked up for the first time.
sections.Notes:
* Using the item will give Isaac's tears a golden tint that becomes more noticeable with each use, up to a maximum of three times. This effect is purely cosmetic.
* When unlocking the item, coins do not actually have to be spent, just removed. Actions such as donating to a {{e|Donation Machine}} or items like {{i|Magic Fingers}} will also count as long as the coin amount goes from 99 to 0.
** Similarly, losing coins by getting damaged by {{e|Greed}} or similar enemies counts as spending coins when it comes to unlocking Golden Razor.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, converts one Red [[Heart Container]] into three {{e|Soul Heart}}s.
* {{transformation contribution|Guppy}}
sections.Notes:
* {{e|Bone Heart}}s cannot be converted.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Guppy's Paw's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Belial synergy|description=Grants a permanent 0.5 damage up for every converted heart.}}
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns 3 wisps in the middle ring for every Red Heart Container consumed, in addition to granting Soul Hearts. These wisps have a large amount of health.}}
* {{t|Broken Remote|nr}}: The teleport will activate whenever Guppy's Paw is used, even if Isaac has no Red Heart Containers to trade. This can give any characters with no Red Hearts the ability to teleport any number of times for free.
* {{i|Converter}}:
** {{dlc|nr}} Allows Isaac to attain up to 10 Red Heart Containers and 1 Soul Heart.
** {{dlc|r}} Allows Isaac to attain up to 12 Red Heart Containers or any combination of Red Heart Containers and Soul Hearts.
*** + {{i|Potato Peeler|r}} + {{i|Sharp Plug|r}}: Allows Isaac to generate infinite damage upgrades and {{i|Cube of Meat||Cubes of Meat}}.
* {{c|Tainted Eden}}: Soul Hearts granted by Guppy's Paw are not rerolled when Tainted Eden takes damage.
* {{I|Dead Cat}}: In addition to contributing to the transformation, converting the Red Heart Container obtained after revival into three Soul Hearts effectively triples Isaac's HP.
sections.Interactions:
* {{c|Bethany}}: Guppy's Paw will remove one Heart Container in exchange for Soul Heart charges. This will kill Bethany if she has no health left afterward.
* {{I|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{c|Keeper}}: Guppy's Paw will take away one Coin Heart, but will only grant [[Blue Fly|Blue Flies]] in return.
* {{p|XI - Strength}}: Converts the temporary Red Heart Container into three Soul Hearts (however, Isaac will still lose one Red Heart Container upon leaving the room if he has any left).

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, fires a powerful {{i|Brimstone}} beam in the four cardinal directions, similar to that of the attack used by {{e|The Fallen}} and {{e|Krampus}}.
** {{dlc|ana+}} Has a 50% chance to rotate all beams around Isaac 90 degrees, similar to Krampus' second Brimstone attack.
sections.Notes:
* Head of Krampus is one of two items that can drop by defeating {{e|Krampus}}. The other one is {{i|A Lump of Coal}}.
** This is the only way to get this item normally.
* {{dlc|nr}} Each beam deals 22 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 440 damage per use.
* {{dlc|r}} Each beam deals 10 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 200 damage per use.
* Damaging enemies with the effect of this item as {{tf|Guppy}} will spawn multiple [[Blue Fly|Blue Flies]].
* By standing really close to large enemies such as bosses, it's possible to hit them with multiple beams at once, dealing significantly more damage than a single beam.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns red wisps in the middle ring. The wisps fire small {{I|Brimstone}} lasers in the cardinal directions when destroyed. The lasers deal the wisps' tear damage per tick, and can hit up to 20 times. {{I|BFFS!}} will not increase this damage, despite it scaling with the wisps' tear damage.}}
* {{i|Car Battery}}: Doubles the damage the brimstone beams deal, but not their durations.
** {{dlc|nr}} Each beam now deals 44 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 880 damage per use.
** {{dlc|r}} Each beam now deals 20 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 400 damage per use.

sections.Effects: * Sets the [[Devil Room#Conditions to make Devil Rooms appear|Devil Room chance]] to 100% regardless of all other modifiers, guaranteeing a {{R|Devil Room}} or {{R|Angel Room}} Door will spawn whenever possible and remain open.
sections.Synergies:
* {{T|Black Feather}}: Grants a damage boost.
* {{i|Duality}}: Both Angel and Devil Room doors spawn after every boss, and the selected door will never disappear.
* {{i|Act of Contrition}}: Splits the chance between Angel and Devil Rooms. Items such as {{i|Key Piece 1}} can favor one or the other.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Eucharist}}: Overrides Goat Head.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] who follows Isaac around and fires icicles once every 0.75 seconds that each do 3.5 damage and have a chance to [[petrify]] enemies they hit and [[freeze]] enemies they kill.
** Frozen enemies will block enemy shots, and will slide away when walked into by Isaac.
*** After colliding with an obstacle or getting sufficiently shot by Isaac, frozen enemies will explode into a ring of 10 ice tears that can [[slow]] and [[freeze]].
* {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}
sections.Notes:
* [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Freezer Baby having {{dlcalt|5th|r+=7th}} priority.
* If a non-boss enemy dies within 10 ticks (0.33 seconds) after being hit by a freezing tear, it will be frozen regardless of what killed it.
sections.Synergies: * {{I|Mongo Baby}}: Will copy Freezer Baby’s tears.

sections.Effects:
* Adds a 5% chance to shoot [[Status Effects#Effects|concussive tears]], causing enemies to walk around randomly.
** The confusion caused by Glaucoma tears is effectively permanent for normal enemies, and a very long duration compared to most status effects for bosses.
* Makes the screen darker.
sections.Notes: * Not affected by Luck.

sections.Effects:
* Grants +0.25 [[damage]] for every [[Health#Broken Hearts|broken heart]] Isaac has.
* Immediately grants 3 broken hearts.
** Every otherwise fatal hit will add 2 more, replacing other types of hearts if necessary, and activates {{i|The Necronomicon}}'s effect, dealing 40 damage to all enemies in the room.
** Once Isaac has no non-broken hearts left, he dies. Extra lives will apply at this point.
sections.Notes:
* At the maximum of 11 broken hearts, Isaac gains a total of +2.75 damage.
* The effect does not save Isaac from fatal [[Devil deal]]s.
**However, while taking an item that costs heart/s and will result in death, if Isaac takes any damage, it will leave him on half a blue heart with taken item and will add 2 broken hearts.
sections.Synergies:
* {{t|A Missing Page|r}} / {{I|Missing Page 2|r}}: Deals an additional +40 damage when Isaac dies. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.
* {{t|Found Soul}}: The ghost gains 2 extra hits per floor, and every hit they take will damage all enemies in a room as well.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Damocles}}: Heartbreak does not protect Isaac from Damocles. * {{c|Keeper}}: Keeper will gain 1 broken heart instead of 3. Taking fatal damage will only grant Keeper 1 broken heart. * {{C|Magdalene}} + {{I|Birthright}}: Can hold up to 17 broken hearts, totaling +4.25 damage instead. * {{i|Plan C}} / {{p|Suicide King}}: Heartbreak does not protect Isaac from these effects. * {{c|Tainted Eden}} / {{c|Tainted Isaac}}: The starting broken hearts are removed when Heartbreak is rerolled/dropped. However, any broken hearts gained from lethal damage will persist. * {{C|Tainted Jacob}}: This effect will save Tainted Jacob while he is in his Lost form, adding two broken hearts to his regular health. * {{C|Tainted Keeper}}: Tainted Keeper will gain 1 broken heart instead of 3. Taking any damage will kill him, as he will then have 2 broken hearts. ** {{t|Mother's Kiss}} can mitigate this as it gives Tainted Keeper an extra coin heart. * {{c|The Lost}} / {{c|Tainted Lost}}: The Lost has full benefit of the item. This lets him survive 4 extra hits, each hit adding 1 damage, and the 5th is fatal. ** Tainted Lost can't normally obtain it, as it doesn't have the offensive item tag. ** '''The Lost''' / '''Tainted Lost''' + {{i|Magic Skin}} / {{p|VI - The Lovers?}}: No broken hearts are added by the item/card, thus having no effect on Heartbreak.

sections.Effects:
* On use, spawns a random [[friendly]] monster that mimics Isaac's movements and attacks, similar to {{C|Jacob and Esau}}.
* Friendly monsters can take damage from flames, spikes, and other hazards.
sections.Interactions:
* [[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Monsters spawned by Friend Finder are still affected by Ace Cards.
* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: Either angry version of Blood Puppy will target friendly enemies as well and can drag them along with it when it charges them. Blood Puppy cannot damage friendly enemies however friendly enemies can damage Blood Puppy despite not targeting it outright.
* {{i|Broken Modem}}: Broken Modem also affects friendly enemies and projectiles created by them.
* {{I|Eraser}}: If Friend Finder attempts to spawn an erased monster it will simply fail and waste the charge, instead of choosing a different monster.
* {{I|Ghost Bombs}} / {{i|Hungry Soul}} / {{I|Purgatory}} / {{i|Vade Retro}}: Explosions from ghosts can kill friendly enemies.
* {{I|Saturnus}}: Bullets fired from friendly enemies can still get caught in the orbit.
* {{I|The Soul}}: Projectiles shot from charmed monsters will be repelled by the aura.
* {{t|Tick}}: [[Friendly]] enemies start with less health if they have 60HP or more.

sections.Effects:
* Tears now have a {{dlc|nr+}} 10% / {{dlc|r+}} 20% chance to apply a [[Status Effects#Effects|shrinking]] effect, causing enemies to shrink in size and also run away from Isaac.
** Shrunk enemies can be crushed and killed by walking over them.
** {{dlc|r}} Enemies that spawn from the death of a shrunken enemy will also be shrunken upon spawning. {{dlc|r+}} Enemies that release projectiles, explosions or other effects such as {{e|Soul Sucker}}s no longer perform their effect when killed while shrunken.
* The shrinking effect lasts 5 seconds {{dlc|r+}} and enemies will flash white when the effect is about to end.
* {{transformation contribution|Fun Guy}}
sections.Notes:
* The shrinking effect does not affect bosses or mini-bosses.
* {{dlc|nr+}} [[Champion]]s and enemies that explode upon death will damage Isaac if crushed.
* Shrinking the heart of a {{E|Mask + Heart}} will cause its corresponding Mask to shrink as well. The Mask can be crushed and killed separately.
* The chance to fire a shrinking tear does not scale with [[Luck]].
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Compound Fracture}} / {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Split tears will retain shrinking effect if main tear had shrinking effect. With Compound Fracture and The Parasite, tears with a shrinking effect look like normal tears.
* {{i|Finger!}}: Finger can also apply the shrinking effect.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Will occasionally fire tears with shrinking effect. All burst tears have a chance to apply the shrinking effect.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Tear flickers blue, capable of shrinking enemies when it does.
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: Electricity connected to tears with shrinking effect has a chance to shrink enemies.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: If an angry Blood Puppy is shot with a God's Flesh tear, Isaac can instantly change it back to a tamed Blood Puppy by touching it.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Only main tear has a chance to apply a shrinking effect.
* {{I|Brimstone}} / {{C|Azazel}}: Brimstone laser becomes blue.

sections.Notes:
* {{Dlc|a+nr}} The chance of spawning fires is not affected by [[luck]].
* {{dlc|r}} The chance to shoot fires depends on the [[luck]] stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\min(\frac1 { 12 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor},50\%)</math>
** At base luck (0), the chance is 8.33%, maxing out at 50% at 10 luck.
* The fire can destroy {{E|Shopkeeper}}s.
* {{dlc|nr}}Enemies with fire variants will change to their flaming variants when they get hit with the flame.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Bird's Eye}}: Changes the activation rate to <math>\frac1 { 8 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}</math>
** At base luck (0), the chance is 12.5%, maxing out at 100% at 7 luck. Only one type of fire can be spawned at a time; however, each flame has an equal chance of being launched.
* {{i|Brimstone|nr}}: The flames can still shoot from Isaac while holding the fire button.
** {{dlc|r}} Occasionally emits a flame while the beam is firing.
* {{i|Butter Bean}}, {{i|Mega Bean}}, {{i|The Black Bean}}, {{i|Wait What?}}: Will spawn fires upon use/activation.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Fires can be spawned while firing bombs.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Fires can be spawned while moving the crosshair.
* {{I|Farting Baby|dlc=r}}: The familiar has a chance to spawn a flame upon farting.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Fires are spawned as normal and can be hit by Ipecac tears, making this especially dangerous with a multi-shot ability.
* {{i|Mom's Knife|nr}}: The flames can still shoot from Isaac while holding the fire button.
** {{dlc|r}}Occasionally spawns a fire when thrown.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung|nr}}: The flames can still be shot from Isaac while holding the fire button.
** {{dlc|r}}Occasionally fires a barrage of flames along with the blast. The trajectory of the flames is unaffected, making them stack on top of each other.
* {{i|The Poop}}: Fire will appear behind Isaac.
* {{I|Pupula Duplex|r}}: The fires gain a large size and duration increase.
* {{i|Technology}}/{{i|Tech X}}: Will occasionally spawn a fire while firing lasers. The lasers will not douse the flames.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Will occasionally spawn a fire while firing beams. {{dlc|nr}}Fires' damage is not reduced.
* {{i|Urn of Souls}}: Causes the Urn to emit Ghost Pepper's flames in addition to its regular flames.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|20/20}}/{{i|The Inner Eye}}/{{i|Mutant Spider}}: Will only spawn one fire.
* {{i|Anti-Gravity|nr}}: When holding down the fire button, when the fire spawns, it will be almost immediately put out by the clumps of tears.
* {{i|Blood Clot}}: No effect.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}/{{i|Cricket's Body}}/{{i|The Parasite}}: Fires cannot split.
* {{i|Ghost Pepper}}: No effect. Extra copies will not boost the chances of shooting out a fire like with Bird's Eye.
* [[Homing tears]]: Flames will not be homing.
* {{I|IBS}}: '''Not recommended.''' IBS can trigger farts that automatically release a flame, which detonate the toxic cloud left behind and hurt Isaac, unless he has explosion immunity. While less of a risk than Bird's Eye, the flames spawned by Ghost Pepper can detonate stinky poops held by Isaac when IBS activates.
* {{i|Contagion}}: Has a chance to make Isaac shoot a fire in a random direction after killing an enemy affected by Contagion.
* Tear-copying [[Familiar]]s like {{i|Incubus}}/{{T|Lil Clot}}/{{i|Evil Eye}}: Any fires that would be spawned from the familiars will be shot from Isaac instead.
* {{i|Lachryphagy|nr}}: Feeding tears will quickly douse the flames.
* {{c|Lilith|r}}: Spawns fire from her mouth.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique|nr}}: Fires created from Ghost Pepper will destroy the tear and cause it to respawn on Isaac.
** {{dlc|r}} Isaac now periodically creates fires that shoot towards the Ludovico Technique tear.
* {{i|A Lump of Coal}}: No effect.
* {{i|Pop!|nr}}: Eyeball tears quickly douse flames.
* {{i|Proptosis|nr}}: Flames will not lose damage or shrink as they travel.
** {{dlc|r}} Flame damage is tripled at base, follows Ghost Pepper's damage decay formula instead of the one from Proptosis.
* {{i|Soy Milk|nr}}: No effect on frequency or damage of flames.
* {{i|Sprinkler}}: The sprinkler will not spawn flames.
* {{i|Jupiter}}: No effect.

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|nr}} Spawns a [[familiar]] that bounces diagonally around the [[Rooms|room]], deals 8 damage per tick or 120 damage per second and applies a random [[Status Effects|status effect]] to enemies it comes in contact with. The familiar also has a chance to re-roll [[pickups]] that it passes over into other pickups, {{E|Chest}}s, or [[items]], in an uncleared room only (with at least one enemy alive).
* {{dlc|r}} Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac. Double tapping the fire button launches it forward, causing it to reroll the first [[monster]], [[Trinkets|trinket]], or [[pickup]] it hits. It respawns after clearing a room.
** If it cannot reroll an enemy (e.g. a boss), it will deal 8 damage instead.
** Items and opened chests cannot be rerolled.
** Pickups have a 10% chance of becoming chests (see [[#Algorithm|the algorithm]]).
*** If a chest is rerolled, it has a 28% chance of staying as some kind of a chest.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} GB Bug can block projectiles.
* {{dlc|nr}} GB Bug does more damage per second than {{i|The Peeper}}, with the added random status chance.
* {{dlc|r}} GB Bug is able to reroll {{e|Throwable Bomb|n}}s into normal consumables. After doing so, the corresponding {{e|Bomb Grimace|n}} will generate another Throwable Bomb, making it able to generate a potentially large amount of free consumables.
* {{dlc|r}} Rerolled [[champion]] enemies will retain their color, unless they reroll into a monster that cannot naturally spawn as a champion.
* {{dlc+|r}} Caution is advised as GB Bug can also reroll certain entities such as the hot rock left by a dead {{e|Coal Spider}} adding another enemy to the room.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with GB Bug having {{dlc|nr+}} 5th / {{dlc|r+}} 7th priority.
* {{dlc|r}} While playing {{c|Tainted Isaac|n}}, GB bug can be dropped and picked back up to respawn it, allowing for infinite rerolls.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Blood Puppy}}: Hitting Blood Puppy with GB Bug will transform it into a random enemy and spawn a tamed Blood Puppy.
* {{I|Guppy's Eye}} in {{S|Chest}} / {{S|Dark Room}}: Using the 28% chance to stay as a chest, allows you to reroll chests with undesired items into different items.
* {{I|King Baby|r}}: GB Bug will only throw itself at nearby enemies automatically if a fire button is double tapped while King Baby's effect is active.
* {{I|Marked|r}}: Does not launch itself automatically or at the crosshair while Isaac is firing.
* {{T|The Twins}}: The familiar can be duplicated even if it hasn’t respawned; by constantly moving to new rooms, GB Bug can constantly respawn, allowing pickups to be rerolled indefinitely.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] that follows Isaac around, leaving a trail of [[red creep]] that damages enemies.
** The creep deals 2 damage per tick or 6 damage per second to non-flying enemies.
** {{Dlc|r}} The creep deals damage much more rapidly at 20 damage per second.
* {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}
sections.Notes: * {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Headless Baby having the lowest priority at {{dlc|nr+}} 6th / {{dlc|r+}} 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.
sections.Synergies: * {{t|Lost Cork}}: Creep trail size is bigger.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|BFFS!}}: Familiar is bigger; however, no effect on creep damage.

sections.Effects:
* New item pedestals cycle very quickly between 5 random items.
** The 5 items will cycle in the same order every loop.
** Items are rerolled at a rate of once every 0.2 seconds.
sections.Notes:
* Plot-related items (i.e {{i|The Polaroid}}/{{i|The Negative}}, {{i|Broken Shovel 1}}/{{i|Broken Shovel 2}}, {{i|Knife Piece 1}}/{{i|Knife Piece 2}},{{i|Key Piece 1}},{{i|Key Piece 2}} etc.) are unaffected by Glitched Crown.
* One of the items will be the initial one spawned/rerolled, while the other four will be from the [[item pool]] of the room the item is in.
* {{dlc|nr+}} Items spawned from {{E|Chest||chests}} normally have a small delay between when they spawn and when Isaac can pick them up; if Isaac has Glitched Crown, this delay is removed and he can pick up the item the moment it spawns, effectively forcing him to get a random item.
** Chests have to be lightly tapped and immediately walked away from to avoid accidentally picking up the item so Glitched Crown can be used properly.
* {{c|Isaac}}'s {{i|Birthright}} effect and {{c|Tainted Isaac}}'s inherent ability are overridden by this effect.
* All five options will have their weight decremented on sight like usual.
* A good strategy to get a specific item is to remember the one that comes before it in the cycle. Stand as close to the pedestal as possible and move towards the pedestal when the item that comes before the desired one appears.
** {{dlc|nr+}} Pausing the game between each roll can make this substantially easier.
*** {{dlc|r+}} Pausing the game does not pause the rotation of items. Instead, its cycling speed increases to one per frame, returning to normal once the game is unpaused.
* Due to Glitched Crown's indiscriminate cycling of items, anything that turns item pedestals into blind item pedestals, such as Curse of the Blind, or traveling to a floor that offers blind items such as {{s|Downpour}}, renders Glitched Crown's effect useless or even detrimental, as there is a chance of missing out on desirable items permanently among the blind choices.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Spindown Dice}}: Rerolling a cycling item will reduce the ID number of the displayed item by 1 and randomize the other 4 options.
** This allows {{i|Spindown Dice}} to mimic {{i|The D6}}'s rerolling effect on 4/5 of Glitched crown's displayed items.
* {{i|The D6}}: All 5 items will be re-rolled.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Binge Eater}}: Adds a random food item to the cycle, for a total of 6 items on the cycling pedestal. Only the pedestals generated after picking up Binge Eater will be affected.
* {{i|Damocles}}: Extra item pedestals do not reroll.
* {{i|Diplopia}}: The items on-screen at the moment of activation will be duplicated, but the pedestal will also cycle through four new items.
* {{i|Genesis}}: If Glitched Crown is picked up during the item sequence, the effect will start on the second item after grabbing Glitched Crown.
* {{p|0 - The Fool?}}: Items spawned using the card such as {{I|Boom!}} will not generate a cycling pedestal.

sections.Effects:
* Once thrown, the Friendly Ball will instantly capture any [[monster|non-boss enemy]] it hits, removing them from the room.
* {{dlc|r}} Walking over a Friendly Ball after it captures an enemy will instantly recharge the item.
* The next time the Friendly Ball is thrown, it will release the previously captured enemy as a [[friendly]] enemy.
** Released enemies persist between rooms and floors and will follow Isaac until they die.
** Friendly enemies cannot harm Isaac and do not need to be defeated to clear a room.
** If Isaac leaves the room before the monster is released, the monster will stay in the ball until it is thrown again.
* If the Friendly Ball does not capture an enemy, it will simply disappear after a couple seconds being on the ground. The next throw will work the same.
sections.Notes:
* All enemies that aren't invincible and are not designated as a boss or mini-boss can be captured by the Friendly Ball. This includes enemies summoned from bosses such as {{E|Brownie}}'s spawned {{E|Dip}}s or {{E|The Cage}}'s unique {{E|Vis}}es.
** {{dlc+|a+nr}} One exception to this is if you capture a {{E|Portal}}, as it can spawn enemies such as {{E|Death's Head}}.{{dlc-}}
* It is generally wasteful to use this item on {{E|Mulligan}}s and their variants as they will immediately rush towards enemies and try to kill themselves, leaving behind friendly debris.
* If the captured enemy is a {{E|Globin}} variant (besides {{E|Black Globin}}s for their lack of regenerative abilities) or a [[Champion|Dark Red Champion]], the enemy will regenerate after dying, granting a much longer lifespan.
* {{E|Wall Creep}}s and their variants stick to walls, backing far away from any potential danger they might encounter.
* Stationary enemies that move underground (such as {{E|Round Worm}}s or {{E|Lump}}s) work surprisingly well as an ally as they shoot foes from far away and rarely ever get hurt.
* {{E|Mom's Hand}} and {{E|Mom's Dead Hand}} will both one-shot almost all normal enemies and greatly damage most bosses with an incredibly small window for the hands to be hit, making them ideal for capturing.
* Brimstone-capable enemies are very potent as their lasers can cause an obscene amount of damage to both enemies and most bosses.
* If the captured enemy is one that spawns enemies, those enemies will be friendly as well.
* If the ally is immune to damage (such as a {{E|Mobile Host}} while its head is lowered), it will not take contact damage.
* If the captured enemy is a [[Champion|Solid White Champion]], it will be completely invincible, as it cannot be killed until the room counts as being cleared, at which point it can be killed by [[spikes]] or a {{E|Wall Hugger}}.
* {{dlc|a+}} If the captured enemy is a [[Champion|Pulsing Red Champion]], it will regenerate the health of other monsters in the room, including friendly ones.
* {{dlc|na+}} If an enemy that leaves behind a trail of damaging [[creep]] is caught, the creep created by the friendly mob will still damage Isaac when he walks over it.
** {{dlc|a+}} All creep created by a friendly enemy will only hurt grounded enemies and not the player.
* The ball will only capture one segment of a {{E|Grub}}, one {{E|Buttlicker}}, or one {{E|Swarm|text=Swarm Fly}}. However, when releasing a Swarm Fly, a new swarm is generated for it.
* If a {{E|Mask + Heart}}'s Heart is caught and then released, a Mask can use the friendly heart to live even if its original heart is destroyed. The room will not be cleared unless the Mask is killed.
** The mask will ignore the friendly heart yet can still damage it. Bait the mask to charge towards the heart to destroy both.
* Friendly enemies that produce explosions do not damage Isaac. This includes enemies that explode on death (such as {{E|Boom Fly|text=Boom Flies}}), as well as enemies that create Ipecac explosions (such as {{E|Gurgle}}s).
** On top of that, lit bombs from friendly {{E|Mulligoon}}s, {{E|Fly Bomb|n}}s, and even {{E|Bombgagger|n}}s cannot hurt Isaac.
* The head of {{E|Rag Man}} can be captured by the ball while detached. It will not become a Ragling after being released, and only chases enemies by rolling.
* {{dlc+|r}} Captured {{E|Bishop}}s will protect Isaac with their shield generation ability, as well as all other friendly enemies. Isaac cannot take any damage while the Bishop is alive, as it will protect him with the shield. Protecting the Bishop can be a powerful defensive tool, especially when playing as {{C|The Lost}}.
** The {{e|Bishop}} will die after protecting Isaac 6 times.
** The shield does not protect against instant death effects such as {{p|Suicide King}} or {{i|Plan C}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} Captured {{E|Cultist}}s will revive killed enemies as friendlies, allowing one to slowly amass an army of friendlies by protecting the Cultist.
** Bosses and degraded bosses can be revived by a friendly Cultist, but will not persist between rooms.{{dlc-}}
* Enemies that are spawned by a captured enemy (such as {{E|Dip}}s spawned by a {{E|Dinga}}) will persist between rooms as well.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|The Battery|r}}: Walking over a captured enemy will double charge the ball. This allows Isaac the ability to release a captured enemy and catch a new one in the same room double charging the ball to release and capture more enemies. Attempting to catch a new enemy while the old one is in the process of spawning will result in the ball phasing through the new enemy and wasting the charge.
* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: Using the ball on an angered Blood Puppy will instantly tame it. Using the ball again results in a purely cosmetic blood explosion.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a wisp, all on the middle ring, whenever a [[friendly]] enemy dies. Depending on the enemy that dies, the wisp may have a different effect:
** Normal: Enemies captured by Friendly Ball spawn this wisp when they die if they wouldn't spawn any of the other variants listed below.
** Homing: Enemies captured by Friendly Ball spawn this wisp when they die if they were psychic or had homing shots in some way. Wisps' tears are [[homing]].
** Explosive: Enemies captured by Friendly Ball spawn this wisp when they die if they created explosions in some way. Wisps' tears have a 33% chance to explode. Explosive tears deal no extra damage.
** Brimstone: Enemies captured by Friendly Ball spawn this wisp when they die if they fired lasers in some way. Wisps fire {{I|Brimstone}} lasers. The laser does not need to be charged to be fired, and can tick up to 8 times for a total of 20 damage.}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Friendly monsters are still affected by Ace Cards.
* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: Either angry version of Blood Puppy will target friendly enemies as well and can drag them along with it when it charges them. Blood Puppy cannot damage friendly enemies however friendly enemies can damage Blood Puppy despite not targeting it outright.
* {{i|Broken Modem}}: Broken Modem also affects friendly enemies and projectiles created by them.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{i|Eraser}}: If the ball captures an enemy and then another enemy of the same type is erased the next use of Friendly Ball will release a puff of pink smoke wasting the effect.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{I|Ghost Bombs}} / {{i|Hungry Soul}} / {{I|Purgatory}} / {{i|Vade Retro}}: Explosions from ghosts can kill friendly enemies.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Hive Mind}}: No effect on captured flies or spiders.
* {{i|Skatole}} or {{i|Bursting Sack}}: Friendly Fly/Spider enemies will be unable to shoot, slowed down, and/or reverted to a weaker form, hindering this item's effectiveness on those enemies.
* {{t|Tick}}: [[Friendly]] enemies start with less health if they have 60HP or higher.
* {{i|Void|r}}: Walking over a thrown Friendly Ball that captured an enemy will not recharge Void.
* {{i|Glowing Hourglass}}: Will duplicate friendly enemies if used in the same room multiple times.

sections.Effects:
* After standing still and not pressing the move or attack buttons for one second, Isaac will turn into an [[invulnerability|invulnerable]] statue.
** Using bombs and active items will remove the invincibility state.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|7 Seals}}: One of the more versatile familiars that works with Gnawed Leaf.  The varied forms and attacks of this familiar make it capable of clearing pretty much any room given time.  The locusts it produces often fly to Isaac which takes care of chasing enemies, but its damaging creep and chasing attacks can reach even the farthest enemies.
* {{I|120 Volt}}: With enough damage, 120 Volt's zaps becomes far more efficient at killing than orbitals.
** At 15 damage minimum, it surpasses most orbitals.
** At 30 damage or more, it surpasses {{I|Sacrificial Dagger}}.
* {{I|Angry Fly}}: Aggressively attacks enemies even if they're far away, but can end up harmlessly orbiting slow or stationary enemies indefinitely, or trying to attack invulnerable enemies.  It does better with slow or stationary bosses than regular enemies, diving in to attack periodically instead of harmlessly orbiting.
* {{i|Daddy Longlegs}}: Allows Isaac to easily clear most rooms or bosses while in statue form. Daddy Longlegs cannot damage bosses like {{E|The Shell}} and won't target enemies that are a long distance from Isaac. In a pinch, {{T|Mom's Toenail}} works the same, albeit much slower.
* {{I|Damocles}}: If Isaac is in statue form when the sword falls, he will survive.
* {{I|Dark Arts}}: While Isaac is surrounded by enemies, he will not take damage and will safely go into the shadow state. (Even if enemies are in pointblank range.)
* {{I|Decap Attack}}: The head can be used on stationary bosses to wither them down.
* {{i|E. Coli}} /{{i|Midas' Touch}} /{{I|Serpent's Kiss}} / {{i|The Virus}}: Monsters touching the statue will be affected without Isaac taking collision damage.
* {{I|Empty Vessel}}: if Empty Vessel's requirement is fulfilled, Isaac can safely wait for the shield to activate, allowing to deal damage without leaving invulnerability.
* {{I|IBS}}: Orbitals and other things (such as 120 Volt) can trigger IBS while in statue form, however, Isaac will still be invincible. This can be really good if a Stinky Poop is held above his head.
* {{i|Kamikaze!}}: Statue form will break, but the initial explosion will not damage Isaac, therefore granting Isaac quasi-unlimited bombs.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: The hovering tear will still deal damage and the statue form won't break as long as the attack buttons aren't being pressed.
** '''The Ludovico Technique''' + {{i|Strange Attractor}}: Can pull enemies in while remaining a statue, clearing out rooms easily.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The knife can damage enemies while Isaac is a statue.
* {{Dlc|r}}{{I|Mom's Heels}}: While invincible, Isaac can still deal contact damage.
* {{I|Monstrance}}: The aura makes quick work of chasing enemies.
* {{i|The Pinking Shears}}: Isaac's body will attack enemies while his head is invincible.
* {{i|Placenta}}: Isaac can safely regenerate Red Hearts in any room, making it easy to have enough health from any mistake at the cost of time.
* {{i|Robo-Baby 2.0}}: Since it fires automatically, this familiar is one of the more effective synergies, since it will even shoot off screen as it’s knocked around.
* {{I|Salvation}}: The aura can trigger from nearby enemies while Isaac is safely a statue, and the damaging beams when this happens can reach farther enemies.  This powerful attack can make quick work of bosses that chase Isaac.
* {{I|Spin to Win}}: Gnawed Leaf will activate while using Spin to Win, as long as Isaac is stationary. This allows for a brief moment of high damage against enemies that chase Isaac.
* {{i|Sprinkler}}: Can be placed upon entering a room, and will continue to fire when Isaac is invincible, meaning any room can be cleared without the risk of Isaac taking damage. This theoretically allows end-game bosses to be beaten without having to move.
* {{t|Super Magnet}}: Pulls enemies into Isaac, can be extremely powerful if combined with orbitals that allow contact damage.
* {{dlc|r}}{{C|Tainted Magdalene|n}}: Tainted Magdalene's "Hug" attack still triggers when in the statue state without taking damage, making short work of aggressive enemies as well as providing lots of healing.
* {{dlc|r}}{{C|Tainted Forgotten|n}}: The Soul is invincible as long as the bone club is not used and The Forgotten is not thrown, even if The Soul is holding The Forgotten and moving around.  Combined with orbitals that deal contact damage like {{I|Cube of Meat}} or items that can trigger damage only by movement such as {{I|Purgatory|n}}, can make for a trivial method to beat any boss.
* {{tf|Yes Mother?}}: When worst comes to worst and Isaac has no orbitals or familiars, the knife can be used to deal damage, due to how common the transformation is.
* {{i|Tooth and Nail}}: Allows one second to act and/or reposition without taking damage. Useful in situations such as ranged combat when enemies bombard from a distance, or to attack and move to a safe distance where Isaac can safely regain statue form.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|2Spooky}}: Counterintuitive and should be avoided, as most enemies will never approach orbital range.
* {{I|The Bible}}: Statue invulnerability will not prevent death when the Bible is activated during {{E|Satan}} fight.
* {{i|Blood Oath}}: Standing still at the start of a level will block Blood Oath's damage, preventing it from activating.
* {{i|Blood Rights}} / {{i|IV Bag}} / {{i|Razor Blade}}: Statue invulnerability will not prevent damage from these items when activated.
* {{I|Book of Virtues}} / {{I|Lemegeton}}: Wisps are invincible while invulnerable.
* {{c|Jacob and Esau}}: If Esau picks up the item, he can remain invulnerable even when Jacob is moving but not when firing.
* {{c| Tainted Jacob}} / {{c|Jacob and Esau}}: If Tainted Jacob/Esau picks up the item, Tainted Esau/Jacob will be able to push a character into a {{R|Curse Room}} without taking damage.
* {{i|The Gamekid}} / {{i|My Little Unicorn}} / {{i|Unicorn Stump}}: Statue form can activate while invulnerable.
* {{T|Short Fuse}}: Bombs explode before invincibility kicks in.

sections.Effects:
* +0.5 [[Damage]].
* -0.3 [[Tears]].
* -0.3 [[Shot Speed]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +1.2 [[Range]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +0.8 [[Tear Falling Speed]].
* Grants [[homing tears]].
* Tears gain a damaging aura.
** {{dlc|nr}} The aura deals 30% of Isaac's damage 15 times per second.
** {{dlc|r}} The aura deals 2 damage 30 times per second.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} Godhead is a [[special item]].
* The hitbox of the aura is increased with the size of Isaac's tears.
* This item can be crafted from {{i|Bag of Crafting}} with a {{e|Red Heart}}, {{e|Soul Heart}}, {{e|Gold Heart}}, and five {{e|Eternal Heart}}s.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: Creates a Godhead aura around the head and applies homing effect when thrown.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}/{{i|Cricket's Body}}/{{i|The Parasite}}: Main tears and burst tears retain all effects.
* {{i|Explosivo}}/{{i|Mucormycosis}}: Causes damaging aura to grow once attached to an enemy.
* {{i|Euthanasia|a+nr}}: The aura of a needle tear will also do triple damage, but does not cause tear burst or instant kill.
* {{i|Glass Cannon}}: The huge tear gains the homing ability and a much larger, more powerful damaging aura.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Fired tears and burst tears retain aura and homing effect.
** [[Piercing tears]]: When a tear bursts, the 8 smaller tears' auras can stack, doing massive damage to enemies within.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Tear increases in size and gains the damaging aura effect.
** {{dlc|r}} Tear also gains homing effect. May cause the tear to get stuck near enemies.
* {{i|A Lump of Coal|nr}}: The size and damage of the aura increases as long as the tear is on screen.
** {{dlc|r}} Only the size of the aura increases.
* {{T|Pulse Worm}}: The aura increases and decreases in size.
* {{i|Saturnus}}: The orbiting tears also have the damaging aura, but without the homing effect.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Bombs retain the homing effect, but don't receive a damaging aura.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: The crosshair homes in upon enemies, but neither the crosshair nor the missiles receive the damaging aura.
* {{i|Gello}} / {{c|Tainted Lilith}}: The cosmetic change also is applied to Gello.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Main tear retains all effects, but burst tears do not.
** {{dlc|r}} Burst tears also retain all effects.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: Knife retains the homing effect, but doesn't get the damaging aura.
* [[Piercing tears]]: Once the tear hits the enemy, the aura also ceases to do damage to that particular target.
** {{dlc|r}} Enemies can be damaged by the aura after being pierced, but only if the tear is no longer in contact.
* {{i|Sinus Infection}}: The aura on booger tears stuck to an enemy won't hurt that particular enemy, but still damages other enemies.
* {{i|Technology}}/{{i|Technology 2}}/{{i|Tech.5}}/{{i|Tech X}}/{{i|Brimstone}}/{{i|Revelation}}: Lasers retain the homing effect, but don't receive the damaging aura.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Causes Godhead's aura to visually disappear; however, the aura is still there and can still damage enemies.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns 2-4 friendly [[Blue Fly|Blue Flies]].
* {{transformation contribution|Guppy}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Summons wisps in the outer ring instead of flies. Wisps summon Blue Flies when destroyed. One wisp contains one Blue Fly.}}
* {{i|Car Battery}}: Increases range of flies spawned to 4-8.
* {{T|Fish Tail}}: Doubles flies spawned.
* {{i|9 Volt}}: Guppy's Head slowly gains charge while in a hostile room.

sections.Effects:
* Gives Isaac 5 {{e|Bomb}}s.
* Isaac's bombs create ghosts when they explode, which rapidly chase and deal contact damage to enemies.
** The ghost deals contact damage equal to half of Isaac's [[damage]] per tick (2× Isaac's damage per second).
* After 10 seconds, the ghost explodes, dealing 7 damage to nearby enemies up to 3 times and destroying nearby projectiles. Isaac does not take damage from the explosion.
** If there are no enemies in the room, the ghost follows Isaac. However, it cannot follow Isaac between rooms.
sections.Notes: * [[Friendly]] enemies can be killed by the ghosts.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Has a chance to shoot a Ghost Bomb that also has spectral properties and can travel through objects.
* {{I|Scatter Bombs}}: Split bombs create ghosts that instantly launch themselves at enemies and explode, similar to {{i|Purgatory}}. They each deal 2× Isaac's damage, up to 4 times.
* {{I|Mr. Mega}}: Ghosts appear larger and do extra damage only upon exploding.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Doctor's Remote}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}: No effect.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: The ghosts get only +1 flat damage from Ipecac, not the expected +20.
* {{i|Libra}}: The ghosts ignore damage modification from Libra, both positive and negative: the actual unbalanced damage value is used.

sections.Effects: * Whenever Isaac takes damage, he summons a micro-Isaac [[familiar]], known as Minisaac, that chases nearby enemies and attacks on its own. ** Minisaacs deal 1.35 base damage that scales with +0.15 per floor: damage = 1.35 + 0.15 * (floor - 1) ** Minisaacs shoot 3 tears per second and their tear delay is not affected by Isaac's stats. ** Minisaacs persists between rooms and floors. ** Each Minisaac is spawned with 15 health points that are constantly drained with a rate of 0.4 per second. The draining stops when they reach 0.8 HP. *** They are healed back to full HP whenever Isaac takes damage, even when the familiars cap is reached. ** Enemies can damage Minisaacs by shooting projectiles at them or dealing contact damage. *** Isaac's bomb explosions will also damage the familiars. *** Minisaacs are immune to spikes and lasers.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Polycephalus}}.{{dlc-}}
* The familiar cap for Giant Cell is 16, after which taking damage will not spawn a new Minisaac.
* Minisaacs will change their skin color based on the character that they were spawned from.
** Certain items that change skin color can also affect the familiars' appearance.
* When playing as {{c|The Forgotten}}, the familiars take the style as either The Soul or The Forgotten, depending on who gets hit.
** If the familiar takes the style of The Forgotten, it will also inherit its bone club attack, dealing 8.1 base damage that scales with +0.9 per floor. It will swing its bone club 1.5 times per second. It can also interact with [[pickups]] using the bone club.
* Minisaacs for {{c|Tainted Forgotten}} will spawn from The Forgotten's body and inherit its skin color but they will shoot regular tears.
* Familiars spawned for {{c|Azazel}} or {{c|Tainted Azazel}} will not inherit the {{i|Brimstone}} laser and will fire regular tears.
* If Isaac has any form of flight, the Minisaacs will receive wings and will be able to fly as well.
** Minisaacs spawned before flight was acquired will not get upgraded, unless the flight is acquired by killing {{E|Dogma}} and starting {{E|The Beast}} fight in which case they will get upgraded.
** Minisaacs that acquire temporary flight (e.g. from {{i|The Bible}}) will remain permanently upgraded until they die, even after the effect of The Bible expires.
* If being hit makes Isaac become the {{i|Whore of Babylon}}, a Shadow-like Minisaac will spawn instead of a regular one.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Increases damage dealt by the familiars by 40%.
* {{i|Dull Razor}}: Provides a penalty-free way of spawning Minisaacs and/or healing existing ones.
* {{i|Glowing Hourglass}}: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room than the one he is currently in (such as the starting room of a new floor) will duplicate the Minisaacs. (This is possibly a bug)
* {{i|Sacrificial Altar}}: Converts all Minisaacs into 1 {{E|Penny}} each upon use.

sections.Effects:
* Isaac's tears become coins. Hitting an enemy with tears has a 5% chance to drop a {{e|Penny}} at the point of impact.
** The chance is not affected by [[Luck]].
sections.Notes:
* Head of the Keeper has a 1% chance to drop from destroying normal {{e|Shopkeeper}}s.
* {{Dlc+|r}} The only way of finding Head of the Keeper is from {{e|Shopkeeper}}s, using {{I|Spindown Dice}} on {{I|Papa Fly}}, as a starting item with {{c|Eden}}, or by using {{i|Death Certificate}}.{{dlc-}}
* Does not produce coins other than Pennies.
* Hitting the front side of enemies such as the {{E|Knight}} will still produce Pennies, even though the enemy does not take damage. This can be exploited to produce an infinite amount of Pennies from a single enemy. This however doesn't work with lowered {{E|Host}}s.
** Enemies that spawn other enemies, {{E|Globin}}s, or enemies that regain health can also be farmed for infinite money.
* {{Dlc|nr}} Head of the Keeper does not work with {{C|The Forgotten}} but will work with {{C|The Soul}}.
* When used against {{E|Ultra Greed}}, the coins are spawned directly in front of him and will heal him very often.
sections.Synergies:
* {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Brimstone}}/{{c|Azazel}}/{{c|Tainted Azazel}}/{{i|Tech X}}: The laser is yellow and each tick has a chance to drop a penny.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Every tear in the burst of tears can spawn coins.
* {{T|Nuh Uh!}}: From Chapter 4 and beyond, any coins spawned will be from the loot table of Nuh Uh! instead, with an occasional harmless black fly spawning.
* {{I|Sack Head}}: Coins spawned from hitting enemies have a chance to become sacks.
* {{i|Soy Milk}}: Due to the Soy Milk's high fire rate and low damage, enemies can be hit many more times than usual, resulting in a larger amount of coins dropping.
* {{dlc|r}} {{i|Technology}}: The laser is yellow and has a chance to drop a penny upon damaging an enemy.
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: Coin tears are connected via electricity. Beams of electricity can cause enemies to drop coins.
* {{i|Technology 2}}: Due to Technology 2's constant fire rate, enemies are hit many more times than usual, resulting in a higher likelihood of coins dropping.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Trisagion}}: Each tick that hits an enemy has a chance to spawn a penny.{{dlc-}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone|nr}}/{{C|Azazel}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper.
* {{i|Death's Touch}}: Tears retain Death's Touch's cosmetic effect but both items are fully active.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus|nr}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper.
* {{i|Epic Fetus|nr}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper.
* {{i|Euthanasia|nr}}: Main tears can cause enemies to drop Pennies; however, burst tears do not.
* {{i|Haemolacria|nr}}: Only the main tear retains the effect of Head of the Keeper.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Because Ipecac's high damage will quickly kill enemies, and because enemies will often be hit with explosions rather than tears themselves, Pennies will not drop as frequently.
* {{i|Mom's Knife|nr}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper.
** {{dlc|r}} Knife has a very low chance to drop coins.
* {{i|Sulfuric Acid}}: Tears retain Head of the Keeper's cosmetic effect but both items are fully active. Which tears are acidic can no longer be visually identified.
* {{i|Technology|nr}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper.
* {{i|Tech X|nr}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper.
* {{i|Trisagion|nr}}: Overrides Head of the Keeper. Coin debris will still appear after beams dissipate.

sections.Effect:
* On use, Isaac will be returned to the previous room and everything that happened in the current room will be undone.
** Health, bombs, coins, keys, cards / runes / pills, items, and trinkets, gained or lost, will be restored to their state before having entered the room.
** Time spent and score gained or lost within the room are reverted.
*** {{dlc|nr}} About one second will be spent during the animation after use.
** Most permanent unlocks will be reverted (see below).
* {{dlc|r}} Can only be used 3 times on each floor, after which it functions like {{i|The Hourglass}} until a new floor is entered.
sections.Notes:
* The Glowing Hourglass is very useful for finding out hidden information. For example:
** Every pill on the floor can be accumulated and used in the same room, the pills' effects can be noted and reverted if unwanted.
** Isaac can bomb walls with potential secret rooms, then go back in time if he fails to find one.
** If Isaac has {{cu|Blind}}, Glowing Hourglass can be used to pick up or purchase an unknown item to see what it is, then decide whether or not to undo picking it up.
** It can be even be used in extremely creative ways, such as using {{p|XXI - The World}} and screenshotting the map, then going back in time to get the card back.
* Does not affect the chance for a {{R|Devil Room}}, {{R|Angel Room}}, or a portal to {{s|The Void}} to spawn (it will not spawn if it didn’t initially).
* If used in a Devil Room or Angel Room, the door to it has its normal chance to close.
** If used on the {{R|Boss Rush}} after the time limit expires, the door will not remain open when sent back to the boss room.
* If Isaac goes into a Devil / Angel room, sees undesirable items, activates the Glowing Hourglass, and the Devil / Angel door doesn't stay open, then the game will think that Isaac missed the Devil / Angel deal on the floor, and will thus increase the chance of getting one on the next floor.
** However, if it's the first Devil Deal, and the door doesn't stay open, then you'll still get an Angel deal on the next floor.
*** By combining these two bugged interactions, Isaac can get a Devil Deal on Basement 2, bomb himself to reduce your deal chance to 1%, then go into the Devil Deal, and use the Glowing Hourglass. You then have a 100% Angel Deal chance on Caves 1.
* Finding the Glowing Hourglass in a room and using it to undo picking up Glowing Hourglass will preserve its charges, allowing for infinite resets for that room.
** This effect can also be achieved by replacing the Glowing Hourglass with a different active item, exiting the room, then re-entering and using the Glowing Hourglass.
** {{dlc|nr}} Doing this will remove the charges of the returned active item.
** {{dlc|nr}} If there is a Lil' Battery in a Shop, the Glowing Hourglass can be used infinitely, by entering the Shop without a charge and using the Lil' Battery to recharge and exit the shop. This is useful for duplicating temporary familiars or filling up the Donation Machine, among other uses.
* The delayed effect of the I'm Excited pill will still occur after rewinding.
* {{dlc|nr}} The Retro Vision [[Pill]] will continue to affect the game even after using the Glowing Hourglass.
* {{dlc|na+}} Does not turn a character back into another should they have been revived by {{i|Ankh}}, {{i|Lazarus' Rags}}, or {{i|Judas' Shadow}}.
** {{dlc|a+}} Character changes are reverted by Glowing Hourglass.
* {{dlc|nr}} Does not return keys or health used to enter [[Rooms#Special rooms|special rooms]].
** If a bomb is used to enter a Secret Room, the Secret Room is entered, and the Glowing Hourglass is used, the Secret Room door will stay open and the bomb will not be refunded.
* {{dlc|nr}} Does not return extra lives.
* {{dlc|nr}} Using any teleportation card and then the Glowing Hourglass to return to the previous room does not refund the used card.
** {{dlc|r}} Teleport cards like {{p|Joker}} can be refunded. However, if used on the first room on the floor, the Glowing Hourglass will be uncharged when returning.
* {{Dlc|r}} Using the Glowing Hourglass after entering a new floor will teleport Isaac back to the room in which the trapdoor was entered on the previous floor.
** Going back to the previous floor will transform Glowing Hourglass into {{i|The Hourglass}} for the rest of that previous floor. Going back to the new floor recharges the Glowing Hourglass, which allows for infinite usage of Glowing Hourglass on the starting room of a new floor.
*** If the Glowing Hourglass is held in the secondary slot of {{i|Schoolbag}} when entering the room with the trapdoor, the Glowing Hourglass will not be transformed into The Hourglass after returning to the previous floor.
** After returning to the previous floor, most changes in the room with the trapdoor will be undone. However, enemies / bosses will not be revived.
* {{Dlc|r}} {{C|Bethany|n}}'s soul heart counter does '''<u>not</u>''' get reset upon activating this item.
* {{Dlc|r}} If {{C|Tainted Jacob|n}} is hit by Esau, using the Glowing Hourglass will return him to normal form in the previous room.
* {{dlc|r}} The guaranteed angel room chance can be preserved if the item is used after entering the first devil room.
* {{Dlc|r}} When Isaac enters {{E|The Beast|n}} fight, Glowing Hourglass will transform into a fully charged {{i|The Hourglass}}.
* {{dlc+|r}} May be helpful for finding {{R|Planetarium}}s, as it lets the player effectively skip item rooms while also seeing if what's inside them is worth taking.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} If Isaac enters a Planetarium  for the first time and then uses Glowing Hourglass to leave, the chance of a {{R|Planetarium}} generating on future floors can be preserved, effectively allowing Isaac to reroll his Planetarium until a desired item is found. The likelihood of this being useful is rather low, however, due to Planetariums being rather rare.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} The {{R|Boss Challenge Room}} re-rolls bosses on using the Glowing Hourglass.
* {{t|Perfection}} is still able to drop if the Glowing Hourglass is used to reset damage, and will be brought back by the Glowing Hourglass if used to reset a damage taken while holding it.
* {{Dlc+|r}} If used in the starting room of {{S|Basement}} I without having entered any other rooms, Isaac is taken to the first room of {{S|Home}}. If used again in this room without having entered any other rooms, the room will be rewound to when it was first entered. In a normal game, this is only possible by getting the item as a starting item from {{C|Eden}} / {{C|Tainted Eden}}, or from {{I|Eden's Blessing}}. Having {{i|Schoolbag}} and obtaining {{i|R Key}} and resetting the run also makes this possible.{{dlc-}}
** {{dlc|r+}} Doing the same in {{mode|greed}}[[Greed Mode]] will teleport Isaac to the I AM ERROR room.
* The Glowing Hourglass affects permanent unlocks, event counters, boss kills, etc. differently depending on what is being reset:
** [[Completion Marks|Completion marks]] earned in the room will be removed.
** {{Dlc|na+}} Donations to the {{e|Donation Machine}} or {{e|Greed Donation Machine}} are not reverted, and they can be reset into a working state once jammed.
*** {{dlc|a+}} Event counters will get restored (including {{e|Donation Machine}}s, {{e|Greed Donation Machine}}s, and {{i|Eden's Blessing}}).
*** Other counters not tied to the specific run, such as {{e|Slot Machine}}s or [[Tinted Rock]]s destroyed, continue to accumulate, allowing easy unlocking of secrets such as the {{t|Counterfeit Penny}}, the {{i|D4}}, and {{E|Conquest}} if one has have access to infinite uses of the Glowing Hourglass (see the '''Synergies''' section).
** Does not remove [[collection page]] entries if it undoes collecting an item for the first time.
** No Damage Achievements are still available if the Glowing Hourglass is used to reset damage.
*** If a hit is taken, then reversed, Samson can still be unlocked.
** {{dlc|nr}} Can be used to unlock multiple achievements tied to the killing of certain bosses such as {{E|Mom's Heart}} / {{E|It Lives!}}.
** {{dlc|nr}} Using the Glowing Hourglass right after beating {{E|Mom's Heart}} / {{E|It Lives!}} / {{E|Ultra Greed}} allows additional Eden tokens to be obtained.
sections.Synergies:
* Any reroll item/collectible: Items in the room can be rerolled, and if the result is undesirable, then Isaac can go back in time to save whatever was used to reroll. However, note that activating the reroll on the same items again will result in the same items being generated as the first time. Rerolling different items from the same type of room (such as going to a different Shop) will result in the reroll effect creating new and different items. This technique is useful for saving charges on items like {{I|The D6}}, or getting multiple options with consumables like the {{p|Perthro}}.
* Anything that spawns an item such as {{i|Mystery Gift}} / {{p|XVII - The Stars?}}: After the player activates them, they can then go back in time if the item is undesirable. However, ''unlike'' reroll effects, using something that spawns an item/collectible will always generate that same item, dependent on the room type, even if the player goes to a different one in the future. For example, activating XVII - The Stars? in a Secret Room will create two items from the Secret Room item pool, and even if the player goes to the next floor and uses it again in a new Secret Room, the same exact items will be generated. So, the best way to use something that spawns an item is to activate it in rooms with different item pools (Secret, Devil/Angel, Treasure, Shop, etc.) and see which item would be the best before accepting it.
* {{dlc|na+}} {{p|? Card}}: Allows for infinite usage as the ? Card gets refunded upon usage.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{i|9 Volt}}: Clearing any room is enough to instantly recharge the hourglass, allowing infinite tries for the best outcome.
* {{Dlc|na+}}{{i|The Battery}}: When the item is double charged and used, it will also refund the used extra charge bar, making it possible to use it endlessly.
* {{Dlc|a+nr}}[[48 Hour Energy]] pill: Allows for infinite usage as the pill gets refunded upon use.
* {{Dlc|a+nr}}{{i|Sharp Plug}}: Allows for infinite usage as long as you have more than 2 full hearts as the hearts used to charge will be refunded upon use.
* {{Dlc|a+nr}}{{i|Habit}}: Allows rooms to be repeated infinitely as long as Isaac has enough health to take two hits, which are refunded on use.
* {{t|Hairpin|dlc=a+nr}}: If Hairpin is held while entering any Boss Room for the first time, Glowing Hourglass may be used indefinitely on said room to repeat the fight until you beat it.
* {{i|Moving Box|dlc=a+nr}}: Using the Glowing Hourglass after retrieving it from Moving Box will not deplete its charge.
* {{i|Curse of the Tower|dlc=a+nr}}: If used quickly after taking damage, Troll bombs will spawn in the previous room. If you have the {{t|Safety Scissors}}, these can be harvested as normal.
* {{dlc+|a+nr}}{{i|Crooked Penny}} + {{i|Schoolbag}}: If there is a battery and an item in the same room, you can multiply items an infinite number of times. Every time you fail the Crooked Penny flip, you can activate the Glowing Hourglass, go back in, grab a battery, then try again. Every time you succeed a flip, you must leave the room and enter it again to "save" your progress.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|rnr+}} {{i|More Options}}: If used after entering the Treasure Room in an Alt-Path floor, the items in the room will change.
* {{dlc|r}} If {{C|Tainted Eden}}'s active item re-rolls into Glowing Hourglass, it can be used immediately to return Tainted Eden to their previous state. This allows the player to have practically infinite attempts to keep their loadout of passive items as long as they travel back in time before being hit again.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Any wisps lost in the previous room will be restored, and an additional Glowing Hourglass wisp will be added on the middle ring. This wisp's tears have a 30% chance to [[petrify]] enemies.}}
** While playing as {{C|Tainted Eden}} and rerolling an active item into the Glowing Hourglass, you can infinitely spawn wisps as much as possible until you reroll it again.
* {{i|Duality|r}}: The doors to the {{R|Devil Room}} and {{R|Angel Room}} can stay open if you use the Glowing Hourglass inside their rooms, so Duality lets you check the items of both of them before deciding which room to use, provided two charges are still available by the end of the floor.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{I|Forget Me Now}} + {{I|Schoolbag}}: Using Forget Me Now will fully recharge Glowing Hourglass on the new floor, using Glowing Hourglass after that will take Isaac back to the previous room while also giving back Forget Me Now. This allows for infinite usage of Glowing Hourglass as well as infinite retries of any room as long as Forget Me Now is used before the room is cleared.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Saturnus}}: Using the Glowing Hourglass will activate the effect of Saturnus again, essentially allowing for double the amount of orbiting tears, if the player returns to a room, where the tears created by Saturnus were not destroyed.
* {{Dlc|r}} If activated while under the effect of [[Soul of Azazel]], as long as you had the consumable in the previously visited room, you will keep the Megablast effect while having another copy of the soul in your inventory.
** {{I|Schoolbag}} + {{i|Mega Blast}} + Glowing Hourglass: Works the same way
sections.Interactions:
* {{p|? Card|r}}: The Glowing Hourglass loses a charge when the card is used.
* {{i|Bag of Crafting}}: The bag's contents will be reverted to its previous state. Additionally, Bag of Crafting cannot be used to create Glowing Hourglass.
* {{i|The Battery|nr}}: Glowing Hourglass will receive a maximum of two full charges as normal, however, using the item twice consecutively will not result in the player being teleported two rooms previous, only one. This means that if Glowing Hourglass is used twice in succession, they will rewind as normal with the first use to the previous room, then, upon second use, everything will be rewound, but the player will not be teleported to the room previous to the one they just teleported to and will instead find themselves teleported to the room they are currently in. Rewinding works as normal, but teleportation is limited to the last room visited.
** {{dlc|r}} The battery has no effect on Glowing Hourglass when it is not in {{I|The Hourglass}} form.
* {{I|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{I|Schoolbag}}: Losing your Schoolbag while Glowing Hourglass is in your second active slot will drop it on the ground fully charged.
* {{C|Tainted Jacob|r}}: Using this item in a room where Dark Esau has spawned will cause him to remain with the player after teleporting, but once enough time has passed, he will suddenly disappear and respawn elsewhere. This may be a bug.
* {{i|Void|dlc=a+nr}}: It is impossible to absorb a Glowing Hourglass pedestal without using the item and preventing it from having been absorbed.
** {{Dlc+|r}} The Glowing Hourglass is absorbed like normal. Subsequent uses of '''Void''' send Isaac back to the previous room, reverting most changes, nullifying many other effects that '''Void''' may have absorbed. This will prevent you from consuming any further powers, as you will instead reset the room. This effectively turns '''Void''' into a charged version of Glowing Hourglass, allowing potential infinite uses with items like [[48 Hour Energy]] pills, {{i|Sharp Plug}}, {{i|Habit}}, {{t|Hairpin}}, {{i|4.5 Volt}}, or a room with a {{e|Lil' Battery}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{I|The Stairway}}: Using the Glowing Hourglass whilst in the Angel shop will consume all three charges and remove the ladder.

sections.Effects:
* On use, Isaac is teleported to a unique {{R|Clean Bedroom}} that acts like an {{r|I AM ERROR}} room. It has a [[Bed]], two random {{E|Chest}}s, two {{E|Grab Bag}}s, and a random [[Trinket]]. The only way out is through the beam of light, which teleports Isaac to the next floor (with some exceptions, seen below).
* Isaac loses all items and is reset to a state exactly like if he started a new run, though keeping quest items to not block progression. All [[Attributes|stats]], consumables, trinkets, and all items except for starting items and quest items, are removed. Isaac gains back all of his starting trinkets and consumables. 
* For every item removed using Genesis, there will be a set of three items from the removed item's pool to choose from, each set appearing one after the other at the bottom of the room.
sections.Notes:
* If used on one of the final floors of the game, such as {{s|Chest}}, {{s|Dark Room}}, {{s|The Void}}, or {{s|Corpse}} II, the beam of light will be replaced with a {{r|Crawl Space}} that leads Isaac back to the starting room of the floor he used it on. In addition, on {{s|Chest}} or {{s|Dark Room}} the aforementioned chests will include items. These items will not disappear along the "choice" pedestals.
** {{dlc|nr+}} If used in the final floor of Greedier mode, the beam of light will instead be replaced with a normal trap door that leads Isaac to a brand new Ultra Greed floor, forcing him to repeat the boss fight.
*** {{dlc|r+}} The trapdoor now leads to the starting room of the floor, without resetting it.
* If used in {{s|Womb}} II, {{s|Utero}} II, or {{s|???}}, the beam will always teleport Isaac to {{s|Cathedral}}.
* {{r|Crawl Space}}s can be generated and entered inside the Genesis room, but upon leaving them, Isaac will be returned to the floor Genesis was used on instead of returning to the room.
** Similarly, {{p|Joker}} can teleport Isaac to a {{r|Devil Room}} or {{r|Angel Room}}, and leaving will return Isaac to the room Genesis was used in, instead of the Genesis room.
** Other cards, such as {{p|0 - The Fool}}, can be used to directly teleport to one of the rooms in the current floor, successfully escaping as well. Cards can be obtained by opening a {{E|Chest}}, whose contents could be a {{E|Locked Chest}}, whose contents could be a [[Cards and Runes|Card]].
* [[Item Pool]]s will not be reset, however any lost items can be obtained again if they spawn.
* [[Transformations]] are also removed.
* Does not work during {{E|The Beast}}'s fight, instead merely teleporting Isaac to a random location in the room. No items will be removed.
* Take caution; choosing an active item while holding another one will not drop the previous item to the ground, but replace it.
* Genesis will remove all currently active [[curses]], meaning {{cu|Blind}} will not affect the item pedestals present inside the room (except during the [[Ultra Hard]] challenge).
* Trinkets absorbed using a [[Gulp!]] pill or an item such as {{i|Smelter}} will simply be removed with no extra pedestals granted for them.
* If used as {{C|Jacob and Esau}}, both characters' items are removed to offer choices, but Jacob and Esau cannot take two items at once from the choices. Both characters' items are considered in the amount of choices offered.
* {{C|Tainted Cain}} will be able to pick up the items that appear normally, one of the few times he is able to do so (along with quest items and items in the {{I|Death Certificate}} area).
* If used as {{C|Tainted Lazarus}}, both forms' items are removed and offer the equivalent number of choices, while his initial {{I|Flip}} is granted infinite charges and can be used freely in the special room.
* {{C|Bethany}} will lose all existing wisps and reset the soul charge count to its default of 4 on use, but will gain 3 default wisps upon appearing in the Genesis room.
* {{C|Tainted Bethany}} will lose all of her {{I|Lemegeton}} wisps and reset the blood charge count to its default of 6 on use. She does not gain extra wisps back.
* If used as {{C|Eden}} or {{C|Tainted Eden}}, a new set of items and stats will be generated. The first random passive item Eden starts with is rerolled immediately with no choice of three.
* If Isaac uses Genesis while in {{s|Downpour}} II / {{s|Mines}} II / {{s|Mausoleum}} II or their variants, the beam of light will send him back to the regular floors. However, after using Genesis on {{s|Downpour}} I / {{s|Mines}} I / {{s|Mausoleum}} I / {{s|Corpse}} I, it sends Isaac to the respective second part of the stage.
* Since Genesis resets Isaac's health, it is one way to remove [[Health#Broken Hearts|Broken Hearts]].
* Using Genesis removes the schwag bonus and {{dlc|nr+}} damage penalty on [[Daily Challenges]] and outside.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Genesis' quality is treated as 3 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Belial synergy|description=Grants a free {{i|Pentagram}} that will not be removed by Genesis.}}
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Replaces all of Isaac's wisps with 3 normal wisps. Unlike other reroll items, Isaac does not keep Book of Virtues.}}
sections.Interactions:
