* {{P|? Card}}: If ? Card is used in place of Genesis, Genesis will be counted as an extra item for the choice set.
* {{i|Abyss}}: The locusts created by Abyss are removed without creating items to replace them making Genesis one of the few effects that can remove them.
* {{C|Azazel}} / {{C|Tainted Azazel}}: Both have the ability to return to the floor Genesis was used on, due to them starting with a {{P|0 - The Fool}} card.
* {{I|Book of Revelations}}/{{I|Satanic Bible}}: Effects on the {{R|Boss Room}} and boss item still apply to the floor even after using Genesis.
* {{i|Brittle Bones}}: Genesis removes the [[fire rate]] upgrades upon use.
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{I|Crooked Penny}}: Using it on the choice pedestals has the 50/50 chance of duplicating them as normal, or make them disappear, in which case no new ones will spawn.
* {{I|Damocles}} / {{I|Missing No.}}: Genesis removes these items as well, making it the only item or effect that can remove them besides {{t|Butter!}}.
* {{i|Death Certificate}}: After taking an item in the Death Certificate area, Isaac will return to the Genesis room and the current 3 item pedestals can all be taken, with the next set spawning on top of them.
* {{i|Echo Chamber}}: The consumable pool is reset when Genesis is used, so if it's re-obtained after using Genesis, the previously stored consumable types won't be activated.
* {{I|Eden's Blessing}}: Eden's Blessing will be consumed, and the next run Isaac starts will begin with a random item.
* {{I|Esau Jr.}}: Using Genesis as Esau Jr. will revert back to the original character.
* {{I|Lazarus' Rags}} / {{I|Ankh}} / {{I|Clicker}}: Using Genesis after Lazarus' Rags, Ankh or Clicker activates will continue as the new character.
* {{I|Glowing Hourglass}}: Using it works as intended and will give back all previous stats, items, pickups, and health.
* {{I|Magic Skin}}: Genesis does '''NOT''' remove the downside of Magic Skin; any of the choice pedestals can be replaced by Magic Skin.
* {{I|Sacred Orb}}: Will affect future items while inside the Genesis Room.
* {{I|Teleport!}} / {{I|Teleport 2.0}} / [[Pills|Telepills]] / [[Cards and Runes|Teleport Cards]]: Should such items/consumables be obtained in the Genesis room, they can be used to circumvent the forced floor skip.
** In the case of pills, unidentified pills should only be consumed ''after'' taking all of the items in case telepills is rolled, for the Genesis room cannot be returned to after leaving.
* {{i|Void}}: All effects granted by absorbed items including stat ups and [[activated item]] abilities Void takes are removed without creating items to replace them. Since Void is stripped of any active item abilities it would have gained, any other Void found will also have no other active effects stored in it.
** Void's active effects are reset even if Isaac is currently not holding it.
* {{p|Wild Card}}: Can't activate Genesis.
* {{C|Tainted Lost}}: Will lose his Holy Mantle shield on use but will gain a new {{p|Holy Card|n}}.

sections.Effect:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] that follows Isaac around and fires [[spectral tears]] that deal 3.5 damage each.
** {{dlc|nr}} Ghost Baby shoots once per second.
** {{dlc|r}} Ghost Baby shoots 1.36 times a second.
* {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}
sections.Notes:
* This item can rarely drop from destroying [[Rocks#Skulls|skulls]].
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Ghost Baby having {{dlc|nr+}} 5th / {{dlc|r+}} 7th priority.
sections.Synergies: * {{I|Mongo Baby}}: Will copy Ghost Baby’s tears.

sections.Effects:
* When Isaac takes damage, there is a chance that a {{E|Soul Heart}} may spawn.
* [[Monster]]s have a chance to drop a {{E|Half Red Heart}} after being killed. Chance depends on killed monster's base health.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Sisters Vis}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|nr}} The chance for Gimpy to spawn a Soul Heart depends on the [[luck]] stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\min(\frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.4 \right \rfloor},50\%)</math>
** At base luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 50% at 20 luck.
* {{dlc|r}} The chance for Gimpy to spawn a Soul Heart depends on the [[luck]] stat and is based on this formula: <math>8\% + (2\% * \mathit{Luck})</math>
** This means that the chance starts at 8% at 0 luck, minimizes at 0% at -4 luck, and maximizes at 100% at 46 luck.
* Monsters that have less than 10 HP have a 1% chance to drop a Half Red Heart.
* Monsters that have 10 to 29 HP have a 5% chance to drop a Half Red Heart.
* Monsters that have more than 30 HP have a 10% chance to drop a Half Red Heart.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Blood Oath}}: For each half heart damaged by Blood Oath, Gimpy has a chance to drop a soul heart. Synergy further improves with luck.
* {{i|Dark Bum}}: Dark Bum can collect the Half Red Hearts that enemies drop, which when combined with the chance to drop Soul Hearts when damaged, is a good way to generate Soul and {{E|Black Heart}}s as well as other pickups.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Enemies that are turned into [[pickup]]s can't drop hearts.
* {{i|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Enemies that are turned into poop can't drop hearts.

sections.Effects:
* Grants 2 Soul Hearts.
* Modifies drops from Champion enemies depending on certain conditions.
* {{dlc|r}} Also modifies room clear drops.
* {{Dlc|r}} Every room is guaranteed to drop a reward.
* The priorities of the drops, in order, are as follows:
** '''{{E|Soul Heart}}s''': When Isaac has no Red Heart containers and less than 2 Soul Hearts.
** '''{{E|Red Heart}}s''': While at 0.5 Red Hearts.
** '''{{E|Key}}s''': When Isaac has no keys. 
** '''{{E|Bomb}}s''': When Isaac has no bombs.
** '''{{E|Red Heart}}s''': When Isaac has at least half a Red Heart container empty.
*** {{c|Tainted Bethany}} will always get this drop until she reaches 12 "blood charges".
** '''{{E|Penny|text=Pennies}}''': While Isaac has less than 15 pennies.
** '''{{E|Key}}s''': When Isaac has less than 5 keys. 
** '''{{E|Bomb}}s''': When Isaac has less than 5 bombs.
** '''Trinkets''': If Isaac has no trinkets and there are no trinkets on the ground in the room.
** '''{{E|Soul Heart}}s''': When Isaac has less than 6 total Heart containers of any kind.
*** {{c|Bethany}} will only get this drop until she reaches 12 "soul charges". 
*** {{c|Tainted Bethany}} changes blue heart drop to red heart drop until she reaches 12 "blood charges", thus she is unable to receive any blue hearts.
** If none of the above conditions are true, items dropped will be rolled as normal.
** {{Dlc|r}} Chest drops override the Glyph of Balance.
sections.Notes:
* When the conditions for specific drop is met, you can intentionally not pick up the drop to guarantee that same drop (or a chest) every room.
* {{Dlc|r}} Staying at low luck is recommended to take full advantage of Glyph of Balance, as higher luck will make chest drops more common and override the effect of the Glyph.
* The Glyph has no effect in [[Greed Mode]] or Greedier Mode aside from the {{E|Soul Heart}}s granted upon pickup; champions still never drop anything.
* {{dlc|nr}} Because of how the item works in the priorities listed above, this item is not recommended for {{c|The Lost}} (except in combination with {{i|Immaculate Conception}}) as he is always considered to be at half a Soul Heart, and all drops ''from champions'' are replaced with Soul Hearts.
** {{dlc+|r}}{{c|The Lost}} and {{c|Tainted Lost}} ignore both rules for Soul Heart generation. This prevents the item from generating mostly useless Soul Hearts.{{dlc-}}
* When playing as {{c|The Forgotten}}, the priority of the drops is based on the active form's health: for example, if The Forgotten has half a red heart or less, but The Soul was active right before the pickup drop and it had more than 2 soul hearts, the Glyph will skip over the full red heart drops to the next condition. Also if The Forgotten is full on pickups and health, has a trinket but has less than 6 bone hearts, the Glyph will always drop soul hearts unless The Soul is active at the moment of the drop.
* {{dlc+|r}} When playing as {{c|Jacob and Esau}} / {{c|Tainted Lazarus}}, the priority of the drops is based on the health of the character that has the Glyph.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} When playing as {{c|Tainted Lazarus}}, the room drop will be modified when the character switches to the character that has the item on room clear.{{dlc-}}
* {{Dlc|r}} When playing as characters incapable of having red heart containers such as {{C|???}}, the Glyph will skip soul heart and red heart generation.
* While empty room drops are replaced by Glyph of Balance drops, if you get a heart drop in {{mode|hard}} Hard mode, there is a separate chance of it being replaced with an empty drop.
** It is still possible to get hearts if none of the other conditions are true.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Options?}}: Only one of the options will be modified by the Glyph.
* {{T|Perfection}}: Chest spawns are prioritized over Glyph of Balance, meaning it will be very hard to use the Glyph effectively.

sections.Notes:
* Resurrection items activate in a [[:Category:Revival items|set order]]. Guppy's Collar is {{dlcalt|4th|r=6th}} in this order after {{p|Soul of Lazarus}}, {{i|1up!}}, {{dlcalt|{{i|Dead Cat}}, {{c|Lazarus}}' inherent extra life|r={{c|Lazarus}}' inherent extra life, {{i|Dead Cat}}}}, and {{i|Inner Child}}.
* It is possible to obtain two collars by finding one in a {{E|Red Chest}}, without picking it up, and then finding another collar in a different Red Chest. {{dlc|nr}} However, this does not have any additional effects and does not count towards transforming into Guppy.
** {{dlc|r}} Obtaining multiple copies of Guppy's Collar now grants extra lives, depending on how many copies are obtained (obtaining a second collar displays the lives count as '2?', and so on). The chance for Guppy's Collar to activate is defined with separate rolls, but increases the odds for one of the collars to revive Isaac. Additional collars also count towards the Guppy transformation.
* Resurrecting in a {{r|Curse Room}} may trap Isaac if he has no way of recovering health or exiting them without losing health.
* {{dlc|a+}} Resurrecting via Guppy's Collar during a [[Daily Challenge]] will count as a death, even if the run is eventually completed.
* {{dlc|r}} While escaping [[Mother's Shadow]], the HUD states the revive chance is 100% (the question mark is removed). However, since all Isaac's items are removed in the area, the revive will not happen.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns two [[Pretty Fly|Pretty Flies]] that block enemy shots.
** Pretty flies kill some [[fly]] enemies upon contact.
** The orbital limit of three flies cannot be surpassed with this item, reducing its effectiveness if Isaac has two or more orbitals.
* {{transformation contribution|Beelzebub}}
sections.Synergies: * {{I|Abyss}}: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Halo of Flies two gray locusts are created dealing half of Isaac’s damage per tick each.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|D4|nr}}: This item can't be rerolled by the D4 or other items that reroll passive items.

sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Sacrificial Altar}}: This familiar will also reward 2 {{e|Black Heart}}s when sacrificed.
* {{i|Spin to Win}}: The two orbital speed boosts stack.
sections.Interactions: * {{I|Big Fan}}: Overrides Guardian Angel's speed boost. If Guardian Angel was obtained first, it will retain its own increased speed. If Big Fan was obtained first, Guardian Angel will be slower.

sections.Effects:
* Grants an extra Red [[Heart container]] for every 25 {{E|Penny|text=Coins}} Isaac has, up to a maximum of 4 hearts at 99 coins.
** Dropping below the number of coins required for a Red Heart container removes the Red Heart container.
sections.Notes:
* The extra Red Heart container can exceed the maximum Coin Heart container limit of {{C|Keeper}}, allowing him to obtain more than {{Dlc|nr}}2 / {{Dlc|r}}3 Coin Heart containers.
* Depending on the character used, this item only affects Red Heart containers, Soul Hearts ({{C|???}}) or Coin Heart containers ({{C|Keeper}}). It does not affect {{C|The Lost}}.
* {{dlc|nr}} The Red Heart container gain is not retroactive - picking it up at 99 coins will not grant 4 extra Red Heart containers.
** However, picking it up at 99 coins and then dropping below 99 coins will lose a Red Heart container, decreasing the viability of picking this item up the more coins you have.
*** The player will die if they lose their last form of health as a result of Greed's Gullet.
*** If Keeper drops to under 2 Coin Heart containers as a result of Greed's Gullet, or by any other means (Devil deal, etc.), he is unable to use an HP Up to increase his health back to 2 and has to regain the lost coins to do so.
** {{dlc|nr}} If Greed's Gullet is rerolled away after gaining health, the extra health will be preserved even if the player loses the coins afterward.
*** However, if this happens with Keeper, his health will drop back to 2 Coin Heart containers upon picking up an item, unless another Greed's Gullet is picked up.
** {{dlc+|r}} If Greed's Gullet is lost or re-rolled by any means (including the {{e|Mother's Shadow}} chase sequence), the health will be lost. This may cause Isaac to die. After returning from the {{e|Mother's Shadow}} chase sequence, the heart containers will be re-added, but they will be empty.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} The Red Heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet are now retroactive - picking the item up at 99 coins will immediately grant 4 Red Heart containers. Consuming coins will still cause Isaac to lose Red Heart containers.
* {{dlc|r}} This also applies in reverse; consuming Red Heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet through methods such as {{R|Devil Room}} items or {{i|Guppy's Paw}} will cause Isaac to lose an appropriate amount of coins.
* {{dlc|r}} For {{C|Keeper}} specifically, Greed's Gullet in combination with {{I|Deep Pockets}} allows him to bypass the 12 heart container health limit, capping at 15 Coin Hearts at 999 coins.
** Works the same for {{C|Tainted Keeper}} but caps at 14 Coin Hearts instead.
** By using Health Up pills and Health Up items while having {{I|Deep Pockets|dlc=n}} the cap for {{C|Keeper}} can be raised to 54 Coin Hearts. However, additional heart containers beyond 24 will not appear on the health bar.
*** Works the same for {{C|Tainted Keeper}} but caps at 53 Coin Hearts instead.
* Be careful when buying items from the {{R|Shop}}, as it can remove Red Heart containers.
* Enemies that drain Isaac's coins (such as {{E|Keeper}}s, {{E|Hanger}}s, {{E|Greed}}, or {{E|Super Greed}}) can remove Red Heart containers.
* This item allows {{C|Keeper}} and {{C|Tainted Keeper}} to utilize Health Up pills and Health up items, as the Coin Hearts gained this way are kept even if the coins are lost once the coins lost are regained, and can bypass the 99-coin limit.
sections.Synergies:
* {{dlc|r}}{{i|Deep Pockets}}: After exceeding 100 coins, Isaac gains an extra heart container for every 100 coins instead of every 25.
* {{I|Strawman}}: The assisting Keeper may also gain extra coin hearts, and in fact will retain the extra health containers even if coin loss would otherwise drop him below the threshold. However, exiting the game and then continuing thereafter will update Keeper's health.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Abaddon}}: Removes heart containers by removing coins in 25 cent increments.
* {{i|Dead Cat}}: Any extra Red Heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet will be removed upon pickup. If Isaac had more than 24 coins when picking up Dead Cat, then the remaining Red Heart container will be removed if enough coins are lost.
* {{i|A Dollar}}: Isaac will instantly gain the max amount of Red Heart containers.
* {{I|Eye of Greed}}: Coins will be lost for every 20th tear fired, risking Red Heart container loss if Isaac has more than 24 coins.
* {{I|Money Power}}: Isaac will gain both damage and health.
* {{i|A Quarter}}: Isaac will gain a Red Heart container.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] who follows Isaac around and fires two tears at once in a V-shape pattern {{dlcalt|once per second|r=1.36 times a second}} that each do 4 damage.
* {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Mr. Fred}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Harlequin Baby having {{dlcalt|5th|r+=7th}} priority.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Mongo Baby}}: Will copy Harlequin Baby’s spread double shot effect.
* {{c|Tainted Forgotten|r}}: The momentum from the skeleton being tossed makes Harlequin Baby's tears launch at an abnormally high shot speed.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a demon [[familiar]] attached to Isaac by a cord for the current room, floating in the direction Isaac shoots. It automatically fires tears (whenever Isaac is shooting) in the direction of the closest enemy to it, using Isaac's [[damage]], [[tears]], [[range]], [[shot speed]], and [[Status Effects|special]] [[tear effects]].
** The item is initially held over Isaac's head until he fires, which launches the familiar in the direction he shoots, dealing 3x Isaac's damage to all enemies it passes through.
** If Isaac has any tear modifier that requires him to charge his shots (i.e. {{i|Brimstone}}), Gello will automatically release its shot every time it is fully charged.
** Gello's tears deal 0.75x Isaac's damage.
sections.Notes:
* {{c|Tainted Lilith}} attacks in a way nearly identical to this item, except she can recall it and launch it again.
* If used multiple times in the same room, the Gellos will eventually overlap perfectly and appear as one after some movement, but all remain functional. This makes Gello exceptionally powerful in [[Greed Mode]], {{R|Boss Rush}}, and against {{E|The Beast}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a red wisp on the middle ring. The wisps will orbit Gello instead of Isaac while it's active.}}
* {{c|Tainted Azazel}}: Each time Gello starts charging an attack, he will "sneeze" just like Tainted Azazel does, cursing enemies in front of him. This allows Tainted Azazel to keep enemies cursed without needing to come up to a dangerously close distance to them.
* {{c|Tainted Lazarus}}: The familiar persists when switching states.
* {{i|Uranus}}: When the baby is launched, any enemies it kills in its trajectory will freeze and any frozen enemies the baby is launched into slide if Isaac is moving, similarly to when kicked by Isaac.
* {{c|Lilith}} / {{c|Tainted Lilith}}: Gello's tears deal 1.0x of Isaac's damage instead.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone}} / {{i|Dr. Fetus}} / {{i|Godhead}} / {{i|The Inner Eye}} / {{i|Ipecac}} / {{i|Mutant Spider}} / {{i|Polyphemus}} / {{i|Proptosis}} / {{i|Tech X}}: Gello receives a unique appearance, similar to Isaac.
* {{i|Car Battery|nr+}}: No effect.
** {{dlc|r+}} Spawns an additional familiar.

sections.Effects:
* Fires a single high-damage [[piercing]] tear which can travel over [[obstacle]]s.
** The damage dealt by this tear is ten times Isaac's damage, plus a flat 10 damage.
** The shot has an additional 1.5x size multiplier on top of damage-increased size.
* {{dlc|nr}} Sets Isaac's health to half a heart with each use (half a Soul Heart if these are present but there are no Red Heart containers). This also removes any other {{E|Soul Heart}}s or {{E|Black Heart}}s, but not {{E|Eternal Heart}}s.
** {{dlc+|a+nr}} If Isaac has no Red Hearts and at least one {{E|Bone Heart}}, only an empty Bone Heart remains.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} Upon taking damage, this item turns into {{i|Broken Glass Cannon}}, and Isaac will lose an additional 2 hearts of health on top of the damage he already took. Isaac gains 1.5 range and leaves a trail of red [[creep]] behind him for the rest of the current room, identical to the effects of {{i|Anemic}}.
** If the damage from breaking Glass Cannon would result in death, Isaac will remain at half a heart, gaining half a soul heart if necessary. This does not apply if the damage Isaac took would be lethal before the extra damage is taken.
** The damage from breaking Glass Cannon does not count as self-damage and '''will''' result in losing Angel/Devil Room chance if it is taken to Red Hearts.
** Self-damage (e.g. from {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s or {{r|Sacrifice Room}}s) will not break Glass Cannon.{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* Glass Cannon can be fired diagonally, {{dlc+|a+}} even without {{I|Analog Stick}}{{dlc-}}.
* Shooting the Glass Cannon gives a slight [[knockback]] effect to Isaac, which can be dangerous in rooms with obstacles like spikes or Fire Places.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Belial synergy|description=Grants Judas +2.67 damage up while Glass Cannon is broken.}}
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns white wisps on the middle ring. The wisps shatter in one hit and their tears deal 8 damage per shot, but if one of the wisps is destroyed, all the others are also destroyed. Does not affect wisps other than ones made by this item. Despite Glass Cannon having a timed charge, the wisps persist between rooms.}}
* {{i|Chocolate Milk|nr}}: The current charge of Chocolate Milk affects Glass Cannon.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}} / {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Tears fired by Glass Cannon will split.
* {{i|Godhead}}: Creates a giant aura around Glass Cannon tears that almost fills up normal sized rooms.
* {{i|Lachryphagy}}: Glass Cannon will fire giant Lachryphagy tears. Tears are harder to feed as they will burst very quickly but they can be fed if you fire tears beforehand and then fire Glass Cannon into those tears.
* {{i|Multidimensional Baby}}: The Glass Cannon tears will be doubled by Multidimensional Baby.
* {{i|Mysterious Liquid}}: Creates a large pool of creep when tears land.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: Tears produced by Glass Cannon will orbit Isaac.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: The Glass Cannon tears can block enemy shots.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Anti-Gravity}}, {{i|Car Battery}}, {{i|The Inner Eye}}, {{i|Mutant Spider}}, {{i|Brimstone}}, {{i|Dr. Fetus}}, {{i|Epic Fetus}}, {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}, {{i|Marked}}, {{i|Mom's Knife}}, {{i|Monstro's Lung}}, {{i|Technology}}, {{i|Tech X}}, {{i|9 Volt|na+}}, and {{i|20/20|nr}}: No effect, Glass Cannon fires a normal tear.
* {{i|9 Volt|a+}}: Reduces charge time to 2 seconds.
* {{I|20/20|r}}: Gives a 25% damage down, hurting Glass Cannon's performance.
* {{i|Eye of the Occult}}: Cannon shot can be controlled. If a synergy is given a crosshair (e.g. {{i|Brimstone}}, {{i|Technology}} etc.), the tear will follow wherever it's pointed.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Habit}}: Upon taking damage, {{I|Broken Glass Cannon}} will be half-charged. However, taking damage before the last charge will break the cannon again.{{dlc-}}
* Items that trigger upon taking damage (such as {{i|It Hurts}} and {{t|Swallowed Penny}}) will activate 3 times when the Glass Cannon breaks.
* {{i|Holy Mantle|nr}}: Doesn't prevent damage done by Glass Cannon, but will protect against other types of damage.
* {{i|Ipecac|nr}}: As the Glass Cannon tears are so large, even a modest damage increase or a single tear size increasing item is likely to render the tear unable to damage enemies, their explosions too far from them.
* {{i|Pluto}}: Allows Isaac to cross small gaps using the knockback of Glass Cannon.
* {{i|Schoolbag|r}}: The cannon will break on damage, regardless if it or another active is on hand.
** '''Schoolbag''' + {{I|Tear Detonator|n}}: Glass Cannon shots will detonate into normal tears. The tears don't inherit [[spectral]] or [[piercing]].
* {{i|Soy Milk}}: Reduces damage of shots, no effect on charge time.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Fires normal Trisagion beams that do not have increased damage.
* {{i|The Wafer|r}}: Doesn't reduce the damage from breaking the Glass Cannon.
* {{i|Stye}} and {{i|Blood Clot}}: Copies the eye used most recently.

sections.Effects:
* Grants a 1/3 chance of replacing [[Room Clear Awards]] with a {{E|Chest}} or a {{E|Locked Chest}}, but also a 2/9 chance to replace it with nothing at all.
* {{transformation contribution|Guppy}}
sections.Notes:
* The drawback to this item is that Keys become much more scarce, while increasing the amount of Locked Chests. This makes taking Guppy's Tail a potential liability early on.
* Due to any found Chests containing [[item]]s while in {{s|Chest}} or {{s|Dark Room}}, Guppy's Tail can be a good way to quickly stack up more upgrades before facing the final boss.
* {{dlc|a}} The effect does not apply to {{e|Penny|text=Pennies}} dropped in [[Greed Mode]], meaning that this item has no effect in [[Greed Mode]] other than counting towards the Guppy Transformation.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Deep Pockets|r}}: If Guppy's Tail removes the room clear drop, it is turned into coins instead.
* {{I|Guppy's Eye}}: Makes {{e|Key}} management easier by revealing which Locked Chests are worth opening and which are not.
* {{t|The Left Hand}}: Turns all chests into {{e|Red Chest}}s, allowing Isaac to get Red Chest items much more quickly. Useful when pursuing the {{tf|Guppy}} transformation.
* {{i|Mom's Key}}: Increases the number of drops from Chests and counteracts the increased chance to run into Locked Chests.
* {{i|Options?}}: Chests may be accompanied by normal room drops or other chests of a type that's easier to open, mitigating the downsides.
* {{T|Paper Clip}}: The Key scarcity problem is completely prevented, since Paper Clip causes Locked Chests to be openable without Keys, making Guppy's Tail's only downside the chance to replace room clears with nothing at all.
** {{dlc|a}}If {{C|Cain}} starts with the Trinket, entering {{R|Curse Room}}s and opening Red Chests in hopes of finding Guppy's Tail early is a very effective strategy.

* Using this item in a room with enemies, spikes, or other hazards can often make it difficult to see what is happening, as nearly half of the player's screen may be covered by a fortune. This can be circumvented by pausing the game and waiting for the fortune to disappear.
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a green wisp on the middle ring. Each wisp gives Isaac +0.2 [[Luck]].}}

sections.Interactions: * {{i|Glass Eye}}: Picking up a second copy of the item gives Isaac a unique costume with both eyes replaced. The damage up and luck up stack as expected.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns 3 random [[coin]]s and a {{E|Key}} on the floor when picked up.
* Every 3 coins spent on items and pickups grants in a cycle: +0.5 [[damage]], then +0.25 [[range]], then +0.03 [[speed]].
sections.Notes:
* The coins and key spawned on pickup can be any of their variants.
* Keeper's Sack works with anything that costs coins, including [[Devil deal]]s/{{R|Black Market}}s as {{c|Keeper}} / affected by {{t|Keeper's Bargain}} or {{i|A Pound of Flesh}}, items or pickups created by {{i|Keeper's Box}}, the Angel shop created by {{I|The Stairway}}, and the second shop created by {{i|Member Card}}.
* The stat upgrades are tied to Keeper's Sack; losing Keeper's Sack (for instance, using {{i|D4}}, crossing a 1-pip or 6-pip {{R|Dice Room}}, or using {{p|XVII - The Stars?}}) will result in the loss of all obtained stats.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Bag of Crafting}}: Purchasing a pickup by swinging the Bag of Crafting at it will still give the stat upgrades from Keeper's Sack.
* {{i|Diplopia}}/{{i|Crooked Penny}}: Extra copies of Keeper's Sack do not grant any more stats from purchasing items.
* {{i|Steam Sale}}: As items/pickups cost less money, Isaac will gain fewer stats for making the same purchases.
* {{t|Store Credit}}: Anything bought will not give stats.
* {{C|Tainted Keeper}}: Every {{R|Devil Room}}, {{R|Treasure Room}}, {{R|Angel Room}} etc. will give stat ups, as long as the items are bought.

sections.Effects:
* Grants a [[familiar]] that follows Isaac and always appears first in the familiar chain.
* While firing tears, King Baby stops moving and glows white.
* When Isaac stops firing tears, King Baby moves rapidly back towards Isaac.
* While King Baby is stationary, other familiars remain stationary as well. {{dlc|r}} This affects every familiar that has priority in how closely it follows behind Isaac.
** {{dlc|nr}} [[Familiar#Shooting familiars|Shooting familiars]] will fire tears in the direction Isaac is firing, while [[Familiar#Throwable familiars|Throwable familiars]] ignore King Baby.
** {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar#Shooting familiars|Shooting familiars]] fire at nearby enemies automatically and [[Familiar#Throwable familiars|throwable familiars]] launch themselves at nearby enemies automatically.
*** Familiars that have charged attacks will operate on similar rules to {{I|Marked}}: they will immediately fire at full charge, and variable-charged attacks will be released earlier the closer that King Baby is to the target.
* {{dlc|r}} {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{Dlc|nr}}{{i|Isaac's Heart}}: Isaac can fire tears and leave King Baby and the heart behind, and run into a group of enemies without being damaged.
* {{i|Lil Brimstone}}: Can fire in full 360 degrees and will fire as soon as he's fully charged, making him extremely effective.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Increases King Baby's size. No other effect.
* {{T|Child Leash}}: Familiars stay closer to King Baby while Isaac is firing.
* {{I|Cain's Other Eye|r}}: Cain's Other Eye will attempt to fire directly at enemies but only when they are on the same side as the random direction it is firing in.
* {{t|Duct Tape}}: King Baby will stay in place relative to Isaac until Isaac starts firing tears. Then King Baby will remain stationary until Isaac has stopped firing and will rapidly move back to him.
* {{T|Friendship Necklace}}: Familiars will orbit King Baby at all times instead of Isaac, even while not firing. King Baby itself is unaffected.
* {{I|GB Bug|r}}: GB Bug will only throw itself at nearby enemies automatically if a fire button is double tapped while King Baby's effect is active.
* {{I|Gemini}}: Suture will rest near King Baby as long as there are no enemies near Isaac. When Isaac gets near enemies, Suture will rapidly snap from King Baby toward the enemy. Functionally, King Baby has no real effect on Gemini.
** Visually, this can result in the umbilical between Isaac and Suture getting stretched to a long length.
* {{I|Jaw Bone|r}}: After being thrown, Jaw Bone will return to Isaac and then reappear behind King Baby.
* {{T|RC Remote}}: Overrides King Baby's halting; familiars will mimic Isaac's movements even while firing. King Baby's auto-targeting remains active.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] that fires across the [[Rooms|room]] in the direction of the first tear fired and returns to Isaac when it hits a wall, similar to {{i|Little Chubby}}. Deals a flat 7 damage to enemies that come in contact with it.
** When thrown, the familiar will pierce through some fly enemies, instantly killing them, but will instantly bounce back upon hitting other enemies.
** The familiar can pass through [[obstacles]].
** The familiar can retrieve [[pickups]] like {{i|The Boomerang}}.
** Blocks enemy tears when stationary and when thrown.
** After returning to Isaac, it has a short recharge time before it can be fired again.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Familiar grows in size and does a flat 14 damage to enemies.
* {{t|Duct Tape|n}}: Jaw Bone will face in the same direction as Isaac and remain stationary as opposed to trailing behind him. Jaw Bone can still be fired.
* {{I|King Baby|r}}: After being thrown, Jaw Bone will return to Isaac and then reappear behind King Baby.

sections.Effects:
* +0.5 [[damage]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +0.25 [[range]].
* {{dlc|r}} +1.5 [[range]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +0.5 [[tear falling speed]].

* Grants Isaac a chance to spawn a friendly ghost upon killing an enemy, which rapidly chases down and deals contact damage to enemies.
** The chance to spawn a ghost is 33% and is not affected by [[luck]].
** Ghosts deal contact damage equal to half of Isaac's damage, 4 times per second (2x Isaac's damage per second).
* After 7 seconds, the ghost explodes, dealing 7 flat damage to nearby enemies up to 3-4 times.
** The explosion cannot damage Isaac or the environment.
sections.Notes:
* Enemies killed by ghosts are unable to spawn more ghosts, except for those killed by the ghost's final explosion.
* The ghost's explosion is capable of damaging [[friendly]] monsters, such as {{E|Bony|text=Bonies}} summoned by {{i|Book of the Dead}}.
* Ghosts cannot be taken outside the room they spawned in.
* The ghosts are not considered to be [[familiar]]s and as such aren't affected by any items that modify the behavior of familiars.
** This also means that Isaac can have more than 64 ghosts at a time and this won't override other familiars.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Enemies that are turned into [[pickup]]s can’t spawn ghosts.
* {{i|BFFS!}}: No effect.
* {{i|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Enemies that are turned into poop can’t spawn ghosts.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: The ghosts get only +1 flat damage from Ipecac, not the expected +20.
* {{i|Libra}}: The ghosts ignore damage modification from Libra, both positive and negative: the actual unbalanced damage value is used.
* {{i|Sacrificial Altar}}: Ghosts cannot be sacrificed.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, causes Isaac to lose half a heart of [[health]] (or a full heart in [[Chapter 4]] onward) while spawning [[coin]]s.
** {{dlc|nr}} Each use pays out with 1-2 coins.
** {{Dlc|r}} Each use pays out with 1-2 coins on Normal mode or 1 coin on [[Hard mode]].
** IV Bag takes {{e|Red Heart}}s before other heart types.
sections.Notes:
* This item can be found when causing a {{e|Blood Donation Machine}} to explode by donating Hearts to it.
* This effect is counted as inflicted damage for items that spawn [[pickup]]s upon said inflicted damage, such as {{i|Gimpy}} or {{i|Fanny Pack}}, but does not decrease the chance of encountering the {{r|Devil Room}} / {{r|Angel Room}}.
* Can be used before taking damage (getting hit, walking over spikes, going through a {{r|Curse Room}}, etc.) to grant coins without inflicting extra damage.
** {{dlc|nr}} Also allows Isaac to avoid damage taken by using a {{e|Blood Donation Machine}} or {{e|Devil Beggar}}.
* Using this item as {{C|The Lost}} or while in the Lost form after touching the {{E|White Fire Place}} kills Isaac.
sections.Interactions:
* [[Invulnerability]] and [[shield]]s can't be used to prevent damage from IV Bag, even if it normally prevents damage from a {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}.
* {{I|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{t|Cracked Dice}}: Rerolls the coins generated by IV bag, and can be used to generate unlimited pickups and items.
* {{dlc|a}} {{i|Holy Mantle}} and similar items: IV Bag ignores the shield's protection, resulting in Isaac taking damage regardless.

sections.Effect:
* Combined with {{i|Key Piece 1}}, unlocks the golden gate in the starting [[Rooms|room]] of {{S|Chest}} and {{S|Dark Room}} to fight {{E|Mega Satan}}.
* Increases the chance of finding an {{R|Angel Room}}.
* Grants a 2.5% chance of converting {{E|Red Heart}} pickups into {{E|Eternal Heart}}s.
** This effect stacks with {{i|Key Piece 1}}.
sections.Notes:
* This item is a guaranteed drop from {{E|Gabriel}} if not already in possession.
* This item, along with {{i|Key Piece 1}}, can be rerolled into any item from the [[Item Pool#Angel Room|Angel Room pool]].
* This item also counts as a [[familiar]], meaning it takes up a familiar slot.
* Unlocking the Golden Gate with the combined key pieces and then restarting the floor with {{i|Forget Me Now}} or an {{R|I AM ERROR}} room will waste the key, which will not respawn.
* Will not be rerolled by {{i|D4}}, {{i|D100}}, or {{R|Dice Room}} effects.
* Will not be doubled by {{i|Box of Friends}}
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Key Piece 2 having the lowest priority at {{dlc|nr+}} 6th / {{dlc|r+}} 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.Effects: * {{dlc|nr}} Isaac's body becomes immune to all damage. * {{dlc|nr}} Most enemies now target the heart instead of Isaac. {{E|Eye}}s and other similar enemies, however, will still target Isaac. * {{dlc|r}} Isaac's body becomes immune to all damage from enemies and the environment. This does not include interactable objects such as {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s and {{e|Devil Beggar}}s. * A heart [[familiar]] appears and closely follows Isaac. If the heart is hurt, Isaac is hurt. * {{dlc|r}} The heart tries to position itself in the opposite direction of where Isaac is shooting. * {{dlc|r}} The heart charges up as Isaac fires. At full charge, upon releasing the fire button, it knocks back nearby enemies and tears, creates a small puddle of red [[creep]] on the ground, and releases blood shots in 8 directions that deal 8 damage. * {{dlc|r}} Enemies pushed into walls or [[obstacles]] by the knockback blast take 10 + 2 * (floor - 1) damage. * {{dlc|r}} Enemies that come in contact with Isaac take 2x Isaac's current damage per tick or 4x Isaac's damage per second.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s and {{e|Devil Beggar}}s can be used for free.
** During {{chal|The Guardian}}, Devil Beggars and Blood Donation Machines deal damage to Isaac.
* [[Spikes]], {{R|Curse Room}} doors and {{E|Spiked Chest}}s do no damage. {{R|Sacrifice Room}} spikes still work, though the heart has to go on the spikes instead of Isaac. {{dlc+|r}} The door to {{s|Mausoleum}} / {{s|Gehenna}} is not affected.{{dlc-}}
* Picking up a non-orbital familiar will cause either Isaac's Heart or the other familiar to be layered over the other's sprite. This is due to the heart not taking up the spot that the other familiar follows in.
* Co-op babies gain the immunity effect without spawning additional hearts.
* {{dlc|na}} Enemy Brimstone shots (such as from {{E|The Bloat}}) will not do any damage to the heart.
** {{dlc|r}} Enemy Brimstone shots will now be blocked by the body. This visually resembles the blocking effect of {{I|Divine Intervention}}.
* The tracking lasers from {{E|Hush}} and light pillars from {{E|Isaac}} do not damage the heart.
* Isaac will turn into {{c|The Lost}} form if either he or the heart touches a {{e|White Fire Place}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|120 Volt}}/{{i|Monstrance}}: These items become much safer to use offensively as they are centered around Isaac's body which no longer takes damage.
* {{i|Blood Rights|nr}}: Blood Rights doesn't deal damage to Isaac, allowing repeated usage without penalty. {{dlc-}}
* {{i|Box of Friends}}: Box of Friends does not duplicate the heart, making it safe to use.
* {{i|Breath of Life|nr}}: Isaac can be infinitely invulnerable, as invincibility carries out to the heart without hurting the player. Note that the item needs to be activated for longer than one second for the invulnerability to kick in, however.
** {{dlc|r}} Works as normal except for the fact that the damage to the heart must be blocked to spawn the 4 beams.
* {{t|Duct Tape}}: Makes dodging significantly easier.
* {{i|E. Coli}}: Isaac can turn enemies into poop without taking damage.
* {{i|Holy Mantle}}: The shield effect carries over to the heart.
* {{t|Gigante Bean}}: Makes the heart much easier to defend as it increases the knockback amount and radius of the heart when fully charged and the heart makes farting noises when it shoots.
* Items granting [[invulnerability]] or a [[shield]]: The invincibility carries over to the heart.
** {{dlc|r}} Due to the contact damage, {{i|Gnawed Leaf}} allows Isaac to clear most rooms without moving.
* {{i|IV Bag|nr}}: Can be used without taking damage, resulting in an infinite amount of coins.
* {{i|Kamikaze!}}: As long as the heart is away from the blast radius, no damage is taken. The character must be at high enough speed for this.
* {{i|Pyromaniac}} / {{i|Host Hat}}: Explosion immunity carries over to the heart.
** The heart must be in range of explosion for Pyromaniac to heal Isaac.
* {{i|Razor Blade|nr}}: Isaac cannot take damage from the Razor Blade, allowing for infinite uses of the item.
* {{i|Sacrificial Altar|a+nr}}: Can remove the Isaac's Heart familiar while the item remains, making Isaac invulnerable.
** {{dlc|r}} Sacrificial Altar now doesn't remove Isaac's Heart.
* {{i|Serpent's Kiss}}: Isaac can poison enemies by contact without taking damage, allowing for free black hearts.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Aries|r}}: The invulnerability does not extend to the heart.
* {{T|Baby-Bender}}: The heart's tears do not gain homing.
* {{i|BFFS!|dlc=r}}: Fires additional shots in random directions, and leaves larger puddles of creep.
* {{i|Dry Baby|nr}}: If Isaac has obtained Dry Baby in the first familiar spot ''before'' Isaac's Heart, the baby will block enemy tears before they can hit the heart. Enemies touching the heart can still do damage, and picking up the baby after the heart will cause the heart's hitbox to be checked first against shots.
** {{dlc|r}} Isaac's Heart no longer follows Isaac in a way where Dry Baby can constantly block it from tears.
* {{i|Farting Baby|anr}}: If Isaac has obtained Farting Baby in the first familiar spot ''before'' Isaac's Heart, the baby will block enemy tears before they can hit the heart. Enemies touching the heart can still do damage, and picking up the baby after the heart will cause the heart's hitbox to be checked first against shots.
** {{dlc|r}} Isaac's Heart no longer follows Isaac in a way where Farting Baby can constantly block it from tears.
* {{i|King Baby|a+nr}}: The Heart will follow King Baby. This makes it much harder to avoid damage, but also makes other synergies like {{i|Kamikaze!}} much easier to use.
* {{I|A Pound of Flesh}}: Consumables can no longer be picked up in Shops.
* {{i|Sharp Plug|nr}}: Sharp Plug can no longer be used.
* {{i|The Soul}}: Isaac's body repels projectiles, but Isaac's Heart doesn't.
* {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}: The heart follows Tainted Soul.

sections.Effect:
* Combined with {{i|Key Piece 2}}, unlocks the golden gate in the starting [[Rooms|room]] of {{S|Chest}} and {{S|Dark Room}} to fight {{E|Mega Satan}}.
* Increases the chance of finding an {{R|Angel Room}}.
* Grants a 2.5% chance of converting {{E|Red Heart}} pickups into {{E|Eternal Heart}}s.
** This effect stacks with {{i|Key Piece 2}}.
sections.Notes:
* This item is a guaranteed drop from {{E|Uriel}} if not already in possession.
* This item, along with {{i|Key Piece 2}}, can be rerolled into any item from the [[Item Pool#Angel Room|Angel Room pool]].
* This item also counts as a [[familiar]], meaning it takes up a familiar slot.
* Unlocking the Golden Gate with the combined key pieces and then restarting the floor with {{i|Forget Me Now}} or an {{R|I AM ERROR}} room will waste the key, which will not respawn.
* Will not be rerolled by {{i|D4}}, {{i|D100}}, or {{R|Dice Room}} effects.
* Will not be doubled by {{i|Box of Friends}}
* Picking up two copies with {{I|Diplopia}} will not double its{{E|Eternal Heart}} effect.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Key Piece 1 having the lowest priority at {{dlc|nr+}} 6th / {{dlc|r+}} 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|nr}} Transforms all {{e|Bomb}}s, {{e|Key}}s, {{e|Penny|text=Pennies}}, and {{e|Red Heart}}s into their respective Double versions.
* {{dlc|r}} All {{e|Bomb}}s, {{e|Key}}s, {{e|Penny|text=Pennies}}, and {{e|Red Heart}}s have a 50% chance to be replaced by their respective Double versions.
sections.Notes:
* Only works specifically on {{e|Bomb}}s, {{e|Key}}s, {{e|Penny|text=Pennies}}, and {{e|Red Heart}}s; other variants, like {{e|Nickel}}s or {{e|Soul Heart}}s, etc., are not doubled.
* {{dlc|nr}} By bombing {{e|Donation Machine}}s, Isaac can earn more money than is taken from the machine, giving an endless supply of coins until the machine breaks or he runs out of bombs.
* {{dlc|nr}} When used while fighting {{e|Greed}}, {{e|Hanger}}s, or {{e|Keeper}}s, every coin knocked out of Isaac will be worth two coins, allowing Isaac to net a profit.
* {{dlc|r}} Coins dropped when taking damage from enemies such as {{e|Greed}}, {{e|Hanger}}s, or {{e|Keeper}}s have a chance to be doubled, allowing Isaac to potentially recover all lost money or even net a profit.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Contract From Below}}: Single pickup drops have a 2/3 chance to be doubled, which then become their doubled versions by Humbling Bundle.
** This results in an average increase from 1.33x more pickups to {{dlcalt|2.67x|r=2x}} more.
* {{I|IV Bag}} + {{i|Old Bandage}} + {{i|Humbleing Bundle}} / {{i|Maggy's Bow}}: The damage from IV Bag has a chance to spawn 2 hearts, which can be picked up to create further coins and possibly even heal hearts with enough Luck.
** {{dlc|r}} Humbleing Bundle only has a 50% chance to double the hearts dropped, but Old Bandage may still drop 1 heart.
* {{i|The Jar|nr}}: Allows for replicating hearts. Using the jar with 4 hearts inside it will cause 8 to drop, allowing Isaac to create an infinite amount of Red Hearts.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BOGO Bombs|nr}}: No further effect.
** {{dlc|r}} Due to Humbleing Bundle no longer guaranteeing double pickups, BOGO Bombs will ''always'' double bombs.
* {{i|Humbleing Bundle}}: No further effect if multiple copies are obtained.

sections.Effect:
* Upon use, creates an explosion on Isaac's position.
** The explosion damages Isaac for half a heart of [[health]] (or a full heart in [[Chapter 4]] onward).
** {{dlc|nr}} The explosion deals 40 damage.
** {{dlc|r}} The size and damage of the Kamikaze! explosion is identical to that of a {{I|Mr. Mega}} bomb, dealing 185 damage in a wide radius.
sections.Notes:
* The explosion will damage {{e|Soul Heart}}s before {{e|Red Heart}}s, unlike most other self-damaging active items.
* Despite the explosion usually damaging Isaac, Kamikaze! is not considered a self-damaging item because it is not the item's use which causes the damage, but rather the resulting explosion. This has a few consequences:
** Kamikaze! does not bypass invincibility, which means items such as {{i|Holy Mantle}} or {{i|Tooth and Nail}} work normally.
** {{dlc|nr}} {{r|Devil Room}}/{{r|Angel Room}} chance is lowered if red heart damage is taken.
** {{dlc|r}} {{r|Devil Room}}/{{r|Angel Room}} chance will not be lowered if red heart damage is taken.
* Kamikaze!'s cool down length is as long as the invincibility frames Isaac normally gets from being hit. This means that Isaac cannot activate Kamikaze!, and then activate Kamikaze! again before the invincibility frames end.
* Synergizes with many bomb-enhancing items such as {{i|Bob's Curse}}, with exceptions listed in Interactions.
sections.Synergies:
* {{t|Blind Rage}}: With longer invincibility, Isaac can use Kamikaze! a second time without taking damage.
* {{Book of Belial synergy|description=Invokes the effect of {{i|The Necronomicon}} effect along with the original effect.}}
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns wisps in the middle ring that looks like small sticks of dynamite. The wisps fire explosive projectiles and explode when destroyed, dealing 30 damage to enemies that are close to it. This explosion is small enough to not always hit Isaac, although it will hurt him should he get caught in it. All explosions the wisps make are unaffected by {{I|BFFS!}} and bomb synergies. Using Kamikaze! will also trigger an explosion on each dynamite wisp.}}
* {{i|Dark Arts}}: Kamikaze can be used for free while Dark Arts is active.
* {{i|Glitter Bombs}}: Has a chance to drop a [[pickup]] or [[trinket]] each time it is used.
* {{i|Gnawed Leaf}}: Activating Kamikaze will cancel out of the statue state, but Isaac will not be damaged by the resulting explosion.
* {{i|Host Hat}}: Allows unlimited uses without consequences.
* {{i|Mars}}: Isaac is invincible during the dash, allowing for unlimited uses with careful timing.
* {{I|Nancy Bombs}}: Gains the effect of a random bomb synergy each time it is used.
* {{I|Pyromaniac}}: Allows unlimited uses and heals without consequences.
** Each use will heal Isaac for {{dlc|nr}} one full / {{dlc|r}} half a red heart.
* {{I|Scapular}}: Damage from the explosion will trigger Scapular's effect, allowing Isaac to trigger on-damage effects infinitely between rooms.
* {{t|Sigil of Baphomet}}: Isaac can chain-kill enemies without taking explosion damage while the shield is active.
* {{i|Schoolbag|a+nr}}: The cool down before the player can use Kamikaze! again is eliminated when switching items. Depending on how fast the player can push the buttons, Kamikaze! can be used multiple times during Isaac's invincibility frames.
* {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}: Explodes on Tainted Forgotten’s body, meaning that it is safe to use infinitely, so long as Tainted Soul is not within the blast radius.

sections.Effect:
* Spawns a knife handle familiar that follows Isaac.
* Generates a room in {{s|Mines}} / {{s|Ashpit}} II for {{i|Knife Piece 2}} to spawn in.
* Combines with {{i|Knife Piece 2}} to form a knife familiar that launches itself in the direction Isaac shoots, dealing 25 damage to and piercing enemies it hits.
* Launching it at the red door at the end of {{s|Mausoleum}}/{{s|Gehenna}} II will open the door, destroying the knife in the process.
sections.Notes:
* Isaac will remain as The Lost until after he has cleared a room of enemies; it does not matter whether this room is in the mirror world. His normal form will be restored upon entering any room outside the mirror world. This effect can extend to the next floor.
* If you don't have {{i|Holy Mantle}} unlocked on {{C|The Lost}}, you don't get Holy Mantle while in ghost form.
* The red door can alternatively be opened using {{i|Cracked Orb}}, {{i|Sharp Key}}, or {{p|Soul of Cain}}.
* The knife piece can be rerolled, in the event that {{E|Mother}} is not the desired completion mark.
* '''Knife Piece 1''' takes 6th priority on the line of following [[familiar]]s while the knife familiar created from both knife pieces takes 5th priority.
* It's possible to see the Knife Piece 1 multiple times by using {{i|Forget Me Now}} or {{i|R Key}}, allowing you to use the {{i|The D6}} or {{i|Void}} on one of the duplicates while still collecting the other.

* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|The Wretched}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars.
** {{dlc|nr+}} Juicy Sack has 6th priority.
** {{dlc|r+}} Juicy Sack has 8th priority.
sections.Synergies: * {{i|BFFS!}}: Juicy Sack spawns an extra Blue Spider.

sections.Effects:
* Enemy shots that hit Isaac have a 50% chance to be blocked.
** After effectively blocking a projectile, Isaac will briefly flash blue. Isaac in this state can still take damage from another projectile.
** Can block:
*** Fireballs (e.g. from {{E|Crackle}}), but their lines of fire harm Isaac.
*** Fire projectiles (e.g. from {{E|Mega Satan}}).
*** Obstacles thrown by {{E|Polty}} or {{E|Kineti}}.
** Does not block:
*** Explosive projectiles (e.g. from {{E|Gurgle}}).
*** Lasers or beams.
*** Lines of fire from fireballs.
*** Projectiles from {{E|Big Bony}}, {{E|Coal Boy}}, {{E|Danny}}.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Mask of Infamy}}.{{dlc-}}
* Although the mask is seen only on Isaac's face, projectiles still have a 50% chance to be blocked from any direction.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Cone Head}}: Blocking effect from either item can occur.
** This leaves Isaac 60% chance to negate tears.
* {{P|Holy Card}} / {{I|Holy Mantle}}: Infamy's chance of blocking projectiles is applied before the shield, allowing the shield to be saved.
* {{I|Host Hat}}: Infamy's blocking effect is applied first. Host Hat does not fire tears when a tear is blocked by Infamy.
** This leaves Isaac 60% chance to negate tears in any way.
* '''Infamy''': Additional copies of this item, such as from {{I|Diplopia}} / {{I|Crooked Penny}}, have no effect.
* {{I|Metal Plate}}: Infamy's blocking effect is applied first. Tears blocked by Infamy are not reflected by Metal Plate.
** This leaves Isaac 62.5% chance to negate tears in any way.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a [[familiar]] who follows Isaac around and fires copies of Isaac's tears with reduced size (or width for some special attacks).
** {{Dlc|nr}} Incubus' tears ignore Isaac's range and shot speed.
** {{dlc|r}} Incubus' damage is reduced by 25% when playing as characters other than {{C|Lilith}} and {{C|Tainted Lilith|n}}.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{transformation contribution|Conjoined}}{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* Lilith's starting Incubus is technically not a collected item but an intrinsic part of the character, and is removed if an item such as {{i|Ankh}} or {{i|Clicker}} are used to become a different character. As such, playing as Lilith will not add Incubus to the [[collection page]], nor does her personal Incubus count towards the {{tf|Conjoined}} transformation.
* Incubus is one of the familiars that can be spawned by {{i|Cambion Conception}}. However, receiving one in this way does not count towards Conjoined.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Incubus having 2nd priority.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Dlc|nr}} {{C|Azazel}} / {{i|Brimstone}}: Fires a full-length Brimstone laser that can be charged while still firing the previous laser, allowing it to fire more rapidly than normal.
** The laser fired by Incubus has the same width as {{i|Lil Brimstone}}'s.
** {{Dlc|r}} When playing as {{C|Azazel}}, Incubus' Brimstone laser has the same range as him.
** {{Dlc|r}} Multiple copies of {{I|Brimstone}} will not grant Incubus the mega brimstone effect.
* {{Dlc+|r}} {{I|Berserk!}} / {{C|The Forgotten}} / {{I|Spirit Sword}}: Incubus will carry the respective melee weapon, using it exactly like Isaac.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Shoots tears that do {{Dlcalt|2x|r=1.5x (2x as {{c|Lilith}})}} Isaac's damage.
* {{I|Cursed Eye|a+nr}}: A burst of 3 tears is fired at the regular tear delay without needing to charge.
** {{dlc|r}} Incubus now charges and fires a burst of up to 5 tears just as Isaac would.
* {{t|Forgotten Lullaby}}: Doubles the fire rate of Incubus. This notably makes it fire and charge-attack faster than Isaac does.
* {{i|Immaculate Heart}}: Incubus can create its own orbiting tears, which will orbit the Incubus that created it, and not Isaac.
* {{i|Technology 2|r}}: Incubus can fire the Technology 2 laser too.
* {{i|Tractor Beam|r}}: The Incubus tears will follow the beam. This makes it seem as if the tears come directly from Isaac, even if blindfolded.
** {{dlc|anr}}'''Tractor Beam''' + {{i|Monstro's Lung}}: Also allows the Incubus tears to follow the beam.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns an allied [[Blue Spider]] from each enemy that is killed.
* {{Dlc+|r}}{{transformation contribution|Spider Baby}}{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* Enemies do not spawn Blue Spiders when killed by anything not controlled by Isaac (environmental hazards, charmed enemies, death upon clearing room, etc).
* Enemies do not spawn Blue Spiders when killed by Blue Spiders.
* Blue Flies can also spawn Blue Spiders.
* Enemies killed by [[familiar]]s will spawn Blue Spiders.
* {{dlc|nr}} Destroyed {{e|Shopkeeper}}s will spawn Blue Spiders.
* Destroying normally invulnerable enemies such as {{e|Poky}} will spawn Blue Spiders.
* {{dlc|nr}} Killing {{E|Pin}} will give one Blue Spider for each of his segments.
* {{E|Dark Ball}}s spawned by {{E|Little Horn}} can also drop Blue Spiders upon death.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Enemies that are turned into [[pickup]]s can’t spawn spiders.
* {{i|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Enemies that are turned into poop can’t spawn spiders.
* {{I|Jar of Flies}}: Blue Flies spawned by Jar of Flies spawn Blue Spiders, and Blue Spiders spawned by Infestation 2 grant extra flies for Jar of Flies

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, Isaac farts, [[charm]]ing all nearby enemies.
** {{dlc|nr}} The cloud deals 5 damage.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|Car Battery}}: Spawns two charming farts on top of each other {{dlc|nr}} and the cloud deals double damage.

sections.Effects: * Grants an active item charge every 15 enemies killed.
sections.Notes:
* Destroying a {{E|Shopkeeper}} will count as an enemy killed.
* Multiple copies of this item do not grant more charges.
sections.Synergies: * {{i|Jacob's Ladder}} / {{i|120 Volt}}: Increases the amount of arcs a spark can generate.
sections.Interactions:
* {{dlc|r}}[[Cards and Runes|Ace Cards]]: Enemies that are turned into [[pickup]]s don't count towards the kills needed to grant an active item charge.
* {{i|E. Coli}}/{{i|Flush!}}: Turning enemies into poop doesn’t count towards the kills needed to grant an active item charge.
* {{dlc|r}}[[Freeze|Freeze Effects]]: Enemies that die from being frozen don't count towards the kills needed to grant an active item charge.
** {{dlc|r+}} Frozen enemies do contribute to the charge counter.
* {{i|Isaac's Tears}}: No effect.

sections.Effects:
* Isaac's tears decelerate as they travel. Upon stopping or hitting an obstacle, they burst into tears that fly in all directions. Hitting an enemy will not cause them to burst.
** {{dlc|nr}} They burst into 8 tears.
** {{dlc|r}} They burst into 5-8 tears, depending on tear size.
* Tears can be fired into other tears to feed them, increasing their damage and the damage of the burst tears.
** If one tear is fed 5 other tears, it will immediately burst.
** The tears will have their damage added together, with the first consumed tear giving additional damage.
** Tears in the burst will deal half the damage the main tear would have.
** This also applies to [[Familiar]] tears.
sections.Notes:
* Certain items that cause tears to split and feed each other, when combined, can cause the resulting tear to become so large that the game will crash.
* Tears can also burst from shot size. With sufficiently high damage or several tear-size increasing items, the tears will burst almost immediately after firing.
* The distance burst tears fly depends on [[tear height]] and not [[range]].
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|20/20}} / {{i|The Inner Eye}} / {{i|Mutant Spider}}: Tears tend to clump together soon after firing for high damage shots. It may take more than 5 tears in total to cause a burst.
* {{I|Akeldama}}: Akeldama tears can feed and be fed by the Lachryphagy tears. Fed Akeldama tears will gain increased damage but will not burst, and will cap at 5 tears fed each.
* {{i|Bob's Rotten Head}}: The head act as a tear, dividing itself if enough time has passed and interacting with other tears. The five heads coming from the main head deal half damage. Feeding a head with another increases damage by the amount of damage Isaac has. If a tear is fed with a head, the tear will gain the head's damage.
* {{i|Book of Virtues}} / {{i|Jar of Wisps}}: Wisps' tears can feed the Lachryphagy tears.
* {{dlc|r}} {{i|Brimstone}}: Brimstone's range is now limited, but [[piercing]] Lachryphagy tears will quickly form at the end of the beam.
** {{c|Azazel}}: Lachryphagy effectively leaves Azazel's brimstone unchanged given it already has limited range.
** {{i|Rubber Cement}}: Reflected brimstone will still have its full range.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}}: Bone tears split into a random spread of fractured tears and bone tears.
* {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Fed tears split into 12 tears.
* {{I|Dead Eye}} Firing into the floating tear won't reset the multiplier as long as that tear doesn't hit a wall.  The burst tears will never reset the multiplier.
* {{I|Euthanasia}}: Needle shots will allow the tears to burst at least twice.
* {{I|Eye of Belial}}: Tear burst retains Eye of Belial's effect, greatly increasing the effectiveness of the tear burst due to the [[piercing]], [[spectral]], and increased tear damage. By proxy, piercing, spectral, and continuum tears all improve the value of Lachyphagy.
* {{I|Evil Eye}}: can compound tears with Lachryphagy.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Tears look like Haemolacria. They can be fed and will burst into 8 tears that have Haemolacria's burst effect upon hitting obstacles or enemies.
** {{Dlc|r}} '''Haemolacria''' + {{I|Brimstone}} / {{i|Tech X}} / {{I|Technology}}: The tears behave like Lachryphagy tears. On hitting enemies, they always burst into respective Lachryphagy-synergized lasers (if available), but on hitting a wall or an obstacle, slower-moving shots burst into normal shots and faster ones into lasers.
* {{i|Kidney Stone}}: When a barrage of tears is fired, tears clump together and burst at a high rate. The stone also behaves as a Lachryphagy tear. Because of the [[tear height]] decrease, burst tears cover much shorter distance before falling, making the combination less effective.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: Both the original tear and the burst tears can block enemy shots. The tears' size is increased, so it is easier to feed them.
* {{i|A Lump of Coal}}: Tears continually grow in size without being fed other tears, but they will still only deal bonus damage based strictly on how far they travel. Burst tears will still grow in size and damage as they travel.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung}} / {{i|Lead Pencil}}: The tears clump together soon after firing, causing potentially up to 20x tear damage on a direct hit on an enemy.
* {{I|My Reflection}}: Causes tears to float back towards Isaac and clump together with any tears they come along.
* {{t|Pulse Worm}}: The fluctuating hitboxes of the tears causes them to clump together at a faster rate.
* {{I|Revelation}}: The beam's range is now limited, but [[piercing]] Lachryphagy tears will form at the end of it.
* {{i|Sinus Infection}}: Boogers will always burst into more boogers, though some of the boogers may incorrectly appear to be normal tears. When a booger sticks to an enemy, it will burst into 8 boogers which have a high chance of sticking again to the same enemy.
* {{dlc|r}} {{i|Technology}}: Technology's range is now limited, but [[piercing]] Lachryphagy tears will form at the end of the beam.
* {{Dlc|r}} {{I|Technology 2}}: Significantly shortens the range of the laser. A [[piercing]] Lachryphagy tear spawns at the end of the laser every tick, rapidly feeding off of each other and bursting when standing still. This is an extremely powerful combo that alone can provide enough damage output to challenge any boss in the game.
** A fire rate reduction such as from {{i|The Inner Eye}} or a few [[Tears Down]] pills makes the combo even stronger, as tears will grow even larger before bursting.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: {{dlc|nr}} Tears will orbit until they are behind the character. Tears will burst into 8 tears that follow the orbit in 2 close groups of 4. One group travels clockwise and the other travels counterclockwise.
** {{dlc|r}} Tears orbit the player without slowing down, and can be fed as normal. When a tear bursts, the created tears orbit the place of burst.
* {{i|Tractor Beam|nr}}: All split tears will travel along the beam.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Trisagion}}: Trisagion tears will fade faster, but will constantly spit out more [[piercing]] Lachryphagy tears while they are active.{{dlc-}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Brimstone|nr}}: Lachryphagy does not affect regular Brimstone beams, but tears from other sources such as {{i|Isaac's Tears}} or {{i|Fate's Reward}} will burst into 8 Brimstone beams. Lachryphagy affects Chocolate Milk + Brimstone.
* {{p|Chaos Card}}: Counts as a tear and will be wasted if thrown into another tear.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Overrides Lachryphagy.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Overrides Lachryphagy.
* {{i|Flat Stone}}: Overridden by Lachryphagy.
* {{I|Ipecac}}: Lachryphagy tears will burst into ipecac shots and explode. The Ipecac tear burst will travel like a normal tear instead of an arc. Due to tear slowdown effect it becomes hard to hit enemies without standing in the explosion radius.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Overrides Lachryphagy.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: No effect.
* {{i|Pop!}}: Tears behave erratically, with freshly fired tears usually behaving like Lachryphagy and burst tears like Pop!.
* {{i|Saturnus}}: Orbiting tears are Lachryphagy tears, including enemy tears caught in orbit. Tears will still burst after a set duration, greatly the reducing the amount of time the tears orbit for. Burst tears will remain in an orbital path instead of spreading out.
* {{i|Stop Watch}} / {{i|Broken Watch}} / {{p|Era Walk}}: Tears are slowed/sped up along with enemies.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Overrides Lachryphagy.
* {{i|Technology|nr}}: Overrides Lachryphagy.
* {{i|Technology Zero}}: Tears will generate arcs of electricity until they burst. As the tears will hang in the air for several seconds, this significantly increases the uptime of electricity arcs. Burst tears are similarly connected to each other by electricity. 
* {{i|Trisagion|nr}}: Tears will split but cannot be grown by feeding tears.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a {{E|Hush}} [[familiar]] that floats and travels diagonally around the [[Rooms|room]], bouncing on walls, and deals contact damage to enemies. While firing tears, Hushy stops moving. In this state, it will:
** Block enemy projectiles.
** {{dlc|r+}} Fire out rings of 8 blue projectiles that deal 6 damage each, once every 1.033 seconds.
* Hushy deals 2 contact damage per tick or 30 damage per second.
sections.Notes:
* Hushy can be pushed by explosions, both while stationary and during movement (in this case, the explosion may cause the familiar to change the direction it is moving in).
* {{dlc|r+}} Although Hushy can float over obstacles, its projectiles are not [[spectral]], meaning its shots will be blocked if it's positioned directly over a rock.

* Key Bum will not pick up {{e|Golden Key}}s.
* {{dlc|a+nr}} Key Bum will pick up {{E|Charged Key|n}} without additional benefit.
** {{dlc|r}} Key Bum will leave a {{E|Lil' Battery}} behind when picking up {{E|Charged Key|n}}.
* {{dlc|nr}} From a scoring perspective, Keys that Key Bum picks up count towards your Schwag bonus on daily runs.
* Key Bum does not join the line of familiars that follow behind Isaac.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Familiar is bigger and drops chests more often.
* {{T|Flat Penny}}: Chests frequently contain pennies, which have a chance of spawning more keys for Key Bum to pick up, possibly lead to a loop.
* {{i|King Baby}} / {{t|RC Remote}}: No effect.
* {{T|Gilded Key}} / {{T|The Left Hand}}: Works as expected.
* {{I|Guppy's Eye}}: Allows Isaac to choose which Locked Chests are worth opening and which to pass, thus saving keys. Great for min-maxing.
