sections.Effects:
* Upon use, picks up the [[Obstacles|obstacle]] in front of Isaac. The obstacle can be thrown at enemies, dealing 40 damage and breaking on impact, dropping any contents they may contain.
** Obstacles can be carried between rooms.
** Using it on a {{E|Host}} / {{e|Mobile Host}} will lift the shell off and transform it into a {{E|Red Host}} / {{e|Flesh Mobile Host}}. Isaac can throw the shell after picking it up.
*** The affected hosts will still fire 3 shots instead of 5.
** Isaac can throw bombs using this, either his bombs or {{e|Troll Bomb}}s.
*** {{E|Golden Troll Bomb}}s grant Isaac unlimited bombs for the floor as they can be carried through rooms this way.
** {{C|Tainted Forgotten}} can be picked up by any other player using it.
* {{transformation contribution|Yes Mother?}}
sections.Notes:
* The item will cost 10 cents if found in a {{r|Shop}}.
* Throwing a {{E|Throwable Bomb}} or Poops and bombs created by {{c|Tainted ???}} and {{i|IBS}} counts as using the bracelet, using up a charge.
* The item's charge will only be depleted once an object is thrown.
** Activating the item again will drop the picked up obstacle where Isaac is standing without consuming a charge. This doesn't damage Isaac directly, but any break effects the obstacle has can still occur.
*** This makes it easy to quickly clear paths through large amounts of rocks.
*** While the dropped obstacle is falling toward the ground, it can be picked up again by activating Mom's Bracelet.
**** Obstacles thrown by enemies, such as {{E|Polty|text=Polties}}, can be caught in the same way.
* Spiked rocks cannot be picked up, even if their spikes are retracted.
* Similarly, [[Blocks#Metal Blocks|Metal Blocks]], [[Blocks#Key Blocks|Key Blocks]] and [[Blocks#Pillars|Pillars]] also cannot be picked up.
* Thrown Poops deal less damage when they are more degraded.
* Throwing a [[Poops|Giant Poop]] at an enemy deals 320 damage instead of 40.
* Activating the item while running into a {{g|Red Poop}} will allow Isaac to chuck it and effectively remove it from the room.
* Poops created by {{c|Tainted ???}} and {{i|IBS}} can be picked up and thrown again freely. You can carry them between rooms and using Mom's Bracelet while holding one will drop them on top of Isaac without destroying them.
** Unlike other obstacles, dropping them under a pit will spawn them to the nearest open space available. 
** Picking up a Corn Poop, will cause the blue flies to follow Isaac, but Corn Poop will not spawn more flies unless the ones around Isaac get used. 
** Rapidly dropping and picking up a Stinky Poop in one spot will create a potent fart cloud, which when detonated deals a lot of damage.
* While carrying a rock, Isaac cannot drop down a trapdoor to the next floor. This can be used as a way to get pickups close to an open trapdoor without accidentally dropping to the next floor.
sections.Synergies:

sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|a+}} This item has a 1% chance to spawn when bombing {{e|Mom's Dressing Table}}. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method.{{dlc-}}
* Despite granting the [[Yes Mother?]] transformation, duplicated items will not contribute to unlocking Mom's Contacts. Three '''different''' items are required to unlock it.
* The chance to fire a petrifying tear depends on the [[luck]] stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\min(\frac1 { 5 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.15 \right \rfloor},50\%)</math>
** At base Luck (0), the chance is 20%, maxing out at 50% at 20 Luck.
* Petrifying the Heart of a {{E|Mask + Heart}} also freezes the Mask bound to it.
* Petrifying an enemy with a weak zone ({{E|Scolex}} or {{E|Carrion Queen}}) will make the enemy take damage anywhere while it is petrified, making combat significantly easier.
sections.Synergies:

sections.Effects:
* +0.4 [[speed]].
* Opens most doors after entering a room, even in rooms with enemies, allowing Isaac to leave at any time.
sections.Notes:
* While {{t|Door Stop}} has a similar effect, Mercurius has the added benefit of opening the doors that Isaac did not enter through.
* Does not open the {{r|Boss Rush}} door.
* Does not open any Special Rooms, including those that require [[pickup]]s to unlock. Doors won't be opened even if they were open already (such as {{r|Treasure Room}}s and {{r|Shop}}s on the first floor, {{r|Sacrifice Room}}s, etc.) or have been entered before.
** {{r|Mini-Boss Room}}s, despite looking identical to normal rooms, are considered Special and will not be opened. This makes it possible to distinguish between regular rooms and mini-boss rooms without map-revealing effects (such as {{i|The Compass}}).
* Does not open doors to {{r|Red Room}}s if those doors are created while there are enemies inside the current room.
sections.Synergies:

* {{I|Head of the Keeper}}: With enough patience, [[Coins]] can be gathered infinitely.
* {{c|Tainted Keeper}}: Leaving and re-entering the room allows for unlimited coin farming; however, enemies in rooms Tainted Keeper has already visited will eventually stop dropping coins.

sections.Effects:
* Isaac's tears are replaced by a knife that pierces enemies and can travel through obstacles. Holding down the fire button increases its range and power.
* The knife deals damage 20 times per second upon contact with enemies while Isaac is holding it.
* {{dlc|nr}} The knife deals 2× Isaac's damage while held and 6× damage at the furthest possible point of its throw distance, regardless of the actual maximum range stat.
* {{dlc|r}} Damage dealt by the knife depends on its charge state. The knife deals 2× Isaac's damage when held and 6× damage at about 1/3 of full charge. The knife damage quickly drops to 2× Isaac's damage when returning regardless of charge state. Further charging only increases its maximum range.
* {{transformation contribution|Yes Mother?}}
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc|nr}} Mom's Knife is a [[special item]].
* {{dlc|nr}} The knife can be held and fired diagonally with frame perfect input. This can be done easily with a controller's analog stick or with {{i|Analog Stick}}.
* {{dlc+|r}} The knife can be held and fired diagonally as if Isaac was holding {{i|Analog Stick}}.
** The knife can be fired in any direction if using mouse controls (enabled in options.ini).{{dlc-}}
* The knife will not work in challenges with the [[blindfolded]] effect.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|20/20}} / {{tf|Conjoined}} / {{i|The Inner Eye}} / {{i|Mutant Spider}}: Isaac holds only one, but shoots multiple knives at their typical spread.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Apple!}} / {{i|Tough Love}}: The knife deals increased damage sometimes based on luck.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Brimstone}} / {{i|Sulfur}}: Shooting the knife also shoots a barrage of knives that goes across the screen, with each knife doing 80% ({{dlc|r}} 2×) of Isaac's damage; the extra knives do not return. The longer the charge, the more knives are added. This effect does not work with {{c|Azazel}}'s default mini brimstone. The brimstone-knives do not benefit from {{i|A Lump of Coal}}.
* {{i|Compound Fracture|r}}: The knife creates bone shards while in contact with an enemy.
* {{i|C Section}}: Fetuses hold small knives that spin around them slowly, causing extra damage.
* {{i|Diplopia}} / {{i|Crooked Penny}}: Each additional copy of the item will grant an extra knife that fires slightly diagonally from the original one, up to a maximum of 16. Picking up more than 16 knives won't fire more knives but will still modify the angle at which they're shot.
* {{i|Epic Fetus|a}}: Each explosion shoots 10 knives in a circle from the point of impact.
* {{dlc+|r}}{{i|Euthanasia}} / {{i|Little Horn}}: The knife can sometimes instantly kill enemies or deal extra damage to bosses.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Eye Sore}}: Will occasionally release 1-3 extra knives when shooting Mom's knife.
* {{i|Fire Mind}}: Still applies [[Status Effects#Burn|burning]], but no longer explodes.
* {{i|Flat Stone}}: Knife bounces as it flies away from Isaac, each bounce causing Isaac's tear damage.
* {{i|Fruit Cake}}: The benefits of Fruit Cake still occur, but are short-lived due to the high damage of Mom's Knife.
* {{c|The Forgotten}}: +4 damage. The knife will attach to The Forgotten's bone club, forming a scythe. Increases the size of both the melee swing and the bone throw, and allows a single melee swing to deal damage to an enemy twice instead of just once.
* {{i|Ghost Pepper|a+nr}}: The flames can shoot from Isaac while holding the fire button.
** {{dlc|r}} The flames only shoot when the fire button is released.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{tf|Guppy}}: Knife hits will rarely spawn a blue fly.
** {{dlc|r}} Knife hits will frequently spawn a blue fly.
* {{i|Holy Light|a+}}: Holy Light can trigger on both held and thrown knives.
* {{i|Ipecac|na+r}}: Knife turns green and [[Status Effects#Poison|poisons]] monsters that hit it. Removes Ipecac's damage increase.
** {{dlc|a+nr}} Adds a flat +4 damage instead of Ipecac's +40. Knife turns green and poison monsters that hit it.
** {{dlc|r}} Adds a flat +2 damage and the knife explodes on contact, once per throw. Will not explode while held without throwing and while coming back to the Player after being thrown. Knife turns green and poison monsters that hit it.
*** {{dlc|r}} '''Ipecac''' + {{i|Technology}}: Not recommended. Isaac will always take explosion damage when throwing the knife.
* [[Invulnerability]]: Even though the knife cannot be fired, the knife will deal damage while Isaac is invincible.
* {{i|Jacob's Ladder|r}}: The knife will sometimes generate sparks when hitting an enemy.
* {{i|Lost Contact|nr}}: The knife will block bullets, even when held (similar to {{i|Trinity Shield}} but has a smaller blocking area).
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Isaac controls a floating knife that does 2× Isaac's damage. Tears stat is ignored and damage is dealt at a rate equivalent of 5 tear delay.
** '''The Ludovico Technique''' + '''any multi-shot item''': Isaac controls a floating knife surrounded by additional rotating knives.
*** Losing The Ludovico Technique will leave the additional knives, which are no longer controlled and appear in the same spot in every room.
** {{dlc|nr}} '''The Ludovico Technique''' + {{i|Lost Contact}}: Floating knife loses almost all ability to block bullets, with a tiny area around the hilt that can stop shots.
** '''The Ludovico Technique''' + {{i|Loki's Horns}}: Loses Loki's Horns effect; Isaac controls only one floating knife.
** '''The Ludovico Technique''' + {{i|Brimstone}}: Mom's Knife overrides Brimstone, leaving only the floating knife.
* {{i|Marked|r}}: The knife fires in the direction of the crosshair, charging automatically, with charging time proportionate to the distance of the crosshair from Isaac.
* {{i|Mom's Eye}}: Another knife is permanently behind Isaac, able to deal contact damage. The chance to fire the rear knife is still affected by luck as usual.
* {{i|Mom's Knife|r}}: Isaac shoots one extra knife per additional copy of the item in a spread pattern.
* {{i|Monstro's Lung|a}}: Firing a knife causes several other knives to shoot out in random directions.
* {{i|Mysterious Liquid|a+}}: The knife leaves creep trails while fired.
* {{i|The Parasite|r}}: The knife fires two knives in perpendicular directions from the first point of contact with an enemy. Additional knives can also fire more knives themselves.
** '''The Parasite''' + {{i|Technology}}: Lasers will also split with the knives.
* {{i|Pause}}: Mom's Knife will not stop the pause effect, allowing Isaac to kill or chip bosses easily by standing near them for the duration of the pause effect.
* {{i|Proptosis|nr}}: The Knife deals double damage regardless of range.
** {{dlc|r}} The Knife deals triple damage regardless of range.
* {{i|Spirit Sword}}: Allows the spirit sword to be thrown during charged attacks.
* {{i|Strange Attractor}}: Enemies are pulled towards the knife. The effect is minor while not firing and much stronger while the knife is launched.
* {{c|Tainted Lilith|r}}: Her familiar will carry the knife. When firing once, Gello will not return back to Lilith, instead hanging around stationary. She can drag him around the room and the knife will still deal damage. Pressing any fire button again will whip out Gello, just as normal.
* {{i|Technology|a+nr}} Both the knife and the laser fire normally.
** {{dlc|r}} There is a connecting laser between Isaac and the knife, similar to {{c|The Forgotten}}'s club throw.
* {{i|Tech X|a+nr}}: Both fire normally.
** {{dlc|r}} The knife is fired with a Tech X ring around it, similarly to {{c|The Forgotten}}'s club throw.
* {{i|The Wiz}}: Isaac holds two knives. Knives are shot diagonally.

sections.Effects:

sections.Effects:
* Double tapping a direction makes Isaac quickly dash in that direction.
** Isaac is immune to damage from all sources during the dash, with the exception of {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s, {{e|Devil Beggar}}s, and similar self-damage active items.
*** {{dlc|r+}} At the end of the dash, Isaac gains i-frames that protect him against {{e|Blood Donation Machine}}s and {{e|Devil Beggar}}s damage. They will also not activate if touched during those i-frames.
** The dash deals damage equal to 4× Isaac's [[damage]] + 8.
** The direction of the dash can be angled by holding another button.
** The dash has an approximate 3 second cooldown.
** {{dlc|r+}} If Isaac collides with a wall or obstacle, he releases 8 columns of fire that deal 10 damage and can [[burn]] enemies.
sections.Notes:
* The dash can be used to enter {{R|Curse Room}}s and open {{E|Spiked Chest}}s/{{E|Mimic Chest}}s without taking damage.
* The dash can destroy {{e|Shopkeeper}}s.
* With a controller, tapping the joystick is rather inconsistent, and the dash can often activate by accident. Using the directional pad instead is recommended.
* When Mars's dash is charged, Isaac will occasionally flash brightly, and visible steam will emit from his nose.
* Extra care needs to be taken with this item, as tapping for precise movements too quickly will cause a dash.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Mars' quality is treated as 1 for the purposes of {{I|Bag of Crafting}}.{{dlc-}}
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Camo Undies}}: Can be used to deal damage without breaking the confusion effect.
* {{i|Kamikaze!}}: Kamikaze can be used without taking damage while dashing.
* {{i|A Pony}} / {{i|White Pony}}: Lowers the dash cooldown to approximately 1.5 seconds.
* {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}: Tainted Forgotten will charge on double-tap if Tainted Soul is not holding him. This can be used to let Tainted Forgotten attack enemies from a resting position, or move him away from damaging hazards so Tainted Soul can pick him up.

sections.Effects:
* Grants a charged shot that fires 14 tears in the same fashion as {{E|Monstro}}.
** The attack can be released only when fully charged.
** Each tear deals 100% Isaac's [[damage]].
** Each tear has a random size multiplier between 0.9x to 1.33x, but there is no effect on damage.
* [[Tears]] down: {{Dlc|nr}}Tear Delay × 4.3 / {{Dlc|r}} Fire Rate ÷ 4.3 (roughly 0.23x).
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating {{e|Monstro II}}.{{dlc-}}
* Charge time can be found with the following equation:
: <math>\text{time} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\text{Tear Delay)}) \approx \frac{1}{\text{Fire Rate}}</math>
* Each tear has independant chance to have [[Tear Effects]].
* [[Tear falling speed]] ups will slightly reduce the effective range of Monstro's Lung.
** {{dlc|rnr+}} Since range ups always add to tear falling speed, every range up reduces effective range.
* {{dlc|r}} Multi-shot effects such as {{I|20/20}} or {{C|Keeper}} adds 2.4 tears to the barrage per tear they normally grant. The resulting amount is rounded, and is capped at 50.
* {{dlc|r}} Reaching above 30 fire rate will release the charge automatically when full. Since this is nearly instant, it results in a constant spray of tears.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|20/20}} / {{I|The Inner Eye}} / {{I|Mutant Spider}}:
** {{Dlc|nr}} Adds 2, 5 or 7 tears to the barrage respectively. For the latter two, greatly slows down the charge.
** {{dlc|r}} Adds 2.4 extra tears to the barrage per extra tear added by the item, rounded down to the nearest whole number. For the latter two, greatly slows down the charge.
* {{I|Almond Milk}} / {{I|Soy Milk|dlc=r}}: Fires automatically upon reaching full charge, regardless of fire rate.
* {{I|Anti-Gravity}}: Hover effect is overidden, but tear delay down still applies, which greatly reduces the charge time.
* {{I|Blood Clot}}: All tears are larger, with increased damage (as opposed to every 2nd tear like Blood Clot alone).
** {{Dlc|a+}} Tears have a 50% chance to be Blood Clot tears.
* {{I|Brimstone|dlc=a}}: Brimstone has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Fires 3-5 additional beams in random directions around Isaac. This effect also applies to {{C|Azazel}} and {{C|Tainted Azazel}}'s versions of Brimstone.
** Brimstone + {{I|Eye Sore}}: Overrides this synergy with a chance to shoot 1-3 additional beams in random directions.
* {{I|Chocolate Milk|nr}}: Reduces Isaac's tear delay by 20%, and each tear from Monstro's Lung is a charged Chocolate Milk shot, massively increasing fire rate and damage.
** This does not apply to {{C|Lilith}}'s Incubus; picking up Chocolate Milk will significantly reduce damage and increase charge time.
** {{Dlc|r}} The tear damage and the barrage size scale with charge amount. At 50% charge, the tear damage is 100%, the barrage size reaches 100% and is capped there. At 100% charge, the tear damage is 200%.
*** <math>\text{Charge Time (s)} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\text{Tear Delay} \times \frac{5}{2} + 1)) \approx \frac{5}{2 \times \text{Fire Rate}}</math>
**** This makes damage per second drop to 80%.
* {{I|Dr. Fetus|anr}}: Monstro's Lung has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. Fires 6 bombs which detonate simultaneously.
** {{dlc|r}} Monstro's Lung has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. Fires 6 mini-bombs which detonate at different times. Multi-shot effects add 1 bomb to the barrage, up to 21 bombs.
* {{I|Epic Fetus|dlc=a}}: Epic Fetus has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. 2-4 extra cursors rotate around the main cursor before the missiles land.
* {{I|Eye Sore}}: Adds a chance to fire 1-3 additional barrages in random directions.
* {{c|The Forgotten}}: Melee swing is unaffected, but the throw attack is replaced by the burst attack with small bones instead of tears. Each additional copy of Monstro's lung adds 5 bone clubs in his melee attack, up to a limit of 16. {{c|The Soul}} behaves normally, including the tears down.
* {{I|Flat Stone}}: All tears bounce simultaneously; the effective range is greatly increased.
* {{I|Haemolacria}}: Monstro's Lung has priority. Applies +43 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Monstro's Lung tears down. The barrage size is reduced to 4/7 (roughly 0.57), tears of which all burst.
** The barrage size is 8 without any multi-shot effect. The resulting amount is rounded, and is capped at 29.
* {{i|Immaculate Heart}}: Fires a large number of extra tears alongside the burst that begin orbiting Isaac once they reach the orbit range.
* {{I|Ipecac}}: Fires Ipecac tears, with no increase in charge time.
** {{Dlc|r}} Applies Ipecac's tears down.
* {{I|Technology|dlc=r}}: Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Grants a charged shot, fires 12 lasers in 30° spread that arc 3-4 times. A laser can hit an enemy multiple times between their arcings.
** <math>\text{Charge Time (s)} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\frac{43}{10} (\text{Tear Delay} + 1))) \approx \frac{43}{10 \times \text{Fire Rate}}</math>
*** This is equivalent of applying Monstro's Lung's tears down and its charge time, without actually altering tear delay.
** Multi-shot effects add 12 lasers to the barrage, up to 128 lasers total.
** Technology + {{I|Mysterious Liquid}}: The lasers leave creep each time they arc, resulting in a massive amount of creep.
** Technology + {{I|Proptosis}}: The 6x damage is recovered each time they arc, nearly nullifying the distance penalty.
* {{I|Tech X}}: Fires 3-5 extra rings in 30° spread. Extra rings deal from 50% to 100% damage of the main ring.
** Additional copy of Monstro's Lung adds 3-5 more rings.
** {{Dlc|nr}} Increases Tear Delay.
** {{Dlc|r}} Fire Rate is divided by 3.1.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique|dlc=a}}: The Ludovico Technique has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. A cluster of variably sized tears orbit the main tear.
* {{I|Mom's Knife|dlc=a}}: Mom's Knife has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Fires additional knives depending on charge amount, each dealing 2x tear damage. Fires 3-5 knives at maximum charge.
* {{I|Mom's Wig|nr}}: Charging an attack spawns spiders in rapid succession.
** {{Dlc|r}} Spawns spiders upon firing, not charging. The amount of spiders spawned is dependent on luck.
* '''Monstro's Lung''': Additional copies of this item, such as from {{I|Diplopia}} / {{I|Crooked Penny}}, add {{Dlc|nr}} 10/{{Dlc|r}} 12 tears to the barrage.
** This effects is equivalent of adding {{Dlc|nr}} 4/{{Dlc|r}} 5 multi-shot effects. The items which have priority over Monstro's Lung or override it (e.g. {{I|Brimstone}}/{{I|C Section}}) benefit from this multi-shot effect.
* {{I|My Reflection}}: Tears stay in the air much longer and consistently, allowing better reach and more focused blasts before the tears returning to Isaac.
* {{I|Tractor Beam}}: All the tears follow the beam at different heights without spreading out, making it much easier for multiple tears to hit a target.

sections.Effects:

sections.Notes:

sections.Effects: * Upon use, spawns a random item from the current room's [[Item Pool|item pool]], with a base ~17% chance to spawn {{i|A Lump of Coal}} or {{i|The Poop}} instead.
sections.Notes:
* The chance to get {{i|A Lump of Coal}} or {{i|The Poop}} is determined by [[Luck]] using this formula: <math>\frac2 { 12 + \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck}  \right \rfloor}</math>
** A table showing an example is below. There's no cap, with diminishing returns. At 88 Luck the chance drops to 2%.
{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Luck !! Item Pool !! Poop/Coal
|-
| -10 || 0% || 100%
|-
| 0 || 83.3% || 16.6%
|-
| 8 || 90%|| 10%
|}

* {{I|Sacrificial Altar}}: Baby Plum can be sacrificed for free, instead of a familiar. Plum Flute can still be used as normal afterwards.
sections.Interactions:
* {{T|Baby-Bender}}: No effect.
* {{I|Eraser}}: Plum Flute will still function normally if the boss Baby Plum is erased.

sections.Effects:
* Upon use, deals 9,999,999 damage to every enemy in the room, then kills Isaac 3 seconds later.
* {{dlc+|r+}} Kills Isaac 10 seconds later in {{e|Delirium}}'s room and 11.5 seconds later in {{e|Mother}}'s room.{{dlc-}}
sections.Notes:
* Plan C does not kill both or all phases of bosses like {{E|The Lamb}}, {{E|Hush}}, {{E|Ultra Greed}},  {{E|Mega Satan}}, {{E|Mother}}, and {{E|The Beast}}.
* Some bosses have special interactions with this item:
** {{dlc|nr+}} Attempting to use this item to kill {{E|Delirium}} or {{E|Mother}} will not work. Their death animation is much longer than the time between using Plan C and Isaac's Last Will appearing, meaning Isaac will die first and it will not count as a kill. Having extra lives that revive Isaac outside the room will not help, either; they must be fought again.
*** However, items that revive Isaac in the same room he died in, namely {{I|Lazarus' Rags}} (or being {{C|Lazarus}}), {{I|Inner Child}}, {{P|Soul of Lazarus}}, and {{C|Tainted Lost}}'s {{I|Birthright}}, will allow Isaac to bypass this and kill them with this item. In the case of Lazarus' Rags, though, the completion mark will go toward Lazarus and not the character originally selected.
**** Similarly, if playing as {{C|Tainted Lazarus}}, using Plan C and then using {{I|Flip}} to switch to the other form pauses the death counter until the player switches back to the form that originally used the item.
*** It is possible to kill Delirium by carefully timing pauses after each screen static. Each screen static plays a cutscene that continues to play even while paused, so by pausing and unpausing at the right timings, Delirium's death animation can be shortened to just under 3 seconds allowing for his completion mark to be awarded.
*** Using the effect of Plan C while Isaac is already under the timer of Plan C (such as through the use of another Plan C, {{P|? Card}}, {{P|Wild Card}}, etc.) will reset the timer each use, allowing to stall bosses with long death animations.
** {{dlc|r}} Killing {{E|Mother|n}}'s second phase with Plan C will kill Isaac just at the end of her death animation. No completion mark is awarded.
*** However, if Isaac is revived outside the boss room, the boss will be considered dead and the mark ''will'' be awarded. This does not work for {{C|The Lost}}, {{C|Tainted Lost}}, {{C|The Forgotten}} (when playing as The Soul), and {{C|Tainted Forgotten}} since ghost characters have a slightly shorter death animation.
** {{mode|greedier}} Killing {{E|Ultra Greedier|n}} with Plan C will give a completion mark, with the exception of {{C|The Lost}}, {{C|Tainted Lost}}, {{C|The Forgotten}} (when playing as The Soul), and {{C|Tainted Forgotten}}. This is because ghost characters have a slightly shorter death animation, resulting in Isaac's Last Will appearing more quickly.
** {{Dlc|r}} If used in {{E|The Beast|n}} battle, Plan C will only kill the harbinger that Isaac is fighting on screen. It won't have any effect on the other harbingers nor The Beast itself (The Beast can still be killed if Isaac is fighting it when Plan C is used, and there is enough time to earn the completion mark).
* It is recommended not to use this item in Challenges, as even if the goal is within the bosses that dies before Isaac does, the player will likely die before the end of the rising trophy animation.
* For the game's sake, a run is not truly over until [[Isaac's Last Will]] appears. This means that some bosses that might seem to finish their death animations after Isaac dies, such as Ultra Greed, will still be technically killed and will still give their completion marks, even if Isaac does not enter the Final Boss Chest.
* Invulnerable enemies and closed {{E|Host}}s will not be killed by Plan C.
* Isaac's last will shows his last damage source as the cause of death, not Plan C. If Isaac has not taken damage or lost health from any source, Isaac's face is shown.
* Invincibility or the {{I|Holy Mantle}} shield will not save Isaac from being killed.
* Some items that activate when Isaac reaches zero hearts, such as {{I|Heartbreak}} and {{I|Spirit Shackles}}, will not activate, killing Isaac.
* Even if Isaac enters a trapdoor immediately after using Plan C, he will still die after arriving at the next floor.
** Isaac will also die after accepting a [[Victory Lap]] or performing a [[RERUN]].
* Plan C has an 80% decreased item pool weight, making it less likely to appear than other collectibles.
** {{dlc|r}} It has a 90% decreased weight in the [[Red Chest (Item Pool)|Red Chest pool]], and normal weight in the [[Ultra Secret Room (Item Pool)|Ultra Secret Room pool]].
* {{dlc|nr}} Plan C is found in 6 item pools, the second highest count amongst all items, behind {{I|Cube of Meat}}. Its lowered weight, however, offsets its presence.
** {{dlc|r}} Plan C is found in 8 item pools, the highest count amongst all items. Its lowered weight, however, offsets its presence.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Belial synergy|description=Respawns Judas as {{c|Black Judas}} if he has an extra life.}}
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns 8 red wisps that shoot red tears at 12 damage per tear. Using Plan C will kill Isaac as expected, but wisps won't disappear if used with an item that grants an extra life.}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{dlc|r}} [[Co-op|Multiplayer]]: Only the player who uses Plan C dies.
** If the user dies from other causes before the effects of Plan C can conclude, their ghost will die, resulting in a run loss, regardless of there being other players alive.

sections.Effects: * Gives Isaac a candle familiar that grants a [[Fire Rate]] bonus of +0.4 for each room cleared in a row without taking damage, which stacks up to 5 times (Max. +2 [[Fire Rate]]), represented by how brightly the flame burns. Starts at 1 stack, and resets to zero if damage is taken.
sections.Notes:
* The Fire Rate bonus can exceed the normal Fire Rate cap.
** Any self-damage, such as from {{r|Curse Room}}s, {{r|Sacrifice Room}}s, the [[Bad Trip]] pill, spiked chests, and self-damaging items such as {{i|IV Bag}}, won't reset the bonus.
* Clearing waves in [[Greed Mode]] will give the candle charges as if you cleared rooms.
* [[Familiar]]s that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Paschal Candle having the lowest priority at {{dlc|nr+}} 6th / {{dlc|r+}} 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.
sections.Synergies: * {{i|Holy Mantle}} / any similar item: The flame is not snuffed out when damage is negated by the shield.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: The candle appears larger, but otherwise does not change.
* {{i|Paschal Candle}}: No extra familiars or stat boosts are granted from copies.

sections.Effects:
* Grants one full Red [[Heart container]] when picked up.
* Isaac has a 50% chance to regenerate a {{E|Half Red Heart}} every time the in-game timer hits a new minute (00:01:00, 00:02:00, etc).
* {{Dlc|r}} Heals 1 additional {{E|Red Heart}} when picked up.
sections.Notes:
* This item can rarely drop from destroying [[Rocks#Polyps|polyps]] (outside of {{s|Corpse}}).
* The regeneration can happen multiple times in the same room, so there is no need to move between rooms to continue regeneration.
** {{dlc|nr}} However, regeneration '''does not occur''' when standing in a {{R|Crawl Space}}.
* Regeneration will only occur when Isaac has Red Heart containers or '''something equivalent''':
** {{c|Keeper}}'s and {{c|Tainted Keeper|r}}'s coin hearts will regenerate, one coin at a time.
** {{E|Bone Heart}}s regenerate like red hearts.
** Consequently, characters with no applicable health -- {{c|???}}, {{c|The Lost}}, {{c|Black Judas}}, {{c|Tainted ???}}, {{c|Tainted Bethany}}, {{c|Tainted Judas}},{{c|Tainted Forgotten}}, and {{c|Tainted Lost}}—do not benefit from the effect.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Blood Oath}}: With enough patience, health can be safely restored each floor by waiting in the starting room.
* {{i|Gnawed Leaf}}: Regeneration works while turned to stone, allowing Isaac to become invincible and regenerate while in any room.
* {{i|Sanguine Bond}}: Can be used indefinitely with placenta’s regen. Also works with normal sacrifice rooms.
* {{i|Sharp Plug}}: With enough patience, any active item can be reused indefinitely.
* {{i|Habit}}: Like Sharp Plug, any active item can be reused indefinitely with enough patience. 
* {{i|IV Bag}}, {{i|Piggy Bank}}, {{i|Fanny Pack}}, {{t|Swallowed Penny}}, {{i|Gimpy}}, {{i|Old Bandage}}: Can produce infinite of their respective consumables if given enough time
*{{e|Blood Donation Machine}},{{e|Devil Beggar}} & {{e|Hell Game}}: If given enough time will always reach their item payout.
*{{i|Razor Blade}}: Can be used to stack damage before triggering boss fights that do not automatically trigger upon room entry such as {{e|Hush}}, {{e|Mega Satan}}, or {{e|Dogma}}
*{{t|Cracked Dice}}: Can be used to re-roll items many times in a room if a damage source is present or the player has enough bombs.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Maggy's Bow}}: No effect on regen.
* {{c|Tainted Magdalene}}: Receives 1 full red heart per regen trigger.

sections.Effects:
* {{dlc|nr+}} +1.7 [[tears]].
** Additional copies only grant +0.7 tears.
* {{dlc|r+}} +1.7 [[fire rate]].
** Additional copies only grant +0.7 fire rate.
* +0.3 [[speed]].
* -0.4 [[damage]].
* x0.9 total damage up multiplier.
** This penalty is not a total damage multiplier and applies only to certain "standard" damage ups, the specific details are available in the [[Damage#The_order_that_damage_multipliers_and_flat_damage_are_applied|damage order]] list.
* Decreases Isaac's size.
* {{transformation contribution|Fun Guy}}
sections.Notes:
* There are two collectible items in the game named [[Odd Mushroom]]; they can be told apart from the sprites.
* This item's damage multiplier works differently than other items in the game: instead of directly multiplying the damage stat, it multiplies the total added damage from other items. As a result, flat damage upgrades aren't affected by Odd Mushroom.
** Multiple copies of the item will grant a speed and fire rate boost with no additional decrease in damage.
* Despite only the head part gets smaller visually, Isaac's size also gets smaller. Isaac can walk between some gaps while only the body stays the same size if enough copies of the item are taken.
* {{dlc|r+}} Since the damage penalty doesn't apply to everything and the item grants a straight fire rate bonus instead of tears, it is often an upgrade to total damage output. Some combinations of high tears/fire rate with few or no damage ups will result in DPS down.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a blue fly [[familiar]] that will follow Isaac's movement with a 1-second delay and fires tears at nearby enemies.
** {{dlc|r}} Papa fly follows Isaac on a 0.66 second delay instead.
* Papa Fly's tears deal Isaac's damage, and are fired once per second.
* {{transformation contribution|Beelzebub}}
sections.Notes: * Since Papa Fly's damage scales off of Isaac's own damage, any item that provides a massive damage increase (such as {{i|Ipecac}} or {{i|Polyphemus}}) will prove benefitial.

sections.Effects:
* Summons a ghost near Isaac that will follow him around, and summons a controllable blue crosshair. After a few seconds, the crosshair disappears, and the ghost will act depending on what the crosshair was targeting:
** [[Items]] / [[Pickups]] / [[Trinkets]] / {{e|Chest}}s / {{e|Red Chest}}s / {{e|Spiked Chest}}s / {{e|Mega Chest}}s: Brings it to Isaac.
*** Can steal from {{r|Shop}}s, {{r|Devil Room}}s, and {{r|Black Market}}s, making the item/pickup free. Stealing an item has a 33% chance to fail. If that happens, a buzzer sound will play and the ghost will disappear without doing anything.
*** {{dlc|nr}} Stealing an item from a Shop will restock it with another item, as if Isaac had {{i|Restock}}. This does not happen in other room types.
** {{e|Locked Chest}}s / {{e|Eternal Chest}}s / {{e|Bomb Chest}}s: Opens the chest for free.
** {{g|Pressure Plate}}/{{g|Reward Plate}}: Presses the button. This includes the wave pause button in [[Greed Mode]].
** [[Monsters|Enemies]]: Attacks the enemy until it dies or can no longer be targeted due to a form change or similar cause. The ghost does 3 damage per tick, for 9 damage per second.
** [[Rooms#special rooms|Doors]]: Opens the door, even if it is locked. Functions the same as {{I|Dad's Key}} when being used in this way. This includes the door to {{e|Mega Satan}}, exiting {{e|Hush}}'s room, and exiting {{r|Boss Rush}}.
*** {{dlc+|r}} This does not work on {{A|A Strange Door}}. However, it does work on doors leading to alternate path levels.{{dlc-}}
*** {{dlc+|r}} This does not work on the flesh door leading to {{e|Mom's Heart}} that appears after defeating {{e|Mom}} in {{s|Mausoleum}} or {{s|Gehenna}}.{{dlc-}}
*** {{dlc+|r}} This does not work on the hidden closet in {{s|Home}} to unlock the tainted characters.{{dlc-}}
** {{r|Secret Room}} entrances: Explodes, opening the entrance.
** Some destructible [[obstacles]], {{e|Shopkeeper}}s, {{e|Slot Machine}}s, {{e|Beggar}}s, and {{dlc|nr}} [[angel]] statues: Explodes and destroys them.
*** Can't target regular [[rocks]], [[Rocks#Bomb Rocks|bomb rocks]], [[Rocks#Spiked Rocks|spiked rocks]], [[Rocks#Fool's Gold Rocks|fool's gold rocks]], [[blocks]], [[Blocks#Key Blocks|key blocks]], normal and red [[Fire Places|fire places]], any [[Poops|poop]], or {{dlc|r}} [[angel]] statues.
** If the room has nothing to interact with, the ghost will disappear without doing anything.
sections.Notes: * If the crosshair is not targeting anything when the crosshair disappears, the ghost will interact with the object closest to the crosshair. * Picking up a stolen Devil deal will not prevent {{r|Angel Room}}s from appearing. {{dlc|r}} It will also not despawn the other Devil items for characters like {{c|The Lost}}. * The ghost cannot pick up {{e|Sticky Nickel}}s and will disappear upon touching them. * The ghost can open chests in {{r|Challenge Room}}s without triggering the room. * Unlike chests, stealing an item pedestal from a {{r|Challenge Room}} will trigger the waves to spawn upon picking up the stolen item. * In rooms with multiple pedestal items where only one can be taken, if the ghost is carrying a pedestal while Isaac picks up a different pedestal item, the ghost will disappear. This prevents taking both items for free. * {{dlc|nr}} If used in an {{R|Angel Room}} with no item pedestals, Mr. ME! will target the angel statue, blowing it up. * If used with MouseControl=1 enabled, while pressing mouse left button, the blue crosshair will keep going away from the character, not following the mouse. ** Having {{I|Marked}} make the blue crosshair follow the mouse instead. * If the ghost is currently out and moving, putting down Mr. ME! by any means will destroy the ghost and consume the charge.
sections.Synergies: * {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a wisp that looks like a face in the middle ring. The wisp cannot shoot. If the current room is cleared, the wisps automatically move toward and unlock [[chest]]s (Except for  {{e|Bomb Chest}}s and {{e|Mega Chest|n}}s) and special room doors, destroying themselves in the process. The wisps can open almost any locked doors, including the ones to {{e|Mega Satan}}, the [[Ascent]], but excluding {{s|Corpse}}.}}
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|BFFS!}}: Does not increase the ghost's damage when attacking enemies.
* {{I|Car Battery}}: May sometimes glitch pedestal items, resulting in Isaac being unable to pick them up without leaving and re-entering the room. Otherwise has no effect.
* {{i|Flip}}: Ghostly items cannot be targeted.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{i|Restock}}: Stolen items will not be restocked, even in [[Greed Mode]].{{dlc-}}
* {{I|Sack Head}}: If Mr. ME! successfully stole a consumable from the shop, there is a chance he will drop a sack instead.
* {{I|Glitched Crown}}/{{I|Binge Eater}}/{{c|Tainted Isaac}}/{{p|Soul of Isaac}}/{{I|Everything Jar}}: Stealing a cycling item pedestal will give you whichever item is currently present when Mr. ME! picks up the item, making it risky to steal items this way, and entirely unreliable with Glitched Crown

sections.Notes:

* {{dlc|a}} When playing [[Greed Mode]], the normal [[Devil Room (Item Pool)|Devil Room item pool]] is still used in Sheol, instead of the [[Devil Room (Greed Mode Item Pool)|Greed Mode Devil Room item pool]].
* {{dlc+|a+}} In [[Greed Mode]], it will always generate its 2nd floor drops for each Chapter that is before the {{s|Womb}}, such as 20 pennies in the {{s|Depths}}, etc.{{dlc-}}
** The {{s|Womb}} is the exception, generating its 1st floor drop: 2 Boss Room items.

sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{p|? Card}}:
** {{dlc|anr}} Will consume both the card and Pandora's Box, but nothing will happen, wasting both of them.
** {{dlc|r}} Will activate Pandora's Box without consuming it, allowing for multiple activations.

sections.Effects:
* A cone of light shines from Isaac's chest that slows all enemies and enemy shots.
** The light will face the direction Isaac is moving.
** The light doesn't affect [[boss]]es, but it will slow their shots.
** The slow effect will disappear from enemies when the light stops shining on them, but shots will remain slow.
* Removes {{curse|darkness}} for the current floor.
** Doesn't provide immunity on later floors, but lessens the visual effect significantly, effectively removing the curse.
sections.Notes:
* The light only needs to touch a shot once to slow it permanently.
** Doing a quick circular motion is effective to slow surrounding enemy shots, especially while fighting {{E|Hush}}.
** Overuse of this effect can cause unavoidable patterns, as the slowed shots will often still travel most of their original distance.
* {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}'s light will always face right.
* {{dlc|r}} This item is '''not recommended''' against {{E|The Beast|n}}, as the fires spawned by her will be slowed down significantly and pile up quickly, leading to no room to dodge.
* {{dlc+|r}} Doesn't remove Curse of Darkness afflicted by {{p|XIX - The Sun?}}, no matter if Night Light was picked up before or after using the card. However, the visual effect is still lessened by the beam of light.{{dlc-}}

sections.Effects:
* +1.5 [[tears]].
* {{dlc|nr}} -17.62 [[range]].
* {{dlc|r}} -1.5 [[range]] and -20% [[range]] multiplier. Will not decrease range below 4.00.
* {{dlc|nr}} +0.76 [[tear falling speed]].
* Tears turn yellow and are fired from Isaac's lower body rather than his head.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Abyss}}: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Number One it turns into a yellow locust that is faster, deals damage quicker, but has a limited range.
* {{i|Brimstone}} / {{c|Tainted Azazel|r}}: The laser turns yellow and charges at a much faster rate with no decrease to the range.
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Increases fire-rate with no decrease in range. Explosive clouds are now yellow.
* {{i|Incubus|anr}}: The Incubus fires at a much faster rate with no decrease to the range.
** {{dlc|r}}: Incubus' range decreases like normal.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Turns tear yellow and allows it to be moved much faster.
* {{i|Number One}}: Gives an additional fire rate bonus without further reducing range.
* {{i|Pop!}}: Eyeball tears are yellow, can be fired much quicker, and does not affect their airtime.
* {{i|Technology}}: The laser turns yellow and Technology's firing rate is greatly increased with no decrease to the range.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Laser turns yellow, charge time is greatly decreased, and no decrease to the range.
* {{i|Tiny Planet}}: Tears travel a slightly smaller distance but can be fired much quicker.
sections.Interactions:
* {{C|Azazel}}: Lowers range, reduces charge time.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: Tears often disappear before being able to split. Split tears also only travel a very short distance.
* {{i|Cricket's Body}}: Tears disappear '''very''' quickly after being fired, and split tears barely travel at all.
** {{dlc|r}} '''Not recommended.''' Number One's x0.8 range multiplier stacks with Cricket's Body's own x0.8 range multiplier, thus drastically reducing range.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: '''Not recommended.''' Makes bombs travel distance very short. The extremely reduced range can turn simple rooms into a challenge and self-damage a constant concern.
* {{i|Haemolacria}}: Does not affect the main tear; however, burst tears travel significantly less far.
** {{dlc|r}} '''Not recommended.''' Number One's x0.8 range multiplier stacks with Haemolacria's own x0.8 range multiplier, thus drastically reducing range.
* {{i|Ipecac}}: Increases fire rate moderately, and decreases range only slightly.
** {{dlc|r}} '''Not recommended.''' Number One's x0.8 range multiplier does stack with Ipecac's own x0.8 range multiplier, making self-damage more likely.
* {{i|Kidney Stone}}: The stone is not affected by short range, otherwise the combo behaves as expected. {{dlc|nr}} Number One's range penalty overrides Kidney Stone's.
* {{i|A Lump of Coal}}: Tears still increase in size and damage as they travel; however, the short-ranged distance limits tear size and damage.
* {{i|Marked}}: Tears become orange. The firing rate is increased, Marked's effect is unaffected but the range is reduced.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The knife turns yellow and the maximum range is significantly reduced.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{i|Monstro's Lung}} / {{i|Lead Pencil}}: '''Not recommended.''' Tear barrage disappears very close to Isaac.
** {{dlc|r}} Range is more forgiving.
* {{i|Proptosis|nr}}: '''Not recommended.''' Tears disappear after traveling a very short distance.
** {{dlc|r}} This is now fixed and works as expected.
* {{i|Rubber Cement}}: Tears often disappear before being able to bounce off walls.
* {{i|Tooth Picks}}: Tears become orange.

sections.Effects:
* At 0 Luck and with no other modifiers, reduces the chance for a room clear to give no reward from 22% to 16%.
* Whenever a room clear reward spawns, a different alternative reward is spawned next to it. Picking up either reward causes the other to disappear.
sections.Notes:
* If one of the rewards is a troll bomb, picking up the other reward will not make the troll bomb disappear. Likewise, the other reward will not disappear if the troll bomb blows up.
* If one of the consumables generated by this effect is a heart, converting it with {{t|Apple of Sodom}} or {{c|Keeper}} will not cause the other consumable to disappear.
* If one of the consumables generated is a {{E|Haunted Chest}} and is picked up and thrown by the {{E|Polty}} (thus opening it), picking up the contents of the chest will not make the other consumable disappear, and taking the other consumable will only make the opened chest disappear.
** Killing the Polty after it awakens but before it can properly pick up the chest will result in the other reward disappearing, however.
* If one of the consumables is a {{e|Bomb Chest}}, blowing it up and picking up its contents will not make the other consumable disappear, and taking the other consumable will only make the opened chest disappear.
** However, this doesn't apply if the {{e|Bomb Chest}} has an item in it. Taking the other consumable will cause the Stone Chest item to disappear and vice versa.
* Unlike item-based Options effects like {{i|There's Options}}, it is not possible to take both consumables as {{c|Jacob and Esau}}, with {{i|Strawman}}, or in [[Co-op|True Co-op]]. One consumable will always disappear even if both are collected at the same time.
sections.Synergies:
* {{T|Broken Padlock}}: Bombing any chest spawned by Options?, including the ones not requiring keys, allows picking up the contents of the chest without the other reward disappearing, unless the empty chest is touched. This can be easily avoided by simply exiting and reentering the room.
* {{I|Contract From Below}}: Spawns a second set of consumables. The "Options?" consumable is not guaranteed to be the same for each copy of the original consumable. Each pair of consumables functions independently for "Options?", meaning Isaac can pick up one of the first two rewards and one of the second two rewards.
* {{i|Deep Pockets}}/{{t|Old Capacitor}}: Every extra coin or battery generated will have its own alternative reward.
* {{T|Equality!|nr+}}: While Equality! is active, both rewards can be collected without the other despawning. Options? also makes Equality! easier to keep active.
* {{i|Guppy's Eye}}: Takes the guesswork out of choosing between a chest/sack and a pickup by allowing you to see what the chest/sack will give.
* {{i|Guppy's Tail}}: Gives a choice between a golden chest and something else in case Isaac is low on keys.
* {{i|Magneto}}: Opening a chest does not make the other reward disappear. Picking up the other reward afterwards will only remove the empty chest, and picking up the contents of the chest will not make the other reward disappear, letting Isaac take both rewards. This does not apply to chests with items in them, which disappear or make the other reward disappear as normal. Touching a chest will still make the other reward disappear.
** Magneto + {{i|Broken Modem}}: If Broken Modem duplicates a chest that was spawned by Options?, using Magneto to immediately open the chest while in its glitched form will create a {{i|TMTRAINER}} item if the chest contained an item.
* {{t|Safety Scissors}}: If a {{e|Troll Bomb}}/{{e|Mega Troll Bomb}}/{{E|Golden Troll Bomb}} is turned into another form of bomb, it can be picked up without causing the other reward to despawn.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Bag of Crafting}}: Only one of the rewards can be grabbed.
* {{I|Broken Modem}}: If the room drops are doubled, only the original set is affected by "Options?"; both consumables of the duplicate set can be collected.
** Caution should be approached if you take this item and {{I|Magneto}} when you're in {{S|Chest}} or {{S|Dark Room}}, as there's a chance the chest will "glitch" out via Broken Modem and opening it during the "glitching" will turn the item into a glitched item, as if it was spawned by {{I|TMTRAINER}}.<ref>https://youtu.be/xCWYBb2VREU?t=97</ref>
* {{i|Bum Friend}}, {{i|Bumbo}}, {{i|Dark Bum}}, {{i|Key Bum}}, and the familiar gained from the {{tf|Super Bum}} transformation will cause other items to disappear when they take their respective pickups.
* {{i|D20}}: Can re-roll both pickups created by Options?, but only one can still be taken.
* {{i|Glyph of Balance}}: Only one of the rewards is modified by the Glyph.
* {{i|Moving Box}}: One of the pickups will disappear when using Moving Box.
* {{p|IX - The Hermit?}}: Only one of the rewards will be "sold".

sections.Effects:

* {{dlcalt|+0.3|r=+1}} [[damage]].
* {{dlcalt|+0.25|r=+1.5}} [[range]].
* {{dlc|nr}} +0.5 [[tear falling speed]].
* {{dlcalt|-0.1|r=-0.2}} [[speed]].
* Makes Isaac's head larger, which on its own is only a visual effect.

sections.Notes: * There are two collectible items in the game named [[Odd Mushroom]]; you can tell them apart from the sprites, or in the case of {{curse|blind}}, by looking at the change in Isaac's stats (usually health is the most noticeable).
sections.Interactions: * {{i|The Virus|nr}}: The speed down from the Virus does not stack with the Odd Mushroom; if both are collected, only a total of -0.1 applies.

sections.Effects:
* While Isaac is not firing tears, a charge bar will start to fill up. Holding down the fire button will release the stored tears rapidly. The fire rate is greater and the bar drains faster when more full.
* The charge time and maximum tears per charge scale with Isaac's [[tears]] stat, with higher tears charging faster and having more of them.
sections.Notes:
* While at 0 charge, Isaac fires at his normal tear delay, meaning there is no downside.
* This item has no effect for {{C|Tainted Lilith}} or {{c|Tainted Forgotten}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Camo Undies}}: The passive charge of Neptunus does not disrupt Camo, and the initial burst of damage is enhanced by Neptunus.
* {{i|Chocolate Milk}}: Neptunus' passive charge overrides Chocolate Milk's active charge. Tear damage is determined by how charged Neptunus is.
** Once Neptunus' charge is used up, Isaac will fire uncharged Chocolate Milk tears, resulting in a much lower damage output than without Chocolate Milk.
** '''Chocolate Milk''' + {{i|Kidney Stone}}: Isaac will not fire any tears during the Kidney Stone burst.
* {{i|Kidney Stone}}: Tear bursts stack, firing a very large number of tears in combination with each other.

sections.Notes: * If other familiars that move with a similar pattern such as {{i|Multidimensional Baby}} have been collected before the Obsessed Fan, it will follow them instead with further delay.

sections.Effects:
* Grants four {{E|Soul Heart}}s.
* Heals 12 [[Hearts]].
sections.Interactions: * {{C|Tainted Bethany}}: Grants 12 blood charges.

sections.Notes:
* The chance to shoot egg sacs depends on the [[luck]] stat and is based on this formula: <math>min(\frac1 { 7 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck}   \right \rfloor}, 50\%)</math>
** At base luck (0), the chance is 14.29%, maxing out at 50% at 5 luck.
* Egg sacks will also spawn blue flies or spiders if they hit {{e|Fire Place}}s or invincible enemies like {{E|Death's Head}} and {{E|Stoney}}.
* It is possible to create a large number of Spiders and Flies by repeatedly shooting a closed {{E|Host}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|C Section}}: Parasitoid fetuses spawn spiders/flies and slowing creep with every hit on an enemy.
* {{i|Compound Fracture}} / {{i|Cricket's Body}} / {{i|The Parasite}}: When egg sacks are fired, they will split into smaller egg sacks. Split egg sacks from The Parasite will not look like egg sacks.
* {{i|Cupid's Arrow}}: Egg sacks will apply their effect to every enemy hit.
* {{i|Fire Mind}} / {{I|Explosivo|dlc=a}} : If the explosion effect triggers on an egg sack, it will produce a much larger pool of slowing creep.
* {{i|Hive Mind}}: Flies and spiders are bigger and deal double damage.
* {{i|Technology 2|r+}}: Rapid damage ticks can cause a large amount of flies and spiders to spawn.

sections.Effects:
* Tears leave a small, short-lasting pool of [[creep]] upon hitting an enemy or when their range is depleted.
** The creep deals 1 damage per tick or 30 damage per second.
** {{Dlc|r}} The creep can deal up to 25 damage.
** Multiple creep pools can inflict damage on an enemy simultaneously.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Compound Fracture}} / {{I|Cricket's Body}} / {{I|The Parasite}}: Each split tear leaves a creep, creating lots of creep pools.
* {{I|Explosivo}}: Leaves an explosion-sized creep whenever the Explosivo tear goes off.
* {{I|Flat Stone}}: Each tear bounce leaves a pool of creep.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}}: Spawns creep trail under the tear on a constant time interval.
* {{I|Mom's Knife}}: Spawns a line of creep behind the knife as it shoots towards enemies, each one left on random time interval.
* {{I|Spirit Sword}}: The projectiles from the sword spawn creep pools, sword attacks do not.
* {{I|Tech.5|dlc=a+}}: The lasers spawn creep pools always when it hits obstacles and occasionally on enemies.
* {{I|Technology 2|dlc=a+}}: The lasers rapidly spawn creep pools on hitting both obstacles and enemies.
* {{I|Tech X}}: The laser rings spawn creep pools when it hits enemies on a constant time interval.
* {{I|Trisagion}}: The blasts leave long trails of creep pools, and a creep for each damaging tick. Since the effect stacks, they cause massive damage.

sections.Effects:
* +0.7 [[tears]]
* Significantly shrinks Isaac, allowing him to squeeze between objects and makes some enemy shots pass over him.
sections.Notes:
* With enough speed and the correct angle or being pushed by an explosion, it is possible to cross pits and pass through obstacles, allowing Isaac to reach places he usually isn't able to reach.
* Pluto can stack with other size reduction effects.
* May allow Isaac to squeeze through the walls and floors in {{R|Crawl Space}}s and 2nd/3rd phase of {{e|Rotgut}}. Passing through the outermost wall in an unintended direction leads to the {{R|I AM ERROR}} room.
* The decrease in size makes dodging certain tear effects easier, most notably {{E|Hush}}'s continuum tears, and {{E|Dogma}}'s feather attacks from their respective second phases.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Cricket's Body}}: Split tears' range is dropped drastically. Range ups do not mitigate the effect.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}: Drops the bombs' range drastically despite no change in the [[range]] stat, greatly increasing chance of self-damage. Range ups do not mitigate the effect.

sections.Effects:
* Gives Isaac a chance to fire tears that create rifts where they land, which damage nearby enemies and pull in enemies, [[pickups]], and tears/shots from all sources for 2 seconds.
** Rifts deal half of the tear's damage twice each tick (3x its damage per second), and enemy shots pulled into the rift will damage other enemies.
** The size of the rift increases with Isaac's damage.
sections.Notes:
* The chance to fire a rift tear depends on the [[luck]] stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: <math>\min(\frac1 { 20 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor},20\%)</math><ref>https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15K8Xgxoxdx68AIaxuLXgZoJJlG36UPgy3_aeDpAM5tU/edit?usp=sharing</ref>
** At base Luck (0), the chance is 5%, maxing out at 20% at 15 Luck.
sections.Tips:
* Rift tears can be used to move pickups that might be located behind [[spikes]].
** Placement of the rifts is easier with items which provide a degree of control over tears, e.g. {{I|Eye of the Occult}}.
* Because the pull of Ocular Rift affects enemy shots, it can be used defensively to dismantle the curtains of bullets that Isaac would otherwise have to dodge. This is especially useful for bosses like {{E|Hush}} and {{E|Delirium}}.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Brimstone}}: Rifts may appear where a brimstone beam hits rock, walls or enemies.
* {{i|The Parasite}} / {{i|Compound Fracture}}: Causes many smaller rifts to also spawn.
* {{i|The Ludovico Technique}}: Each tick of damage has chance of creating rift, which will be slightly bigger in size.
* {{i|Tech X}}: Rifts may appear where a laser ring hits rock, walls or enemies.
* {{i|Technology}} / {{i|Technology 2}}: Rifts may appear where a laser hits rock, walls or enemies.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: May spawn a line of rifts where the laser travels.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Epic Fetus}}: Overridden by Epic Fetus.
* {{I|Mom's Knife}}: Overridden by Mom's Knife.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns seven [[coin]]s around Isaac.
** These coins may be any normal type with their respective usual chances: {{E|Penny|text=Pennies}}, {{E|Nickel}}s, {{E|Dime}}s, {{E|Lucky Penny|text=Lucky Pennies}}, {{E|Sticky Nickel}}s or {{E|Golden Penny|text=Golden Pennies}}.
** Denomination of coins that spawn is not affected by [[luck]].
* {{dlc|r+}} Spawns one of the following trinkets: {{T|Blessed Penny|n}}, {{T|Bloody Penny}}, {{T|Burnt Penny}}, {{T|Butt Penny}}, {{T|Charged Penny|n}}, {{T|Counterfeit Penny}}, {{T|Cursed Penny|n}}, {{T|Flat Penny}} and {{T|Rotten Penny|n}}.
sections.Synergies: * {{T|Nuh Uh!}}: On the low chance this item spawns in {{s|Womb}} or {{s|Corpse|n}}, coins dropped will instead be replaced by drops from Nuh Uh!'s drop table.

sections.Effects:
* Gives Isaac a 25% chance to shoot a spore that, in addition to dealing damage, will stick to enemies.
** The chance is not affected by [[Luck]].<ref>https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15K8Xgxoxdx68AIaxuLXgZoJJlG36UPgy3_aeDpAM5tU/edit?usp=sharing</ref>
* Spores will explode 2.5 seconds after sticking to an enemy, dealing 5 damage to and [[poison]]ing nearby enemies and firing four more spores in a cross pattern.
** Spores produced from Isaac's spores have [[Tear Effects#Homing|homing]].
** The spore effects will not damage Isaac.
* {{transformation contribution|Fun Guy}}
sections.Notes:
* Items that deal continuous damage such as {{i|Brimstone}}, and {{i|Technology 2}} will apply spores to enemies as well, despite the absence of tears.
* Spores can stick to [[Frozen]] enemies, and will act normally.
sections.Synergies:
* {{i|Bird's Eye}} / {{i|Ghost Pepper}} / {{t|Gigante Bean}}: Spore explosions are considered farts, meaning Isaac will occasionally spawn fires when a spore bursts if he has either pepper, and Gigante Bean will increase their size.
* {{i|C Section}}: Some fetuses stick to enemies, expand, then burst.
* {{I|Godhead}}: Godhead's aura expands as the spore tear grows on enemies.
* {{I|Lodestone}}: Magnetized enemies draw other enemies to them, greatly increasing the chance that spores spread to other enemies.
* {{i|Lost Contact}}: Stuck tears will block projectiles shot by attached enemies, crippling or even stopping their ability to shoot projectiles entirely.
* {{i|My Reflection}}: The mini-spores generated by the spore explosions are affected by My Reflection.
sections.Interactions: * {{I|Dr. Fetus}}/{{I|Epic Fetus}}/{{I|Mom's Knife}}: No effect.

sections.Effects:
* Stops all enemies including bosses until a fire button is pressed.
** This does not affect troll bombs.
** Touching frozen enemies will still damage Isaac.
** Co-op babies can fire without ending the effect.
** Stops {{E|Red Fire Place}}s/{{E|Purple Fire Place}}s from shooting projectiles.
** Bosses will resume their actions after 30 seconds have passed, while non-boss enemies (except {{E|Lil' Haunt}}) are still paused.
*** {{Dlc|r}} All enemies resume actions after 30 seconds
sections.Notes:
* New enemies generated during Pause being active will not be frozen and act normally. This applies for spawn-upon-death effects such as {{E|Attack Fly|text=Attack Flies}} created by a {{E|Moter}}, or a Boss that stopped becoming frozen and began summoning enemies.
* Damage against paused multi-segmented bosses works unpredictably, most notably allowing you to damage {{E|Scolex}} on normally invulnerable parts.
** The health bars of multi-segmented bosses may not be updated properly, making it seem as if they died without running out of health.
* Reducing a boss to zero health whilst they are paused will initiate their death animation but they will not die until a fire button is pressed or the 30 second timer has lapsed.
* {{C|The Forgotten}}'s Soul will be able to extend far past the normal limits of the chain when activated while {{C|The Soul}} is out.
* {{dlc+|r}} Pausing in the room before entering the minecart in the {{s|Mines}} causes the minecart to freeze, trapping the player inside of it until they exit to the main menu.{{dlc-}}
* Using {{I|Dark Arts}} will not stop the effect.
* Pausing in {{r|Boss Rush}} just as bosses spawn will cause the bosses to not deal contact damage to Isaac for the full duration. This allows for contact damage items, such as {{I|Mom's Heels}}, to be extremely viable in completing Boss Rush.
* If you freeze {{e|Haunted Chest}} at a time when {{e|Polty}} has not yet picked it up, the chest will be impossible to open in any way until {{e|Polty}} unfreezes or dies. If you try to push {{e|Haunted Chest}} away from {{e|Polty}}, the ghost will appear immediately at the current chest after unfreezing.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|120 Volt}} / {{I|Monstrance}} / {{I|Mom's Knife}}: Continues to damage enemies even while paused, allowing for insane amounts of damage.
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns green wisps on the middle ring. Wisps pause all enemies and enemy shots for 3 seconds when destroyed. This effect is not cancelled by shooting tears.}}
* Items that can be used without firing, such a Mom's knife and orbitals can do massive amounts of damage.
** Any item that does damage without firing + {{i|4.5 Volt}}: Pause can be recharged while the effect is active, allowing for potentially infinite uptime.
* {{I|Daddy Longlegs}}: Hitting pause stops all enemies from moving but Daddy Longlegs will continue his normal attack pattern, potentially clearing many rooms without any risk of damage unless spawn-on-death enemies are killed and Isaac has trouble avoiding them, forcing him to fire. This strategy is also time demanding so if going for Boss Rush etc. this synergy is detrimental.
* {{C|Tainted Jacob}}: Dark Esau will also be affected by Pause. With proper timing, this allows him to melt through endgame bosses with large amounts of armor-piercing damage by having Dark Esau sit on top of them.
* {{I|The Ludovico Technique}}: The giant tear keeps dealing damage in stopped time, making it easy for boss kills.
sections.Interactions:
* {{I|Car Battery}}: No effect.
* {{I|Marked}}: While the crosshair is out, immediately ends Pause's effect upon use. The player can cancel the use of Marked by pressing the "drop" key or button to then use Pause.
* Using the item in [[Greed Mode]] will freeze all enemies but will not pause the timer. New waves of enemies will continue to spawn even while the effect is active.

sections.Effects:
* Gives Isaac +0.3 [[speed]] and 2 {{e|Soul Heart}}s.
* Isaac becomes immune to [[spikes]] and [[creep]].
sections.Notes:
* Does not prevent damage from {{R|Curse Room}} doors, {{E|Spiked Chest}}s, or [[Rocks#Spiked Rocks|spiked rocks]], but does protect against spiked rock bridges.
* Does not prevent use of a {{R|Sacrifice Room}}.
sections.Interactions: * {{i|A Pound of Flesh}}: Does not offer immunity against spikes placed around pickups.

sections.Effects:
* Increases [[Knock-back|tear knockback]].
** If the player has [[piercing tears]], the knockback effect is reduced.
* {{Dlc|nr}} Tear size multiplier: 1.25x.
* {{Dlc|r}} +0.12 tear size.
* {{dlc|nr}} {{tear delay down|1}}
* {{dlc|r}} +0.5 [[fire rate]].
sections.Interactions:
* {{t|Blister}}: Overrides Pisces.
* {{i|Brimstone}}: The beam gains knockback.
* {{I|Cupid's Arrow}}/{{i|Death's Touch}}/{{i|Dead Onion}}/{{i|Sagittarius}}: Tears gain knockback.
* {{i|Dr. Fetus}}/{{i|Epic Fetus}}/{{i|Ipecac}}: Explosions also gain increased knockback.
* {{i|Mom's Knife}}: The knife gains knockback.
* {{i|Technology}}/{{i|Technology 2}}/{{i|Tech X}}: The lasers gain knockback.
** Technology 2's constant laser has such strong knockback, it can pin enemies to walls.
* {{i|Trisagion}}: Adds knockback to blasts, which can not only significantly repel enemies when used correctly, it can deal a high amount of damage to enemies unable to escape the knockback.

sections.Effects:
* Spawns a bone [[familiar]] that can be aimed with the fire buttons in all directions and does contact damage.
** The familiar will continuously hover back and forth in the direction that it is pointing in.
* The damage is equal to Isaac's [[Damage|tear damage]] and is dealt 6 times per second.
** The damage increases when Isaac is moving on the direction the familiar is pointing in based on Isaac's current [[speed]], up to twice of its base damage.
* The familiar will damage {{g|Poop}}s and {{e|Fire Place}}s.
sections.Synergies:
* {{I|Proptosis}}: Triples the contact damage. Has no penalty with range.
* {{i|Spin to Win}}: As Spin to Win allows moving faster than the normal limit, the bonus damage from jabbing can also be over 100%.
* {{i|Spirit Sword}}: When doing a spin attack, the familiar will spin with the sword.
sections.Interactions: * {{I|BFFS!}}: Doubles the base contact damage, but not the bonus damage granted from Isaac's movement.

sections.Notes:

* Multiple friendly enemies can spawn at the same time.
* For enemies that spawn other enemies, the spawned enemies will also be friendly.
* Enemy variants may spawn.
sections.Interactions:

* {{i|Blood Puppy}}: Either angry version of Blood Puppy will target friendly enemies as well and can drag them along with it when it charges them. Blood Puppy cannot damage friendly enemies however friendly enemies can damage Blood Puppy despite not targeting it outright.
* {{i|Broken Modem}}: Broken Modem also affects friendly enemies and projectiles created by them.
* {{I|Eraser}}: Enemies erased via Eraser will never spawn again. This can be a detriment if Vises are erased, as it greatly reduces the usefulness of Poke Go.
* {{dlc+|r}} {{I|Ghost Bombs}} / {{i|Hungry Soul}} / {{I|Purgatory}} / {{i|Vade Retro}}: Explosions from ghosts can kill friendly enemies.{{dlc-}}

* Spawns a combination of 3 {{E|Red Heart}}s, {{E|Soul Heart}}s or {{E|Black Heart}}s on the floor when picked up.

sections.Effects: * Spawns a [[familiar]] that drops a [[Heart]], [[coin]], {{e|Bomb}}, or {{e|Key}} (or any of their variations) alternatively every 5 or 6 [[rooms]].

* Can spawn troll bombs.
sections.Synergies: * {{i|BFFS!}}: The familiar drops pickups alternatingly every 4 or 5 rooms.

sections.Effects:
* If the box is empty, it picks up items and pickups in a room and stores them.
** {{dlc|r}} Moving Box can carry up to 10 items or pickups at once, randomly picked (i.e. items are not prioritized).
* If the box is not empty, places all stored items and pickups in the current room.
sections.Notes:
* {{dlc+|r+}} Moving Box can sometimes spawn within the special bedroom created by {{i|Lil Portal}}.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc|nr}} There is no limit to the number of items and pickups that can be held in the box.
* The best way to utilize Moving Box is often to absorb a large number of weaker items, then place them all into one room, and use a reroll effect to reroll them all at the same time. This is especially effective in Secret Rooms.
* Any stored items and pickups unpacked from Moving Box will remain identical to what was originally packed; [[pills]], [[Cards and Runes|cards, and runes]] will stay the same, {{e|Sticky Nickel}}s will remain stuck to the floor, active items keep their charge in the box, and {{E|Chest}}s will have the same contents as they would if they had been opened immediately.
* Stealing from {{r|Shop}}s and {{r|Devil Room}}s is not possible; only items on pedestals will be packed up.
* All existing Moving Boxes share their opened/closed state. Therefore, it is not possible to carry a Moving Box that is holding items within another Moving Box as the items must be unpacked first.
* If used in a room with a choice of multiple item pedestals, only one of the choice objects will be packed up and {{dlc|nr}} the rest will remain and behave normally / {{dlc|r}} the rest will disappear.
** {{dlc|nr}} Both items presented by {{i|There's Options}} and {{i|More Options}} can be taken.
** {{dlc|nr}} Both {{i|The Polaroid}} and {{i|The Negative}} can be taken.
** {{dlc|nr}} If used in the {{r|Boss Rush}} room, one of the objects is packed up but the rush is not started. The remaining item choices start the rush as normal.
*** {{dlc|r}} Using Moving Box to pack items in {{r|Boss Rush}} starts the challenge.
* {{dlc|nr}} If used in a {{r|Challenge Room}} or {{r|Boss Challenge Room}} the objects within can be packed up without starting the challenge.
** {{dlc|r}} Using Moving Box in these rooms starts the challenge.
* {{dlc|r}} Disappearing pickups that are spawned by {{c|Tainted Magdalene}} / {{p|Soul of Magdalene|n}} or {{c|Tainted Keeper}} can't be packed into Moving Box.
sections.Synergies:
* {{Book of Virtues synergy|description=Spawns a box wisp on the middle ring. Moving Box must drop a pickup/item in order for it to spawn wisps. The wisps invoke the effect of {{I|The Book of Sin}} when destroyed.}}
* {{i|Glowing Hourglass}}: If a charged Glowing Hourglass is stored in the Moving Box, it can be unpacked and used to rewind time and regain some item charges.
** {{dlc|nr}} Both items regain their charges, essentially allowing unlimited use.
** {{dlc|r}} Moving Box charges are regained, but Glowing Hourglass will lose one charge.
sections.Interactions:
* {{i|Car Battery|nr}}: Activation swaps the contents of the box with the contents of the room.
** {{dlc|r}} No effect.
* {{I|Death Certificate}}: Takes one random item from a Death Certificate room which is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.
* {{i|Flip}}: Moving items that are able to be swapped by Flip will still be able to be swapped after placing them down again. However, empty item pedestals that only contain the "ghostly" item cannot be moved unless flipped.
* {{i|Options?}}: Only one of the choice pickups will be packed up and the other will disappear.
* {{i|Void}}: This item's effect cannot be absorbed by Void. It will be treated as a passive item by the Void.

sections.Effects:
* Identifies all [[pills]] upon pickup.
